## 2026-08-06 — #305 — parser: the five top-level named kinds stop each minting their own `{name}` and take it from one `producer.topLevelName`, so a nameless `<attributeGroup>`/`<element>`/`<attribute>` is a CONTENT-INDEPENDENT grammar fault instead of a `QName{tns, ""}` carried on — but the arbiter's round-1 reject was not about the helper at all, it was about the TWO GUARDS THE CHANGE LEFT BEHIND: one retained guard's freshly-written justification named a path `xsd.NewParticle` had already closed, and BOTH retained guards turned out provably deletable with the whole suite still green, because the new helper shadows them on every path the existing rows exercise

- Shipped on `wip/issue-305` as two commits on top of `origin/main` @ `8b3aa8d`
  (`conformance: claim the twenty half-bounded integer lexical fixtures (#449)`)
  — `17768e1` (`parser: route all five top-level kinds through one topLevelName
  helper (#305)`, mason, 4 files, +172/−68) and `9eb4f22` (`parser: repair round
  for #305 — correct retained-guard docs, add coverage, fix GAP ref`, mason,
  4 files, +83/−4) — plus this LOG commit. Branch total before the LOG commit:
  **5 files, +251/−68**, all under `parser/` — `parser/produce.go`,
  `parser/produce_complex.go`, `parser/produce_absentname_test.go`,
  `parser/produce_groups_test.go`, `parser/redefine_test.go`. **Arbiter REJECT on
  round 1, ACCEPT on round 2 — one repair round of the two-round cap consumed**,
  three blocking findings, all three fixed at the root rather than papered over.
- **Ratchet: unchanged, on BOTH arbiter runs. schema 9251 pass / 6181 fail
  (15432), datatypes 1151 / 22 (1173), instance 0 / 26426 — identical to
  `origin/main` before and after.** The arbiter's figures, copied not recomputed;
  it read them straight out of the expectations files rather than off mason's
  report, on each round. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` at `9eb4f22` **wrote nothing** and
  `git status --porcelain` was empty afterwards, so there is no flip in either
  direction to explain and nothing regressed. This is the outcome the #295
  post-land cartographer comment predicted for a *knowable* reason rather than a
  hopeful one: #295 already banked the +10 that every nameless/empty-named
  construct in the suite was worth (`attQ005`, `attC004`, `attgB007`,
  `notatB011`, `addB010`, `Notation/name00201m1`, `idA031/B031/C031`), so #305's
  flips were **already taken** and this issue converts rejections into
  better-cited rejections rather than moving a lane. It was still MEASURED, per
  the issue body's own warning about #206's wrong "unchanged" prediction.
- **The change is one helper and five call sites, and the whole of its value is
  WHERE the rejection happens rather than THAT it happens.** `producer.topLevelName`
  (`parser/produce.go:736`) expands the `name` attribute of a top-level
  `<complexType>`, `<group>`, `<attributeGroup>`, `<element>` or `<attribute>`
  into the document's target namespace (§3.17.2) and rejects an unusable one
  before any child is walked; `run`'s switch takes all five names from it
  (`:602`, `:612`, `:622`, `:637`, `:647`). Three of the five previously minted
  `QName{Space: tns, Local: ""}` and carried on — `attributeGroup` via
  `buildAttributeGroup`, plus `element` and `attribute`; the other two had
  guarded it inside their own producer since #206. **After #295 all five were
  already rejected one layer down** with a real rule ID, so the improvement is
  not the outcome but the diagnostic: the schema author now gets a grammar
  message about the document they wrote instead of a component-invariant about a
  component they never saw, and gets it **content-independently** — the #206
  defect was that a nameless container's verdict depended on whether its body
  happened to hold a local element, whose `xsd.NewLocalScope` would charge
  `e-props-correct`, an unrelated rule, and only sometimes.
- **The fault carries NO rule ID, uniformly across all five, and that abstention
  is the grounding's central holding.** `name` is `use="required"` typed
  `xs:NCName` on `xs:topLevelComplexType`, `xs:namedGroup`,
  `xs:namedAttributeGroup`, `xs:topLevelElement` and `xs:topLevelAttribute` in
  the schema for schema documents, and no numbered Schema Representation
  Constraint states a clause of its own for it — §3.4.3 `src-ct` has exactly five
  clauses, none about `name`, and §3.6.3 `src-attribute_group` is literally "None
  as such". A plain `fmt.Errorf`, the footing `<include>` with no `schemaLocation`
  already stands on. **For the two DECLARATION kinds the oracle ruled the same
  way for a different reason**: `e-props-correct` cl.1 (§3.3.6.1) and
  `a-props-correct` cl.1 (§3.2.6.1) already exist at the xsd constructor layer,
  both riding the generic "properties as tableau'd" clause (there is no
  `e-name-correct`/`a-name-correct`), so attaching either at the grammar layer
  would **duplicate and compete with** a citation already in use rather than
  close a gap — legitimate defense in depth, not new enforcement. STYLE E2 was
  held on both halves, and the new tests pin the abstention by asserting
  `errors.As(err, &xe)` does **not** match — the right shape for pinning an
  abstention rather than merely a message.
- **The grounding corrected the issue body's own citation, and the correction is
  a one-digit section slip of exactly the class this log has been counting.** The
  body cited §3.7.3 for attribute-group's "None as such"; §3.7.3 is the
  **model-group-definition** section (`xmlschema11-1.md:2286`, also "None as
  such"), and the attribute-group anchor is **§3.6.3** `src-attribute_group`
  (`:2198`). Both are "None as such", so the body's *claim* was true and its
  *citation* was wrong — the failure mode nothing in the gate can see. The
  corrected §3.6.3 is used in `topLevelName`'s doc and the test doc; the arbiter
  separately verified that `produceModelGroupDefinition`'s pre-existing §3.7.3
  citation for `<group>` is correct and stays.
- **Finding 1 — the retained `<group>` guard's justification named a path that
  cannot reach it, which is the P3a failure mode in its purest form.** `17768e1`
  kept both #206 guards and argued at length for keeping them; for the `<group>`
  half it named `resolveModelGroup`'s on-demand build via a `<group ref>` lexical.
  That path **cannot deliver an empty local part**: `resolveModelGroup`'s only
  non-test caller is `allGroupOf`, the only non-test construction site of
  `xsd.ModelGroupRef` is `produceGroupRefParticle` (`produce_complex.go:1124`)
  feeding straight into `xsd.NewParticle`, and `xsd/particle.go:89-93` rejects an
  empty `ModelGroupRef` local part as `RuleComponentInvariant` unconditionally —
  **#294's guard fires first**. The arbiter reproduced that, then did the thing
  that made the finding useful rather than merely correct: **it went and found a
  path that IS live.** `produceRedefinition` (`parser/redefine.go:505,533`) mints
  `qn` from a `<redefine>` child's own `name` attribute and calls
  `buildModelGroupDefinition` directly, never touching `run`'s switch or
  `topLevelName`. So the conclusion ("keep the guard") was right and every word
  of the reasoning was wrong — and a comment asserting a false invariant is worse
  than no comment (P2), because the next session that trusts it deletes the guard
  when #294's coverage is noticed and silently reopens the #206 shape on the
  redefine path. The complexType half's account (`resolveBaseType`'s on-demand
  build off a `base=` lexical resolved against the prescan index, which indexes a
  `name=""` declaration under `QName{tns, ""}`) was checked and was accurate
  throughout.
- **Finding 2 is the one with teeth, and it names a defect class this project has
  no automated defence against: an upstream guard SILENTLY UN-TESTS the
  downstream guard it shadows.** Before this branch the seven rows of
  `TestProduceNamelessTopLevelContainerRejected` were the only thing pinning the
  two #206 guards. `topLevelName` now intercepts on exactly the path those rows
  drive, so after `17768e1` all sixteen rows pinned `topLevelName` **and nothing
  else** — the arbiter stubbed each retained guard with `if false` and `go test
  ./...` stayed **fully green both times**. The branch retained two guards,
  argued for retaining them, and left both provably deletable. That reproduces
  the issue's own thesis one layer down: its `## Notes` say *"'harmless today' is
  not 'leave it'"* because the empty local part "sat latent until a new consumer
  read it", and a retained guard with a wrong rationale and no test is the same
  latency. Nothing in build, vet, lint or conformance can see this — the suite
  going green is precisely the symptom.
- **The repair added one end-to-end test per retained guard, each reaching it by
  its OWN real live path, and both were mutation-proved twice — by mason and
  independently by the arbiter.**
  `TestProduceNamelessBaseTypeRejectedOffDispatch`
  (`parser/produce_groups_test.go:427`) drives the complexType guard through
  `resolveBaseType`: a `<complexType name="d">` restricting `base=""` binds to
  the `QName{"", ""}` key the prescan indexed a later `<complexType name="">`
  under, so the on-demand build pulls the nameless type in **before `run` ever
  dispatches on it** — and DOCUMENT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and documented as such,
  because with the declarations swapped `topLevelName` raises the fault first and
  the guard goes untested again. Under the mutation it fails by **panic**, in
  `complexTypeIdentity.scopeParent`'s zero-identity assertion, with the arbiter's
  stack trace showing `resolveBaseType` entered with the zero QName — the panic
  being exactly why the fault must be charged before anything is built. Because a
  panic aborts the binary, the arbiter could not read "only this test fails" off
  that run and **did the exclusion run properly**: enumerated the package with
  `go test ./parser -list '.*'`, dropped the new test, ran the remaining **265**
  under the same mutation — `ok`. `TestParseRedefineNamelessGroupRejected`
  (`parser/redefine_test.go:460`) drives the group guard through the redefine
  path, two documents both declaring `<group name="">`; under the mutation it
  fails with the **#206 defect verbatim** — `[e-props-correct]` charged against
  the `{scope}.{parent}` because the body happens to hold a local `<element>`.
  The seven pre-existing rows stay green under both mutations.
- **The redefine test only works because THREE separate filters let `name=""`
  through, and the arbiter re-walked all three rather than trusting the trace.**
  `newRedefineSet` (`redefine.go:179-183`) does `name, ok := c.Attr("name")` and
  rejects only `!ok`, so an **absent** name dies there and an **empty** one
  survives; the prescan's `recordOriginal` branch (`produce.go:465-472`) records a
  `name=""` original after the same `ok`-only check, which is what carries the
  case past `produceRedefinition`'s `src-expredef` closing-requirement check
  (`redefine.go:506-510`); and only then does `redefine.go:533` reach the guard.
  Miss any one and the test would pass for the wrong reason.
- **Finding 3 — the new `GAP(parser)` marker landed pointing at the issue the
  commit closes**, i.e. a dead end on arrival, which STYLE P3 forbids in as many
  words. The gap is real and the arbiter reproduced it: a top-level
  `<xs:simpleType>` with `name` absent **or** `name=""` produces end to end
  **without error** — `run` expands its name inline and `xsd.NewSimpleType` has
  no `{name}` guard, unlike `NewElementDeclaration`, `NewAttributeDeclaration` and
  `NewNotation`, so the type is registered under `QName{target, ""}` and both
  layers stay silent. Filed as **#523** (`kind/gap`, open) and the marker at
  `parser/produce.go:735` repointed at it. The marker claims **no error
  direction** — what a schema so registered goes on to do downstream is not
  established — which the arbiter called textbook P3a rather than a hedge.
- **Exported surface: unchanged** — `go doc -all ./parser` byte-identical against
  a throwaway worktree at `origin/main`, verified by the arbiter on both rounds.
  `topLevelName` is unexported and no new exported identifier appears, so no T5
  question arises. `produceElement` and `produceAttribute` gained a `qname`
  parameter; `grep` confirms `run` is each one's only caller, so the signature
  change is total and no path is left reading `name` itself for these five kinds.
- **Gate at the tip of this LOG commit, on a clean tree:** `go build ./...` OK,
  `go vet ./...` OK, `go test ./...` all ok, **`golangci-lint run` → 0 issues**.
  The arbiter additionally ran `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance
  -count=1` (ok, 28s) and the ratchet write run (ok, 30s, wrote nothing) at
  `9eb4f22`; this LOG commit is docs-only and moves no expectation.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Both #206 guards are KEPT, not deleted, even though `run` can no longer
     reach either.** Each has a live non-`run` entry path whose name never passes
     through `topLevelName` — `resolveBaseType`'s on-demand build for the
     complexType half, `produceRedefinition` for the group half — and deleting
     them would restore the #206 content-dependent verdict on exactly those
     paths. The issue's Acceptance left "unreachable-from-`run` or folded into
     the helper" open; this answers it as *retained and re-documented*, and the
     repair round is what made the answer defensible rather than merely stated.
  2. **The fault stays a plain `fmt.Errorf` for the two declaration kinds too**,
     rather than borrowing `e-props-correct`/`a-props-correct`. Per the
     grounding: those verdicts belong to the constructor layer, still fire on the
     LOCAL paths, and duplicating them at the grammar layer would put two
     citations in competition for one condition.
  3. **`TestProduceNamelessTopLevelContainerRejected` → `TestProduceNamelessTopLevelRejected`.**
     All seven original rows survive verbatim and nine were added for the three
     newly-guarded kinds (each with `name` absent AND `name=""` pinned identical,
     each with a content-bearing body as the content-independence guard). The
     test's subject genuinely widened past "container"; the arbiter accepted the
     rename explicitly as the more honest choice rather than charging it as a
     deviation.
  4. **The new tests went in `produce_groups_test.go`/`redefine_test.go`, not in
     `produce_absentname_test.go`.** That file's table is `wantRule`/`wantLine`-
     shaped and these rows assert a plain-error shape; forcing them in would have
     meant two tables in one file for no gain. Cross-references were written in
     both directions and the arbiter verified both.
  5. **`TestProduceAbsentNameAndEmptyRefRejected` lost its `nameless global
     <element>` row** — that shape now fails at the grammar layer before reaching
     `xsd.NewElementDeclaration`, so it moved to the table above; the
     constructor's own `e-props-correct` verdict stays pinned by the surviving
     LOCAL row, whose `produceLocalElement` path is its only remaining
     parser-visible call site for a missing `{name}`. Verified as leaving no gap.
- Surprises:
  1. **A correct conclusion reached through an entirely false trace, written in
     the same commit that was CORRECTING other people's false traces.** `17768e1`
     kept a guard for a good reason and documented a reason that could not
     happen; the sentence survived because only the consumers in view were
     checked. #449's entry recorded the same shape as a citation defect; this is
     the same defect class in a *reachability* claim, where the gate is equally
     blind and the reader has even less chance of noticing.
  2. **The suite going green was the SYMPTOM, not the evidence.** Both retained
     guards were stubbable with `if false` and nothing turned red, and that is a
     direct consequence of the change being *good* — the new helper intercepts
     earlier on every path the tests drive. Any change that adds an upstream
     guard has this property, and there is no lint, vet or coverage signal for
     it. It cost this issue its one repair round, and it will recur: #518, #433
     and #523 are all upstream-guard issues over the same producers.
  3. **`resolveModelGroup` looked live to two readers and was closed by #294 all
     along.** The path that actually still matters — `<redefine>` — only exists
     because #286 landed `<xs:redefine>` five sessions ago, so the guard's real
     justification is younger than the guard.
- Friction:
  1. **The GitHub thread was READABLE this session, and the difference is worth
     recording against #449's Friction 1.** That entry could cite no comment
     permalinks because `gh` returned 403 for the chronicler; this session read
     all four comments through the GitHub MCP tool, so the Thread record below is
     complete. The gap is therefore **session-scoped and intermittent**, not a
     standing loss — which is the more annoying diagnosis, because a convention
     every entry in this file honours holds or breaks according to which toolset

- **The guard is `citations_test.go` at the module root (292 lines,
  `package goxsd8_test`), and the arbiter verified it NON-VACUOUSLY rather than

  named as the failure mode meta-tests of this shape actually die of. It scans

     consistency**, over the grounding's own medium-confidence alternative of

  1. **The grounding's own prose miscounted its own table, and the miscount
     propagated into the landed comment — in the issue whose entire subject is
     the reliability of numbers written into comments.** §3's summary line says
     "34 sites" for the `5`→`9` bucket and "6" for `4`→`5`; the per-site table

     21, and `value/valuespace.go` one. The title's scope was inherited from the

     37 sites, since every wrong number was a real PRINCIPLES.md item. The
     bound half is nearly worthless alone and only earns its place because it
     also proves the list is gap-free; all the enforcement is in the per-file

  (`Ratchet` writes both `d.Improved` and `d.New`,
  `conformance/expectations.go:177,180`, while `runConformanceLane` logs only
  `d.Improved`), so a non-arbiter `Ratchet:` line is still a prediction *of the

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Verdict-contract over mechanical check** — not a preference for the
     weaker option but the grounding's finding that the write is a working-tree
     filesystem write no Go code can stage or commit. A "fails when the run
     would write" check would still have to be run by someone and its result
     still banked by someone; the seam is the verdict step either way.
  2. **The addendum was folded in rather than deferred**, because the issue's
     own addendum comment argued a check of the preferred shape *"necessarily
     computes the improvement set"* — surfacing it is the same mechanism, and
     adopting only the banking half would have closed the banking seam while
     leaving every non-arbiter agent blind to its own lane movement.

     sentence.** The value of the passage is that the #202 defect is named as a
     defect; a rewrite risks demoting that. Three states plus "there is no
     fourth state" preserves it exactly.

     invocation.** The repair instruction named that slot; mason did not exceed

     seam: #303 is *run-vs-bank* on the **accept** path; #354 is

## 2026-08-07 — #304 — process: the phantom `go tool logguard` is struck rather than built, by naming ONE authority for the gate and making the other three texts defer to it — CLAUDE.md's "Commands" block is now the single source of truth, a step absent from it is not a gate step however confidently a brief/LOG/issue names one, and its absence is not a gate failure; the arbiter is told in as many words to say that in one line and move on instead of re-deriving it, which is the actual cost this issue was filed over: **#206, #217 and #219 each spent a full adjudication reaching the identical conclusion by the identical route**; docs/config only, +30/−0, no Go code, arbiter ACCEPT on round 1

- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** The
  arbiter's figures, copied not recomputed: `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test
  ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` passed in 34.9s, and
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` checked
  immediately after — before anything else, per the contract #303 landed

  outcome for a docs-only change with no validation behavior; nothing to
  commit and nothing discarded. Gate on the judged tree: build/test/vet pass,
  `golangci-lint run` `0 issues.`, conformance PASS in 37.98s over **41858
  cases across 6 lanes** with no improved-but-unbanked cases reported.
- **The decision was Branch A ("strike it"), not Branch B ("build it"), and
  the count is what decided it.** The issue offered both and required the
  choice to be stated and argued as part of the deliverable. Branch A closes
  the drift *permanently and independently of whether the tool is ever built*
  — the issue says so itself, calling A "cheapest" and noting it "closes the
  drift regardless." Branch B would reattempt a build that already took two
  arbiter rejections on `wip/issue-195` (`63c2e69`, parked `needs-replan`
  2026-07-28) and would leave the per-session adjudication toll running until
  it landed. The arbiter agreed on the record. This is worth naming as a
  pattern: **an issue that offers a cheap fix and an expensive one, where the
  cheap one fully discharges the stated complaint, is not a real choice** —
  the expensive branch was really a separate feature wearing the same issue
  number, and #195's park is the evidence that it is not cheap.
- **Decision: the fix is placed at all four texts that state the gate, not
  just the one the Acceptance named.** The Acceptance said "add one line to
  `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (or CLAUDE.md's Commands block)"; mason wrote all four
  and flagged the `.claude/agents/arbiter.md` edit for scrutiny as possible
  scope creep. The arbiter ruled it **justified scope, not creep**, on two
  grounds worth preserving: the issue's own **Spec** section names
  `.claude/agents/arbiter.md` among the governing texts, and "Concretely:"
  introduces a floor rather than a ceiling. The merits argument is the
  stronger one — *the arbiter is where the cost was actually paid*, so a rule
  living only in CLAUDE.md would still have made the arbiter go look. The
  arbiter separately confirmed the two constitutional boundaries were
  respected: neither CLAUDE.md's "one rule" nor the ratchet-integrity section
  of `.claude/agents/arbiter.md` was touched.
- **Decision: the wording departs from the issue's on purpose.** The issue
  says the gate is "those four commands"; CLAUDE.md now says "build/test/vet
  + `golangci-lint run` + the conformance run." The block also lists the
  ratchet, `go generate` and `fetchspecs`, which are *not* gate steps, so
  "four commands" would have been a fresh ambiguity inside the paragraph
  written to remove one. The arbiter accepted the better wording explicitly.
- Surprises — **the phantom's last live anchor had already dissolved on its
  own.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md` now asserts that `go tool logguard` "has never
  existed," and the arbiter checked whether a reachable counterexample could
  embarrass that claim: `git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/wip/*'`
  lists only 256, 271, 287 and 304 — **`wip/issue-195` is gone from the
  remote**, so the one branch that ever contained a `tools/logguard` is no
  longer fetchable. The design survives only as prose in
  `docs/LOG/2026-07.md:8399-8480`. Branch B was therefore more expensive than
  the issue body assumed when it said to "cherry-pick what is reusable" from
  `63c2e69`: there is nothing left to cherry-pick from. That strengthens the
  Branch A choice after the fact, and it is a reminder that **an issue body's
  cost estimate ages with the refs it depends on.**
- Surprises — **`logguard` is now more written-down than it was, not less,
  and that is the point.** Striking a phantom did not mean deleting the name:
  it now appears in exactly two non-LOG files, both times labelled as the
  standing example of a step that is *not* a gate step. Deleting the name
  would have left the next brief that utters it with nothing to resolve
  against, which is precisely the state that cost three sessions.
- Friction — **none in this session, and that is the whole finding.** This
  issue exists to bill the friction of three *previous* sessions, and it was
  discharged in one round with a docs-only diff. The cost curve is the record
  worth keeping: #206 (2026-07-29) discovered the phantom while running the
  gate and closed with "do not leave a phantom gate step in circulation";
  #217 re-established it; #219 (2026-07-30, `dbcfd161`) spent verdict space
  confirming *from scratch* that `tools/logguard` is absent, that `go.mod`'s
  tool block does not list it, that #195 is parked, and that neither
  CLAUDE.md nor WORKFLOW step 5 names it. Three identical adjudications by
  the identical route, ~9 days between the filing and the fix, and the issue
  sat `ready` the whole time — **this was never a ledger leak; it was a
  correctly-filed issue outrun by the queue.** Note for the next `/retro`:
  the priority-evidence comment on #304 was posted 2026-07-30 and the issue
  was still not pulled forward until 2026-08-07, so posting cost evidence on
  a thread is demonstrably not the same as changing its scheduling.

- **The unchanged prediction was measured, and this time it held.** The issue
  body demanded exactly that, on the record that "#206 made the identical
  prediction and it was wrong — its repair round moved the schema lane by one."
  A structural back-pointer with no validation consumer really is lane-neutral
  *here*; what made #206's twin prediction fail was a repair, not the property.
  The lesson stands as the issue wrote it: **the prediction is cheap, the
  measurement is the deliverable.**
- **Decision (warden, blocking, pre-flight): the attribute-group hop REBINDS
  the scope parent; it does not thread its caller's.** The design comment
  proposed threading `scopeParent` all the way down `produceAttributeUses` →
  `collectAttributeContent` → `produceAttributeUse` → `produceLocalAttribute`.
  That is right for the element side, where a model group "is not a scope
  boundary" and the value passes through nesting unchanged — but
  `collectReferencedGroup` does not splice an already-built AGD component, it
  **re-walks the referenced top-level `<attributeGroup>`'s own element children
  under that group's owning producer**, so the threaded value would have been
  the *referencing* complex type's. §3.2.2.2 `dcl.att.local` maps `{parent}` off
  the `<attribute>` item's OWN ancestor axis: an `<attribute>` child of a
  top-level `<attributeGroup>` has no `<complexType>` ancestor, so its `{parent}`
  is that AGD **however many complex types reference the group**. Landed shape:
  `collectReferencedGroup` (`parser/produce_complex.go:1757`) takes **no**
  `scopeParent` parameter at all and rebinds in both exit branches — the
  `src-expredef` self-reference branch (`:1776`) and the ordinary branch
  (`:1787`) — from the QName it had already resolved, which is the same
  `AttributeGroupScopeParent{Name: …}` `buildAttributeGroup` (`:1653`) passes when
  it builds the group's own component. That identity is what keeps the
  component-level and inline foldings equal **by construction rather than by
  coincidence**, and the producer's own doc block already claimed the two folds
  compute the same §3.4.2.4 c-add2 union — a claim that would have gone false the
  moment the re-walked declarations differed in `{scope}.{parent}`. The
  invariant is now written down at `:1746-1756` where the next editor hits it.
  **The general form worth keeping: an explicit parameter is not merely tidier
  than a `*producer` field, it is what makes a REBINDING visible** — a stashed
  field would have hidden a value that must *change* at a boundary, across a
  producer switch, which is strictly worse than the mis-attribution the
  element-side note was already warning about.
- **Decision: the sum is its own type, three arms, and shares nothing with the
  element side but `ScopeVariety`.** `sc_a`'s alternation is CTD | **AGD**;
  `sc_e`'s is CTD | **MGD**. Merging them re-opens "an element scoped to an
  attribute group" as representable — the reason #206 named its sum
  `ElementScopeParent` in the first place, leaving this name free. Arms:
  `AttributeComplexTypeScopeParent`, `AttributeAnonymousComplexTypeScopeParent`
  (the named/anonymous split is a *representation* split inside CTD, forced by
  §3.4.1 `ctd-context`'s strict `{name}`/`{context}` XOR, not a second component
  kind), `AttributeGroupScopeParent`. The warden verified there is **no hidden
  fourth arm and no anonymous AGD twin**: §3.6.1 `agd-name` is "An xs:NCName
  value. Required." unconditionally, and §3.6.2.1 makes a *nested*
  `<attributeGroup>` correspond to no component at all, so the only AGD that can
  ever be a `{scope}.{parent}` is a top-level named one.
- **Decision: `AttributeScope` stores only `{parent}` and derives `Variety()`
  from its nil-ness, which made the tableau's correlation unrepresentable and
  the old check DEAD.** The tableau says `{parent}` is "Required if `{variety}`
  is *local*, otherwise must be ·absent·" — a correlation, i.e. exactly the
  shape STYLE D3/T1 say to encode away rather than check. With the record in
  place, `NewAttributeDeclaration`'s `switch scopeVariety { case ScopeGlobal,
  ScopeLocal: … }` was unreachable and was deleted along with its "unknown
  {scope}.{variety}" message; the `scopeVariety` field is gone from the struct,
  `ScopeVariety()` survives as a one-line delegate to `Scope().Variety()`, and
  **both prose sites that had promised the deleted check were updated in the
  same commit**. `NewAttributeDeclaration` is **7 params before and after** —
  #206's no-net-parameter-growth bar, met.
- **Decision: `checkAttributeScopeParent` is its own function, not a reuse of
  the element side's `unnamedScopeParent`.** That helper hardcodes
  `ruleEPropsCorrect` and the words "element declaration". Sharing it to save
  four lines would have emitted an **e-props-correct verdict against an
  attribute** — a wrong rule ID in a conformance-grade error, which is worse
  than the duplication STYLE T4 discourages. The attribute-side helper charges
  `ruleAPropsCorrect` (§3.2.6.1 clause 1) per-arm with attribute wording and
  panics in `default:` on the sealed-sum invariant.
- **Decision (deliberate non-change, ratchet hazard):
  `localAttributeDeclarationsIdentical` still compares `{variety}` ONLY.**
  Under §3.4.2.4 clause 3's fold, a base type B's attribute use and the
  structurally identical use on extension E now have parents B and E; comparing
  `{parent}` would make them non-identical, fail `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.2 on
  **legal** extensions, and regress the ratchet. The only edit to that line is
  the added paragraph saying why `{parent}` is excluded — which is the whole
  point: **the non-change is now defended in the file, so the next reader who
  spots the "incomplete" comparison finds the reason instead of the bug.**

## 2026-08-07 — #336 — conformance: the two `<extension>` forms stop being declined and the schema lane moves **+278** — the largest movement since #340's harness-level jump and the third-largest ever — with the whole safety case resting on ONE structural fact, that `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.5's fail-open can only ever set `observed = valid` and therefore cannot bank a suite-invalid case; the arbiter accepted on round 1 and its single finding is that the prose the diff wrote about its own completeness is wrong in the count (`{final}` is unmapped, so THREE clauses stay fail-open, not one) — and the follow-up issue it recommends filing **already exists, `ready`, five days old**

- Shipped on `wip/issue-336` as two commits on top of `origin/main` @ `86ce634`
  (`xsd/parser: wire AttributeDeclaration {scope}.{parent} (§3.2.1 sc_a)
  (#306)`) — `ae89c83` (`conformance: admit both <extension> forms in the
  schema lane (#336)`, mason, 2 files, **+104/−54**, `conformance/schema.go`
  and `conformance/schema_test.go`) and `db5bf9f` (`conformance: ratchet the
  schema lane for the admitted <extension> forms (#336)`, the arbiter's own
  machine-written ratchet write, 1 file, +278/−278) — plus this LOG commit.
  Branch total before the LOG commit: **3 files, +382/−332**, all under
  `conformance/`. **Arbiter ACCEPT on the first round, no repair round
  consumed**; one non-blocking finding and one nit, neither fixed here (see
  Next).
- **Ratchet: schema 9251 → 9529 of 15432 (+278) — 278 upward flips, 0
  downward, case set unchanged, no other lane touched.** The arbiter's
  figures, copied not recomputed. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` rewrote exactly 278 lines
  of `expectations/schema.txt` and touched nothing else; no expectation was
  hand-edited and no case moved between lanes. Mason's `Ratchet:` trailer on
  `ae89c83` forecast `+278 (9251 → 9529 of 15432)` from a read-only
  diagnostic run and the banking run confirmed it **figure for figure** — the
  fifth consecutive honest trailer after #235, #344 (low-by-one, explained),
  #331 and #449, and the first one to forecast a three-digit movement.
- **Third-largest schema-lane movement in the project's history, and the
  largest that comes from admitting a spec construct.** The lane's banked
  sequence is `3072 → 3094 → 4284 → … → 4283 → 9155 → … → 9251 → 9529`;
  only #340 (+4872, inline anonymous complex types) and #229 (+1190, the
  `{type definition}` sealed sum) are bigger, and both were harness-wide
  rebuilds. This one is **two predicate arms**. That ratio is the whole point
  of the issue: #264 and #265 each landed `Ratchet: unchanged` on the explicit
  promise that the movement would land here, and until this session that
  investment was unmeasured.
- **The change is small and everything interesting about it is what stays
  DECLINED.** `complexTypeDecidable` (`conformance/schema.go`) now admits
  `<simpleContent><extension>` and either `<complexContent>` alternant; it
  still declines `<simpleContent><restriction>` (§3.4.2.2 cases 1-2 are not
  produced) and a `<complexContent>`/`<simpleContent>` carrying **neither**
  alternant — the latter is a §3.4.2.3 grammar fault about the source item, so
  it declines as a limitation rather than being dressed up as a rule verdict.
  The stale doc bullet that pointed forward at #336 is deleted rather than
  reworded, which is the right end for a pointer whose target has arrived.
- **The one piece of the diff that is not in the issue's text is the one the
  arbiter spent the most words on, and it was right to be there.** Mason added
  `simpleContentExtensionDecidable`, which declines a `<simpleContent>
  <extension>` carrying a `<sequence>`/`<choice>`/`<all>`/`<group>` child.
  `xs:simpleExtensionType` (§3.4.2.2, `xmlschema11-1.md:4979`) is
  `(annotation?, attrDecls, assertions)` with the spec's own inline note
  reading *"No typeDefParticle group reference"*, and `typeDefParticle`
  (`:4645`) is exactly those four names — so the helper's allowlist is the
  grammar, neither wider nor narrower. The rationale is **not** hypothetical:
  `produceSimpleContent` (`parser/produce_complex.go:308-337`) builds
  `{content type}` from `simpleContentSimpleType(base, …)` alone and never
  reads a particle, so such a child is dropped **with no error at all**.
  Without the helper `contentDecidable` reaches its `"sequence"`/`"group"`
  arms and returns true, and the lane would report "valid" for a grammar
  fault — a fabricated verdict in the one direction that corrupts the ratchet.
  The arbiter mutation-tested it to a bare `return contentDecidable(ext)` in a
  scratch worktree and got exactly the two intended failures in
  `TestSchemaShapeDecidableDeclines`, so the guard is pinned rather than
  decorative. **Scope creep would have been leaving it out.**
- **The load-bearing safety argument is structural, not statistical, and that
  is why it survives.** The oracle's grounding named `cos-ct-extends` clause
  1.5 (§3.4.6.2, the two-step extension-then-restriction derivability check)
  as a real documented fail-open: `checkExtensionTwoStepDerivable`
  (`xsd/complexextension.go:416-421`) proves it only for a pure-extension
  chain and accepts everything else unconditionally under a marked
  `GAP(xsd)` — which includes the extremely common shape where the base is
  itself an implicit-content or `restriction base="xs:anyType"` type, so
  clause 1.5 produces **no rejection anywhere in the tree**. The grounding
  therefore required auditing newly-passing suite-invalid cases before
  ratcheting. The argument that discharges it needs no audit at all:
  `decideSchema` (`conformance/schema.go:516-521`) passes **iff**
  `observed == expected`, and the fail-open returns `nil` on both branches, so
  it can only ever set `observed = valid`; on a suite-**invalid** case that is
  `valid ≠ invalid` → **Fail**, a recorded gap, never a banked pass. A
  clause-1.5 fail-open is **structurally incapable of manufacturing a ratchet
  win.** The arbiter re-derived this from the code rather than reading mason's
  version of it, which is the correct treatment for the one claim the whole
  landing rests on.
- **Mason audited it three independent ways anyway, and the numbers agree with
  the structure.** A structural argument on `decideSchema`; an empirical
  decline-set diff — **of 417 newly-decided cases, 278 agree with the suite
  and 139 disagree, all 139 in the safe direction (suite invalid, observed
  valid), with zero newly-declined cases and zero false rejects**; and a
  manual read of all 15 newly-passing `cos-ct-extends` rejection messages. No
  clause-1.5 false accept among the banked passes. The 139 are exactly the
  recorded gaps the structure predicts, and they are the reason this lands as
  +278 rather than +417.
- **Attribution was measured, not assumed.** The arbiter built a worktree at
  `86ce634` with the suite linked in and ran the lane there: PASS with **zero
  "improved, not yet banked" lines in any lane**, so the entire +278 belongs
  to this diff. This is the check #303's addendum made available to non-
  arbiters read-only, used here by the arbiter to close the attribution
  question outright rather than argue it.
- **The flip families look wrong until you remember the gate is per-DOCUMENT.**
  92 of the 278 are `MS-ComplexType2006-07-15`, and after that it is a long
  tail nobody would forecast: 16 `MS-IdentityConstraint`, 14 `MS-Particles`,
  14 `CType`, 12 `MS-ModelGroups`, 12 `MS-AttributeGroup`, 11 `assertion`, 10
  `suntest`, 10 `ElemDecl`, 9 `MS-Element`, 9 `All`, 8 `Wild`, 8 `Assert`, and
  singletons down to `Id` and `MS-DataTypes`. `schemaShapeDecidable` is
  all-or-nothing per schema document, so a document flips the moment *any*
  top-level complexType in it stops being declined — `msData/annotations/
  annotA009.xsd` carries one `<xsd:extension base="address">`, `saxonData/Id/
  id008.xsd` carries `<xs:extension base="xs:ID">`. The arbiter spot-checked
  the outlier categories directly rather than accepting the family histogram
  as self-explanatory.
- **Surprise — the diff's own prose about its own completeness is wrong, and
  the arbiter caught it in the count rather than the direction.** The new
  comment says "One clause stays fail-open inside the admitted shape" and
  "Case 2 (simple base, clauses 2.1-2.2) is complete". Both are false for one
  shared reason: **`{final}` is never mapped from source anywhere in the
  repo.** All three `newComplexType` call sites pass `final = nil`
  (`parser/produce_complex.go:286, 334, 430`), the single `xsd.NewSimpleType`
  call passes `nil` (`parser/produce.go:961`), and the builtins are seeded
  `nil` (`builtin/seed.go:150, 165`), so `finalContains` is unreachable-true
  at all six of its call sites — including `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.1
  (`xsd/complexextension.go:151`) and clause 2.2 (`:489`). **Three clauses
  stay fail-open in the admitted shape, not one, and Case 2 is not complete.**
  Non-blocking and correctly so: the unmentioned gaps are under-rejections in
  the *same* direction the prose claims, so STYLE P3a's actual prohibition
  (asserting a *wrong* direction) is not violated — what is wrong is the
  count; the identical dead-`{final}` gap already sits under the
  already-admitted `<restriction>` path via `derivation-ok-restriction` clause
  1 (`xsd/complexderivation.go:235`), so #336 neither introduces nor worsens
  it; and #290's `cebe9f2` is the repo's precedent for handling an
  over-promising doc claim as its own issue rather than as a rejection of the
  diff that wrote it.
- **Mason's out-of-scope note was re-diagnosed rather than forwarded, which is
  what kept it from becoming a wrong issue.** Mason flagged
  `MS-ComplexType2006-07-15/ctI007` — a `final="#all"` base observed "valid" —
  as a possible `#all`-spelling bug. It is not: `disallowedSubstitutions`
  (`parser/produce.go:1287`) handles `#all` correctly, but it maps `block=`,
  and only from `<element>`. `<complexType final=…>` is not read **for any
  spelling**. Same root cause as the finding above, so it folds into it
  instead of becoming a second issue chasing a token that is not the problem.
- **Friction — the arbiter recommended filing a follow-up issue that has been
  open and `ready` since 2026-08-02.** #436 is titled *"parser: `final=`/
  `finalDefault=` and `<complexType>`'s `block=` are never read, so `{final}`

## 2026-08-07 — #443 — conformance: `anonymousComplexTypeDecidable`'s two-line explicit-content narrowing is pinned, and the session's central finding is that the mutant it was filed over is **behaviourally EQUIVALENT** — `contentDecidable`'s own `default` arm declines `simpleContent`/`complexContent` independently, over the same children slice and the same (namespace, local-name) pairs, so NO input can make the guarded and unguarded functions disagree on a return value and no verdict-based assertion can ever catch the deletion; the pin therefore lands as TWO complementary tests (a verdict/separability pair plus a `go/ast` source scan), and the oracle's grounding turned up that the ISSUE BODY's own `Spec:` section was wrong twice about xs:anyType while the shipped doc comment it was quoting was already right; arbiter ACCEPT on round 1, zero production diff, ratchet unchanged and measured

- Shipped on `wip/issue-443` as one commit on top of `5cced88` (#291's
  landing) — **`b3ef049`** (`conformance: pin anonymousComplexTypeDecidable's
  explicit-content narrowing (#443)`), **1 file, +171/−0**, the whole change a
  new `conformance/schema_anonymous_test.go`. **Zero production-code
  changes**: `conformance/schema.go` is byte-identical to `main`.
  **Arbiter ACCEPT on the first round, no repair round consumed.**
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** Copied
  from the arbiter's verdict, not recomputed: gate green across the board —
  `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean, `golangci-lint run`
  0 issues, `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1 -v` PASS over
  **41,858 cases across 6 lanes, no lane movement**. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1`
  produced no write to `conformance/testdata/expectations/` — expected and
  structurally guaranteed here, since the diff adds only a test file and
  touches no engine, harness-gate, or decidability logic.
- **The finding that reframed the issue (mason, verified empirically): the
  deletion mutant is EQUIVALENT, not merely unpinned.** #443 was filed off an
  earlier arbiter mutation-test observing that deleting the narrowing left the
  whole suite green, and the issue read that as a coverage hole. It is not:
  the narrowing's `childXSD(el, "simpleContent") != nil ||
  childXSD(el, "complexContent") != nil` and `contentDecidable`'s `default`
  arm match the *same* (namespace, local-name) pairs over the *same* children
  slice, so the guard can only ever return `false` on inputs where delegation
  would also return `false`. No `*parser.Element` separates them. A pure
  verdict-based test **structurally cannot** pin this site without a
  production-code seam, and #443's own acceptance criteria explicitly forbade
  adding one — so "write a test that fails when the two lines are deleted" was
  not satisfiable in the form the issue imagined it.
- **Decision: split the pin into two tests with different instruments rather
  than argue the site untestable.** Neither half alone is sufficient and the
  arbiter confirmed the complementarity by mutation rather than by reading:
  1. `TestAnonymousComplexTypeDecidableNarrowsExplicitContent` — the
     **verdict/separability** half. Drives
     `anonymousComplexTypeDecidable` directly on inline `<complexType>`
     elements reached by navigation, pairing each explicit-content form with
     an implicit-content sibling of *identical inner content*, and
     cross-checking that `complexTypeDecidable` ADMITS the same element. That
     cross-check is what makes the decline attributable to the anonymity
     narrowing specifically, rather than to the content being undecidable on
     its own merits.
  2. `TestAnonymousComplexTypeNarrowingPrecedesDelegation` — the **structural**
     half, and the one that actually kills the deletion mutant. A `go/ast`
     source scan (precedent: `xsderr/rulecatalog_enforcement_test.go`)
     asserting the early `return false` guard and both string literals are
     present *ahead of* the `contentDecidable` delegation.
  - **Mutation evidence, run twice by mason and re-verified independently by
    the arbiter in a detached worktree:** deletion mutant → verdict test still
    PASSES (which is the equivalence claim, confirmed rather than asserted),
    AST scan FAILS with 3 errors. Always-false mutant → verdict test FAILS on
    both polarities, AST scan PASSES. Each half catches exactly what the other
    cannot.
- **Surprise — the oracle corrected the ISSUE BODY, not the code.** #443's own
  `Spec:` section justified the narrowing with two claims that are wrong:
  (a) it said xs:anyType "has no attribute wildcard to union" per §3.4.7 —
  false, xs:anyType carries a `##any`/`lax` wildcard; what is empty is only
  its `{attribute uses}`; and (b) it characterised §3.4.2.5 clause 2 as "a
  union that reduces to identity" — also false, since clause **2.1**
  (restriction) never unions with the base wildcard at all, it takes "the
  complete wildcard" unconditionally. The shipped doc comment at
  `conformance/schema.go:793-819` was then checked line-by-line against the
  spec and found **already accurate** — it says "§3.4.7 gives xs:anyType an
  empty `{attribute uses}`" and "§3.4.2.5 clause 2 unions the base's wildcard
  only for an EXTENSION, which this form is not", both correct. So the defect
  was confined to the issue's restatement of the comment, the comment needed
  no fix, and the session correctly shipped no doc change. Recorded here
  because the tempting move — "the issue says the comment is wrong, so edit
  the comment" — would have made a correct comment wrong.
- Friction — low, and concentrated in one place: the issue was filed on a
  premise ("this line is unpinned") that had to be *disproved* before the work
  could be scoped, which cost the grounding-and-design phase a full extra
  round-trip that a correctly framed issue would not have needed. The
  originating mutation-test observation (deletion → suite still green) is
  equally consistent with "unpinned" and with "equivalent", and the filing
  took the first reading without testing the second. Cheap to avoid next time;
  see Next item 3.
- Next:
  1. **[non-gating advisory, arbiter]** The `go/ast` scan asserts ordering by
     walking the function body generically; a tighter assertion scoped to the
     specific `*ast.IfStmt` is possible and would narrow what a future
     refactor can silently satisfy. Explicitly **not required** for this
     accept — recorded as an available tightening, not a debt.
  2. **[non-gating advisory, arbiter]** The scan reads `schema.go` by relative
     path, where its precedent `xsderr/rulecatalog_enforcement_test.go`
     resolves through `moduleRoot()`. A stylistic divergence, **not a defect**
     (the test's package dir is the file's dir), but worth folding if the
     enforcement-scan pattern is ever generalised into a shared helper.
  3. **[non-gating advisory, arbiter — explicitly NOT a hole]** The
     `||`→`&&` mutant survives both tests. It is in the **same equivalence
     class** as the pinned deletion mutant: with `&&`, either child alone
     still falls through to `contentDecidable`'s `default` arm and is declined
     there. This is a property of the SITE — the guard is a pure early-exit
     shadowing a total downstream arm — not a gap in the pin, and filing it as
     a coverage issue would re-file #443 on the same misreading. **Dismissed
     on the record here rather than tracked**; no follow-up issue owed.
- Thread record (do not duplicate) — all on
  <https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/443>. **[ORACLE GROUNDING]**
  <https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/443#issuecomment-5221625002> — the
  two corrections to the issue body's `Spec:` section (xs:anyType's wildcard
  exists and only `{attribute uses}` is empty; §3.4.2.5 cl.2.1 restriction
  takes the complete wildcard unconditionally, no union), plus the finding
  that the production comment at `schema.go:793-819` needed no change.
  **[ARBITER VERDICT — `accept` @ `b3ef049`]**
  <https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/443#issuecomment-5221779006> — the
  green gate table, `RATCHET: unchanged` in #303's required phrasing over a
  clean expectations tree, the two mutants re-applied and their pass/fail
  polarities independently reproduced in a detached worktree, and the three
  non-gating advisories above. Spec rule IDs relied on across the session:
  **§3.4.2.3.2** (implicit content ⇒ base = xs:anyType, derivation
  restriction), **§3.4.7** (xs:anyType's `{attribute uses}` vs. its wildcard —
  the corrected reading), **§3.4.2.4 cl.3** (attribute-uses fold),
  **§3.4.2.5 cl.2.1** (attribute-wildcard, corrected), **§3.17.2**
  (`{type definitions}` scoped to `<schema>` children only). This entry is

- **Decision: the four Phase A helpers take an `xsderr.Loc` parameter and the
  walk RE-ROOTS it, rather than each site inventing a position.**
  `resolveTypeName`/`resolveElementName`/`resolveAttributeName`/
  `resolveModelGroupName` grow a `loc` argument (all unexported — no exported
  surface movement), threaded by a referrer-Loc convention now documented on
  `resolveReferences`: `ComplexType`, `ElementDeclaration`,
  `AttributeDeclaration` and `ModelGroupDefinition` re-root at their own
  `Loc()` as the walk enters them, while `Particle`, `AttributeUse`,
  `ModelGroup`, `TypeTable` and `TypeAlternative` inherit the enclosing
  component's because none of the five retains a position.
- **Decision: the `Particle.Loc()`/`AttributeUse.Loc()` decision point the
  issue flagged is resolved with NO new exported surface.** The two sites
  reached from a `Particle` (`<element ref>`) and an `AttributeUse`
  (`<attribute ref>`) take the enclosing `ComplexType`'s `Loc()`, so
  `xsd/doc.go`'s T5 note — "nothing consumes those positions yet, so no
  accessor is exported for them" — stays TRUE and unedited rather than being
  falsified and then patched. Arbiter confirmed by `go doc -all ./xsd` diffed
  against `origin/main` in a worktree: **the only change is doc prose in
  `doc.go`**, exported surface diff empty. `resolve_test.go` is
  `package xsd_test`, so the repair round cannot touch the surface at all.
- **The #208 T5 exported-surface watch-item is DISCHARGED**, stated in one
  line of the landing commit body rather than left implicit: these ten sites
  are the **second** real consumer of #208's `.Loc()` accessors
  (sch-props-correct clause 2 in `schema.go` was the first), which is the
  condition #208's own verdict set for the accessors to have earned their
  export. `xsd/doc.go` now records both consumers by name.
- **Determinism (STYLE D2): documented in place, no fix needed.** The three
  cycle sites were already order-independent before this change and remain so
  — entry points are the document-order `s.types`/`s.modelGroups`/`s.elements`
  slices, out-edges are collected in document order (`groupRefsIn`,
  `SubstitutionGroupAffiliationNames`), and `path`/`color` are read only BY
  KEY, never ranged. So the newly reported POSITION is map-order independent
  for the same reason the already-reported name was. Two supporting arguments
  the arbiter re-derived rather than accepted: the bare index reads at sites
  668/759 always hit (a name absent from the index contributes no out-edges,
  so it reaches `done` before any recursion can return to it and can never be
  re-encountered `onStack` — and both types are value structs with
  value-receiver `Loc()`, so even a miss would yield the zero Loc, not a
  panic); and `path[anyTypeName]` is never set (the §3.4.7 break precedes the
  record), so `nextCT` at 624 can never be the zero-Loc synthesized
  `xs:anyType`.
- **The round-1 REJECT, and why it was blocking rather than a coverage note —
  the entry worth mining.** `50861b7`'s implementation was correct at all ten
  sites; the arbiter said so explicitly and re-verified it end to end through
  `parser.Parse` on hand-written schemas, not just through the builder. The
  defect was in the test: `TestResolveRejectionsCiteTheOffendingComponent` was
  organised **by rule family — "one case per rule" — for rules that have
  multiple call sites**, so it guarded 7 of 10 sites while reading as though
  it guarded all ten. Independent mutation matrix (isolated worktree, green
  baseline, caught control) found sites **329** (src-resolve 1.5 — the clause
  rides a *different helper* than its src-resolve siblings), **367** and
  **371** (two of the three `ic.Loc()` keyref sites, covered only by the
  third, because the category check returns before the cardinality check is
  reached) all revertible to `xsderr.Loc{}` **with the entire suite green**.
  Mason's own report was true *as worded* ("each of the seven **asserted**
  sites"); the gap was between that and what the docstring claimed. What made
  it blocking: `resolve_test.go:522` asserted the opposite in prose the next
  agent will trust — *"no site can drift back to the zero 'position unknown'
  Loc unnoticed"* — **STYLE T6, a false guarantee banked into a test file**.
  Nothing else in the repo can cover those sites: conformance is verdict-only
  by file format, so it can never guard a position.
- **Repair round `8839399` — test-only, `resolve.go` byte-identical.** Three
  site-specific cases added (`<group ref>` → enclosing CT; dangling keyref →
  the keyref; wrong-category keyref → the *referring* keyref, via a mutually
  referring kr1/kr2 pair), and the docstring re-scoped to say the table is
  **per-SITE**, with the generalisation that is the actual anti-recurrence
  sentence: *a shared rule ID is no evidence that a sibling site is guarded*.
  Also folded `TestResolveCircularSubstitutionGroups` onto the existing
  `elementAffiliatedAt` helper (STYLE T4) and dropped its `else` (STYLE S2),
  net −26 lines; the same `else` shape was deliberately LEFT in three
  neighbouring pre-existing tests rather than widening the diff past the
  one-focused-change boundary, and the arbiter called that the correct call.
  Scope confirmed by **blob hash, not diff output**: `xsd/resolve.go`
  `68c720ae` and `xsd/doc.go` `c4a8e83a` identical across both commits, so
  round 1's implementation verification was not re-litigated.
- **Surprise — the arbiter's re-verification went STRICTLY beyond the repair
  it asked for, and the extra probe is the one that mattered.** Zeroing a Loc
  only proves an assertion rejects non-positions; it does not prove the case
  pins the RIGHT component when two of the same kind are in play. So site 371
  was also mutated to `target.Loc()` — a real, non-zero position, the *other*
  keyref — and **caught**. It further checked the kr1→kr2→kr1 construction is
  sound rather than incidentally lucky on two counts: iteration is
  `for _, ic := range s.identityConstraints` (`resolve.go:231`), a
  `cloneSlice` of builder append order, so "kr1 first" is deterministic (D2,
  no map range); and equal `{fields}` counts keep clause 2 at `:375` from
  firing, so `:371` is reached on the merits. Every mutation in both rounds
  failed **exactly one** subtest with every other package still `ok` — no
  over-broad assertion soaking up unrelated mutations.
- **Surprise — the docstring's "every" claim was verified EXHAUSTIVELY, not
  charitably.** The arbiter grepped `resolve.go` for `fmt.Errorf`,
  `errors.New` and `xsderr.Wrap` (none) and for `New[A-Z]…` constructor calls
  (none), establishing that every other error path in the file is a bare
  `return err` propagating one of the ten. There is no eleventh origin the
  pass can raise, so the repaired claim is exhaustive rather than merely
  un-falsified. It also confirmed the three CT-charged cases build their
  `Particle`/`AttributeUse` at the ZERO Loc **on purpose** (`termParticle` at
  `:27`, `NewAttributeUse(xsderr.Loc{}, …)` at `:562`), so abandoning the
  enclosing-CT substitution really would fail them.
- **Oracle grounding settled one thing the issue had wrong-shaped and one
  STYLE-vs-spec boundary.** src-resolve is **one** kind-dispatched clause
  governing BOTH failure shapes — a name present only in a *different* kind's
  table still fails clause 1 for the requested kind — so the existing
  "dangling and wrong-kind are the SAME failure" framing is spec-accurate and
  must not be split into two clauses. And the keyref rule ID is
  **`c-props-correct`, not `ic-props-correct`** (§3.11.6.1), with the category
  check folding into clause 1 via the {referenced key} tableau entry in
  §3.11.1. For mg-props-correct 2 and e-props-correct 5 the spec charges the
  constraint to the definition/element *you return to*, not to the referring
  use — which is what the two index reads implement. For ct-props-correct 3
  BOTH `cur` and `next` are spec-defensible (the constraint is symmetric over
  the cycle), so the choice is a STYLE call, not a spec one: take whichever
  the loop already has in hand — `next`. The arbiter separately pinned that
  choice as *consistent rather than arbitrary*: the message prints `base` and
  `nextCT` is exactly `s.Type(base)`, so the component named and the
  component charged are always the same one; mutating to `cur.Loc()` fails
  with `Loc = resolve.xsd:52:3, want resolve.xsd:51:3`.
- Friction — one repair round, entirely avoidable, and its cause is a
  **test-organisation habit rather than a mistake about this code**: a table
  built "one case per rule" is only equivalent to "one case per site" when
  every rule has exactly one call site, and in `resolve.go` three rules do
  not. The rule-family framing is the natural way to *write* such a table
  (rule IDs are what the messages cite) and it silently under-covers the
  moment a clause moves to a sibling helper or a second check shares a rule
  ID. See Next item 1 — flagged for /retro rather than fixed here, because
  the fix belongs in test-writing guidance, not in this diff.
- Next:
  1. **[for the weekly /retro — candidate STYLE/guidance edit, NOT a code
     follow-up]** Name the failure mode: *coverage tables organised per RULE
     when a rule has multiple call sites*, plus the T6 half — a docstring

  2. **[non-gating, dismissed on the record — no follow-up owed]** The `else`

- **Decision: two locations, one fact, one pointer — and the pointer stays.**
  `Facet.Values()` is the canonical location and carries the whole paragraph;
  `FacetPattern`'s own `FacetKind` doc gains a single clause — "for how its
  multiple `{value}` members combine, see `Facet.Values`" — that restates *no*
  fact (it names no OR, no AND, no derivation step) and is therefore a pure
  cross-reference, which is what the issue's "cross-reference rather than
  duplicating" criterion asks for, not an exception it tolerates (STYLE D3
  applied to prose). `NewFacet`'s doc correctly did **not** get a third
  pointer — it mentions `FacetPattern` only for the `{fixed}` normalization.
  The "not in three places" criterion is satisfied at two.
- **Decision: cite `#214` by issue number inside exported godoc.** Precedent
  verified by the arbiter rather than assumed, and it covers the exported
  surface, not just internal comments: `parser/tree.go:56` ("issue #272") sits
  on the exported `Element.Attr`, `value/list.go:60` ("issue #224"); the bare
  `(#N)` form mason actually used appears in exported *package* godoc at
  `builtin/doc.go:87`, `value/backendtest/doc.go:30`, `parser/doc.go:169` and
  `parser/produce_complex.go:236`. Beyond precedent it is the issue's own
  instruction — #313's body says "see the arbiter's spec-fidelity note on
  #214" and "the grounding already exists … Read it rather than re-deriving".
- **Decision: no oracle round, on the issue's explicit say-so.** #313's Notes
  section says the grounding already exists as the GROUNDING comment on #214
  and to read it rather than re-derive. The session honoured that and posted a
  GROUNDING comment recording the *reuse* plus the facts carried over, so the
  #313 thread is self-sufficient for a later reader without duplicating #214's
  derivation. Scratch copy at `.agent/grounding-issue-313.md` (gitignored).
- **Spec fidelity — the arbiter re-checked every claim against
  `docs/specs/md/xmlschema11-2.md` rather than taking the reuse on report.**
  **§4.3.4.2 `xr-pattern`** (line 3208): `R` is the single `<pattern>`'s value
  *or* "the concatenation of the actual values of all the `<pattern>`
  children's `value` attributes, in order, separated by `|`, so forming a
  single regular expression with multiple branches", and `{value}` is then the
  union with the base's pattern facet — so the comment's "first joins
  same-step siblings into ONE regex with `|`" is verbatim right, and the
  clause's own Note ("pattern facets specified on the *same* step are ORed
  together, while pattern facets specified on *different* steps are ANDed
  together") is exactly the comment's "a multi-member `{value}` can only have
  come from union ACROSS steps". **§4.3.4.4 `cvc-pattern-valid`** (line 3224)
  supplies the per-member AND. The equivalence argument rests on **Appendix G**
  (line 6464) — "the regular expression language defined here implicitly
  anchors all regular expressions at the head and tail" — plus the fact that
  `|` is the lowest-precedence operator in the XSD regex grammar, so the
  alternation is top-level and anchored `a|b` ≡ anchored `a` OR anchored `b`.
- **Surprise — the arbiter checked the prose against the CODE THAT PRODUCES
  the values, not only against the spec, and that is what makes the godoc a
  guarantee rather than an aspiration.** It enumerated every `NewFacet` call
  site capable of yielding a multi-value `FacetPattern`: `parser/produce.go:1097`
  (accumulates the siblings of one `<restriction>`) and
  `conformance/datatypes.go:2412` (accumulates over one restriction's
  `children`) — both same-step **by construction** — with
  `builtin/seed.go:248` always single-value. **Nothing anywhere builds a
  cross-step multi-value `FacetPattern`**, so no existing producer can falsify
  the new paragraph. It also confirmed the paragraph contradicts none of the
  three sites that already carry the convention (`xsd.overlayFacet` at
  `xsd/simpletype.go:846-870`, `value.patternFacet` at `value/facets.go:436-450`,
  `parser.restrictionFacets` via `produce.go:1086-1103`) and adds no fourth
  restatement of it.

- **The five classes as landed, each traceable to the landings that paid for
  it.** The bullet opens with the reason it exists — *a defective issue BODY
  outlives the session that filed it* — and covers:
  1. **A stale or wrong premise is corrected IN THE BODY**, not only in a

     angle-bracket tags and bare-URL autolinks out of replacement text, since
     GitHub entity-escapes both on store and an edit round-trips unchanged only
     if the new text introduces neither. Evidence: #189, #190, #238, #272.
  2. **A runtime-mechanism claim states whether it was reproduced** against the
     tree, or is written as a hypothesis pending verification; a memory of
     prior discussion is not reproduction. Evidence: #214.
  3. **Every static citation is checked against the tree before filing**, with
     three sharpenings each of which caught a real defect a generic "check your
     citations" habit missed — (a) **kind-match**: a `cvc-*` Validation Rule ID
     belongs under a "… Validation Rules" subsection and a Schema Component
     Constraint under the sibling "Constraints on … Schema Components", so the
     right number under the wrong-kind subsection is still a wrong citation
     (#449's `cvc-fractionDigits-valid` cited as §4.3.12.4 when it is
     §4.3.12.3); (b) **two numbering spaces**: CLAUDE.md's headline bullets and

     ID (`STYLE T1`), never the headline bullet number (#215's phantom `T7`);

     unrelated edits move (#279, whose line numbers were corrected twice and
     were wrong again by the time work started).
  4. **Search the open queue for the primary file path and identifier, and
     record what the hit was** — same change → close one as duplicate *and say
     which*; adjacent change → one-line cross-reference on both; never proceed
     past a hit without recording which of the two it was. Applies before
     filing **and** before grounding. Evidence: the #326/#224 overlap miss.
  5. **An `## Acceptance` ratchet-movement clause names its condition**
     ("moves the `schema` lane **provided** #N has landed"), so a later
     planning pass chartering #N differently leaves the staleness one grep
     away. Evidence: the #228/#264 decay.
