## 2026-08-08 — #319 — builtin/xsd: the anonymous intermediate list is INTERPOSED, so `xs:NMTOKENS`/`xs:IDREFS`/`xs:ENTITIES` seed as restrictions of a real list instead of flattening onto `xs:anySimpleType` — and `cos-st-restricts` clause **2.2.1.2**, the one facet-value clause #217 explicitly could not charge, becomes chargeable at last; the shape is SYNTHESIZED from the row's `{variety}` rather than added to the generated table (STYLE D3 — a new `TypeSpec` field could only ever be filled one way), and the warden's pre-flight is what earned the session, catching a **confirmed ratchet regression before a line was written** — `conformance/datatypes.go`'s own list harness built the same flattened shape `builtin.Seed` did, so charging the clause would have flipped banked `msData boolean018` pass→fail; arbiter REJECT on round 1 for two stale-prose survivors (a FOURTH deferral site the sweep's own report claimed was complete at three, plus a test whose name outlived its premise), ACCEPT on round 2, ratchet unchanged and measured on both

- Shipped on `wip/issue-319` off `origin/main` @ **`c048780`** (#315's landing)
  as two commits, **15 files, +524/−101**:
  **`5b870b4`** (`builtin/xsd: interpose the anonymous intermediate list so
  cos-st-restricts 2.2.1.2 is chargeable (#319)`) and the repair
  **`e62886c`** (`xsd/value: fix stale 2.2.1.2 deferral comment and misnamed
  panic test (#319)`, 2 files, +16/−12). The load-bearing pieces:
  `builtin/seed.go`'s new `interposeListBase`, `xsd/derivation.go`'s new
  `checkConstructedListFacets`, `tools/hfnextract/builtins/builtins.go`'s new
  `resolveOwnListFacets`, and the `conformance/datatypes.go` split into
  `constructedListFacets()` + `buildListRestrictionFacets()`. Five new tests
  (`TestInterposeListBase`, `TestSeedListTwoStepDerivation`,
  `TestSeedExcludesAnonymousIntermediates`,
  `TestListEnumerationResolvesThroughAnonymousBase`,
  `TestEffectiveWhiteSpaceListNoUsableModePanics`). **Zero new exported
  identifiers** — the arbiter diffed `go doc -all -short` over every package
  on round 1 and got **479 identifiers, byte-identical**.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** Copied
  from the arbiter's final verdict, not recomputed: **datatypes 1151/1173,
  schema 9529/15432, instance 0/26426**. Gate green on `e62886c` —
  `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean, `golangci-lint run`
  **0 issues**, `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1 -v`
  **PASS** (24.8s) over **41,858 cases / 6 lanes**, **zero
  improved-but-unbanked logged**. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` produced no write to
  `conformance/testdata/expectations/`, checked immediately after the run and
  before any branch switch (#303); `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD --
  conformance/testdata/expectations/` is **empty** — no expectation file was
  touched in either direction.
- **The issue's own Acceptance predicted upward `schema` movement and got
  none — recorded as a FACT, not a defect.** The body says "expect `schema`
  movement on any W3C case that constructs a list with stray facets"; the
  banked corpus contains no such case, so a change that genuinely widens
  `cos-st-restricts` enforcement moved zero lanes. The prediction was a
  reasonable hedge, not a wrong premise (contrast #295, where `unchanged` was
  wrong in the good direction by +10) — and it is a reminder that the
  conformance corpus is silent about clauses that only bite on
  PROGRAMMATICALLY built components. `checkConstructedListFacets`' own doc
  says so in as many words: a conforming §3.16.2.1 mapping always satisfies
  2.2.1.2, so the clause "bites only on a programmatically built component,
  never on one parsed from a schema document". The value banked here is the
  deferral removal and the unit tests, not a lane number.
- **Decision: SYNTHESIZE the intermediate node, do not widen the table
  (STYLE D3) — the issue offered both and (b) won on unfalsifiability.**
  `builtin.TypeSpec` carries `Base string` + `Variety` and cannot express "base
  is an anonymous list of item X", so #319's Surface section weighed (a) a new
  sealed row field naming the interposed list against (b) synthesizing it in
  `Seed`. Mason's decisive argument: grounding §5 shows §3.16.2.1
  `map.std.common` case 2 (`<list>` ⇒ base `xs:anySimpleType`) and case 3
  (`<list>` ⇒ `{facets}` = exactly one fixed collapse whiteSpace) fix **both
  halves of the first step with no per-type variation**, so the row's
  `{variety}` alone already determines the whole component — a new field would
  be a second encoding of a derivable fact, and *unfalsifiable data*, since the
  generator could only ever fill it one way. (a) also adds generated exported
  surface for zero information (STYLE T5). `Base` therefore stays
  `"anySimpleType"` on the plural rows and its godoc was corrected instead
  (warden C3): on a LIST row `Base` is **not** the named type's
  `{base type definition}` — it names the ANONYMOUS list's base.
- **Warden C1 was the session's highest-value single finding: a confirmed
  pass→fail ratchet regression, identified before implementation started.**
  `conformance/datatypes.go:1111-1113`'s `execListCase` built the flattened
  one-step shape exactly as `builtin.Seed` did, and `buildListOwnFacets`
  returned `{whiteSpace collapse fixed}` **plus an enumeration facet** whenever
  the fixture had `<enumeration>` children. `msData/datatypes/boolean018.xsd`
  is precisely that shape and
  `conformance/testdata/expectations/datatypes.txt:181` banks it **pass** — so
  the new closed-set check would have made `NewSimpleType` error, `execListCase`
  return `Fail()`, and a banked lane regress. The prescribed fix is also the
  spec-correct one: the fixture LITERALLY writes two steps
  (`<simpleType name="myList"><list itemType="xsd:boolean"/>` then
  `<restriction base="myList"><enumeration …>`), so splitting into
  `constructedListFacets()` (always exactly the one fixed collapse whiteSpace)
  and `buildListRestrictionFacets()` (the enumerations, on the restricting hop)
  puts each facet where the fixture puts it. The harness had been carrying the
  same modelling error as `Seed`, which is why one change broke both.
  `buildD34Type`'s `buildListOwnFacets(nil)` path is behaviour-preserving under
  the split — it returned the identical single facet before.
- **Warden C2: the discriminant is `Variety == List` ALONE, and a mismatched
  row is a LOUD REFUSAL rather than a silent fallback (STYLE D3/T1).** Mason's
  design tested `(Variety == List && Base == "anySimpleType")`; the warden
  showed the second conjunct carries zero information — `builtins.go:56,259-260`
  sets `Base = listBase` *because* `Variety == "list"` — so testing the
  conjunction would let a future disagreement between the two fields fall
  silently back to today's flattened shape. That is a **false-accept**, and
  specifically a false-accept of the exact shape 2.2.1.2 exists to reject: the
  worst available failure mode. As landed, `interposeListBase` branches on
  `spec.Variety.(List)` and returns a construction error naming both the row
  and its base when `spec.Base != "anySimpleType"`, converting a smuggled
  invariant into a tested failure. `TestInterposeListBase`'s third subtest pins
  the refusal AND that the message names both.
- **Warden C4 / STYLE L1: the facet-strip landed as a general extractor RULE,
  never a per-type hardcode.** `resolveOwnListFacets` keys on
  `Variety == "list"`; the three builtin names appear nowhere in code. It
  follows `resolveOwnPatterns`/`subtractOperands`' existing precedent of
  converting a spec-rendered EFFECTIVE value into an OWN value by a general
  rule — the §3.4.5.1/.10.1/.12.1 "Facets" subsections render the effective
  cross-step set, which grounding §2 warned not to misread as two facets on one
  component. It also clears `Fixed`, which the arbiter flagged as mattering in
  its own right: `typespecgen` emits `Fixed: true` independently of `Default`,
  so leaving it would have written a row encoding fixedness with no value
  (STYLE D3). Leaving the VALUE would have been actively wrong in a *silent*
  way — `overlayFacet` puts `FacetWhiteSpace` in the `default:` replace branch
  with no fixed-override check anywhere, so the plural row's unfixed whiteSpace
  would have quietly cleared the intermediate list's `{fixed} = true` with no
  diagnostic. The arbiter verified generation end-to-end by re-running
  `go tool typespecgen` into a scratch path: **byte-identical** to the
  committed `builtin/gen_typespec.go`.
- **One repair round, both items stale PROSE, zero logic.** The round-1 reject
  found (R1) `xsd/derivation.go:923-928` — `checkVarietyApplicableFacets`' LIST
  bullet still saying 2.2.1.2 "is still otherwise deferred (see checkSTGraph)",
  a cross-reference now pointing at prose the same diff had rewritten to say
  the opposite — and (R2) `value/whitespace_test.go:140,156`, where
  `TestEffectiveWhiteSpaceListNoFacetPanics` and its failure message described
  a setup the test no longer built. The arm at R1 is **still live and was
  correctly NOT deleted**: `checkSTGraph` calls `checkVarietyApplicableFacets`
  (line 193) *before* the switch that dispatches `checkListGraph` (line 199),
  so a facet inapplicable to a list at all is still rejected there and reported
  as an applicability violation rather than a closed-set one — only the
  justification changed. The arbiter confirmed the repair comment-only by
  filtering `git diff 5b870b4 e62886c` to non-`//` lines and getting the empty
  set.
- **Surprise — the sweep's own completeness claim was off by one, and the
  missed site is the fourth.** The implementation report enumerated three
  deferral-prose sites (`checkSTGraph`, `checkListGraph`, `checkUnionGraph`)
  and called the sweep complete; `checkVarietyApplicableFacets` was a fourth.
  The arbiter's note is the sharp part: **STYLE T6's own rationale records this
  exact failure mode — a stale rationale a commit message claimed to have
  updated — already costing one repair round.** So the rule that catches it
  was written from a previous instance of itself, and the instance recurred
  anyway. A `/retro` datapoint: "I swept all N sites" is a claim the author is
  structurally worst placed to verify, and neither the gate nor the linter can
  check it.
- **Surprise — the renamed test's premise change was ADJUDICATED, not merely
  accepted, and the adjudication is what kept the test alive.** Mason flagged
  that the old `...NoFacetPanics` setup had become unconstructible (a
  no-whiteSpace list is now refused at construction). The arbiter ruled the
  test must STAY: `effectiveWhiteSpace` has a single no-usable-mode branch
  (`whitespace.go:144`) onto which absent-facet, wrong-arity and out-of-domain
  `{value}` all collapse, so the mutation it guards — a blanket "non-atomic ⇒
  `(0, false)`" — is still caught; only the *route* to the branch became
  unconstructible, and deleting it would have removed a live mutation guard on
  a reachable branch. The round-2 re-judge then proved that by mutating
  `value/whitespace.go`'s union guard to exactly that blanket and watching the
  renamed test fail. **A test whose name was wrong turned out to be a test that
  earned its name once renamed** — the opposite of the usual finding.
- **Verification the arbiter refused to take on report.** `whiteSpaceOf(prim)`
  now returns `""` for the three list rows (C4's consequence), and the warden
  demanded proof that `normalizeWhiteSpace` can never silently fall through to
  `preserve`. The arbiter re-derived it rather than trusting the grep: all
  three `parseOK` call sites gate on `backend.Mapping`
  (`datatypes.go:895`/`:857`/`:1029`), `builtin/strict/strict.go:126` is a
  23-case switch over atomic types only with no plural among them, and
  `builtin/native/` contains `doc.go` alone with no `Mapping` at all. Genuinely
  unreachable ⇒ defensive code there would be dead code ⇒ **a comment is the
  correct treatment**, which is the ruling that let the fix stay comment-only.
- **`declaringFacetSpace`'s "safety by coincidence" is now stated and tested
  rather than left implicit.** The warden's sharpest secondary finding: the
  sentence at `value/facets.go:395-396` claiming "anonymous declaring types
  (the zero QName) are outside this runner's manually-built scope" became FALSE
  the moment every builtin list chain acquired an anonymous node. It is still
  *safe* — only enumeration and the four bound facets route there, bounds are
  inapplicable to lists, and an enum's declaring type is always the nearest
  node matched first from `leaf` — but that is a coincidence, not a guarantee.
  The comment was corrected and `TestListEnumerationResolvesThroughAnonymousBase`
  now drives the full anon → plural → user-restriction chain, which would
  false-accept `"aa ccc"` if either resolution missed the extra hop.
- **Two observable, correct changes worth recording for whoever hits them
  next.** (1) `xs:NMTOKENS`' `EffectiveFacets()` whiteSpace entry flips to
  `fixed = true` with a **zero `declaring` QName**. (2) The EffectiveFacets
  ORDER flips for all three plural types, from row order `[minLength,
  whiteSpace]` to base-to-derived `[whiteSpace, minLength]`; since
  `checkApplicableFacetSet` rejects the FIRST failing facet and `compile`
  builds checkers in that order, **first-error messages can move**. STYLE D2 is
  satisfied throughout — the order is still deterministic — but a golden-text
  consumer could see different text for the same input.
- Friction — **none in execution beyond the one repair round, and that round
  cost only prose.** The design pre-flight, warden pre-flight and grounding all
  landed before any code, and every one of the warden's four conditions was
  satisfied first-try. The single avoidable cost is R1's missed fourth site,
  logged as a Surprise above rather than here because it is a pattern, not a
  one-off delay.

## 2026-08-08 — #320 — xsd: `length-minLength-maxLength` clauses **1.2/2.2** land, so `length` beside a `minLength`/`maxLength` SPECIFIED AT THE SAME derivation step is finally rejected — and the session's whole weight is on a **collision between the two most absolute rules in the repo**: a second oracle round ruled the LITERAL reading textually correct against the local (pre-errata) spec text, that reading regresses the banked `MS-Errata102006-07-15/errF001`, and CLAUDE.md's one rule forbids regression categorically with an exception mechanism (a human-filed issue) that **no agent in the loop can reach**; the arbiter ACCEPTED mason's two accepting-direction deviations not as a fixture carve-out but as **erratum E2-35's own rule implemented whole**, after reproducing the tension in an isolated worktree (exactly one case costs, nothing else) and proving the under-rejection claim *mathematically* rather than by enumeration — schema lane **+20**, arbiter ACCEPT on round 1

- **THE ENTRY'S POINT — the spec-vs-ratchet collision, and why the resolution
  is not a route around the constitutional rule.** The sequence: (1) the first
  GROUNDING answered the issue's four questions and said candidates are the
  base-chain walk including all hop kinds, tested against effective `{facets}`;
  (2) mason implemented that literal/strict reading, found it flips banked
  `MS-Errata102006-07-15/errF001` `pass`→`fail`, and narrowed the reading in two
  places rather than regress; (3) the orchestrator, given mason's flagged
  ambiguity, requested a **second oracle opinion**, which ruled **against mason**
  — the strict reading is textually correct, because `dt-derived` (§2.4.3) says
  in as many words *"A datatype must not be derived from itself"*, so `t` cannot
  be its own witness, and `{facets}` means the overlay everywhere else in §4.3
  including two sentences earlier in this same clause; (4) that adjudication
  recommended PRINCIPLES 25 (treat `errF001` as a known-disputed suite case) —
  which would have meant a banked `pass`→`fail`, i.e. exactly the thing
  CLAUDE.md's one rule forbids; (5) the tension was handed to the arbiter as the
  explicit judgment call, since the ratchet verdict is its role and no one else's.
  **Four things carried the accept**, and they are worth reading in the verdict
  itself rather than paraphrase:
  1. **The arbiter reproduced the tension instead of taking it on report.** In a
     detached worktree it applied the strict reading (`for s := t.base` plus
     `findEffectiveFacet(stepEff, FacetLength)` in place of
     `findFacet(s.ownFacets, ...)`) and ran the suite: same 20 improvements,
     **exactly one regression, `errF001`, nothing else**. So the two deviations
     are **jointly necessary** (neither is an independent hedge), minimally
     scoped, and cost precisely one banked case. Mason's account checked out.
  2. **The under-rejection claim is PROVEN, not enumerated.** `ownFacets ⊆` the
     effective facet kinds (the overlay's clause 1 puts every member of `S` into
     `R`), and `{t} ∪ ancestors ⊇ ancestors`, while both walks break on identical
     conditions off the same `EffectiveFacets` — therefore the implemented
     reject-set is a **strict subset** of the strict reading's reject-set.
     **Whichever reading is right, no rejection this code makes is a false
     reject.** That is a much stronger guarantee than a consumer walk can give,
     and it is the shape to reuse the next time a GAP has to argue its direction.
  3. **The decisive point: this is not a fixture-specific carve-out, it is
     E2-35's own rule implemented whole.** A GAP that special-cased one fixture
     would have been a dodge. What `checkLengthFreeStep` encodes is the erratum
     sentence the suite's own testGroup annotation quotes — *"length facet is now
     allowed with either minLength or maxLength if they are specified in
     different derivation steps"* — and the arbiter traced it against **seven
     chain shapes** (same-step introduction; inherited-then-length-below;
     length-then-facet-below; restated-length-plus-facet;
     raised-value-at-the-length-step; restated-facet-at-same-value; multi-hop)
     and found agreement in every one. The local spec snapshot carries
     **pre-errata** text (`docs/specs/md/xmlschema11-2.md:3093`; no "E2-35" hit
     anywhere near §4.3.1.4 in either spec file), so what mason declines is the
     pre-errata literalism, not the rule.
  4. **The direction is the safe one and the rule leaves no other route.** The
     alternatives were regress `errF001` (forbidden) or revert and forfeit 20
     undisputed wins. `errF001`'s suite expectation is `status="queried"` against
     bugzilla 4681, **re-opened from a prior `accepted`** — a *disputed* case, not
     an established broken one, so PRINCIPLES 25 does not cleanly apply to it.
     And with two live readings the corpus cannot separate, the fail-open
     discipline says take the one that cannot false-reject and mark it. **The
     rule forbids lowering an expectation; it does not compel a particular
     reading of an ambiguous clause.** Mason lowered nothing and hand-edited
     nothing. *(The verdict writes that last point as "STYLE 9's fail-open
     discipline" — which is a **CLAUDE.md headline number, not a citable
     STYLE.md ID**, the exact mistake #299 corrected at 37 sites; the rule
     meant is **STYLE P3/P3a**. Recorded, not silently repaired: the arbiter's
     reasoning is sound and only its label is wrong. See Next item 3.)
- **Decision: the two deviations, both accepting-direction, recorded as one
  `GAP(xsd)` at `xsd/derivation.go:994` with a STYLE P3a consumer enumeration.**
  (a) **`t` itself is a candidate step** (the strict reading admits only proper
  ancestors); (b) **"length is not specified" reads the step's OWN directly
  specified facets** — §3.16.6.4's `S` — **not the effective overlay**. The
  doc comment argues (b) on the clause's own wording: it says *"specified"* here
  where it says *"is a member of `{facets}`"* everywhere else, which is also what
  the erratum's "in different derivation steps" summary means — a step that
  inherits `length` without restating it did not specify it. The GAP text names
  the concrete divergent shape (`st = string(length=5)`, `st2` adds
  `maxLength=5`), names `errF001` as the one published fixture bearing on it, and
  states the condition for revisiting: *not adopted without an oracle grounding
  that reaches this fixture*.
- **Surprise — the oracle was overruled, and that is the correct outcome, not a
  process failure.** Two groundings on one issue, the second contradicting
  mason's shipped reading, and the shipped reading survived. The reason is a
  clean division of authority worth stating plainly for future sessions: **the
  oracle owns what the spec text says; it does not own what this repo ships when
  the spec text and the constitutional rule collide.** The second grounding is

## 2026-08-08 — #321 — value/xsd: the seven facet-pipeline capability **panics become `*xsderr.Error`** — the design decision this issue existed to make, taken toward "convert", and the two things that made it a real session rather than a mechanical rewrite are that **the issue's own blast radius was wrong in mason's favour** (nothing ripples through `newBoundFacet`/`CheckValue`/`compile` — they already return `error`; what the edit actually needed was THREE DISCRIMINATION sites so the new fault class is not mis-scored as an ordinary validity verdict) and that the warden's pre-flight found a **LIVE BUG on the two widest types in the language** — `effectiveWhiteSpace` panicked on the ·special· datatypes `anySimpleType`/`anyAtomicType`, where §4.1.5 says no facets are applicable at all and §4.1.4 makes them unconditionally Datatype Valid, so a naive conversion would have turned a crash into a **false reject**; arbiter ACCEPT on round 1 after a warden `revise` round, one new export (`value.IsFacetPrecondition`), ratchet unchanged and MEASURED

- Shipped on `wip/issue-321` as **two commits**, both retained (the repair round is a
  new commit, not an amend), on top of `origin/main` @ `b9b5641` (#538's landing):
  **`010d5e093d6e792055d8db45faaabeb17ddadf06`**
  (`value: return *xsderr.Error for the seven facet-pipeline capability panics
  (#321)`), **15 files, +717/−171**; then
  **`d0a42db6da44cd565c1c121ef8f366ad448ffe73`**
  (`value/xsd: address warden diff-review findings on #321 — ValueSpace contract
  bullet, facet-precondition Loc consistency (#321)`), **2 files, +21/−1**
  (`value/facets.go`, `xsd/valuespace.go`). Combined against the merge-base:
  **16 files, +737/−171**. **Arbiter ACCEPT on the first round** — the warden's
  diff-review `revise` is not an arbiter rejection and consumed no repair round
  against the two-reject cap.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** The arbiter's
  figures, copied not recomputed: `go build ./... && go test ./... && go vet ./...`
  pass (exit 0, all 16 test packages `ok`), `golangci-lint run` **0 issues**,
  `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1 -v` **PASS (24.76s)** over
  **41,858 cases / 6 lanes** with **zero** `regressed` and **zero**
  `improved … not yet banked`. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run
  TestConformance -count=1` → `ok … 25.221s`, and immediately after the run —
  before any branch switch (#303) — `git status --porcelain --
  conformance/testdata/expectations/` was **empty**: no upward movement, so nothing
  to bank and no expectations file touched. Zero lane movement was the *predicted*
  and *required* outcome here, and for a specific reason worth keeping: the warden
  made it a watch item that **no suite fixture should reach the new class at all**,
  because `conformance/datatypes.go` owns applicability itself. Any lane movement
  would have been evidence a fixture *had* been reaching a panic path and would
  have needed explaining case by case rather than banking.
- **The decision, and what actually decided it.** Two branches were on the table
  since #217 deliberately scoped this out: "stay panics" (a documented precondition
  of a leaf-construction API) or "convert to `*xsderr.Error`". The **oracle ruled
  the spec silent** — Structures §2.4 ("This specification defines no API or other
  interface for interacting with schemas") and §5.1's report-the-fact obligation
  scoped to schema-document → component *construction*, not to a library's
  in-process constructor API. So no spec clause picks a branch; this was a pure
  goxsd8 API-contract call, exactly as the issue framed it. The **libuser consult
  picked it**: the library's own documented taxonomy already excludes this case
  from the panic bucket — the panics elsewhere in the exported surface (`AddType`'s
  nil guard, `WithBackend`/`WithResolver`, `NewFacet`'s wrong-constructor case) are
  all "no reasonable value is representable at all", while a `totalDigits` facet on
  a non-decimal primitive is a **well-formed value pairing**, the shape
  `xsderr`'s own doc reserves for `*Error`. The persona's sharpest complaint was
  not taxonomy but **deferred blast radius**: the panic fires later, inside
  `ValidateLexical` at instance-validation time, against whatever payload happens
  to hit that facet first — turning a schema-assembly mistake into a
  validation-service crash.
- **Grounding — oracle, and its most useful output was a citation it RULED OUT.**
  The issue's Acceptance offered `cos-applicable-facets` / `st-restrict-facets` as
  the rule ID for the converted sites. **`st-restrict-facets` (Structures
  §3.16.6.4) is not on point** — it governs R-vs-B variety/primitive agreement and
  the facet-overlay algorithm during `<restriction>` derivation, a different
  question from "is this facet legal on this primitive/variety at all"; grepping
  `xmlschema11-2.md` for `cos-applicable-facets` finds exactly one anchor (§4.1.5
  itself) and no §4.3.x facet subsection cross-references it. **§4.1.5
  `cos-applicable-facets` alone** is correct and sufficient for the six. The same
  grounding is what separated the seventh site from the other six rather than
  merging them: §4.1.5's per-variety table gives **union** only
  `pattern, enumeration, assertions` — **no `whiteSpace`** — so `effectiveWhiteSpace`
  is a structurally different question. Posted in full on the thread; scratch at
  `.agent/grounding-issue-321.md`, gitignored and deliberately not committed.
  `st-restrict-facets` and `whiteSpace-valid-restriction` are cited **nowhere** in
  the landed diff.
- **The seventh site takes a different rule, on a spec sentence that settles it in
  one line.** §4.3.6.3: *"There are no ·Validation Rule·s associated with
  ·whiteSpace·"* — so no `cvc-*` exists and this cannot be an instance verdict;
  §4.3.6.4 `whiteSpace-valid-restriction` constrains restriction *ordering*, not
  presence. The three causes the old panic collapsed (multi-valued `Values()`, an
  out-of-domain token, an absent facet on atomic/list) violate §4.3.6.1 `f-w-value`
  and §3.16.7.4 / §3.16.2.1 `map.std.common` case 3 — **none is a numbered SCC**,
  which is the literal definition of `xsderr.RuleComponentInvariant`. So the cohort
  ships as **six `cos-applicable-facets` + one `RuleComponentInvariant`**, two rule
  IDs, deliberately not conflated.
- **Warden pre-flight — `revise`, and it is the single highest-value artifact of
  the session.** It agreed with the decision and rejected the SCOPE, on the finding
  that a literal "return the error instead of panicking" edit introduces three
  mis-attributions and one silent swallow, **all of them false rejects or false
  accepts of valid schemas/instances**:
  1. **`xsd`/`value/valuespace.go` — gate 4.** A capability error arriving at
     `ValidDefault` became decided-**invalid**, which charges
     `a-props-correct`/`au-props-correct` clause 2 — **a schema rejected for a
     precondition fault**, for a default no lexical form could ever have satisfied.
  2. **`value/union.go` — `dispatchUnion`.** The rejection-collecting loop folded a
     member's error into a rejection string and **continued**: a fault on member 0
     silently becomes "member 0 rejected", member 1 accepts, and the union reports
     **valid**. A silent FALSE ACCEPT, in the STYLE S3 loop — the one place in the
     module where an error is the control flow.
  3. **`value/restriction.go` — `checkEnumerationRestriction`.** It re-wrapped *any*
     `ValidateLexical` error under `ruleEnumerationValidRestriction`, naming a
     constraint with nothing to say about the fault (STYLE E2) — the exact mistake
     `boundLimit`'s own doc forbids, and `boundLimit` already models the right
     answer: **skip, don't charge**.
  The pre-flight also corrected the issue body's blast-radius table site by site
  (all six `facets.go` sites already sit inside `error`-returning functions;
  **exactly one signature changes**), ruled out discriminating the class by
  **matching the shared marker string**, and mandated
  `effectiveWhiteSpace(st) (whiteSpace, error)` over a three-result
  `(ws, applicable, err)` — eight combinations for three legal states, with the
  `whiteSpace` zero value already documented as the single "no mode applies"
  encoding (STYLE D3). Every one of those four instructions is in the landed diff.
- **Surprise (the one that would have shipped a regression) — the ·special·
  datatypes were ALREADY broken, and the conversion would have upgraded a crash
  into a wrong answer.** Warden verified by executing the current exported API
  against `builtin/strict`: `anySimpleType` and `anyAtomicType` both **panic
  today** inside `effectiveWhiteSpace`, because `value/facets.go` runs the
  whiteSpace stage *before* the `governingMapping` gate, so neither ·special·
  reaches the "no backend mapping governs" answer. Per §4.1.5 both are
  no-facets-applicable ({variety} absent; atomic with {primitive type definition}
  absent) and per §4.1.4 a ·special· is **unconditionally Datatype Valid** — so
  this is spec-mandated not-applicable, exactly like union, and the old code
  special-cased **union only**. Converted naively, `ValidateLexical` against
  `xs:anySimpleType` would have started returning decided **invalid**: a false
  reject on the widest type in the language, reachable from `SchemaBuilder` and
  from any library user. `noFacetsApplicable` now covers **all three** §4.1.5 cases
  (`Variety() == nil`; `Atomic{}` with `Primitive() == nil`; `Union`) and each is
  pinned.
- **Surprise, second order — fixing the ·specials· made a NEW panic reachable, and
  it was found by probing rather than by reading.** Because `dispatchUnion` can now
  legitimately return `ws == 0`, `normalizeWhiteSpace(raw, 0)` would have panicked
  in `validateUnion`'s clause-1 stage: an atomic type with an absent
  `{primitive type definition}` that is *not* the `xs:anyAtomicType` anchor **is**
  constructible and **is** admissible as a union member, since `cos-st-restricts`
  clause 3.1 rejects only the two ·special· anchors by identity. Mason verified
  reachability with a throwaway probe before adding the `if ws != 0` guard, so it
  is not speculative code; the warden independently confirmed it is **in scope, not
  creep** by deleting it in a scratch copy and watching
  `TestValidateLexicalUnionMemberWithNoApplicableFacets` panic — the same class
  this issue removes, made newly reachable by this branch's own widening.
- **Decision: one construction site and ONE new export, not a marker string and not
  an exported sentinel.** The class is `var errFacetPrecondition` (unexported) +
  `func facetPrecondition(rule, loc, format, args…) *xsderr.Error` (the single
  construction site, so `grep 'facetPrecondition('` enumerates the cohort where a
  literal string used to) + **`func IsFacetPrecondition(err error) bool`** — the
  only new exported symbol in the branch. A predicate beats an exported `var`
  (caller-**reassignable**, under three deciders) and beats exporting the two
  `Rule`s (forces every caller to enumerate a cohort that may grow). The export is
  load-bearing for the change's own rationale, not a convenience: without a
  discriminator the conversion turns a **loud** bug into an **indistinguishable**
  false reject — strictly worse than panicking, and it voids the libuser argument.
  Named for the **class** rather than warden's suggested `IsFacetNotApplicable`,
  because the seventh member is not an applicability question.
- **Decision: `conformance`'s applicability ownership becomes EXECUTED, and it
  panics.** All 7 `value.ValidateLexical` sites in `conformance/datatypes.go` route
  through `mustNotBeFacetPrecondition`, which panics — the executors return
  `Status` and hold no `*testing.T`, and there is no `recover()` anywhere under
  `conformance/`, so this is the file's own "programming error, not a runtime
  condition" convention. This is the **ratchet-integrity hazard** the warden named
  and the reason it could not stay prose: a fault silently scored `invalid` is, for
  an `nK`-expected case, a **banked false pass**. The `:248-255` and `:2385-2388`
  paragraphs now say the ownership is executed, not merely documented.
- **Decision: `GAP(xsd)` is DELETED, not reworded** (STYLE P3, the #334/#346
  precedent) — `grep 'GAP('` over `xsd/valueconstraintvalid.go` returns nothing.
  `xsd/schema.go`'s `FinalizeWith` "may panic" precondition was made false by this
  change and is **rewritten** rather than left standing: it now states the fault is
  reported undecided, so `FinalizeWith` neither rejects nor fails. This retires the
  panic surface #371 disclosed on 2026-08-03 and that this issue absorbed by its
  own post-land pass instead of spawning a duplicate ticket.
- **Warden diff review — `revise`, two required findings, both doc-surface, and the
  first is the one that mattered.** The implementation shape, the discrimination
  wiring and the test pinning were approved as built; nothing asked code to move.
  1. **[T3] `xsd/valuespace.go` — the deleted `GAP(xsd)` marker was resting on a
     coincidence, not a contract.** `xsd/valueconstraintvalid.go` and
     `xsd/schema.go` now assert to their own callers that the fault is *always*
     reported undecided — but `ValueSpace` is an **injected interface**, so
     undecided-on-fault was a property of `value`'s implementation that `xsd` had
     no standing to rely on. Fixed by a fourth bullet on `ValidDefault`'s
     "decided=false is required for at least" list, whose last sentence is the
     load-bearing half: it names the two sites that assert the guarantee and says
     explicitly that stating it here is what makes it bind **every**
     implementation. Mason's wording note is worth keeping: the bullet says "the
     construction seam every parsed type goes through" rather than naming
     `builtin.CheckSimpleTypeRestriction`, because `xsd` is a pure leaf and
     naming the higher package in its own godoc would point a reader **upward
     across the dependency direction**.
  2. **[E3] the class ships location-less for 5 of its 7 members, and silence is
     what E3 forbids.** `newBoundFacet` held `st` and passed `xsderr.Loc{}` while
     its cohort sibling in `whitespace.go` passed `st.Loc()`; that one is now
     `st.Loc()` too (**2 of 7 located**). For the five `CheckValue`-time members no
     component is in hand and nothing downstream re-supplies one, so mason took
     warden's **documented-omission** option over threading a `loc` field —
     five struct fields, three constructor widenings, eight test call sites, and a
     residual *within-method* asymmetry (a located precondition error beside
     unlocated verdict errors) that needs the same sentence anyway. The arbiter
     checked two points in mason's favour rather than assuming them: the ordinary
     verdict errors in those same five bodies have **always** carried
     `xsderr.Loc{}`, so this is the file's existing convention rather than a new
     gap; and warden explicitly offered the option taken.
- **The arbiter mutation-tested the deciders in a throwaway worktree rather than
  reading the tests, and each site failed for exactly the reason its own doc
  comment predicts** — which is the strongest thing that can be said about a change
  whose entire risk is silent false accepts. Deleting all three at once:
  `TestValidDefaultAcceptsFacetPreconditionFaults` fails
  `ValidDefault("ab") = (false, true), want undecided` (the clause-2 false schema
  rejection); `TestDispatchUnionAbortsOnFacetPreconditionFault` fails with
  `member 1 wrongly decided a union member 0 never decided` (the false ACCEPT);
  `TestEnumerationRestrictionSkipsFacetPreconditionFault` fails with the
  mis-attribution visible in the message text
  (`[enumeration-valid-restriction] … [cos-applicable-facets] …`). Narrowing
  `noFacetsApplicable` back to union-only fails **both** ·special·-datatype tests.
  The guard in the other direction is `TestFacetRejectionIsNotAPrecondition`: a
  genuine `cvc-maxScale-valid` verdict must **not** satisfy the predicate, since a
  widened predicate is the single mutation that would make `ValidDefault` wave
  through real invalid defaults, `dispatchUnion` abort on a mere rejection, and
  `checkEnumerationRestriction` skip real §4.3.5.5 violations.
- Panic-asserting tests were **inverted, not deleted** —
  `TestScaleFacetNonScaledPanics` folded into a five-site table
  (`TestValueFacetCapabilityFaultsAreErrors`), `…NoFacetPanics` → `…NoFacetErrors`,
  `…ListNoUsableModePanics` → `…ListNoUsableModeErrors` — each asserting three
  things (error returned, correct rule ID, `IsFacetPrecondition` true) so a

## 2026-08-08 — #323 — parser/builtin: the THIRD hand-typed facet-name↔`FacetKind` table is DELETED — `parser.facetKindOf`'s 14-arm switch becomes one call to a new `builtin.FacetKindByName`, the exported twin of the `facetNames` scanner, so a future `FacetKind` costs ONE bridge-table row instead of three synchronized edits (STYLE D3/T4) — and the session's entire value sits in the **warden's pre-flight**, which found before a line was written that a bare delegation hands `xsd.NewFacet` a `FacetAssertions` kind and **panics the parser on parseable schema input**, because the bridge table spells the facet in the PLURAL (`assertions`) while `restrictionFacets`' upstream pre-check intercepts only the SINGULAR element (`<assertion>`); arbiter ACCEPT on round 1 after reproducing that panic itself, exactly one new export, ratchet unchanged and MEASURED

- Shipped on `wip/issue-323` as a **single commit**,
  **`8432fc6c41686ab274778364e5e699a8b142f2ab`**
  (`parser/builtin: delegate facetKindOf to builtin.FacetKindByName (#323)`),
  **5 files, +99/−40** (`builtin/doc.go`, `builtin/seed.go`,
  `builtin/seed_test.go`, `parser/produce.go`, `parser/produce_test.go`), on top of
  `origin/main` @ **`085b007`** (#321's landing) with **no drift** — the arbiter
  confirmed `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` = `085b007`, so the branch is exactly
  one commit on main with nothing to pre-merge, unlike #321's session. **Arbiter
  ACCEPT on the first round** — the warden's pre-flight `revise` is not an arbiter
  rejection and consumed no repair round against the two-reject cap.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** The arbiter's
  figures, copied not recomputed: `go build ./... && go test ./... && go vet ./...`
  pass (**all 30 packages `ok`**), `golangci-lint run` **`0 issues.`**,
  `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1 -v` →
  **`--- PASS: TestConformance (24.36s)`** with **no improved-but-unbanked cases**.
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` → `ok`, and
  immediately after the run — before any branch switch (#303) —
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` was **empty**: no
  upward movement, nothing to bank, no expectations file touched. Zero lane movement
  was the *predicted* and *required* outcome, and the issue's own Acceptance said so:
  this is a behavior-preserving refactor, and any lane movement would have been
  evidence the delegation had **widened** the accepted facet-name set rather than
  reproduced it.
- **The equivalence is arithmetic, not assertion, and the arbiter did it that way.**
  `builtin/restriction.go`'s `facetNames` has **16 rows**; the deleted
  `facetKindOf` switch had **14 arms** — precisely the 16 minus `enumeration` and
  `assertions`. Delegating and then excluding those two kinds reproduces the old
  accepted-name set element for element. Neither the bridge table nor the
  `xsd.FacetKind` enum contains a name the old switch lacked, so **there is no
  widening hiding in the delegation** — which is the only way a pure consolidation
  can go wrong.
- **Grounding — oracle, and its most load-bearing output was a shape constraint,
  not a citation.** The new export must be a **function wrapping the EXISTING
  unexported `facetKind`**, never a second scanning implementation, and
  **`facetNames` must stay unexported**: exporting the raw slice would force
  `parser` to write its own linear scan (reintroducing the duplicate the issue
  exists to delete, STYLE T4/D3) and would freeze the linear-scan representation and
  row ordering into the public API — and, since it is a mutable package-level slice,
  would let a consumer append or reorder it into a **non-injective bijection**, an
  illegal state (the warden made the same call independently, on T3/T5). The oracle
  also pinned the rule for the new producer case: **`cos-st-restricts`**, charged by
  `checkAtomicApplicableFacets` in `builtin/restriction.go` and reached from
  `parser/produce.go`'s `builtin.CheckSimpleTypeRestriction` call —
  **`cos-applicable-facets` (§4.1.5) appears in the message TEXT only and is never
  the `xsderr.Rule`**, so a test asserting `xsderr.RuleOf(err)` must expect
  `cos-st-restricts`. And it flagged the ordering hazard the warden then made
  blocking: the `enumeration`/`assertion` pre-checks in `restrictionFacets` **must
  stay strictly above** the delegated lookup.
- **Warden pre-flight — `revise`, and it is the single highest-value artifact of the
  session, exactly as in #321.** It approved the signature, the `FacetName`-over-
  `string` boundary, the wrapper-over-slice call and the (unchanged) dependency
  direction, and rejected the SCOPE on one finding: **[T1]** a naive delegation to
  the full 16-row bijection lets `<xs:assertions value="x"/>` under `<restriction>`
  reach `xsd.NewFacet(FacetAssertions, …)`, which **panics**
  (`xsd/simpletype.go:319-324`, because neither kind's `{value}` is a lexical
  string, §4.3.5/§4.3.13). The upstream pre-checks test `"enumeration"` and
  `"assertion"` **singular**, while the bridge table's row is
  `{"assertions", xsd.FacetAssertions}` — so today `<xs:assertions>` falls off the
  end of the 14-arm switch and is harmlessly skipped, and after a bare delegation it
  becomes a **parser panic on parseable input, one commit after #321 spent a whole
  session converting facet-pipeline panics to errors**. The required shape —
  `if !ok || kind == xsd.FacetEnumeration || kind == xsd.FacetAssertions` — is in
  the landed diff verbatim, and `restrictionFacets` is **not in the diff at all**,
  so the pre-checks are provably untouched.
- **Decision: the exclusion lives in `facetKindOf`, not in call ordering.** The
  upstream pre-checks would have sufficed *if* the two spellings agreed; they do
  not, and depending on caller ordering to keep `NewFacet`'s panic kinds unreachable
  is precisely the coupling that rots. Excluding both kinds at the lookup puts the
  restriction **where `facetKindOf`'s own doc comment already claimed it lived** —
  the doc was accurate about the subset and the code was accidentally accurate about
  it, and now one of them enforces it.
- **Two tests, both mutation-verified by the arbiter rather than read.**
  `TestFacetKindByNameCoversTheGeneratedTable` (builtin/seed_test.go) walks every
  `FacetName` the generated `Types` table is keyed by through the **exported**
  surface, requires each to resolve, and requires the resolved kinds to cover the
  whole `FacetKind` range **injectively** — so a `FacetKind` added without a bridge
  row, or a row misspelled against the generated table, fails there instead of
  becoming a silent lookup miss in the parser. The producer case
  (`precisionDecimal extension facet inapplicable to the primitive`) puts
  `<xs:maxScale value="2"/>` on `base="xs:int"` and requires `cos-st-restricts`:
  the facet must be **RECOGNIZED into `{facets}` and only then rejected**, because a
  silently dropped facet yields **no error at all** — the exact #219 symptom, where
  `nil` is the false-accept rather than the pass. Arbiter mutation: adding
  `|| kind == xsd.FacetMaxScale` to the exclusion made it fail with
  `Produce accepted an invalid restriction, want cos-st-restricts`.
- **Surprise — the test the oracle called optional is the one that pins the
  singular/plural distinction the whole correction rests on.** The grounding noted
  that `TestFacetNamesBijection` already loops over `facetName`/`facetKind` and
  therefore *transitively* covers a pure delegation, making a direct test "a style
  choice, not a functional gap." Mason added it anyway, and it turned out to carry a
  fact no internal test carries: its final assertion is that
  **`FacetKindByName("assertion")` is `false`** — the singular element name resolves
  to nothing, which is the premise `facetKindOf`'s exclusion depends on and the
  reason the plural row is dangerous. An "exercise the exported surface" test earned
  its place by discovering a claim to make.
- **`builtin/doc.go`'s new "# Facet names" section was MANDATORY, not scope creep,
  and the warden said so in those terms.** STYLE T6 requires the same commit to
  reconcile a package's status prose when its exported surface changes; the warden's
  disposition is worth keeping verbatim for the next mason who is handed a
  task list that omits it — *"Mason's judgment call was right; do not revert.
  Acceptance criteria in an issue never override STYLE."*
- **Arbiter's one substantive finding — the new guard is invisible to the entire
  gate, and it proved it rather than suspected it.** With the enumeration/assertions
  exclusion deleted outright, `go test ./parser ./conformance -count=1` stayed
  **green in both packages**, while the three-line `<xs:assertions value="x"/>`
  schema **crashes the library**: the arbiter reproduced the panic at
  `xsd/simpletype.go:323` via `parser/produce.go:1110`, restored the exclusion, and
  confirmed the same input returns `err = <nil>` — silently skipped, **identical to
  `origin/main`**. So the exclusion is the only genuinely new logic in the diff and
  the suite cannot see its removal. Ruled **non-blocking because it is not a
  regression** (main does not panic on that input either, and neither does this
  branch) — but the guard's own doc calls itself "belt-and-suspenders," which is
  exactly the phrasing that invites a future cleanup pass to delete it with nothing
  objecting. Filed forward as Next item 2, with the repro ready to paste.

  and the grounding overrode it.** #326's acceptance text instructs, in as many
  words, that if the item type's whiteSpace mode is unobservable the comment
  must state it "is a no-op *because of what `Fields` already guarantees*, not

  that "whiteSpace facets and other ·pre-lexical· facets do not take part in

  whiteSpace is never consulted by `cvc-datatype-valid` at all. The `Fields`

## 2026-08-08 — #384 — parser: the identity-constraint pre-scan stops indexing what it does not map — a `<xs:key name="hidden">` buried under a FOREIGN-NAMESPACE host is no longer registered in `symbols.identityConstraints`, so a `ref=` to it fails `src-resolve` clause 1.7 instead of resolving to markup Appendix A gives no wildcard for; and the session's whole substance is that the issue's literal Acceptance §1 wording, the oracle's grounding, and mason's own commit message were EACH wrong in a different place while the landed code is right: the body prescribed hoisting the namespace check inside the loop **tested on the child**, the grounding closed by blessing that same "two-line fix" as "spec-correct and complete", and mason — who correctly refused both and moved the check onto `el` itself at function entry — then justified the move with a **reachability claim the arbiter empirically falsified** (`<xs:schema><xs:key name="tl">` does reach the root-indexing path, and behaviour differs between `main` and the branch); arbiter ACCEPT on round 1 after rebuilding the literal-wording version in a throwaway worktree and proving it fails the issue's own required test case, ratchet unchanged and MEASURED

- Shipped on `wip/issue-384` as one commit on top of **`d2a2fd9`** (#326's
  landing) — **`4ec3109c67eed9ee6628797685eb2ac2163f36f0`** (`parser: exclude
  foreign-namespace elements from the identity-constraint pre-scan (#384)`,
  2 files, `parser/produce.go` **+50/−28**, `parser/produce_xpath_test.go`
  **+32**, branch total **+82/−28**). **Arbiter ACCEPT on round 1, no repair
  round** — neither of the two rejections consumed. No exported surface change:
  the one new top-level name in production code, `indexIdentityConstraint`, is
  an unexported method, and the other is the new test func.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** Copied
  from the verdict, not recomputed: the full gate green (`go build ./... &&
  go test ./... && go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, and
  `go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1 -v`) over **41,858 cases
  across all 6 lanes**, with **no lane movement in any lane**, and
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` empty after the
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run and before any branch switch (#303's required phrasing
  and its required moment). **The absence of movement is the expected result,
  not a disappointment**: no W3C fixture exercises the shape — a conformant
  schema document cannot contain a foreign-namespace host outside an annotation
  in the first place, which is exactly *why* the suite is silent about it and
  why the pin has to be a unit test.
- **Origin — harvested, not planned.** #384 is an ADVISORY FINDING lifted out of
  #240's landing (PR #383) rather than a roadmap item: the arbiter reading that
  diff noticed the pre-scan recursed before it discriminated. Worth naming as a
  category alongside #538 and #336 — the advisory-finding pipeline produced a
  real, independently-grounded defect again, and it landed one issue after being
  written down.
- **Decision — BOTH exclusions move onto `el` at function entry, against the
  issue body's literal wording, and the arbiter agreed the deviation was
  necessary rather than merely nicer.** #384's Acceptance §1 says to hoist the
  `c.Name().Space() != xsd.XMLSchemaNS` check inside the loop, above the
  recursive call, tested on the child `c`. That fix is **incomplete for the
  shape the issue itself requires a test for**: `prescan` (`produce.go:459`) and
  `prescanRedefine` (`redefine.go:453`) call `prescanIdentityConstraints`
  directly on a top-level declaration, so a foreign-namespace host written as a
  `<xs:schema>` child arrives **as the root `el`**, which no loop-body check on
  `c` can ever see. Mason moved the namespace check *and* the pre-existing
  `isXSD(el, "annotation")` guard onto `el` at entry — before indexing, before
  recursion — so each exclusion governs its whole subtree *including its root*,
  at both entry points, written **once** instead of duplicated per call site
  (STYLE D3). The indexing step split out to `indexIdentityConstraint`, which
  now answers only "does this **mapped** element declare an identity
  constraint", leaving "is it mapped at all" to the caller. One question per
  function; the doc comments say which owns which.
- **Decision — the issue's literal test case was SUBSTITUTED, on the arbiter's
  own confirmation that it tests nothing.** The body asked for the `<xs:key>`
  nested inside `<xs:appinfo>`. That case is already excluded by the
  `<annotation>` guard **regardless of the namespace bug**, and is already
  pinned by `TestProduceIdentityConstraintRefToAnnotationOnlyNameUnresolvable` —
  it would have been green before the fix. The landed
  `TestProduceIdentityConstraintRefToForeignHostedNameUnresolvable` instead
  builds two subtests whose host is **not** inside an annotation, so only the
  namespace check can reject them: *foreign host at the top level* (the root
  case the literal wording cannot reach) and *foreign host under a global
  `<xs:element>`* (the nested case it can). The `ref=` is placed FIRST in
  document order so no already-built component can stand in for the missing one.
  Same family as #326's substituted justification: the body was right about the
  outcome and wrong about the mechanism that would demonstrate it.
- **Verification — the arbiter did not take the deviation on report; it rebuilt
  the rejected design and executed it.** In a throwaway worktree it implemented
  the issue's literal Acceptance §1 wording and ran the new test against it: the
  *foreign host at the top level* subtest **fails**. That is what converts
  mason's argument from a plausible reading of the call sites into an
  established fact, and it is the reason a deviation from a written acceptance
  criterion accepted on round 1 without a repair round.
- **Surprise — the ORACLE blessed the wrong fix, in its own closing sentence.**
  The grounding is correct and load-bearing on all three questions it was asked
  (§3.1.3 `mapping.xr.c` verbatim; Appendix A's `<xs:any processContents="lax"/>`
  appearing **only** inside `appinfo`/`documentation`, with everything else
  extending `openAttrs`' attribute-only wildcard; `src-resolve` clause 1.7 as
  the property a superset index falsely satisfies). But it then volunteered
  *"The two-line fix (hoist the `c.Name().Space() != xsd.XMLSchemaNS` check
  above the recursive call) is spec-correct and complete"* — endorsing the
  body's literal wording on a **spec** argument ("there is no valid document
  shape where …") that is true about the spec and silent about the call graph.
  The oracle is read-only and scoped to spec exegesis, so this is not a failure
  of its mandate; it is a reminder that a grounding's *codeward* asides carry no
  more authority than any other unverified claim, and that "complete" is a
  property of an implementation, not of a spec reading. Mason overrode it
  anyway, which is the right outcome.
- **Surprise — the code comment already asserted the invariant the code
  violated.** The oracle flagged it: `parser/produce.go`'s pre-existing comment
  block already carried the "strict SUPERSET of {identity-constraint
  definitions}" framing and already cited `src-resolve` clause 1.7, and even
  claimed *"The guard covers foreign-namespace elements too: in a schema
  document they occur only inside annotations."* That last sentence is the bug
  in one line — it reasons about **conformant** documents to justify the
  behaviour on **non-conformant** ones, which is precisely the input class the
  check exists for. The fix deletes it. Comments that state an invariant the
  implementation does not enforce are worse than no comment, because they
  actively stop the next reader from checking.
- **Surprise — the arbiter found TWO true things the implementation report did
  not contain, and one of them contradicts it.** Recorded because both outlive
  this session:
  1. **A top-level `<xs:annotation><xs:appinfo><xs:key name="…">` was ALSO
     falsely indexed before this commit** — the same root-blindness as the
     namespace bug, in the *other* exclusion. The old loop tested
     `isXSD(c, "annotation")` on children only, so a `<xs:schema>`-level
     `<xs:annotation>` passed in as `el` was walked straight into. It is now
     correctly excluded by the same entry check, per the same §3.1.3 rule. **No
     test pinned this before the fix and none pins it after** — the existing
     annotation test uses an annotation nested under an `<xs:element>`, which
     the old code did catch. Advisory, non-blocking, carried to Next.
  2. **Mason's "unreachable in practice" claim about root-level indexing is
     WRONG.** The commit/report justified indexing `el` itself as harmless on
     the grounds that the root is never an identity constraint; the arbiter

## 2026-08-08 — #327 — conformance: every decline is RE-ATTEMPTED rather than trusted — the runner re-runs each recorded failure with its declared outcome FLIPPED, and "Fail under both polarities" is not a heuristic for "no executor decided this case" but an exact test of it, because every decline exit returns `Fail()` strictly before the one comparison that reads the expectation; the whole guard therefore costs **zero changes to ~240KB of executor code**, and the arbiter proved the premise by COUNTING rather than sampling — `expectation` is read at exactly eleven sites in the package and `return Pass()` appears at exactly the same eleven, so no other exit can distinguish the polarities; the payoff landed on the issue's own evidence #1 the first time it ran, with the `datatypes` lane's 22 failures splitting **18 declined / 4 decided-and-disagreed** and the candidate list naming `d3_3_4v15` and `v18`–`v22`, the six direct siblings of the case that named the pattern; arbiter ACCEPT on round 1, three advisory findings, ratchet **proven** unchanged by md5 rather than observed unchanged by `git status`

- Shipped on `wip/issue-327` as one commit on top of **`d2a2fd9`** (#326's
  landing) — **`6b53e232a7d42f7e6d407b5815e2fd89f9c7c560`** (`conformance:
  surface the declined-and-fail candidate list for TestConformance (#327)`),
  4 files, **+277/−0**, no deletions anywhere: `conformance/declines.go` **+100**
  (new — `declinesEnv`, `declineCensus`, `takeDeclineCensus`,
  `flipExpectation`), `conformance/declines_test.go` **+127** (new — three
  tests), `conformance/conformance_test.go` **+28** (the new `reportDeclines`
  helper plus its one call site in `runConformanceLane`), `conformance/doc.go`
  **+22** (a new `# The decline census` section). **Zero new exported
  identifiers** — the issue's `Surface: none` is met literally; the only capitals
  the branch adds are three `Test*` functions in a `_test.go`.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank.** Copied from
  the verdict, not recomputed: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`
  all pass, `golangci-lint run` **0 issues**, `go test ./conformance -run
  TestConformance -count=1 -v` **ok — 32.87s (wall 33.2s)**, and
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` **ok,
  32.87s** with `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/`
  **empty** immediately after the run and before any branch switch (#303's
  required phrasing at its required moment). Worth recording that the arbiter
  went **past** that requirement here, because the branch's whole risk is that a
  reporting-only guard might not be reporting-only: it md5-summed all seven
  expectation files BEFORE the runs and re-checked them after the read-only run,
  after the `GOXSD_DECLINES=1` run, and after the ratchet run — **byte-identical
  every time**. That is *proven* unchanged, not *observed* unchanged, and it is
  the right standard for a diff whose entire safety argument is "this code path
  cannot reach a writer."
- **Decision — detect the decline at the LANE SEAM by flipping the expectation,
  rather than by instrumenting the decline sites.** The issue offered three
  shapes in preference order; this is option 1, the preferred mechanical one. The
  alternative reading of option 1 — enumerate the `ok=false` decline lists and
  report them — was rejected for a reason the thread had already supplied: the
  #276 post-land pass (2026-08-01, folded into this issue rather than filed
  separately) added a **fourth** instance of the pattern that is *computed*, not
  hand-written — `conformance/schema.go:443`'s `scan.unresolved && perr != nil`
  conjunction, a scan-scoped bool that can decline a case whose unresolved
  directive is unrelated to whatever broke the parse. A detector keyed to literal
  decline lists misses it by construction. Observing at the seam ("declined AND
  currently recorded `fail`") covers hand-written and computed declines
  identically, which is exactly what that comment argued for.
- **Decision — the probe flips the EXPECTATION, so no executor changes at all.**
  `flipExpectation` (`declines.go:93`) returns a **copy** of the `caseSpec`
  carrying the other decided outcome; `takeDeclineCensus` re-runs `l.exec` on
  that copy. An executor that decided the case reaches its terminal
  `observedValid == c.expect.wantsValid()` and necessarily answers the opposite
  `Status`; one that declined never reads the outcome and answers `Fail` twice.
  The design's whole appeal is what it does NOT require: no decline site records
  a reason, no executor grows a third return value, no `Status` gains a variant.
- **Decision — count always, IDs opt-in behind `GOXSD_DECLINES=1`.** The count
  goes through the same `t.Logf` channel `Improved` already uses (#303), so `-v`
  always shows the queue's size; the sorted IDs are gated because the `instance`
  lane, having no engine before M5, declines **all 26,422** of the cases it
  claims and would bury every other line the run prints. Indeterminate declines
  (the #277 convention) are counted on a **separate** line rather than folded in,
  because no executor may ever score them a pass — they are declines but never
  harvest candidates, and `declineCensus`'s two fields are two distinct facts
  neither derivable from the other (STYLE D3; the count-vs-list asymmetry is
  documented in place at `declines.go:52-58`).
- **The soundness argument is a COUNT, not a sample, and that is why a
  zero-executor-change design was acceptable.** The arbiter grepped the package:
  `expectation` is read at **exactly eleven** sites outside the census —
  `schema.go:483` (`decideSchema`, the terminal statement of `execSchemaCase`)
  and `datatypes.go:908, 962, 1001, 1045, 1139, 1228, 1298, 1405, 1461, 1706` —
  and `return Pass()` appears at **exactly the same eleven** (plus
  `expectations.go:119`, the parser). Both directions follow mechanically. *No
  decline can be read as a decision*: every other exit is a bare `Fail()` reached
  without touching `expect`, so the two polarities take **identical control
  flow**. *No decision can be read as a decline*: reaching the comparison means
  the status is `observedValid == wantsValid`, and negating `wantsValid` negates
  it, so exactly one polarity passes. The arbiter then walked both requested
  executors by hand anyway — `execSchemaCase`'s five decline exits (`:438`,
  `:451`, `:458`, `:467`, `:470`) plus the `Unfollowed() && perr != nil`
  conjunction (`:481`), and `datatypes.go`'s `execLexicalCase` `!mapped &&
  !strictGoverns` (`:869`) and `execItemCase` `!decided` (`:1043`) — confirming
  none consults `expect`.
- **Two secondary hazards checked and cleared, both of which would have been easy
  to leave as silences.** (1) `observedValid` must be **reproducible across the
  two calls** or the probe compares different observations: the datatypes
  executor's `sym` is written once at construction (`datatypes.go:790`) and
  read-only after, `newSchemaExec` captures no symbol table (`schema.go:398-402`
  — `Parse` seeds per call), and the one map range that could feed a verdict,
  `enumerationMember` at `datatypes.go:2495`, collects keys and `sort.Strings`
  them before use — so the observation is a pure function of the fixture.
  (2) `mustNotBeFacetPrecondition` (`datatypes.go:1731`) **panics**, so the probe
  could in principle double the panic surface: it keys on `verr`, which is
  polarity-independent, and control flow up to it is identical, so it cannot fire
  on a flipped run without having fired on the original.
- **Surprise — the census's first real run paid off directly on the issue's own
  evidence #1, and it is a real partition rather than a mechanism that returns
  everything.** The `datatypes` lane records 22 failures; the census splits them
  **18 declined / 4 decided-and-disagreed**. The four it EXCLUDES —
  `anyURI_a004_1339.i`, `gMonth002_2061.v`, `gMonth004_2063.v`,
  `pdecimal006.n2.xml` — are genuine engine disagreements, correctly kept out of
  the harvest queue; an engine that answered wrongly is not a shape nothing
  recognized, and conflating them would refill the queue with exactly the noise
  the issue exists to remove. The candidates include `d3_3_4v15`, `d3_3_4v18`,
  `d3_3_4v19`, `d3_3_4v20`, `d3_3_4v21`, `d3_3_4v22` — **the six direct siblings
  of `d3_3_4v16`**, the case whose nine-day wrong decline named the pattern in
  the first place. The queue the issue called invisible is printed on the first
  run. Both directions were spot-checked end to end with `GOXSD_CASE`.
- **Surprise — the test that looked unfalsifiable under Go value semantics is
  genuinely load-bearing.** `TestTakeDeclineCensusLeavesDiscoveryUntouched` pins
  that the probe flips a **copy**, which reads at first like a tautology given
  that `flipExpectation` takes `caseSpec` by value. The arbiter mutation-verified
  it anyway and it trips on an **in-place refactor** of `takeDeclineCensus` — a
  narrow but real pin, and the kind of test that gets deleted by a later reader
  who reasons about it the way this paragraph's first sentence does. All three
  tests were mutation-verified by the arbiter itself rather than taken on report
  (drop the flip; drop the indeterminate skip; make `flipExpectation` a no-op;
  mutate `cases` in place — each applied, run, reverted, tree re-verified clean).
- **Cost, measured rather than hand-waved: the census is ~18% of wall time and
  the reason is asymmetric.** 27.7s → 32.7s, reproduced independently by the
  arbiter. Almost all of it is the **`schema` lane re-running 4,103 declined
  parses**; the `instance` lane's 26,422 re-runs hit `stubFail` and cost
  essentially nothing. That asymmetry inverts at M5 — when the `instance` lane
  gets an engine its re-runs stop being free — which is worth knowing before
  someone reads the number as a fixed 18%.
- **Ratchet safety is STRUCTURAL, not merely observed.** `takeDeclineCensus`
  returns a value; `reportDeclines` only calls `t.Logf`. Neither reaches
  `Ratchet` or `WriteExpectations`, and neither writes to `actual` — the map is
  read through a two-value lookup only. The single writer, `WriteExpectations`,
  stays reachable solely from the `ratcheting` branch of `runConformanceLane`.
  That is what makes it safe to run the census on the ratcheting path too, which
  it does.

- **Ratchet: schema +23 — `9549 → 9572` pass of `15432`; `datatypes` and
  `instance` unchanged. Run and banked BY THE ARBITER, in `32c8cbe`, before

  **zero downward flips**, no other lane file touched, and a re-run after

  `particlesR004` (`{0,3}` → `{1,3}`), `particlesJa005` (`{1,4}` → `{2,4}`),
  `particlesHa102` (`{2,2}` → `{3,3}`) — this issue's class exactly, and all far
  under the ceiling, so **none of the 23 is a ceiling fail-open**. The
  cross-check that matters more than the gain: per-lane **declined counts are
  `18 / 4103 / 12 / 26422 / 4`, bit-identical to `origin/main` in every lane**,
  on both rounds. A collapse that changed a verdict anywhere in the 41,858
  cases would have shown there. Gate green, run by the arbiter on `7572276`:
  `go build ./...` · `go vet ./...` · `go test ./...` · `golangci-lint run`
  **0 issues** · conformance. (`go tool logguard` correctly not re-adjudicated
  — CLAUDE.md's Commands block is the source of truth, #304 — and the arbiter
  said so in one line on both rounds, which is what #304 asked for.)
- **Decision — an `unfold` POLICY on `automaton`, not a bigger constant.** The
  issue forbade resolving this by raising `maxMandatoryCopies`/
  `maxOptionalCopies` ("at 5/5, `e{3,6}` unfolds exactly but `e{0,100}` still
  collapses to `e{0,5}`"), and the oracle's grounding closed the door on any
  spec-derived bound: §3.4.6.4 clause 1 is pure set-containment with **no
  algorithm**, XSD 1.1 dropped 1.0's separate `cos-particle-restrict`, and
  **Appendix J's unfolding guidance is scoped by its own text strictly to
  `cos-nonambig`** and is never cited in connection with restriction. So the
  bound was replaced rather than retuned: `cos-nonambig`'s two construction
  sites keep `unfoldCopies` byte-for-byte, and `contentAutomatonOf` passes
  `unfoldExactly`, which emits `{max occurs}` copies for a bounded range and
  `{min occurs}` copies plus a loop-back for an unbounded one. The arbiter
  re-derived language-exactness against `addParticle`/`appendToSequence`
  independently: bounded `{m,n}` composes to `∪_{j=m..n} L^j`, unbounded to
  `L^m·L*` (and `L*` at `m = 0`), vacuous `{0,0}` to no fragment. **Not an
  approximation** — no false accept and no false reject from the unfolding.
- **Decision — `maxContentPositions = 4096` bounds automaton SIZE and
  abandons wholesale, and that is the difference between a fail-open and a
  truncation-into-a-verdict.** `contentTypeRestricts:440` returns `true`
  *before* `contentAutomatonOf` is reached, and `contentAutomatonOf` has no
  other call site, so an unmaterializable model is never half-built and never
  scored; `TestContentRestrictsBeyondPositionCeiling` pins the direction.
  Termination holds because the ceiling refuses the construction before it
  starts. `unfoldedPositions`' saturating arithmetic is overflow-safe against
  `maxOccurs="4294967295"` (the `inner | 4097` case returns exactly `4097`,
  still over).
- **Decision — the repair collapses CALLS, never the state set.** Copies of
  one particle replay one `particleID` over one source subtree
  (`addParticle` resets `b.nextParticleID` before *each* copy and re-walks the
  same deterministic `p.Term()`), so within one automaton `particleID`
  determines `{term}`, and `{term}` is **all `positionAdmits` reads**
  (`position` has exactly two fields; `elementParticleAdmits` reads names,
  `wildcardSubset` reads constraints, and clause 2's `someBindingSubsumes`
  touches the R position only through `elementPositionBinding(p)`). So the
  memo key is a function of the answer memoized. `matchPositions` still
  appends **every** live position whose group admits — copies keep their
  distinct `·follow·` sets and are still enqueued as their own R-states — only
  the `positionAdmits` calls (once per group) and the transition decision
  (once per R `particleID` per state) are deduplicated. B-subsets are interned
  so a product state is a pair of ints, and `liveIn` marks a scratch `[]bool`
  instead of folding follow sets through `mergePositions`.
- **Decision — `liveSet.reps` is derived state and lands anyway (STYLE D3).**
  It is recoverable from `positions`+`group` by a scan, which D3 normally
  forbids; it sits on a hot path with a **160× measurement** behind it, which
  is precisely the profile D3's "no memoized caches without a profile showing
  a hot path" asks for. The arbiter ruled it acceptable and documented rather
  than waived.
- **Decision — the ceiling-boundary residual is REPORTED and landed, not
  fixed in-round.** Mason measured it, attributed it (60% of a profile at
  n=1024 in `addFollow`/`mergePositions`, against 8% in this walk), stated it
  in the `maxContentPositions` comment, and told the arbiter rather than
  shipping it quietly. The arbiter accepted on four grounds worth preserving:
  the harm **moved out of the populated band** (the suite has 1532 models at
  ≤ 2970 positions and then jumps straight to 30001, which declines — "rare
  tail" is *measured* here, not asserted); it is **bounded and one-time**
  (~82 s worst case at schema-compile time, where round 1's problem was an
  extrapolated ~40 minutes with no bound in sight); what it buys is
  **unconditional** (the false-reject class hits `{0,6}` → `{1,6}`); and the
  residual lives in the builder **shared with the `cos-nonambig` path**, so
  changing the follow-set representation there puts every UPA verdict in the
  suite at risk — doing that in the final minutes of a final repair round
  would be strictly worse engineering than landing with the measurements in
  hand.
- **`citations_test.go`'s allowance for `xsd/contentrestricts.go` goes 2 → 3**
  because `unfoldedPositions` is a real second traversal following
  `ModelGroupRef`, leaning on the same Phase B `checkModelGroupsAcyclic`
  licence `addTerm` already leans on. The arbiter's phrasing: the bump is
  **honest** — no cycle check was added and none was papered over.

     high-water **2970**) and that *was* the finding: 2970-position models
     cost nothing (suite wall time 37.0 s branch vs 38.3 s main) while a

     are uncorrelated, so the constant could not be the bound its comment
     claimed. Corrected in round 2 to state what it does and does not bound,

  4. **The residual needs only ONE wide side, which mason's symmetric table

  5. **The false idempotence lemma was refuted by the same file, two
     paragraphs above it.** `coveringWildcardUnion`'s guard moved from
     `len(wildcards) < 2` to `len(constraints) < 2`, justified as
     verdict-identical because "§3.10.6.3's union is idempotent … so X ∪ X =
     X". It is not: `unionDisallowedNameKeywords` drops `sibling`
     **unconditionally**, as `contentrestricts.go`'s own GAP marker already
     states, so `X ∪ X` = X-minus-sibling ⊋ X. Cases 2/3/4/5 and the QName
     half are idempotent; the keyword half is not. **The code is right
     anyway**, for the reason the next sentence gives — with one distinct live
     wildcard particle, B's alphabet is exactly X and `wildcardSubset`
     (`cos-ns-subset`, whose `disallowedNamesSubset` condition 3 *does* compare
     sibling) has already answered exactly, so the new path is spec-exact and
     the old one was an accidental fail-open applying attribute-only union
     algebra to one particle's own copies. `cade242` therefore keeps the
     conclusion and rewrites the justification into a claim about which
     **operands** the fold sees.
