## 2026-08-08 — #576 — conformance: the ratchet learns its **first line-deleting class** — `Delta.Removed`, a case discovery stops producing because the W3C suite's own `@version` metadata scopes it away from an XSD 1.1 processor — and the whole design is that **neither of the two locks can lower a score alone**: the runner's `withheld` slice classifies (never a heuristic `Compare` infers from the diff), the arbiter counts (`GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS=lane=N`, refusing the entire merge on any mismatch in either direction), and `Regressed`/`Vanished` still abort whatever the assertion says; this is the mechanism #446's reject verdict asked for and was barred from authorizing itself, landing on the authority of a **human-filed repo-owner ruling** with CLAUDE.md's one rule deliberately unamended; arbiter ACCEPT on round 1 with 9-of-9 guards killed by named tests, **`Ratchet: unchanged`** — the plumbing lands **unfired**

- Shipped: `wip/issue-576` @ `7207daf` (mason's implementation) plus this LOG
  entry, squash-merged as one commit. 12 files, **+770 / −77**: five in
  `conformance/`, seven docs. **Ratchet: unchanged** — copied from the
  arbiter's verdict, not recomputed here. The arbiter's own
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1`
  returned `ok 31.8s` and
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` was
  **empty** immediately after: nothing withholds anything yet, so no lane
  moved and the run **wrote nothing**. Read-only gate: 41858 cases across 6
  lanes, **0 withheld as inapplicable**, no `Regressed`, no `Improved`
  pending. `RATCHET: unchanged` is the honest state here, not a discarded
  write — there was no upward movement to commit. This is exactly what
  #576's own Gate predicted ("on `main` this change moves no lane … if it
  writes anything, that is a finding"), so the null result is the deliverable
  rather than a disappointment.
- **The mechanism, in the two pieces the ruling required.**
  1. **`Delta.Removed`** (`conformance/expectations.go:58-64`) — a fifth
     field beside `Improved`/`Regressed`/`New`/`Vanished`, sorted, listing
     expected cases the run no longer produced **because discovery ruled
     them inapplicable**. `Compare` gains the input it needs to tell the
     two apart — `Compare(expected, actual, withheld []string)` — and the
     **only** thing that moves a case out of `Vanished` is membership in
     the runner's `withheld` slice. `parseSuite` now returns a `discovery`
     carrying produced cases *and* withheld IDs, both built through one
     shared `caseID` construction (STYLE D3/T4), so the two sets are
     comparable by construction rather than by convention;
     `TestWithheldIDsUseTheSameConstructionAsProducedCases` asserts the
     recorders against `casesFromSet`'s **own output** instead of a
     hand-written literal, which is the shape that will not drift when the
     ID format does. Disjointness is structural, not asserted: a withheld ID
     cannot appear in `actual` (the contradiction check errors first), so it
     can never be `New`/`Improved`/`Regressed`, and `Removed`/`Vanished` are
     the two mutually exclusive branches of a single `if`. A withheld ID the
     run also **produced** is a runner bug and comes back as an error with an
     empty `Delta` — surfaced, never tie-broken — and mason's reasoning that
     this may fail even the read-only path (which otherwise fails on
     `Regressed` only) is right: a self-contradicting case list is not a
     conformance result at all. A withheld ID with no committed expectation
     is a no-op.
  2. **The assertion lock** (`expectations.go:202-266`) —
     `RemovalAssertion`, constructed only via `AssertRemovals(n)`, passed to
     `Ratchet(expected, actual, withheld, removals)`. It is a **second,
     independent lock and not the classifier**: it never decides which cases
     are sanctioned, it only refuses to bank a set whose size the arbiter did
     not predict, in **either direction**. Per lane, because `d.Removed` is
     `expected(lane) ∩ withheld` and a removal drifting between lanes must
     not net out to a passing total. The count check runs **after** the
     unconditional `Regressed`/`Vanished` refusal, so a correct removal
     assertion buys no tolerance for a real regression. Banking **deletes**
     the case's line (`delete(merged, id)`) — tolerating without deleting is
     precisely #446's permanent-freeze failure mode, where stale lines make
     every future run refuse both lanes forever.
  - The env boundary is `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS=<lane>=<n>,...`
    (`conformance/runner.go:231`, `removalAssertions` at `:242`), and it
    **errors before it parses** if `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` is absent — asserting
    removals is arbiter-only and never applies to a read-only run. The
    arbiter exercised both directions live: set without the ratchet, the run
    ends with `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS is set but GOXSD_RATCHET=1 is not` and
    writes nothing; asserted-but-wrong on the ratchet path
    (`schema=34,instance=65` against a suite that withholds nothing), **both
    lanes refuse** with `run asserted N sanctioned applicability removal(s),
    found 0 []`, the refusing lane returns before `WriteExpectations`, and
    the expectations directory stays clean.
- Decisions:
  - **#576 is the human-filed authority, and it is the only reason this
    could land at all.** CLAUDE.md scopes its one rule and the arbiter's
    ratchet-integrity section to change "only via a human-filed issue"; #576
    is the repo owner ruling in direct conversation, verbatim: *"When suite
    discovery stops producing a case because the W3C suite's own @version
    metadata scopes it away from an XSD 1.1 processor, that is a sanctioned
    applicability removal, not a Vanished regression."* The ruling also fixed
    what may **not** move: scores still only move up, expectations are still
    machine-written only, and genuine `Regressed`/`Vanished` still abort the
    whole merge. **CLAUDE.md itself was deliberately NOT amended** — verified
    here against the branch, empty diffstat, as the arbiter also confirmed.
    The seven files that did change are exactly the list #576 authorizes:
    `conformance/testdata/expectations/README.md`, `conformance/doc.go`,
    `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, `.claude/agents/arbiter.md`, `docs/ROUTINES.md`,
    `.claude/commands/ratchet.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The base ratchet
    invocation spelling did not change either — what was added is an
    optional arbiter-only variant, which is why CLAUDE.md's command block
    needed no touch.
  - **The arbiter's doc amendment carries a duty the machinery cannot
    enforce.** `.claude/agents/arbiter.md` now requires that a verdict
    banking removals **enumerate the removed case IDs and state the
    applicability justification for each** — which `@version` token scopes it
    away and why this processor does not claim that token — and says in as
    many words that *"the runner withheld them" is not a justification*. The
    count lock proves the arbiter predicted the size; only the prose proves
    the arbiter read the cases. It also forbids asserting a count not first
    read off a read-only run's lane log.
  - **`RemovalAssertion`'s zero value asserts none, and there is no `set
    bool` beside the count.** Asserting zero and asserting nothing permit
    exactly the same set (`len(d.Removed) == 0`), so a flag would be a second
    encoding of one fact (STYLE D3) for no gain — and the default falls the
    safe way: a caller who forgets gets the pre-#576 hard refusal, never a
    silent bank. Unexported field plus constructor means no caller can spell
    an assertion by struct literal.
  - **The exported surface is five entries and every one is *forced*.**
    `Delta.Removed` (its four siblings are exported), the `Compare` and
    `Ratchet` signature changes (both authorized by #576's Surface),
    `RemovalAssertion` (it appears in exported `Ratchet`'s signature), and
    `AssertRemovals` (the type has only unexported fields, so construction is
    otherwise impossible). Nothing convenience-shaped was added; `conformance`
    has zero importers outside itself, so the blast radius is nil.
- Surprises:
  - **The plumbing lands with zero production callers, and that is the
    Acceptance rather than a defect.** `withholdTest`/`withholdGroup`/
    `withholdSet` (`conformance/runner.go:395-425`) are called by tests only.
    #576's Gate says so explicitly, and **#446 is the branch that wires the
    four `casesFromSet` filter sites to the `withhold*` recorders** and will
    be the first run to assert a nonzero count. Until then this is a
    mechanism proven by its tests and unfired in production — reap it only
    if #446 dies, not before.
  - **Every guard is proven by deletion, not by inspection.** The arbiter
    reverted each of the nine new guards in turn and recorded which named
    test died: **9 killed, 0 survived**, tree restored clean after each. The
    two that matter most for ratchet integrity — `Ratchet` **deleting** the
    banked line, and the `Regressed`/`Vanished` refusal surviving any
    removal assertion — are killed by
    `TestRatchetBanksAssertedRemovalsByDeletingTheirLines` (which covers a
    banked `pass` *and* a banked `fail` in one run) and by
    `TestRatchetRefusesRegressionAndVanishWhateverTheRemovalAssertion`.
  - **The count-only design was explicitly rejected by the issue, and the
    reason is compositional.** "N vanished are fine" passes when the total
    matches but the composition is wrong — one applicability case reappears
    while an unrelated case genuinely vanishes. The ID set is the classifier;
    the count is only the second lock. Both were built.
- Friction: **the one conflict this landing hit was in `docs/LOG/2026-08.md`

  a #576 problem; it is the shape of a monthly append-only log under

- **Carried findings (non-blocking, for future reapers):**
  1. **`conformance/expectations.go:207` cites "STYLE T7" and #576's own

  2. **`AssertRemovals` does not validate a negative count** — `AssertRemovals(-1)`

## 2026-08-08 — #581 — conformance: the ratchet's lane writes become **all-or-nothing**, closing out the #576 → #446 → #581 chain — and the durable lesson is the *instrument*, not the fix: a stray expectations write is **invisible to `git status`** when there is no pending movement, because the rewritten bytes are identical, so inode+mtime is the only thing that can prove a refusal wrote nothing; the bug existed at all only because the arbiter runs a **negative control before banking**, and that habit — not any test in the tree — is what caught it

- Shipped: `wip/issue-581` @ `d439f83`, one commit on top of `af0b3c3`
  (`main` at the time = #446's landing), squash-merged to `main`.
  5 files, +223/−41: `conformance/expectations.go` (the new `ratchetAll`),
  `conformance/expectations_test.go`, `conformance/conformance_test.go`,
  `conformance/runner.go`, `conformance/doc.go`.
  Arbiter verdict `accept`, round 1, no blocking findings:
  https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/581#issuecomment-5227830265
- **Ratchet movement, copied from that verdict: unchanged — ratchet run,
  tree clean, nothing to bank.** All six lane files were rewritten with
  byte-identical content (fresh inodes confirm the write phase executed and
  every lane merged clean), so
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` came back
  empty. There was no upward movement to commit: #446 had already banked the
  applicability removals, and this change is pure runner mechanics that moves
  no case. No removals asserted, so nothing to enumerate.
- The fix: **two passes instead of one loop.** `observeConformanceLane` runs
  and reports one lane and returns a `laneRun{name, expected, actual}`; the
  read-only verdict path and the new `ratchetAll` (in
  `conformance/expectations.go`) both consume the whole slice. `ratchetAll`
  merges *every* lane first, `errors.Join`s every refusal rather than stopping
  at the first, and reaches its write phase only when every lane merged — so
  one lane's refusal now leaves EVERY lane's file untouched. `laneFileIn` takes
  the directory, which both makes the write phase testable against a temp dir
  and collapses lane-path construction to a single site (the arbiter scored
  that as a D3/T4 *tightening* relative to `main`, not merely compliance).
- Decision — **the three-way doc conflict was resolved upward, toward the
  stronger promise.** #581 offered two resolutions: make the code atomic, or
  align the docs down to the per-lane reality. `conformance/doc.go:102` and
  `.claude/agents/arbiter.md:103` both already promised "the entire merge";
  only `doc.go:125` ("the lane's whole merge") described what the code did.
  Moving the code up rather than the prose down means the **arbiter brief was
  never wrong** — it was aspirational, and is now honored. `arbiter.md:103` is
  therefore **unchanged, and correctly so**: the right resolution here looks
  like an untouched file, not an edited one, and a later reader should not
  mistake that for an oversight.
- **The durable lesson, and the reason this entry is longer than the diff
  deserves: `git status` is not an instrument for this class of bug.** When
  there is nothing pending to ratchet, a stray lane rewrite produces
  byte-identical content, and `WriteExpectations`' rename-into-place leaves the
  tree *clean*. The arbiter instrumented **inode + mtime** instead, which
  detects the rename even when the bytes do not move:
  - On the OLD (buggy) shape, re-applied deliberately as a sensitivity control,
    `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS=schema=999,instance=0` gave **5 of 6 lanes fresh
    inodes** — `datatypes`, `instance`, `json`, `xpath`, `ber` all rewritten
    behind the FAIL. Only the refusing `schema` lane was spared, and
    `git status` stayed empty throughout.
  - On the FIXED shape, the identical command refuses and **all six lanes keep
    their original inode and mtime** — nothing was even opened, and no stray
    `.expectations-*.tmp` was left behind.
  The control is what makes the evidence load-bearing: it proves the instrument
  is *sensitive*, not merely that the fixed run was quiet. Any future claim of
  the form "the ratchet wrote nothing" should be made this way, and a claim
  resting on `git status` alone should be read as unproven. (Cf. #327's entry,
  which reached the neighbouring conclusion from the other side — "ratchet
  **proven** unchanged by md5 rather than observed unchanged by `git status`".
  Two independent sessions have now hit the same blind spot in the same tool;
  that is a pattern, not a coincidence, and belongs in the next /retro.)
- The arbiter also **re-ran mason's mutation check rather than trusting the
  report**: reverting `ratchetAll` to the per-lane-write shape makes
  `TestRatchetAllWritesNoLaneUnlessEveryLaneMerged` fail with precisely the
  original symptom (`lane instance: got: improving pass / want: improving
  fail`) — the correctly-asserted lane rewritten while its sibling refused.
  `TestRatchetAllReportsEveryRefusal` survives that mutation, as it should: it
  pins a different property (every refusal reported, not just the first), and
  in its scenario both lanes refuse so nothing is written either way. Additive,
  not redundant — worth recording because "two tests, one bug" is usually the
  smell this was checked for and found not to be.
- Surprise — **the bug was found by process, not by testing.** Nothing in the
  tree could have caught it: the per-lane refusal was correct as a
  *classifier*, no score could be lowered through it, and the only observable
  was a dirty tree that in the common case is not even dirty. It surfaced
  because the arbiter, while banking #446, ran a deliberately-wrong assertion
  as a negative control *before* the real run. The lesson generalises past this
  file: a mechanism whose whole job is to refuse is only tested by making it
  refuse, and #576 shipped **unfired** (its own log entry says so in those
  words). The first real firing found a defect in the surrounding driver within
  one session of the mechanism's first use.
- Chain closed: **#576** built the sanctioned-removal mechanism and landed it
  unfired (`fc87875`), **#446** fired it for real and banked 99 deletions
  (`7db4173`), **#581** repaired the driver defect that firing exposed
  (`d439f83`). All three landed the same day; the ordering was not planned that
  far ahead, but the "land the banking machinery before anything is allowed to
  delete a line" discipline is what made the defect cheap — it was found in a
  control run, not in a real bank.
- Friction: essentially none on this issue — one implementation round, one
  arbiter round, accept. The cost was concentrated upstream, in #446's landing,
  which is where the hazard was discovered and where the tree had to be
  restored by hand.
- Footnote on the review itself, disclosed by the arbiter and recorded here so
  anyone re-reading the verdict comment has the full picture: mid-review it
  fumbled a stray `git checkout origin/main -- .`, which clobbered the working
  tree's diff files. It caught this immediately, verified the damage was
  confined to its own session, and restored before producing any of the results
  above. Nothing that landed is affected; the inode/mtime evidence and the
  mutation check were all produced after the restore.
- Next:
  1. **New, from the verdict's non-blocking observation 3** — the *write* phase
     is still not itself transactional: `WriteExpectations` renames each lane's
     file into place separately, so an I/O fault partway through can leave
     earlier lanes written. The arbiter ruled this an acceptable scope boundary
     (a failing disk is a different failure class, and `ratchetAll`'s doc
     comment says so honestly rather than papering over it), but named the

## 2026-08-08 — #574 — conformance: `buildD34Type` resolves a `<restriction base=>` through the schema's OWN declarations instead of the seeded builtin table, so `d3_3_4v18`–`v22`'s one-to-three-step chains build and five of the `datatypes` lane's twenty-two residual failures are DECIDED — and all five **AGREE**, an outcome the issue deliberately did not promise (its Acceptance licensed decided-and-disagree as equally valid); the oracle's grounding upgraded the widening from *permissible* to **spec-MANDATED** — `cos-applicable-facets` (§4.1.5) keys applicability on `{primitive type definition}`, which `st-restrict-facets` clause 2 (§3.16.6.2) holds invariant at every step of an atomic chain, so computing it from the ultimate primitive rather than the immediate base is what the spec requires, not a shortcut that happens to work; and the session's entire cost was a **stale numeral copied out of the issue body into the very comment the issue existed to de-stale** — `0/26426`, already wrong by 65 two commits below this branch's own base — arbiter REJECT on round 1, ACCEPT on round 2, `datatypes` **1151 pass / 22 fail → 1156 pass / 17 fail**

- Shipped on `wip/issue-574` as three commits on top of `fce25f2` (`main` at
  the time = #581's landing) — `b766119` (`conformance: decide d3_3_4v18-v22 via
  a multi-step restriction chain (#574)`, 2 files, +99/−47), `e60d8ea`
  (`conformance: correct two stale comment claims flagged by #574's repair
  round (#574)`, 1 file, +16/−13, comment-only) and `0752026` (`conformance:
  bank the datatypes ratchet for the d3_3_4v18-v22 chain (#574)`, 1 file,
  +5/−5, the arbiter's own ratchet write). Branch total 3 files, +115/−60:
  `conformance/datatypes.go`, `conformance/datatypes_test.go`,
  `conformance/testdata/expectations/datatypes.txt`. Arbiter REJECT round 1
  (https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/574#issuecomment-5228075653),
  ACCEPT round 2, repair round 1 of 1
  (https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/574#issuecomment-5228155485).
- **Ratchet: `datatypes` +5 — 1151 pass / 22 fail → 1156 pass / 17 fail; every
  other lane unchanged (`schema` 9567/5831, `instance` 0/26361, `xpath`/`json`/
  `ber` 0 cases).** The arbiter's figures, copied not recomputed. Five upward
  flips, all `fail -> pass`, all in `PrecisionDecimalTests`:
  `d3_3_4v18/instance/d3_3_4v18i` and the same shape for `v19i`, `v20i`,
  `v21i`, `v22i`. `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` rewrote exactly five lines and touched only
  `expectations/datatypes.txt` — no line deleted, no line lowered, no
  `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS` assertion made or owed (the 99 withheld-as-
  inapplicable are #446's standing baseline, untouched by this branch).
  `d3_3_4v15i` correctly stays `fail` — still an honest gap.
- **The change is one resolution call and one applicability source.**
  `buildD34Type`'s `<restriction base="B">` branch looked `B` up directly in the
  seeded builtin symbol table, so a base naming another type declared in the
  *same schema document* had no component to hand `xsd.NewSimpleType` and the
  whole case declined. `B` now resolves through the existing `d34TypeRef` — the
  same helper a list's `itemType=` and a union's `memberTypes=` entry already
  used, which consults the schema's own declarations FIRST and falls back to a
  seeded, strict-governed builtin — and facet applicability now comes from
  `primitiveOfType(base)` walked to the chain's ultimate primitive rather than
  from the immediate base. **Depth needs no new machinery**: a base not yet
  built simply declines its round and `buildD34Types`' existing fixed point
  retries it, so there is no depth counter, no ordering logic and no cycle check
  (STYLE 5). The facet overlay across the chain stays `xsd.NewSimpleType`'s
  (`st-restrict-facets`/`key-facets-overlay` §3.16.6.4), never re-implemented in
  `conformance/` — the STYLE D3 violation the issue told the arbiter to reject.
  `dt-restriction`/`dt-derived` (§2.4.3) caps no chain depth; the only constraint
  is acyclicity.
- **The widening is general, and the arbiter verified that by sweeping rather
  than reading.** No case ID or fixture type name appears in any non-comment
  line of `datatypes.go` (zero hits for `d3_3_4v*` / `v18`–`v22` outside
  comments). The literal type names in the new test are assertion data, which is
  where they belong. Two latent improvements fell out: the new `primitive == nil`
  guard closes a hole the old line had (it passed a possibly-nil
  `primitiveOfType(builtinType)` straight into `xsd.NewAtomic`), and the
  exported surface is unchanged — zero new exported identifiers across the whole
  branch, as #574's `Surface: none` required.
- **The result beat the issue's own Acceptance, in the direction that costs
  nothing to explain.** #574 was explicit that it *"does not promise five new
  passes"* and that a case which becomes decidable and then disagrees is a
  legitimate, valuable outcome — it converts a reader gap into a measured engine
  gap. The split came back **5 pass / 0 decided-and-disagree**. The `datatypes`
  lane's decline census, the instrument #327 landed one session earlier, moved
  **18 candidates → 13**, with `d3_3_4v18`–`v22` gone from the list and
  `d3_3_4v15` still on it. That is #327's mechanism paying off a second time in
  two sessions: it named these five as harvest candidates, and this is the
  harvest.
- **The reject, and why it is worth more than the diff.** Round 1 was rejected on
  two STYLE T6 comment-accuracy defects, both in prose about staleness:
  1. `datatypes.go:1375` — the rewritten `execPDecimalCase` doc landed
     *"(The INSTANCE lane, 0/26426, is the inert one …)"*. `26426` is not the
     instance lane's size; it is the size the lane had **before `af0b3c3` (#446)
     filtered 65 cases out by `testGroup/@version`**, and `af0b3c3` is the second
     commit below this branch's base. So it was not a figure a future landing
     would invalidate — it was **already wrong the moment it was typed**,
     inherited from #574's own issue body (which says *"The `instance` lane is
     the inert one (0 / 26426)"*), which in turn had copied it out of
     `docs/PLAN.md`'s **correctly stamped** `as of 2026-08-03` sentence. PLAN.md
     is not at fault — its preamble's add-don't-rewrite rule means a stamped
     count is never corrected in place. The defect is the *unstamping*: a dated
     snapshot re-published as an undated present-tense claim in a code comment.
  2. `datatypes.go:1475-1477` — `buildD34Types`' doc comment, untouched by the
     diff and thirty lines above the changed code, still said the cohort cannot
     back *"anything but a single-step restriction of a seeded builtin"*. This
     commit is precisely what falsifies that. Five stale sites were swept; **this
     was the sixth, and it was the one nearest the change.**
- **Decision of record, made by the arbiter and worth quoting because it will
  recur: for a lane count in a code comment, prefer QUALITATIVE prose over a
  dated numeral.** Mason had already backed the `datatypes` numbers out in favour
  of *"the residual failures number in the tens against over a thousand passes"*
  and asked whether that met T6. Ruling: yes, and it was the right call — the
  claim the comment must carry is qualitative (*this lane is dense, so a decline
  here costs a real point, unlike the inert instance lane*), and the prose
  survives every future banking including this one (post-bank 17/1156 is still
  "in the tens", still "over a thousand"). A dated snapshot would have been
  defensible under the PLAN.md convention but buys nothing and adds a maintenance
  obligation. What was **not** acceptable was the two halves of one parenthetical
  in different registers — qualitative for `datatypes`, a bare wrong integer for
  `instance`. The repair dropped the numeral entirely: *"(The INSTANCE lane,
  which scores zero, is the actually-inert one …)"*.
- **The repair was proven comment-only by AST-diff, not by inspection.** Every
  changed line in `b766119..e60d8ea` matches `^[+-]\s*//`, and — the stronger
  check — both revisions parsed with `go/parser` (comments dropped) and printed
  render **identically**, so the compiled program at `e60d8ea` is byte-identical
  to `b766119`. The repair also folded in the two advisory (non-blocking) sites
  from the same defect family, and the arbiter confirmed both were genuinely
  stale rather than taking the report's word: `d34TypeRef`'s contract enumeration
  now names three callers (`itemType=`, `memberTypes=` entry, `base=`) — checked
  against the call site, not the comment claiming it — and the cohort's
  package-doc shape list now reads *"restrictions of those restrictions (v18 and
  v19–v22, chains one to three steps deep)"*, with the depth claim checked
  against the fixtures: `v18` runs builtin → `decTFDigits` → `decTFDigitsDerived`
  → `elEnumerationB`'s inline type (3), and `v19`–`v22` run `decDigits` →
  `decDigits{Min,Max}{Inclusive,Exclusive}` → the four `dec*_*` leaves (3), with
  1 the shallowest. "One to three" is exact in both directions.
- Surprise — **the correction the issue was filed to make was the one the commit
  got wrong.** #574's last Acceptance bullet exists *because* `execPDecimalCase`
  mislabelled these gaps as living in "the inert instance lane"; the fix for that
  mislabel is what shipped a wrong instance-lane number. The failure is the exact
  shape #315 settled into `docs/WORKFLOW.md` as a filing-discipline class (a
  stale premise carried out of an issue body without re-verification), and it is
  now an instance of that class **found inside the sweep meant to eliminate the
  class**. Cheap to fix, and the qualitative-prose ruling above is the durable
  form of the fix.
- Surprise, minor — **`readD34Case`'s comment at `datatypes.go:3002` was correctly
  left alone** and the arbiter said so on the record. It reads that `v19`–`v22`'s
  *"named types are still declared and so still reach the build pass"*, which is
  still true after the widening. A stale-doc sweep that touches an accurate
  neighbouring comment is its own defect; recording the non-edit keeps a later
  reader from mistaking it for an oversight.
- The new test earns its place under both polarities. `TestDatatypesD34Cohort`
  moves `v18`/`v19`–`v22` out of the must-DECLINE loop into the must-PASS loop (a
  straight polarity flip that fails on revert), and adds a chain-WALK assertion on
  `v22`'s three-step `decMaxExclusive_MinInclusive`: its `{base type definition}`
  must be the declared intermediate `d34-decDigitsMaxExclusive` (fails if base
  resolution regresses to builtin-only) and its `{primitive type definition}` must
  be `precisionDecimal` (fails if the base is flattened to the primitive). Two
  distinct regressions, two distinct failing assertions. `d3_3_4v15` is still
  asserted declined under BOTH polarities, so the honest-gap convention survives.
- Friction: **one repair round, entirely comment-accuracy, zero code churn** — the
  implementation was accepted intact on round 1 and never touched again. The only
  other friction was infrastructural and cost nothing durable: `gh issue view`
  hit the shared GraphQL rate limit mid-session, and the thread had to be read
  through the REST endpoint (`gh api repos/kud360/goxsd8/issues/574/comments`)
  instead. Non-blocking, but the REST path is the one to reach for first when a
  session needs a whole thread. One cosmetic residue was disclosed and explicitly
  not made a condition of the accept: `d34TypeRef`'s reflowed doc leaves a short
  ragged line mid-paragraph (`gofmt` does not reflow comments, and no STYLE rule
  speaks to it).
- Next:

- **Ratchet, copied from the verdicts, not recomputed — `unchanged` BOTH times.**
  Round 1 at `23ca948`: *"RATCHET: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to
  bank"*; `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run, `git status --porcelain --
  conformance/testdata/expectations/` immediately after **empty**; discovery
  **41858 cases, 0 withheld as inapplicable**, schema lane **15432 cases / 4103
  declined**, no `regressed` and no `improved, not yet banked` line; gate green
  (`golangci-lint run` → **0 issues**). Merged-tree re-verification at `6c0034b`
  (https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/392#issuecomment-5228158375): read-only
  conformance PASS with discovery **41759 cases across 6 lanes, 99 withheld as
  inapplicable (schema 15398, instance 26361, datatypes 1173)**, no regressed, no

  with `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS` unset is the correct assertion rather than a
  shortcut around one. This lands as pure structural-test proof, exactly as the
  issue's Notes forecast.
- **THE ENTRY'S POINT — what landing someone else's branch has to look like.**
  The orchestrator did not run this session's ground/implement/judge steps; it
  picked the branch up from a stop-hook notice about unpushed commits. What it did
  itself: pushed the three unpushed commits, read the full arc off the issue thread
  (that thread is why the hand-off was recoverable at all — CLAUDE.md's
  "issues are the cross-session channel" earning its keep), merged `origin/main`
  in, ran the plain gate on the merged tree, and then **delegated the ratchet
  re-verification back to the arbiter** rather than running `GOXSD_RATCHET=1`
  itself, because that variable is arbiter-only and an orchestrator in a hurry is
  exactly the actor the restriction exists to stop. The discipline worth copying is
  the next part: **every load-bearing claim in the hand-off brief was checked
  against the diff and the thread, and three were wrong** —
  1. the brief said `parser/produce_complex.go` had "3 functions deleted, 1
     renamed, 2 call sites rewired". Three producer methods were indeed deleted
     (`extensionContentType`, `extensionParticle`, `allGroupOf`), but **nothing was
     renamed and there is one rewired call site**: mason's design planned
     `allGroupOf` → `AllGroupOf` to satisfy an `AllGroupResolver` interface, and
     warden's T5 finding **deleted that interface** in favour of a plain func
     parameter, so the landed code passes the pre-existing `p.resolveModelGroup`
     directly (`produce_complex.go:470`) and the method that would have been
     renamed no longer exists. The brief was quoting the DESIGN comment, which the
     review superseded.
  2. the file list omitted four touched files (`xsd/complextype.go`, `xsd/doc.go`,
     `parser/produce.go`, `xsd/extensioncontenttype_test.go`) — 11 files, not 7.
  3. the brief hedged the new filenames ("or similar — check actual filenames").
     Both landed exactly as designed; it is the design's *function* names that
     drifted (`collapsedIntermediate` → `collapsedExtension`, `chainToAnyType` →
     `baseChainToAnyType`, `recoverEffectiveContent` →
     `recoverExtensionStepContent`), which is the thing a later reader grepping
     that DESIGN comment will actually trip over.
  None of these changed the verdict. That is the point: the check was cheap, it was
  run anyway, and it is the only reason this entry describes the tree rather than
  the plan.
- **The layering question the issue was filed to answer got answered: the merge
  MOVES to `xsd`, and `parser` calls in.** §3.4.2.3.3 clause 4.2 existed only as
  producer methods, `xsd` cannot import `parser` (cycle), and re-deriving it inside
  `xsd` would be STYLE T4 — one rule, two encodings. The resolution is dependency
  inversion: the rule lives in `xsd` beside the §3.4.2.4 clause 3 and §3.4.2.5
  clause 2 folds that were already there, and the one package-specific capability
  (`<group ref>` resolution) is a func parameter. **The price is recorded rather
  than hidden**: exporting exactly one name means `parser` keeps its OWN clause
  **4.1** encoding (`produce_complex.go:494-513`), and that function's doc comment
  says so at the site — *"exporting a SECOND name … a change to 4.1.1 or 4.1.2 is
  a change to both sites."* The arbiter accepted the duplication explicitly as
  "the direct consequence of that one-name ruling". A knowingly-documented second
  encoding with the obligation written where the next editor will read it is a
  different object from a T4 violation, and this is the shape to point at next time
  the trade comes up.
- **Warden's pre-flight was worth its round — five required changes, all landed**,
  and the sharpest was a **silent false accept on the one shape the clause exists
  for**: for `A(@x optional) ←restr← R(prohibits @x) ←ext← E(re-declares @x)`, both
  steps are individually legal and folded `E` has no duplicate, but *M* carries two
  `@x` — the Note's own "removed by a restriction … added back by an extension" —
  and `findAttributeUse` returns the FIRST match, so the check would have passed.
  The other four: document the positional-recovery invariant that couples
  `ownAttributeUses` to `inheritAttributeUses` and pin it with a 4-step
  `ext-restr-ext` test (`TestOwnAttributeUsesMixedChain`); build *M* only through
  `newCollapsedExtension` → the validating `newComplexType`, never a literal, and
  never register it in `s.types` (there is a test asserting it did not leak);
  never surface `checkDerivationOKRestriction`'s raw error, since it carries
  `ruleDerivationOKRestriction` and names a synthetic type the user never wrote —
  all three sites re-charge `ruleCosCTExtends` at `t.Loc()` with no `%w`, so
  `RuleOf` cannot reach the wrong rule; and the wildcard direction fix, which is
  the one that mattered most — warden caught that reading the step's own wildcard
  off *T* **under**-approximates for a chain topped by a restriction (§3.4.2.5
  clause 2.1), i.e. fail-CLOSED, i.e. the false reject the issue rules out. The
  landed recipe unions the FOLDED values instead, and the GAP names all three
  readers with each one's direction — including the correction that
  `{process contents}` is **unaffected** rather than fail-open.

     [MS-Element2006-07-15/elemZ015/schema/elemZ015]`, because
     `sameTypeDefinition` reports two anonymous types as distinct, so a *T*
     holding an inline `<complexType>` cannot restrict its own copy. Licensed by

  3. **`TestCosCTExtendsClause16`'s narrowed fixture.** The arbiter walked the

- **The check, and why its two bounds are measured rather than chosen.** A break
  is ragged when it falls `shortSlack` (20) columns short of the paragraph's own
  wrap width AND the next line's first word would have fitted — both halves
  required, so a break placed before an unpullable 40-column identifier is not
  reported. A line is over-long when it stands `longSlack` (12) columns clear of
  every other line in its paragraph and past `maxFillWidth` (88), the widest width
  any paragraph in this repo is filled to. The commit message records the
  calibration against this tree: at 10 columns the report is dominated by breaks a
  human placed on purpose. Every carve-out is pinned by its own test — list items
  and their hanging continuations, verbatim (4-column indented) blocks, `#`
  headings but *not* `#329`-style issue references, directives, markdown table
  rows, Example expected-output blocks, comments sharing a line with code,
  generated files, paragraphs never filled to a width at all, and a paragraph's
  own last line (which is short by right, not by neglect).
- **The one unswept site is deferred by a mechanism that cannot outlive its
  owner.** `value/list.go:68` belongs to open issue #564, whose branch is already
  carrying that paragraph, so sweeping it here would have manufactured a conflict.
  The waiver keys on the line's **exact text** rather than its number (numbers
  drift under every landing), names #564, and — the part that makes it safe —
  `staleWaivers` reports and **fails the gate** the moment that line stops being
  ragged, so the waiver has to be deleted by whatever lands #564. The tool's own
  doc states the analogy it is copying: this is the discipline STYLE P3 puts on
  `GAP(` markers.
- **The reject was a silent-data-loss landmine, and its value is entirely
  prospective.** `go/ast` collects `//` lines, a whole-line `/* */` block, and
  more `//` lines into ONE `CommentGroup`. The non-`//` entry was skipped with a
  bare `continue`, so the accumulator's run stayed contiguous while its **source
  lines no longer were**, and a later paragraph's splice range spanned the block
  comment's line. `-fix` overwrites every line it spans. The block comment would
  have been deleted with no diagnostic. It **never fired on any of the 134 real
  sweep sites** — this repo has no whole-line block comments — and the arbiter
  rejected anyway, correctly: the tool is now a mandatory gate step that every
  future mason runs with `-fix` on a tree they are about to commit, which is the
  single worst place in the repo for an undiagnosed line-deleting bug.
- **The repair's sharpest fact is that the arbiter's OWN round-1 reasoning was
  wrong, and mason's wider fix was right.** There are two skip sites, not one: the
  flagged `!strings.HasPrefix(c.Text, "//")`, and `strings.TrimSpace(raw) !=
  c.Text` — a comment sharing its line with code — which round 1 had explicitly
  reasoned through and cleared. It is the same class (a line the run cannot carry
  paragraph text on, stepped over instead of ending the run) with the same
  consequence. Mason fixed both, and round 2 independently rebuilt both binaries
  and reproduced defect and fix directly rather than trusting the report. The
  landed shape collapses all three exits onto one rule — `flush()` at both skips
  and at the end of the group, so a run ends at any line it cannot carry text on
  and never at a line's absence.
- **The new test fails under three independent mutations, including the vacuity
  one.** `TestFixKeepsABlockCommentInsideItsGroup` builds a fixture with a ragged
  paragraph on each side of `/* keep me */` so `-fix` splices on both sides, then
  asserts (1) the file actually changed — `if string(fixed) == src { t.Fatal }`,
  so the test cannot pass by the fixture ceasing to be reflowable, the failure
  mode a survival assertion invites; (2) the block comment survives on exactly ONE
  whole line, byte-identical; and (3) the defect stated where `-fix` actually
  reads from — `comments()` returns exactly 2 paragraphs and neither one's
  `[first,last]` span contains the block comment's line. Assertion 3 is the
  structural statement; 2 is the observable; 1 is the guard on both.
- **One opportunistic non-blocking finding was folded in rather than deferred.**
  Waiver path matching was `strings.HasSuffix(slash, w.file)`, which lets a waiver
  keyed `value/list.go` cover `xvalue/list.go`. It is now `covers()`: exact match
  or a `/`-boundary suffix. Cheap, in the same file, in the same round — the right
  call, and the arbiter had flagged it as advisory precisely so it would not cost
  a third round if declined.
- **Independent re-measurement done for this entry, because the sweep figure is
  the one number the session rests on.** Built the round-1 binary (`4be512a`) and
  the round-2 binary (`2ad2c9f`) and ran both against the branch base `fce25f2`:
  both report **134 ragged lines across 33 files**, and the two reports are
  **byte-identical**. That settles a question the reject raises on its own — the
  paragraph-closing fix changes how runs are split, so it *could* have changed the
  census under the 134 sites the sweep already rewrote — and the answer is that it
  did not: the repair is purely splice-safety, and mason's figure reconciles
  exactly with the tool's own summary line. The landing tip reports **zero**
  findings (`go tool commentwrap ./...`, exit 0).

  that flips passing instance validations to fail for every element typed by a
  redefined complex type — inside the exact cohort this issue targets;
  (b) `derivationAdmitsSubstitution` returning TRUE at a zero base is
  **fail-OPEN**, an accept, not a reject — the same "conservative fallback"
  premise, false in the other direction; (c) `checkComplexBaseAcyclic` must
  descend the new anonymous arm **or a crafted schema hangs** — `T base="U"`,
  `U base="T"`, D1 redefines `T`, and the fold's `j != i` self-edge guard cannot
  see across the inline hop. Both mason and the arbiter reproduced (c) as a
  genuine `fatal error: stack overflow` cycling `foldTypeAttributeUses →
  baseAttributeUses → foldComponentAttributeUses`, and the arbiter re-ran it
  **after** the repair changed the memo's shape, so the guarantee is pinned
  against the landed code and not against the judged one.
- **Decision — `complexTypeIdentity` becomes a real four-arm unexported sealed
  sum, because the derived predicate it replaced was a representable illegal
  state (STYLE T1).** The old struct derived `anonymous()` from owner presence;
  a redefining type is NAMED *and* carries a minted owner, so `anonymous()`
  answered true for it and `scopeParent()` would have emitted
  `AnonymousComplexTypeScopeParent` for a named top-level type — a wrong
  `{scope}.{parent}` for every local element it declares. Arms:
  `namedComplexType{name}` / `elementOwnedComplexType{owner}` /
  `redefiningComplexType{name, owner}` / `redefineOriginalComplexType{owner}`,
  marker-sealed, exhaustively switched in `topLevelComplexTypeName`,
  `scopeParentOf`, `attributeScopeParentOf`, `newComplexType`. **The three
  "carries neither a name nor an owner" panics are deleted with the zero value
  they guarded** — the only surviving occurrence of that string is the doc
  explaining their removal.
- **Decision — the identity is chosen in `buildComplexType`, not in
  `produceRedefinition`.** `prescanRedefine` registers the redefining
  declaration under its own name, so a reference from EITHER document arrives
  through `resolveBaseType` → `buildComplexType`. Deciding the arm there is what
  makes every route land on one memo entry — which is what makes src-expredef's
  own rationale sentence actually hold ("references … in both the `<redefine>`ing
  and `<redefine>`d schema documents ·resolve· to the redefined component").
  Deciding it at `produceRedefinition` alone would have built a SECOND,
  self-based component for a D2-side reference. `resolveBaseType` now returns
  `(component, slot, error)` — **one decision fixing both**, so a caller cannot
  pair a component with a slot that does not name it.
- **Decision — no new resolver; `typeOf` MOVES to `typedefinition.go` and serves
  every slot.** The pre-flight had proposed a `baseTypeDefinition(c)` helper; the
  warden ruled it a second encoding of `(*Schema).typeOf`, which already follows
  both arms with the same nil semantics (STYLE T4). Mason took the optional half
  too and moved `typeOf` out of `defaultbinding.go` to sit beside the sum it
  reads, **taking the slot rather than the owning component** so it can never
  become arm-meaning-dependent on the caller's origin. `baseComplexType` is now a
  four-line complex-only narrowing over it.
- **Decision — the round-1 repair RE-SEATS the folded value; it does not add a
  second reader.** The arbiter left the choice open (re-seat, or route the two
  restriction readers to the value some other way). Direction (2) would have put
  the folded property in two encodings — the stored one and a read-site
  recomputation — which is exactly what `attributeusefold.go`'s own header
  records **#401** as having removed (STYLE D3/T4). So `baseAttributeUses` and
  `baseAttributeWildcard` now return the `{base type definition}` **slot to store**
  alongside the folded value (a no-op for every arm but the owned inline one),
  and both folds memoise the folded **component** rather than the bare property
  (`uses [][]AttributeUse` → `types []ComplexType`), so the storeback writes
  owner and owned base together. `storeFoldedAttributeWildcards` also stopped
  skipping a component whose own folded wildcard is ·absent· — that skip dropped
  the re-seat on a real shape (a restriction declaring no wildcard of its own but
  declaring a use the base admits **only** through its inherited one), and the
  arbiter singled that change out as the one it was most inclined to suspect as
  unmotivated and confirmed by mutation that it is load-bearing.
- **Decision — ONE `GAP(xsd)` marker for the deferral, not three.** The
  Phase-D hole and the two fold-storeback holes were one root cause (an anonymous
  component reachable only through an owning slot), so three markers would be
  three encodings of one fact. `parser/doc.go`'s composition-gaps bullet is
  deleted as the acceptance asked, replaced by a prose cross-reference. After the
  repair the marker survives deliberately — the storeback half is CLOSED, the
  Phase-D-verdict half and the element/attribute-owned types are real residual
  scope, and **#584** is their open owner and is now named in the text (STYLE P3).
- **Decision — the absent base stays representable (warden Q4).** Closing it
  (rejecting an absent base at the constructor) is a behaviour change with its
  own independent ratchet risk; folding it into a surface change would have
  entangled two things. `Base()`'s doc now says plainly that `nil` is
  representable, means ·absent·, and that `ct-props-correct` clause 1's
  Required-ness is **not** enforced at construction.
- **The durable finding — a deferred-scope claim's DIRECTION must be verified
  reader-by-reader, never asserted from the fold's general shape.** This is the
  whole of the round-1 rejection and it belongs in the recurring family this log
  has now flagged five times: **#336** (prose about its own completeness wrong in
  the count — three fail-open clauses, not one), **#310** (a docstring promising
  "no site can drift back … unnoticed" over a table organised per rule-family
  instead of per SITE — a STYLE T6 false guarantee), **#538** (the same
  `cos-ct-extends` inventory correcting itself a second time), **#501** (three
  fresh STYLE P3a instances created by the round that existed to discharge two,
  plus a false idempotence lemma its own file refuted two paragraphs above).
  **#505 is the sharpest instance yet and differs from all four in kind**: the
  earlier ones were prose that *under-described* what the code checks, and the
  harm was an unenumerated consumer or an undercount. Here the direction claim
  was **INVERTED** — "it UNDER-rejects in every case … nothing here can fabricate
  an 'invalid'" — and the inversion concealed a **live false-reject on an
  ordinary schema**. The mechanism generalises: a fold's *general* shape ("a base
  with fewer uses imposes fewer obligations") is a statement about the property,
  and the direction is a statement about its READERS, which the property's shape
  does not determine. `checkRestrictionAttributes`,
  `checkRestrictionRequiredAttributes` and `checkRestrictionAttributeWildcard`
  all charge on what the base **reports**, not on what it omits, so
  under-reporting makes each of them reject. **The arbiter's round-1 finding
  named two of the three**; `checkRestrictionRequiredAttributes` came out of the
  repair's own proper enumeration, and the arbiter's shape **C** exists
  precisely to exercise it — which is itself the argument for enumerating rather
  than sampling. STYLE P3a's "enumerate the readers
  by identifier and state each one's direction" is not a documentation nicety;
  it is the only step at which this class is catchable, because — as the arbiter
  put it — the condition it was written for is precisely one **neither the gate
  nor the ratchet can see**. Worth a `/retro` look at whether the *implementation*
  step (`.claude/agents/mason.md`) should require the enumeration at the moment a
  `GAP` marker is written, rather than leaving it to be caught at verdict.

## 2026-08-08 — #468 — xsd: an `<all>` group finally gets its own EXIT state — `addAll` stops returning the unconditional union of its members' ·last· positions (the claim that the group may end after ANY member) and transcribes `all(P1 … Pn) ≈ (P1|…|Pn)* · (P1′|…|Pn′)` instead, a **primed replay** of every member that carries the ·last· set an enclosing sequence appends its successor onto, so `sequence(all(a,b), a)` stops false-rejecting on `cos-nonambig`; two of the issue's own prescriptions were **spec-WRONG and both were caught before they could land** — the oracle killed the body's design sketch (gate a member's exit on every OTHER member being ·emptiable·) by showing it degenerates to an **empty exit set** with 2+ mandatory members, and mason then contradicted **Acceptance item 3 outright**, pinning `sequence(all(a,b?), a)` ACCEPTED where the issue demanded a reject, on the ground that a successor's *liveness* in the exit state is not ·compete· (§3.8.4.2 needs a rival path whose last item is the `<all>`'s own `a`, and that member's {max occurs} is 1) — a deviation the **arbiter re-derived from §3.8.4.1.1's path rule rather than from mason's summary**, and the genuine competition of that shape (`sequence(all(a,b?), b)`, the successor colliding with the EMPTIABLE member) is pinned as the reject instead; the fix also kills a false **ACCEPT** nobody had filed (`sequence(all(seq(x,y?), z), y)`), arbiter ACCEPT on round 1, ratchet **unchanged and MEASURED** — but the entry's sharpest fact is procedural: the merge commit at the branch tip says *"Merge origin/main into wip/issue-468"* and **merged a stale `origin/main` (#392) instead of its tip**, so the arbiter's own named land requirement — absorb `1b41ad5` (#329) and re-run the gate *including* `go tool commentwrap` — is **undischarged at `718a2c7`**, and the tree about to be PR'd still has no `tools/commentwrap`, no tool-block entry for it, and a CLAUDE.md whose Commands block does not name gate part 3

- Shipped on `wip/issue-468`, merge-base **`fb547c2`**, as one implementation
  commit **`a54c608`** (`xsd: give an <all> group its own exit state so a
  successor stops competing with a member still owed (#468)`,

  cos-group-emptiable (§3.9.6.3)`, `Ratchet: unchanged`) — **3 files,

  `xsd/particleattribution.go` (+127/−34) carries the whole construction: a new
  unexported `allFragment` struct (`first`/`last`/`residual`/`emptiable`) and
  `addAllMembers`, which `addAll` now runs **twice** over the same members with
  `b.nextParticleID` rewound between passes, so `Pi′` replays `Pi`'s particle
  identifier exactly as `addParticle` replays identifiers across the copies of an
  unfolded numeric occurrence range. The star pass keeps the ·first· set and the
  loop-back byte-for-byte; the primed pass supplies the returned ·last·.
  `xsd/contentrestricts.go` (+19/−8) doubles `modelGroupPositions` for
  `CompositorAll` and corrects its §3.4.6.3 all-group-leniency prose.
  `xsd/particleattribution_test.go` is **purely additive** (+108, one hunk at
  `:432`, zero deletions) — which is how Acceptance item 2 is discharged
  structurally rather than by assertion.
  **Ratchet: unchanged, measured** — `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run by the arbiter,
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` empty
  immediately after, nothing to bank; **41759 cases / 6 lanes, 99 withheld as
  inapplicable**, 0 improved / 0 regressed / 0 vanished, per lane
  `datatypes 1173`, `schema 15398`, `instance 26361`, `xpath/json/ber 0`. Flat
  is the *expected* result and the issue said so in advance: `cos-all-limited`
  clause 1 (§3.8.6.2) keeps this shape out of every schema document, so no suite
  case can reach it, and the defect is live only through the exported `xsd`

- **`residual` is the idea, and it is the thing the issue's sketch could not
  express.** The two meanings the old single `last` collapsed were "more of this
  group may follow here" (the loop-back) and "this group may end here" (what an
  enclosing sequence needs); splitting them is only half the fix, because the
  second one is a fact about the **SUBSET of members taken so far**, and with *k*
  non-emptiable members there are *k* legal orders each ending on a different
  member — no per-member flag can carry that. The primed alternation *is* that
  state: reaching it is taking one more member, and beside the successor only
  `residual` is live there — an ·emptiable· member's own ·first· set (it was
  never taken and may still start) plus every member's own continuation past the
  point it is satisfied but not exhausted (`maxOccurs > 1` on `<all>` children is
  legal in 1.1, Appendix G.1.4). Snapshotted during the **star** pass, before
  `addAll` draws any group-level edge, so it holds each member's own
  continuations and nothing the group adds around them.
- Decision — **`modelGroupPositions` doubles for `CompositorAll`, and the
  arbiter treated that as the flagged risk rather than bookkeeping.** The
  saturation guard moved to `total > maxContentPositions/copies` with a
  `copies * total` return, which under floor division cannot exceed the ceiling
  and cannot overflow; `copies = 1` is byte-equivalent to the old path. The
  arbiter did not take the equality on argument — it wrote a scratch test
  comparing `modelGroupPositions(g)` against `len(b.positions)` after
  `addModelGroup` under `unfoldExactly` over `all(a,b)`, `all(a,b,c)`,
  `all(a{1,3},b)`, `sequence(all(a,b), c)`, `all(all(a,b), c)` and
  `choice(all(a,b), c)`, exact in every case **including the nested `<all>` where
  the factor compounds per level**. This is the "count the automaton's size
  rather than estimate it" invariant staying true across a construction change.
- Decision — **no `GAP(xsd)` marker is owed, and that was argued rather than
  assumed.** Acceptance item 4 demanded that any residual approximation carry a
  P3a-compliant marker. The arbiter checked each `residual` entry against a
  reachable state and found the exit state **exact, not lenient**, so there is no
  residual incompleteness for a marker to track; what remains is the pre-existing
  star superset, which lands on `contentrestricts.go`'s §3.4.6.3 all-group
  allowance that already records why it carries none. The over-claim item 4 was
  filed over is gone the right way: `addAll`'s "exactly equivalent" claim is now
  scoped to **within the star** and to the loop-back, which is where it was ever
  true (STYLE P2/T6).
- **Surprise 1 — the issue body's own design sketch was spec-wrong, and the
  oracle killed it before a line was written.** Note 4 prescribed returning only
  those `p ∈ M.last` for which every member other than *M* is ·emptiable·, hedged
  as "a starting point, NOT a ruling". The grounding ruled it wrong from
  §3.8.4.1.3's `L(M) = S1 × … × Sn` and `cos-group-emptiable` (§3.9.6.3):
  with 2+ non-emptiable members it returns the empty set, erasing *k* real exit
  points. It also refused to over-attribute the remedy — Appendix J is subset-
  construction-based *by construction*, but it is explicitly non-normative
  guidance ("without claiming to be complete"), so subset state is required while
  its **minimal representation is an implementation choice the spec does not
  constrain**, and the grounding said to say so rather than attribute a data
  structure to Appendix J. The hedge in the issue body is what made this cheap;
  a sketch stated as a ruling would have been implemented.
- **Surprise 2 — an Acceptance criterion was corrected in flight, and verified
  twice INDEPENDENTLY.** Item 3 demanded `sequence(all(a, b?), a)` "must still be
  rejected", reasoning that b's emptiability lets the group end after `a` so the
  successor is genuinely live there. Mason implemented and pinned the **opposite**
  (`TestUPAAllGroupNonEmptiableMemberBesideEmptiableOnePasses`) and said so in the
  commit message rather than quietly diverging. The arbiter did not accept the
  argument as given — it re-derived from §3.8.4.1.1's sequence path rule
  (`Si ∈ L(Pi)` for `0 < i < j`, so a path ending in the successor has a prefix
  that is a **complete** path of the `<all>`, and every complete path of
  `all(a, b?)` already contains the `a` particle once, `{max occurs} = 1`) and
  ruled the issue's criterion spec-wrong: **liveness is not competition**, which
  additionally needs the rival path, and `P_a` is spent. The genuine competition
  of that shape is `sequence(all(a, b?), b)` — successor against the **emptiable**
  member — pinned as the reject. This is the good version of a deviation: argued
  in the commit message, reproduced by the judge from spec text, and the wrong
  criterion named on the thread rather than silently dropped.
- **Surprise 3 — the fix corrects a false ACCEPT nobody filed.**
  `sequence(all(seq(x,y?), z), y)` was **wrongly accepted** before this change and
  is now correctly rejected (`<x/><z/><y/>` has `[x, z, succ.y]` and

  exit-state logic right, and both were found by the arbiter checking the

- **The commentwrap gate step is REAL, not a phantom — and this is worth
  recording because CLAUDE.md warns hardest about the opposite.** The Commands

     `cos-all-limited` **clause 2** forbids a non-`all` model group as an `<all>`
     member, "so no conforming schema reaches it". But

     **nowhere**: the only enforcement is clause 1 at
     `parser/produce_complex.go:936`, on the XML spelling, and `:1076` states
     outright that cos-all-limited is not charged at the definition site — which
     is the whole subject of open issue **#469**. The unprobed question is whether
     the exported `xsd` constructors reach that shape, i.e. **the same door this
     entire issue exists because of** (Note 5: the constructors bypass the
     parser's charge, which is what makes the `<all>` defect live rather than a
     curiosity). Stated as a question, not a claim — nobody has built the probe.
     It belongs on #469.
  5. **New — Note 6's reachability probe is explicitly deferred and the hand-off
     has not been made.** The issue asked whether a **second** extension of a
     type whose §3.4.2.3.3 clause 4.2.3.3 synthesized `sequence(base particle,
     effective content)` already holds an `<all>` nests it and supplies a
     successor — i.e. whether this defect's shape is reachable from an ordinary
     schema document with no `<group ref>` at all — and said to report the answer
     on the thread "because it raises the priority of this issue and changes what
     **#469** may safely charge". The arbiter deferred it with reasons ("a 'probe
     it if you can', not an acceptance item") and routed it to #469 — but **no
     comment naming it has been posted on #469**. A reasoned deferral that never
     reaches the receiving thread is indistinguishable from a leak two weeks
     later; post it.
  6. **[carried, undischarged]** every `Next` item carried by the 2026-08-08 #392
     entry above — #396's now-moot item 4, the unmade 139-gap measurement on

  shape" was CHECKED, and this is the difference between an honest `unchanged`
  and a missed harvest.** Surveying every `<xs:override>` under
  `testdata/xsdtests/saxonData/Override/`, exactly one case has two `<xs:override>`
  elements naming the same `schemaLocation` — **`over022.bad.xsd`** (both →
  `over019a.xsd`) — and it is the **NEGATIVE** shape, not this issue's positive
  one: the two substitute `type="xs:date"` and `type="xs:time"`, i.e. the same
  document overridden two *different* ways, which §4.2.5 says must yield duplicate
  conflicting components. Banked `pass` at `schema.txt:14506`, still `pass`. No

- **The design decision the issue was filed to settle came out the opposite way
  from how the issue framed it, and the grounding is why.** The body's Spec
  section leads with `fn:deep-equal` and the Notes call the equivalence test "the
  design decision"; the oracle read both §4.2.5 notes and found they are about
  different questions. The deep-equal sentence is the *idempotence/termination*
  note ("either ... a comparator such as the [XPath 2.0] `fn:deep-equal`
  function, or by observing the conditions that cause *override*(*E*, *D*) to be
  idempotent"), explicitly a menu; the "multiple equivalent overrides" note cites
  **no comparator at all** and says the fallback correctness path is to run the
  construction and establish "identity component by component", with
  pre-deduplication "allowed, indeed encouraged" — an optimization, not a
  requirement. So no algorithm is mandated, the only *forbidden* direction is
  named ("if the same schema document [is] overridden twice in different ways,
  then the resulting schema will have duplicate and conflicting versions of some
  components"), and residual under-collapsing is textually the baseline. That
  reframing is what licensed a structural serialization rather than a hunt for a
  data model to run `fn:deep-equal` on — goxsd8 has none (M6/M7) — and it is also
  what licensed the strengthening below.

  believing the report.** Mason serialized the in-scope namespace bindings
  (default via `lookupPrefix("")`, prefixed via the pre-sorted `inScopePrefixes()`)
  at **every** element, beyond the issue's name+attributes+children guidance,
  because an attribute value may be a QName whose meaning is the binding its
  prefix holds where it occurs (Datatypes §3.3.18) — two overrides both reading
  `type="p:date"` with `p` bound differently are two different transformations,
  and collapsing them is precisely the one direction the grounding forbids. Per
  element, not once per entry, so a child that declares its own binding is not
  mistaken for one that inherits. The arbiter deleted the six binding lines and
  re-ran: `TestParseOverrideEquivalentTextDifferentBindingsLoadsTwice` fails
  (*"Parse succeeded, want a rejection: p:date names {urn:a}date on one side and
  xs:date on the other"*), so the serialization is that test's only discriminator.

  restored `Loc()`-keying (the positive test fails with the exact
  `sch-props-correct` diagnostic the issue body predicts). Three new tests, three
  distinct failure modes — none of them vacuous.

  description.** `writeToken` is a netstring (`writeCount` → `strconv.Itoa(len) +

  no name, attribute value or run of character data can forge a separator. That is
  the property the whole change rests on — a serialization that can be forged is
  an over-collapse engine — and it was checked by reading the code.

## 2026-08-09 — #430 — xsd: cvc-complex-type clause **2.2** stops being charged over names clause **2.1** already owns — `checkRestrictionAttributeWildcard` rendered c-avaw as a whole-record `cos-ns-subset` test, and `cos-ns-subset` knows nothing of `{attribute uses}`, so a QName in B's `{disallowed names}` that BOTH types govern with an attribute use was tested against T's wildcard and **FALSE-REJECTED a spec-valid schema** (base declares `<xs:attribute name="foo"/>` beside `<anyAttribute namespace="##any" notQName="foo"/>`; a restriction inherits the `foo` use per §3.4.2.4 clause 3.2 and opens its own wildcard to bare `##any`); the fix is a call-site gate, `sharedAttributeUseNames` + `NamespaceConstraint.withoutDisallowedNames`, and the load-bearing detail the oracle supplied is that the exempt set is the **INTERSECTION** of the two materialised use sets and can be neither side alone nor the union — a use only T holds still needs B's own clause 2.2 to admit the name, so the asymmetric shape stays charged; arbiter ACCEPT on **round 1**, `Ratchet: unchanged`, **Surface: none** (both new identifiers unexported, `go doc -all` byte-identical to `main`), two non-blocking advisories deferred; and the session's procedural shape is a **user-ordered hold** — landing was blocked behind #379 at the user's instruction until that branch merged, after which `origin/main` came in as a **path-disjoint** merge

- Shipped on `wip/issue-430`, pre-merge base **`51dc129`** (#468's landing), as
  one implementation commit **`892ad15`** (`xsd: exempt names an {attribute use}
  claims on both sides from the c-avaw wildcard subset (#430)`, `Spec:
  cvc-complex-type clause 2 (c-aam), 2.1 (c-ctma), 2.2 (c-avaw),
  derivation-ok-restriction clause 3 (c-ran), cos-ns-subset, dcl.ctd.attuses
  clause 3.2`, `Ratchet: unchanged`) plus one merge **`04e66fc`** (parents
  `892ad15` + `e0285cf`, absorbing #379). Landing diff `git diff
  origin/main...HEAD --stat` is **3 files, +188/−31**: `xsd/complexderivation.go`
  (the `sharedAttributeUseNames` helper, the filtered call site, and the
  `GAP(xsd)` block replaced by the corrected algorithm's documentation),
  `xsd/namespaceconstraint.go` (+32, `withoutDisallowedNames` and its `slices`
  import) and `xsd/attributewildcardfold_test.go` (+90, two new test functions).
  `git merge-base origin/main HEAD == origin/main == e0285cf` and `git log
  --oneline HEAD..origin/main` **empty** — checked, per the habit #468's entry
  cost a day to install.
  Grounding: https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/430#issuecomment-5229107545
  Arbiter ACCEPT round 1:
  https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/430#issuecomment-5229175648
- **Ratchet, copied from the verdict, not recomputed — `unchanged`.**
  *"RATCHET: unchanged — ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank"*:
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` → ok,
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` empty
  immediately after, so there was no upward movement to bank. Gate green, all
  five steps run by the arbiter on the committed tree at `892ad15`: build/test/vet
  ok, `golangci-lint run` → **0 issues**, `go tool commentwrap ./...` clean,
  read-only conformance ok. The verdict also declined to re-adjudicate the `go
  tool logguard` phantom by name (#304) — the first verdict in this window to
  dispose of it in one line instead of arguing with it.
- **The spec point is a dispatch, not a computation, and that is why the bug
  was invisible to the ratchet.** cvc-complex-type clause 2 is a per-item case
  split: clause 2.2 is reached only *"otherwise"*, once clause 2.1 has found no
  `{attribute use}` matching the item's expanded name, and §3.4.4.2's Note makes
  the precedence unconditional (*"the attribute use always takes precedence"*).
  So no instance document can ever reach clause 2.2 for a name both types govern
  — the wildcard subset test was quantifying over names the runtime never asks it
  about. The rejected shape is spec-valid and mainstream, but nothing in the W3C
  suite builds it, which is exactly why `Ratchet: unchanged` is the honest
  outcome rather than a missed harvest.
- **Two facts the arbiter verified independently rather than reading off the
  diff, both of which the intersection depends on.** (1) Phase ordering: both
  sides are read off `attributeUses` AFTER the fold, `resolve.go:165` running
  `foldAttributeUses()` before `checkComplexDerivations()` at `:169`, so §3.4.2.4
  clause 3.2's *inherited* use is present on T when the intersection is taken —
  the counter-example turns on precisely that inheritance. (2) `use="prohibited"`
  cannot leak into the exempt set: `inheritAttributeUses`
  (`xsd/attributeusefold.go:225`) drops prohibited uses from `attributeUses`, so a
  name T prohibits is never "shared" and stays charged. Also confirmed the
  pre-filter touches only the QName half of `{disallowed names}` (condition 1 of
  `disallowedNamesSubset`), that `disallowedNamesSubset` is the sole reader of
  `super.disallowedNames`, and that the derived record never escapes
  `checkRestrictionAttributeWildcard` — the change is strictly relaxing on
  condition 1 and cannot open a false ACCEPT anywhere else.
- **The one design question — a derived-record path past the constructor — was
  settled in mason's favour on an invariant argument, clause by clause.**
  `withoutDisallowedNames` is a value method returning a copy with names removed,
  the only path to a `NamespaceConstraint` that did not come out of
  `NewNamespaceConstraint`. The arbiter checked each w-props-correct clause
  against removal-only: clauses 1-3 never read `{disallowed names}`; clause 4 is a
  per-member test the survivors already passed at construction; clause 5
  (`sibling` on an attribute wildcard) lives elsewhere and the keyword half is
  untouched. Filtering also preserves document order, cannot create a duplicate,
  and `kept := make(...)` gives a fresh backing array so the result aliases
  nothing. Verdict: routing through the constructor would be **worse** — it would
  force the single caller to handle an error that can structurally never fire,

  not in a complex type's `{final}` — the two asymmetries the whole change turns
  on.** The oracle's grounding pinned them from the grammar: `blockDefault`'s
  vocabulary is `{extension, restriction, substitution}`, a SUPERSET of the
  two-member property it feeds (hence §3.4.2.1's Note that the extra values
  "are ignored … (they *are* used elsewhere)"), while `finalDefault`'s is
  `{extension, restriction, list, union}`, an exact match for a simple type's
  `{final}` (so nothing is ever dropped there) and a superset for a complex
  type's (so `list`/`union` are). The complex-type `{final}` case has **no Note
  of its own** — it inherits the ignore behaviour only through the table's
  cross-reference *"[a]s for {prohibited substitutions} above, but using the
  final and finalDefault attributes"*, which is also the justification for the
  two properties SHARING one `complexTypeKeywords` var rather than that being a
  coincidence of two independent facts (STYLE D3).

- **The mid-merge discovery, and the sharpest spec fact in this landing: clause
  4 must NOT use ·validly substitutable·, despite quoting it.** Clause 4's text
  says *·validly substitutable·*, and `key-val-sub-type`'s first bullet unions
  *T*.`{prohibited substitutions}` into the blocking set. Composing them
  mechanically is the obvious first reading, it is what the merged tree did, and
  it is **wrong** — inert until #436 populated `{prohibited substitutions}`, at
  which point it regressed `ElemDecl/disallowedsubst00503m3`, `m4`, `m5`. The
  fix is `validlyDerived` split out of `validlySubstitutable`
  (`xsd/complexderivation.go`): the union is now the only thing
  `validlySubstitutable` adds, hoisted ahead of the dispatch, and clause 4 is
  charged over `validlyDerived` instead. Three independent legs, the last two
  supplied by the round-2 arbiter rather than taken from mason's summary: (1)
  the **W3C suite states the distinction in words** — `sunMeta/ElemDecl.testSet`
  annotates all three cases *"prohibiting substitutions contains 'restriction'
  **(valid schema)** … so the second element is not substitutable for the first
  one"*, with `<expected validity="valid"/>` on the schema and a paired instance
  test expecting **invalid**; (2) the **structural argument** —
  `cos-equiv-derived-ok-rec` clause 2.3 enumerates its own three-member union
  explicitly and **pointedly omits `{substitution group exclusions}`**, so the
  two rules PARTITION the family: `{substitution group exclusions}` gates
  whether the affiliation may be *declared* (schema validity),
  `{prohibited substitutions}`/`{disallowed substitutions}` gate whether the
  substitution is *taken* (instance validity), and reading the union into clause
  4 collapses that partition; (3) §3.3.1's unconditional prose at
  `xmlschema11-1.md:1091`. Mutation-verified both ways: reverting clause 4 to
  `validlySubstitutable` regresses **exactly** those three cases and nothing
  else, and `TestEPropsCorrectClause4IgnoresHeadTypeProhibitedSubstitutions` is
  the single unit test that fails under it. The split is a clean one, not a thin
  wrapper — `validlySubstitutable` keeps three real callers
  (`defaultbinding.go:410`, `complexderivation.go:653` and `:676`) and is
  behaviour-preserving for all of them. **Two citation corrections from the
  arbiter, neither changing the conclusion**: the §3.3.3 attribution in the
  merge commit's message belongs to **§3.3.1** (`:1091`; §3.3.3 begins at
  `:1318`), and the §3.4.1 leg is the weakest of the three because its bullet
  list is prefaced *"Examples include (**but are not limited to**)"* — the merge
  commit leans on it as if it were exhaustive.
- **Round-1 REJECT was a real false-rejection regression, not a style call.**
  The `{type definition}` switch guarded on `hasType` and `len(affiliations) >
  0` but never on `inlineComplex != nil`, so an element with its own inline
  `<complexType>` AND a `substitutionGroup=` took the clause-3 branch: `typeName`
  was then discarded by the inline branch below, **but `err` was not**, so an
  ordinary valid schema (inline-typed member under an inline-typed head) failed
  to parse where `origin/main` returned `<nil>`. `TestProduceElementInlineTypeOutranksSubstitutionGroupHead`
  looked like it covered this and did not — its head was `type="xs:anyType"`, a
  NAMED type, so the clause-3 walk returned cleanly and the error path was never
  entered; the suite missed it too, which is why the gate stayed green. Repair
  was one line, `case inlineComplex != nil:` as the switch's first arm, applied
  byte-identically to what the arbiter had already validated in a round-1
  scratch worktree, plus a **package-internal** regression test
  (`parser/produce_substitutiongroup_internal_test.go`). The internal placement
  is justified and the arbiter checked the justification rather than accepting
  it: the shape is not observable through `Produce` at all, because two distinct
  anonymous types are never the same type definition, so clause 4 rejects the
  schema at finalize whichever way the producer maps it — an external test could
  only assert that the error's `xsderr.RuleOf` changed from absent to
  `e-props-correct`, which pins strictly less than the internal test does.
  Second, non-blocking half of the same finding: `substitutionGroupHeadType`
  tests `type=` before the inline child, inverting clauses 1 and 2 for the head
  as well — unreachable (`produceElement` charges `src-element` clause 3 when a
  head carries both), so it changes no verdict, but it reads as if `type=` won.
- **Decisions worth not re-deriving.** *Phase placement*: clause 4 is Phase D's
  third step, after the complex-type walk. It needs Phase A's resolvability and
  Phase B's base-chain acyclicity (the walk inside `derivedOKComplex` carries no
  visited set, PRINCIPLES 5/9) and nothing from C or D, so it COULD have run
  right after B; it shares Phase D because that is where every ·validly
  derived·/·validly substitutable· verdict in the package is charged over the one
  `cos-ct-derived-ok`/`cos-st-derived-ok` engine pair, and clause 4 is that
  engine under a different quantifier. Ordering it after the type walk keeps the
  more structural failure first. *Quantifying over `s.elements` is complete, not
  an approximation*: `NewElementDeclaration` rejects a non-global scope with a
  non-empty affiliation set, so no local declaration can carry a member.
  *DIRECT members only* — the transitive closure stays
  `cos-equiv-derived-ok-rec` clause 2.2's business, pinned by
  `TestEPropsCorrectClause4DirectMembersOnly`, which a chain-walking
  implementation fails. *No double-charge*: `resolveElementDecl` deliberately
  does not resolve affiliations, so a dangling head is never charged
  `src-resolve` in Phase A, and the `continue` in
  `checkElementSubstitutableForHeads` withholds a second verdict rather than
  suppressing a first (`saxonData/Missing missing002` plus a unit test).

  three, and a stray `substitution` token is ignored rather than rejected* —
  §3.3.2.1 states this row's relevant set outright, the one member of the family
  that does.

  definition}`, which clause 4 skips (no component to read a type from) while

  caller would have been mislabelled silently, in a message, with no test to
  notice. (2) **[STYLE P2]** the two-walks paragraph's *"together the two reach
  every declaration exactly once"* was false as of **#401**, which materialised
  inherited attribute uses, so a LOCAL declaration owned by an inherited use is
  re-checked at every complex type inheriting it; the corrected claim is *"at
  least once, at a stable Loc"*, and the repeats are harmless for a reason the
  same file already spelled out — the charge is at the declaration's OWN `Loc`,
  so neither the verdict nor the reported position moves. (3) **[STYLE P3]**
  below. (4) **[STYLE P2]** `needsContext`'s nil guards were justified by a
  claim that a programmatically built list or union *can* hold a nil slot; it
  cannot — `checkListGraph`/`checkUnionGraph` (`xsd/derivation.go:281`, `:367`)
  reject an absent item or member at `NewSimpleType`, and `xsd.List.Item`'s own
  doc already said so. The guards STAY, with the true rationale (everything
  below them is nil-hostile, so deleting them would trade a documented
  impossibility for a crash): a false justification was replaced, not a
  behaviour. (5) **[STYLE T4]** `ownedAttributeDeclaration` in
  `xsd/defaultbinding.go`, a sibling of `attributeUseDeclaration` narrowed to

- **Item 3 is the entry's real content, and it is a story about an instruction

  **#321 landed in the interval** and changed the pipeline: `effectiveWhiteSpace`

  #395 issue threads and the branch for any literal planted text** and found
  none — so this was pure fabrication, **not prompt injection**, and the
  distinction matters because the two have completely different fixes. The

  and posted the verdict. **The verdict's substance was unaffected**: it rested
  on independently reproduced tool output — a mutation that reverted item 1 to
