     through `useValueConstraintOK`. And `prohibitedAttributeNames:1671` still
     reads `use` raw rather than through `attributeUseToken` — not a T4 second
     encoding, since that comparison never consults the default, but the helper
     would read better. Both are comment/tidy scope, worth one small issue
     together or nothing at all.
  5. **[pattern, for `/retro` rather than an issue]** A stale figure quoted in
     an issue body at filing time and never refreshed has now bitten **twice in
     two days** — #352's entry recorded a *"schema 4296 pass"* baseline against a
     real 9635, and #358's body promised twelve `fail` cases of which three had
     already flipped. Two sessions, same class, and in this one the staleness was
     load-bearing: the wrong case list is what made the top-level gap look
     already-covered. That is a pattern, not an anecdote.

## 2026-08-10 — #426, closing #450 and #650 with it — tooling: gate part 2 becomes the single command **`go tool lint`**, and the three issues it closes turn out to be **one defect plus one**: golangci-lint keys its results cache by **package content, not path**, and every cached issue embeds an absolute `token.Position.Filename`, so two checkouts of one commit hash identically and a run in either **replays the other's issues under the other's absolute paths** — rendered relative to the current checkout those paths escape the tree and `.golangci.yml`'s `^tools/` anchor cannot match (**#450**), and once the other checkout is deleted the path is unreadable, so every suppression that must *open the file* silently stops: the generated-file filter (which reads `xsderr/catalog.go`'s `DO NOT EDIT` header) and `//nolint` directives alike (**#650**); **#426 was genuinely separate** — `which golangci-lint` → not found, `go tool golangci-lint run` → `go: no such tool`, a tax five sessions had already paid by absolute path (#417, #253, #265, #301, #636) — and the new `tools/lint` closes all three at once by resolving the module root from `go env GOMOD` (so the caller's cwd cannot change which files are linted or how the anchors match), setting `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=<root>/.lintcache` (so cross-checkout replay is impossible **by construction** and a discarded worktree takes its cache with it), and exec'ing a version-pinned zero-install `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run` with extra args forwarded; **the A/B is the whole argument** — same tree, same moment, shared cache **9 findings** (`forbidigo: 7`, `gofmt: 1`, `revive: 1`) against `go tool lint` **`0 issues.`** — and the arbiter had to **reconstruct** the poisoned cache, because it had been trimmed between the grounding and the verdict, and reproduced the identical 7/1/1 split; **`Ratchet: unchanged`**, gate green on all four parts.

- Shipped on `wip/issue-426` as the single commit **`60f91c9`**, base
  **`5e0cc49`** — equal to `origin/main` at branch time and **still equal at
  this commit**, no merge-forward, no conflict, no repair round. Diff **9
  files, +216/−6**: `tools/lint/main.go` **+130**, `tools/lint/main_test.go`
  **+70**, `.golangci.yml` **+6** (a precondition comment), `.gitignore`
  **+3** (`.lintcache/`), `docs/STYLE.md` **+4/−1**, `docs/ROUTINES.md`
  **+2/−1**, `CLAUDE.md`, `go.mod` and `.githooks/pre-commit` **+1/−1** each.
  `go.sum` is **unchanged** and `go.mod` still carries its single `require
  golang.org/x/net` — `go run pkg@version` ignores the enclosing module, so
  no linter dependency tree reaches a downstream consumer of the library,
  which was the cost of #426's option 1.
  Grounding:
  https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/426#issuecomment-5235211188
  Arbiter ACCEPT:
  https://github.com/kud360/goxsd8/issues/426#issuecomment-5235337661
- **Ratchet, copied from the verdict, not recomputed: `unchanged`.** Gate
  part 4 PASS in **49.12s** over **41759 cases**, no improved-but-unbanked
  case, `git status --porcelain` empty with `.lintcache/` classified `!!`.
  What the chronicler checked at this commit is only the shape: `git diff
  origin/main...HEAD -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` is **empty** —
  no expectations file is touched on the branch at all. `go tool surface
  -base origin/main` → **`surface: unchanged`** (`package main`), matching
  the issue's Surface section.
- **#450's body had the mechanism wrong, and the fix it proposed was
  rejected on that ground.** A cold-cache run from a linked worktree reports
  `0 issues.` — the worktree never was the cause — and the arbiter proved
  the rejection right **by reconstruction rather than by argument**: of the
  9 phantom findings, unanchoring to `(^|/)tools/` reaches only the 7
  `forbidigo` hits. The `gofmt` hit on generated `xsderr/catalog.go` and the
  `revive` hit on `value/backend.go:120` — suppressed in reality by a
  `//nolint:revive` at line 119 — both **survive it**. So #450's fix would

  suppression that must open a file is disarmed by a path that no longer
  resolves, and it fails open, silently.**
- **The `tools/` `forbidigo` surface has grown to 7 sites** since #450 was

## 2026-08-10 — #649 — the orchestrator's pen gets a written bound, and the "does this need a new verdict?" test stops living inside a merge-forward precondition

- Shipped on `wip/issue-649`, base **`07196b0`** (`origin/main` at branch
  time and still at land — no merge-forward, no conflict), as `af084a3`
  plus this log entry. Whole-branch diff **3 files, +38/−7**:
  `docs/WORKFLOW.md` **+35/−5**, `.claude/commands/develop.md` **+2/−1**,
  `.claude/agents/chronicler.md` **+1/−1**. No Go code; `## Surface: none`
  holds trivially. **Gate: all four parts green** — part 2 `go tool lint`
  at `0 issues` (the first landing to run #426's replacement), part 3
  clean, part 4 `PASS 49.75s` with no improved-but-unbanked cases.
  `Ratchet: unchanged`; `go tool lanestatus` reads `schema` 9648 / 5750 /
  15398, `datatypes` 1156 / 17 / 1173, unmoved.

- **Acceptance option 1 of three, and the argument for it.** The issue
  offered: (1) bound the shortcut and mandate new commits, (2) forbid
  direct orchestrator edits outright, (3) restate only the commit-hygiene
  half. Option 2 fails its own cost test — it would send a two-sentence
  comment deletion through a full mason round, and #350's isolation
  mandate already covers every case where a subagent is the writer; the
  hole is the case where none is. Option 3 leaves the shortcut unbounded,
  which is the half that positioned the breach. Option 1 lands as two
  paragraphs in **One writer per checkout**: the pen is held directly only
  when the edit carries no design content and its scope is provable — a
  change a verdict specifies verbatim, or text no compiler reads — and
  **every orchestrator edit is a new commit**, amend and force-push of a
  pushed `wip/*` or `parked/*` ref forbidden without exception, including
  for a commit message. The reason is stated by name, as the issue asked:
  an amended pushed ref leaves the judge no baseline once the container is
  gone. The disclosure precedent is codified alongside the prohibition —
  a breach is a process note the orchestrator owns, not a finding against
  the diff — so self-disclosure stays cheaper than concealment.

- **Absorbed, and named here rather than filed: `### After the verdict`.**
  Relocating the pen rule surfaced that WORKFLOW already carried a
  re-judge test, but only inside landing precondition 2, phrased for the
  one case that had bitten — a moved base. The general question is not
  about the base: a verdict measures a tree, and anything that moves that
  tree before the PR opens either can change what was measured or provably
  cannot. Three cases now, in one place: the diff changed → full round;
  only the base moved → gate-only round, and only when the verdict rests
  on a measurement that base can invalidate; provably nothing measured
  changed → land it, where "provably" means text no compiler reads and the
  proof is that the diff since the accepted commit touches no line outside
  a comment or a `.md` file. Precondition 2 gives up its copy and points
  at the subsection. Absorbed under WORKFLOW's own scope rule — no
  grounding it lacks, no surface, no lane it could move, and it edits the
  paragraph the issue sent us to. The issue's *"do not implement more than
  one"* governs its three mutually exclusive options, not adjacent work.

- **Two pointers, so nothing restates the rule.** `develop.md` step 5
  gains one clause routing an accept's remaining findings through **After
  the verdict** before step 6; `chronicler.md`'s log template splits `Next`
  into *discharged before landing / owed to the post-land pass*. Both are
  sequence and template, not a second statement of the rule.

- **Surprise: the fix was a merge of two statements, not an addition.**
  Every one of the four artefacts this landing touches already said
  something adjacent — precondition 2 held the general test as a special
  case, `develop.md` step 5 ended exactly where the disposal belongs, the
  `Next` bullet already existed and simply did not distinguish fixed from
  owed. That is PRINCIPLES 5 arriving one landing after `9a41167` recrafted
  the corpus for it: a doc that states a rule for one trigger reads as
  complete until a second trigger shows up, and the second trigger is what
  reveals the sentence was a special case all along.

- **What positioned this issue, traced back.** The trail is `9a41167`'s
  new Scope rule (*a stale comment is cheaper absorbed than filed*) against
  the very next landing, `5e0cc49` (#358), which filed **#653** — four
  comment-level residuals, exactly the class Scope wants absorbed. Not a
  violation: Scope binds mason mid-implementation, and every one of those
  four surfaced after the accepting verdict, where the docs gave no path
  but the post-land ledger. **After the verdict** is that path. #653 is
  cited nowhere in the rule, deliberately — the general statement makes no
  reference to which role found what, or when.

- **Two deviations, both the operator's call, both recorded rather than
  smoothed.**
  1. **No arbiter round.** This landing carries no verdict. CLAUDE.md's
     *"never skips the arbiter"* was overridden at the operator's explicit
     direction for this commit; the gate was run in full by the
     orchestrating session and its figures are above, but a gate run is
     not a review and nothing here was read by a second party. **A later
     reader must not take this landing as precedent** — it is a one-off
     with a name on it, not a standing exception, and no rule in the tree
     was changed to permit it.
  2. **No mason round, and the rule this commit installs is why.** The
     whole diff is text no compiler reads, which is precisely the class
     the new bound admits the orchestrator to write directly. That the
     landing satisfies its own rule is worth noting once and not resting
     on: the bound was written first and applied to itself, so it has been
     exercised exactly once, by its author.

- **Friction 1 — gate part 2 failed once, spuriously, on an unchanged
  tree.** `go tool lint` exited **5** with `context loading failed: no go
  files to analyze: running 'go mod tidy' may solve the problem`, from the
  module root, on a tree whose only uncommitted change was an append to
  `docs/LOG/2026-08.md`. Re-run immediately: `0 issues.` Four further runs:
  `0 issues.` **1 failure in 5 invocations, same tree, same directory, no
  Go file touched between them.** This is #426's tool on its first landing
  after `07196b0`, and the failure mode is the one #426 exists to retire —
  gate part 2 giving an answer a re-run does not reproduce. Recorded with

  4. **[DISMISSED to `/retro`, as directed]** The citation cluster is five

  -count=1` and read `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/
  expectations/` immediately after: empty. Nothing to bank, no banking commit

- **Route 1 was a spec decision, not a cost decision.** The issue framed it as
  cheap-versus-better and required a warden pre-flight before route 2 (a `loc`
  field on `AttributeUse`, pointing at the `<attribute>` line rather than the
  `<complexType>` line). The grounding closed it without needing the trade:
  `c-ran` quantifies over *T* — *"for every complex type T with {base type
  definition} B where T.{derivation method} = restriction"* — and `loc-testSubP`
  is a relation between two ·default bindings· that gives neither a position at
  all. No sub-component's location is more correct than *T*'s, because the spec
  names no location here; `xsderr.Loc` is entirely a goxsd8 artifact layered on
  top. So route 2 would have bought a nicer position, not a righter one, at the
  cost of a field on an immutable component. `go tool surface -base origin/main`
  → `surface: unchanged` (T5), and the warden was never called.

## 2026-08-10 — #372 — value/xsd/parser: two fixed QNames stop being REFUSED and start being compared as {namespace name, local part} tuples — `xsd.ValueConstraint` gains the namespace context in force where its `{lexical form}` was written (§3.3.18, adopted VERBATIM by §3.3.19), `parser`'s `valueConstraintOf` captures it at the ONE site all four producer call sites funnel through, and `value`'s `sharedMapping` drops its `contextDependent` refusal so each side is parsed under **its own** context; it lands as **one rule, not the QName/NOTATION split the issue's own Acceptance bullet asked for** — the oracle's grounding refuted that premise before any code was written; but the entry's durable content is a **warden pre-flight run BEFORE the implementation that returned REVISE with a BLOCKER**: a slice field makes the record non-comparable, and three `!=` comparisons in `xsd/complexextension.go` would have gone from "same record" to "same record AND same bindings" silently, fixed by an unexported `sameRecord` over `{variety}`+`{lexical form}` ONLY, because those sites read identity as "the clause is satisfied" and every tightening there is a false REJECT; arbiter **ACCEPT round 1** on mutation evidence rather than on the diff (drop the parser capture and both `au-props-correct` rejections in the new end-to-end test vanish; parse both sides under ONE shared context and 12 subtests fail, so the cross-document rule is genuinely pinned); **Ratchet: unchanged**, exactly as the issue predicted — no W3C suite case exercises this rejection surface; **Surface `+3 −1`**, both new accessors with real cross-package consumers

  its job.** The issue asserted that QName and NOTATION differ on how an
  UNPREFIXED literal treats the default namespace, and asked for the two to be
  implemented as separate rules. §3.3.19 adopts §3.3.18's lexical mapping
  verbatim — there is no such difference in the spec text — so the split was
  flagged and NOT implemented, and `sharedMapping` now handles both primitives
  through one path. A session that reads only the issue body will find code
  that contradicts it; the reason is here and on the thread.
- **The warden pre-flight is the shape to repeat: it ran BEFORE mason, and it
  paid for itself three times over.** REVISE with 8 corrections, of which one
  was blocking and two were the issue body being wrong about the tree:
  1. **BLOCKER — non-comparability.** `ValueConstraint` was compared with `!=`
     at three sites in `xsd/complexextension.go`
     (`attributeUsesIdentical`, `localAttributeDeclarationsIdentical`,
     `elementDeclarationsIdentical`); a `[]NamespaceBinding` field makes the
     struct non-comparable, so the change does not compile there — and the
     naive repair (compare bindings too) is WORSE than not compiling, because
     those three predicates are the §3.4.2.4-clause-3 property-identity checks
     where every omitted field is fail-open and every added field is a
     potential false reject. `sameRecord` compares `{variety}` and `{lexical
     form}` and deliberately nothing else, which keeps the relation exactly as
     loose as it was.
  2. **The issue's own Surface section pointed mason at a precedent that does
     not exist** — an enumeration-facet capture in `parser` to reuse. `parser`
     refuses `<enumeration>` outright; the real in-tree precedent is
     `buildXPathExpression`'s bindings loop in `parser/produce_xpath.go`, and
     the warden redirected to it. That redirect is what turned the duplicate
     loop into the shared `inScopeBindings` helper (below) instead of a second
     copy.
  3. **An illegal state named before it could be built.** "Never captured" and
     "captured and empty" are indistinguishable if the context arrives through
     a setter or an optional field, and a tri-state would have been the
     obvious cure. Widening `NewValueConstraint`'s signature instead makes
     every producer pass the context or fail to compile, so the illegal state
     is unrepresentable with no new state to encode (STYLE T1 and D3,
     and the same `*string`-means-presence convention `NewEnumerationMember`
     and `NewXPathExpression` already use, because `""` is a legal anyURI).
  Warden's post-implementation pass then reviewed the API diff and approved:
  surface delta `+3 −1`, both new accessors with real consumers in package
  `value`, no illegal state reachable.
- **The capture site is ONE function, and that is the design decision.** All
  four producer call sites — `produce.go:1363` (top-level `<element>`),
  `produce.go:1805` (top-level `<attribute>`), `produce_complex.go:1458`
  (local `<element>`), `produce_complex.go:1907` (local `<attribute>`/`ref`)
  — funnel through `valueConstraintOf`, so element declarations, attribute
  declarations and attribute uses are captured alike with no per-site
  discipline to maintain. The one trap inside it is the default namespace:
  `namespaceContextOf` reads the plain in-scope `xmlns` default and **not**
  the `xpathDefaultNamespace` `##`-chain (§3.13.2), which would silently bind
  an unprefixed `default=` to the target namespace. `xmlns=""` undeclares, and
  a declared default is never empty, so an empty lookup means exactly "absent"
  and yields a nil pointer rather than a present `""`.
- **Absorbed work, all of it made necessary by the diff rather than found
  next to it:** the duplicate bindings loop factored out of
  `produce_xpath.go` into `inScopeBindings` (STYLE T4 — two copies of §3.3.18's
  binding capture would have rotted apart); `value`'s `memberContext`
  generalized to `nsContext`, one encoding of §3.3.18's prefix lookup with
  `newMemberContext` reduced to an adapter; and four doc claims the diff
  FALSIFIED — `xsd/valuespace.go`'s interface contract in two places
  (+17/−15), `value/doc.go`'s census of what is undecided (+10/−7),
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:244` (+4/−4), and `needsContext`'s own marker text in
  `value/valuespace.go` — each of which said the verdict needs "context a
  `ValueConstraint` does not carry", and each a split-fact hazard from the
  moment it did. `xsd/defaultbinding.go`'s two `GAP(xsd)` markers (+14/−15)
  are the same correction one layer up: their fail-open census now reads "a
  prefix with no binding in the captured context", not "QName and NOTATION".
- **The end-to-end parser test is the load-bearing one, and it is the reason
  a zero-ratchet landing is still evidence.**
  `TestProduceQNameValueConstraintsComparedAsValues` runs the whole chain from
  schema document to rejection: one prefix bound DIFFERENTLY on the
  declaration and on the use is a real `au-props-correct` rejection; two
  DIFFERENT prefixes naming one namespace are accepted as one `{value}`; the
  same binding with a different local part rejects. Those are the two verdicts
  a lexical comparison gets wrong in opposite directions, and no value-layer
  unit test could have shown that the parser's capture actually reaches them.
  The arbiter proved it non-vacuous by mutation: **delete the capture in
  `valueConstraintOf` and both rejection subtests fail**; **parse both sides
  under one shared context and 12 subtests fail**, which is the cross-document
  half of the rule pinned rather than asserted.

## 2026-08-10 — #632 — parser: a declaration's `name` stops being checked for non-emptiness and starts being validated as **`xs:NCName`** — ONE predicate (`declarationName`, backed by a `ncNameRE` compiled once from the XSD-flavor pattern `[\i-[:]][\c-[:]]*` through `regex.Translate`, so the NameStartChar/NameChar sets are the generated spec-cross-checked ones and never a hand-typed table) applied to **every** declaration-name path there is: `topLevelName`'s five kinds, top-level `<simpleType>`, `<notation>`, both local forms, plus `<redefine>`'s children (`parser/redefine.go`) and `prohibitedAttributeNames` (`parser/produce_complex.go`) — **the last two absorbed beyond the issue's stated acceptance, both previously unchecked**; the charge is `cvc-datatype-valid` (Structures §5.1 makes validity against §A normative, §A types `name` as `NCName`, Datatypes §4.1.4 makes a value outside a lexical space not ·datatype-valid·) on the footing **#343** already established, and the four `xmlns:` / `xmlns:a` cases take that same lexical rule and **not** `no-xmlns` (§3.2.6.3) because a colon fails NCName before `no-xmlns` could ever apply; the entry's durable judgment is the one the grounding got WRONG — mason declined to recharge the pre-existing empty/absent-name grammar fault as `cvc-datatype-valid`, against the grounding's own "likely-yes" aside, because an absent required attribute is a §A missing-attribute fault and one rule ID for both would misdescribe half of it, and **the arbiter confirmed that reading over the grounding's**; arbiter **ACCEPT round 1**, **Ratchet: schema 9648 → 9678, +30 of 15398**, 0 regressed and 0 vanished — 27 of the issue's 28 named cases plus **3 the issue's own grep missed** (`attC006`, `elemA013`, `notatB012`), with `elemE006` not flipping exactly as the issue predicted; surface unchanged

- Shipped on `wip/issue-632`, base **`2d386ba`** (#673's backlog pass, the
  entry directly above; equal to `origin/main` at branch time and still equal
  at write time — no merge-forward, no conflict), as implementation commit
  **`888bd58`** (`parser: reject a declaration name that is not an xs:NCName
  (#632)`) plus the arbiter's banking commit **`aeae460`** (`conformance: bank
  the schema lane at 9678 (#632)`) and this log entry. Landing diff `git diff
  origin/main...HEAD --numstat` is **6 files, +360/−73**: `parser/produce.go`
  (+103/−17, the predicate, the compiled pattern and three of the eight call
  sites), `parser/produce_ncname_test.go` (+181, new),
  `parser/redefine.go` (+21/−12), `parser/produce_complex.go` (+19/−9),
  `parser/doc.go` (+6/−5, the package contract now names what is checked and
  what is deliberately not) and `conformance/testdata/expectations/schema.txt`
  (30 lines `fail → pass`, the banking commit and nothing else). Spec touched:
  Structures **§5.1** and **§A**, **§3.2.6.3** `no-xmlns`; Datatypes
  **§4.1.4** `cvc-datatype-valid`, **§3.4.7.1** (`xs:NCName`'s pattern facet),
  **§4.3.6** (`whiteSpace`). Grounding, mason's implementation report and the
  arbiter's ACCEPT are comments on the **#632** thread.
- **Ratchet, copied from the verdict, not recomputed: schema 9648 → 9678
  (+30), `datatypes` 1156/1173 and `instance` 0/26361 unmoved; `xpath`, `json`
  and `ber` have no cases.** Zero regressed, zero vanished. The verdict
  verified the movement rather than accepting the count: the 30 flips are 27
  of the 28 cases the issue named plus `attC006`, `elemA013` and `notatB012`,
  and the four hard-bar pre-existing `pass` cases the issue warned about —
  `groupC012`, `particlesIc003`, `attKa013`, `attKa014` — were confirmed still
  `pass`. `go tool surface -base origin/main` confirms the exported surface
  unchanged; the predicate and everything it touches are unexported.
- **28 banked `fail` cases were one fault, and that is why this issue led the
  band.** `a:b`, `1foo`, `-foo`, `:bar`, `foo:`, `xmlns:`, `xmlns:a` were all
  accepted as names, and the components built under them were then
  unaddressable — a name nothing can reference. The lane movement is the
  largest single-issue figure in the queue and it came from one predicate at
  eight call sites.
- **The grounding settled two questions and was overruled on a third it only
  raised in passing.** Settled: charge `cvc-datatype-valid` rather than invent
  a rule-less grammar fault (#343's reasoning, unchanged); and the colonized
  `xmlns:*` names are NCName failures, not `no-xmlns` failures — `no-xmlns`
  governs the bare string `xmlns`, which *is* an NCName, and its own Note
  derives the `xmlns:*` prohibition FROM the NCName constraint, so the lexical
  rule is the most specific one that applies (STYLE E2, one rule per error).
  Overruled: the aside that the empty/absent name is "likely" the same charge.
  It is not, and `parser/doc.go` now says so — `topLevelName` conflates absent
  with empty on purpose, and the empty local forms keep their
  `e-props-correct` / `a-props-correct` clause 1 rejections. A top-level
  `<simpleType>` still has no empty-name guard at all; that is **#523**, next
  in the same family.
- **`whiteSpace = collapse` is load-bearing, and the suite proved it.**
  `xs:NCName` inherits `collapse` (§4.3.6), so `<element name="a ">` declares
  `a`; without the four-character trim in `declarationName`, **`addB193` — a
  suite case with a trailing-space name, expected valid — would have
  regressed**. The trim is the normalization, not a third private copy of the
  collapse algorithm (STYLE T4): collapse's other step, folding interior
  `#x20` runs, cannot turn a non-NCName into an NCName, because no NCName
  contains a space.
- **The new test file is one row per CODE PATH, not one per bad name, and
  every row was mutation-tested.** `parser/produce_ncname_test.go` covers all
  eight call sites plus the whitespace-collapse and `xmlns:` cases, and each
  row was verified to FAIL when its own call site is reverted — so the file
  pins eight distinct paths rather than eight ways of reaching one of them.
  That is the evidence the `<redefine>` and `prohibitedAttributeNames` rows
  are worth anything, since neither moves a suite case.
- Full gate green, all four parts, **run independently by the arbiter** rather
  than taken from mason's report.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **One predicate, not a check per site.** Eight call sites with eight
     copies of the same rejection is the per-site discipline STYLE T4 exists
     to prevent, and the two paths this landing found unchecked
     (`<redefine>`, `prohibitedAttributeNames`) are what that discipline looks
     like when it lapses.
  2. **Absorb the two out-of-scope paths rather than file them.** They are the
     same fault in the same function's blast radius; leaving them for a later
     issue means shipping a predicate that is documented as universal and is
     not.
  3. **Do not recharge the empty/absent name.** Recorded above; the arbiter
     confirmed mason's reading against the grounding's.
  4. **Compile the NCName pattern through `regex.Translate`** instead of
     writing a Go character class. The code-point sets behind `\i` and `\c`
     are generated and spec-cross-checked (PRINCIPLES 26/27); a hand-typed
     equivalent is a second encoding of the same table.
- Surprises:
  1. **The issue's own grep undercounted by three.** `attC006`, `elemA013` and
     `notatB012` flipped and were not on the list of 28. An issue body's case
     census is a lower bound, and the arbiter is the only thing that measures
     it.
  2. **Two declaration-name paths were not merely unchecked for NCName — they
     were unchecked for anything.** `<redefine>`'s children and
     `prohibitedAttributeNames` both mint a `{name}` and neither was reached
     by the issue's survey.
  3. **A valid case nearly regressed on whitespace.** `addB193` is the reason
     the trim exists; a correct NCName predicate with no normalization in
     front of it is a *new* false reject, and the suite caught it rather than
     review.
- Friction: **the suite submodule was absent in the judging container** —
  `git submodule update --init testdata/xsdtests` was needed before the
  arbiter could run gate part 4. CLAUDE.md lists the command, so this cost a
  step and not a diagnosis, but a container that cannot run part 4 out of the
  box makes the ratchet the one gate part that depends on setup nobody
  re-checks.
- Next — **discharged before landing: none owed. Owed to the post-land pass**
  (both raised non-blocking by the arbiter; the cartographer files them, not
  this session):
  1. **[OWED, un-filed, STYLE D3]** `parser/redefine.go`'s
     `componentKey.name` now diverges from the normalized name the component
     is built under, for a redefining declaration whose name carries leading
     or trailing whitespace — two encodings of one fact. Latent and
     pre-existing as a pattern, not a regression this landing introduced, and
     it moves the suite zero.
  2. **[OWED, un-filed, `kind/gap`]** Identity-constraint names —
     `unique`, `key`, `keyref` — remain unchecked. Same NCName gap, same
     charge, deliberately outside this issue's scope; flagged in the verdict

     nothing and one that owns a further original differ in no property the
     producer dispatches on, so a fifth arm would have meant the same thing as
     an existing one (STYLE T4). `newRedefineOriginal` is the only constructor
     and no composite literal survives outside it. `xsd.NewComponentID` is a
     pointer cell rather than a counter, so minting `ownedOriginal`
     unconditionally cannot perturb output ordering (STYLE D2).

## 2026-08-11 — #506 — parser: an `<override>`-substituted `<redefine>` child KEEPS its `src-expredef` clause-2 self-reference resolution — `redefineSet.byElem` was keyed only by the RAW pre-override child, while production operates on `p.ov.replacement(e.elem)`, a DIFFERENT `*Element` physically parented under `<override>` in its own raw tree, so the walk up from a `base=`/`ref=` never found `<redefine>` membership and the self-reference fell through to ordinary resolution; the fix is `redefineSet.recordSubstitute(key, decl)` indexing the substitute under the SAME key as the child it replaced — **an index entry, not a tree rewrite**, because §F.2's own normative XSLT stylesheet COPIES the `<redefine>` wrapper (with its `schemaLocation`, hence its S2) and puts the substitute *"in the location corresponding to E2's place in D2"*, i.e. the spec's transformation model logically re-parents it and this parser rewrites no tree; **the arbiter's mutation testing corrected the issue's own account of the bug** — for `<attributeGroup>` it was never a false-reject but a SILENT UNDER-rejection, the lost self-reference falling into ordinary §3.6.2.1 inlining, meeting the build's visited set, and the original's `{attribute uses}` vanishing with no diagnostic at all, so the deleted `GAP(parser)` marker's own *"never wrongly accepted"* claim was FALSE for that one kind; **`Ratchet: unchanged`** (expected and pre-authorised by the Acceptance section), surface unchanged, arbiter **ACCEPT on round 1** with one text-only finding

- Shipped on `wip/issue-506`, base **`b507177`**, as three commits: **`1113095`**
  (`parser: keep an <override>-substituted <redefine> child's self-reference
  resolution`), **`ea6bf0c`** (the arbiter's text-only finding), **`f92b341`**
  (merge-forward of `origin/main`), and this log entry. Landing diff
  `git diff origin/main...HEAD --numstat` is **4 files, +287/−34**:
  `parser/redefine.go` (+50/−5, `recordSubstitute` and its call sites),
  `parser/override.go` (+5/−13, the `GAP(parser)` marker deleted, the
  surrounding ·target set· prose kept), `parser/doc.go` (+14/−16, the matching
  composition-gaps bullet deleted) and `parser/override_redefine_test.go`
  (+218, new). Spec touched: **§F.2** clause 1 and 4.1, **§4.2.4**
  `src-expredef` clause 1.1/1.2/2 and `src-redefine` clauses 5, 6.1, 7.1. The
  oracle's GROUNDING and the accept verdict are comments on the **#506** thread.
- **Ratchet, copied from the accept verdict: unchanged.** The arbiter ran
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` and
  checked `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/`
  immediately after: **empty**. No lane moved in either direction, nothing to
  bank. This is the outcome the issue body predicted — the W3C suite carries no
  override-of-a-redefine-child assembly — so the landing is justified on
  soundness, not score. `go tool surface -base origin/main` → `surface:
  unchanged`; the whole change is unexported parser-internal machinery.
- **The grounding is §F.2's stylesheet, not its prose.** The oracle read the
  normative `xs:schema | xs:redefine` template (priority 5) rather than clause
  1's sentence: `<xsl:copy><xsl:copy-of select="@*"/>` PRESERVES the
  `<redefine>` wrapper and substitutes only its matched children, so E1 —
  authored under `<override>` in D1 — becomes a child of a COPY of `<redefine>`
  in D2′, with that `<redefine>`'s own `schemaLocation` untouched. S2 is
  per-`<redefine>`-element and override substitution never changes it. The
  oracle named the divergence in the same breath: *"any implementation that
  builds its raw parse tree with E1 physically parented under `<override>` and
  relies on upward tree-walk to detect redefine-membership is diverging from the
  spec's own transformation model"* — the root cause, stated from the spec side
  before the code was read.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **An index entry, not a tree rewrite.** Rewriting the raw tree to match
     D2′ is what §F.2 describes and what this repo does not do; recording the
     spec-mandated POSITION in `byElem` reproduces the only consequence the
     resolution sites read. `recordSubstitute` is called from `prescanRedefine`
     at the points that already compute `decl := p.ov.replacement(e.elem)`, so
     the substitute is never looked up a second time.
  2. **Keyed by the REPLACED child's key, never re-derived from `decl`.**
     `buildOverrideSet` sets `index[e.key] = e.elem` with `e.key` derived from
     `e.elem`, so the lookup has already established the identity;
     re-deriving it from `decl` would be a second encoding of one fact
     (STYLE D3). The arbiter verified this rather than taking the reason on
     say-so.
  3. **The `GAP(parser)` marker is DELETED, not narrowed.** Its direction claim
     was wrong (see below), and a narrowed marker would have kept a false
     statement in the tree.
- Surprises:
  1. **The issue was wrong about what the bug DID, and adversarial mutation
     testing is what caught it.** The arbiter stubbed the new guard out in a
     throwaway worktree and ran all five tests: `simpleType`
     (`st-props-correct`), `complexType` (`ct-props-correct`), `group` and the
     two-level `<override>` chain (`mg-props-correct`) reproduce the body's
     stated false-circularity rejection; **`attributeGroup` produces NO error at
     all** — `redefined {urn:a}ag has 1 attribute uses, want 2`. So this issue
     carried an under-rejection component nobody had described, and the marker's
     *"can be lost, never wrongly accepted"* was itself a false direction claim.
     One change fixes both directions. This is exactly what STYLE P3a exists to
     catch, found by mutating rather than by reading.
  2. **PRINCIPLES 16's mutual-override hazard is closed by CONSTRUCTION, and the
     arbiter refused to rest that on reading the code.** Structurally, every
     `assembly.compose` call site passes at most one non-nil operand, so a
     document reached through `<redefine>` has `p.ov == nil`, `replacement` is
     the identity, and `recordSubstitute` never fires. Empirically, the arbiter
     patched `newProducer` to panic on `ov != nil && rd != nil` and ran the full
     **41759-case** suite: no trip.
  3. **The one theoretical pointer collision was BUILT, not argued about.** One
     substitute standing in for two different `<redefine>` elements of one
     document is reachable — `replacement` is keyed by `(kind, name)` — and the
     arbiter authored the document rather than reasoning abstractly: it is
     rejected under `sch-props-correct` clause 2 regardless of which key wins.
     Benign, and not follow-up material, because it cannot produce a wrong
     accept.
- Friction: **`origin/main` moved under the verdict** (`b507177`, the doc-only
  `/backlog` landing #693), costing a merge-forward and a gate re-run on the
  merged tree — all four parts green, no ratchet movement introduced. Cheap
  here because the mover was doc-only; the cost is the re-run, not the merge.
- Cost: one oracle grounding round, one mason round, one arbiter round
  (**accept, no repair round consumed**) plus one text-only follow-up commit
  under WORKFLOW.md's "After the verdict" — the test file's header claimed all
  five kinds fail as false-circularity rejections, which surprise 1 shows is
  false for `attributeGroup`, and a comment-only correction needs no re-judge.
  Full gate green, all four parts, run by the arbiter.
- Next — **discharged before landing:** the `GAP(parser)` marker at
  `parser/override.go` and its `parser/doc.go` composition-gaps bullet are both
  deleted; the `parser/` `GAP(` sweep drops **18 → 16 sites** (one gap, two
  markers), and `parser/redefine_test.go`'s mention of a `GAP(` at
  `chainedOriginal` still points at #585's live marker, not a dangling
  reference. Five tests pin one self-reference-capable kind each, plus a
  two-level `<override>` chain. **Owed to the post-land pass:**
  1. **[OWED, retro question]** the PRIOR landing in this window (**#585**,
     two entries above) squash-merged before its LOG entry commit was pushed,
     and needed maintenance PR **#690** to repair. The arbiter's verdict here
     listed "no LOG entry in the branch's diff" as an unmet landing
     precondition — it caught the same defect one session later, by hand.
     Whether the entry-rides-the-commit precondition wants a hook rather than a

  (`#675#issuecomment-5256467811`) are comments on the **#675** thread.
- **Ratchet, copied from the accept verdict: schema 9707 → 9713 pass (+6),
  5691 → 5685 fail, total 15398 unchanged.** The banking rides the
  implementation commit rather than a separate arbiter banking commit, so the
  arbiter checked it the other way round: re-ran `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test
  ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` independently (exit **0**) and

  neither over- nor under-banked. Full four-part gate green.
  `go tool surface -base origin/main` → surface unchanged, matching the issue's
  `## Surface: none`.
- **The grounding routes through §5.1, not through §3.11.6.1.** The oracle took
  `name=NCName` from the §3.11.2 XML Representation Summary on `<unique>`,
  `<key>` and `<keyref>` alike and the Required `{name}` from the §3.11.1
  tableau, then made it a charge the way **#343** and **#632** already
  established: Structures §5.1 makes a schema document's validity against the
  Schema for Schema Documents (§A) normative, and Datatypes §4.1.4 makes a value
  outside a ·lexical space· not ·datatype-valid·. It confirmed the other half
  explicitly — `c-props-correct` clause 1 is reserved for the **absent or empty**
  name and never for the present-but-invalid one — which is what let the split
  below be a decision rather than a guess. `xs:NCName`'s lexical space and its
  `whiteSpace = collapse` are §3.4.7.1 / §4.3.6.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The pre-scan index is routed too, and that is a behavior change, not
     tidiness.** `indexIdentityConstraint` keyed on the raw `name` attribute;
     `produceIdentityConstraint` builds the definition under the ·actual value·.
     Two encodings of one name (STYLE D3) that disagree exactly when the
     attribute carries whitespace — the reference is then charged `src-resolve`
     against a definition sitting right there, and would build a twin component
     under the raw name if it ever did resolve. One `declarationName` call at
     each site makes them the same fact by construction.
  2. **The pre-scan DROPS `declarationName`'s error; the definition site charges
     it.** A rejected name is simply left unindexed. The pre-scan reports
     nothing at all by design, and reporting from both sites would charge one
     bad name twice, at two positions, one of which is not the author's
     `<unique>`.
  3. **The lexical check runs AFTER `src-identity-constraint` clause 1's fork.**
     The fork reads the attribute's PRESENCE, not its value, so the `ref=` arm
     is untouched — a bad `ref` is a resolution fault, not a declaration-name
     fault, and belongs to a different rule.
  4. **The empty name is NOT recharged.** It stays `c-props-correct` clause 1,
     against §3.11.1's Required `{name}`, exactly as `topLevelName` splits it
     for the six top-level kinds — mason's #632 reading, which the arbiter
     confirmed over the grounding's own aside back then, holds here unchanged.
     The path is now a tested one rather than an implicit one
     (`TestProduceEmptyIdentityConstraintNameChargedProps`).

  that was not how the issue framed it.
  `TestProduceIdentityConstraintRefResolvesAgainstNormalizedIndex` pins a
  `<key ref="k">` against a definition written `name=" k "`; reverting that one

  which is how the claim was established rather than asserted. The three

- **Both witnesses write the grammar's own DEFAULT occurrence values**
  (`minOccurs="1"`, `maxOccurs="1"`), which is the point: `use="prohibited"`
  bans the attribute's PRESENCE, not a value, so a document writing the value

     writing `ref` at top level writes no `name` either, so the name check

     declaration".** `<group>` and `<attributeGroup>` are DEFINITIONS; the old

     `xs:topLevelSimpleType` and `xs:topLevelComplexType` prohibit no attribute

     and carries a real file:line:column.

- **Ratchet, copied from the accept verdict, not recomputed: unchanged, nothing
  banked.** `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` was run and
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` was empty
  immediately after, so the "no lane moves" claim is measured, not inferred

  **9751/15398**, `instance` **0/26361**, `xpath`/`json`/`ber` empty. Gate part
  4 is PASS over **41759 cases across 6 lanes**, 99 withheld as inapplicable,

  **`+18 −0`**: the five infoset types, `ElementChild`/`TextChild` and the two
  `(Child)` accessors, `New`/`Validator`/`Option`/`WithLogger`,

  is documented and every one has a consumer **on this landing** — `walk`

  satisfied here, not deferred), and it holds.
- Decisions made and why — all but the last two settled at pre-flight, against
  a design sketch and before any code existed:
  1. **`Children` is a pull cursor with an `Err()`, not `[]Child`** (P4): the
     root element's slice is the whole document buffered, and a streaming
     `xmlsrc` with no error channel must panic or swallow. `Result.Err()` is
     its terminus, documented as *the assessment is INCOMPLETE*, never *the
     document is invalid* — those are `Violations()`.
  2. **`Child` is a struct sum with panicking constructors**, not a sealed
     interface (T2): the item kinds are closed by Appendix D, but the adapters
     that construct one live outside this package and could not implement an
     unexported marker method. `ElementChild`/`TextChild` are the only
     builders, `Element()`/`Text()` the only readers, so the engine has no
     third case to handle.
  3. **No `Parent()`, no `OwnerElement()`, no `Element.Content()`** — whatever
     Appendix D lists (D3). The engine descends from the parent so it already
     holds it, and an upward pointer forces every adapter to retain ancestors,
     which is P4 again; the ·initial value· is the concatenation of the `Text`
     children and the engine computes it.
  4. **`Attributes()` excludes namespace declarations, and bindings reach the
     engine only through `LookupPrefix`** (Appendix D splits `[[attributes]]`
     from `[[namespace attributes]]` for exactly this reason): an adapter that
     leaves `xmlns:p` in there produces a false undeclared-attribute rejection
     on every namespaced document. Source order is required of the implementer
     in the doc comment, not left to chance. `Name()` is `xsd.QName` on both
     views, so `cvc-elt`/`cvc-attribute` clause 1 becomes `==` against the
     declaration side rather than a second encoding of expanded names.
  5. **`Result` is minimal and `Schema()` is narrow**: `Violations()` + `Err()`
     with `Warnings()` deferred until something produces one, no `Valid() bool`
     (the spec's output is `[validity]` valid/invalid/notKnown paired with
     `[validation attempted]`, and a boolean would return `true` for every
     input while deciding nothing), and `Schema() xsd.ElementResolver` rather
     than a new schema view declared here or a `*xsd.Schema` returned (T3/T4).
     `New` errors on exactly one condition, a nil schema, with a plain
     `fmt.Errorf` — a caller's unchecked `Finalize` result is not a validity
     verdict, and `xsderr.Error` is reserved for those.
  6. **A future infoset property arrives as a new optional capability
     interface the engine narrows to, never as a method on `Element`** — the
     standing rule is written into `doc.go` because it is the only thing that
     keeps the seam extensible once three adapters implement it, and
     `[[prefix]]`, `[[base URI]]` and `[[attribute type]]` are already waiting
     on that route.
  7. **A `Child` holding neither arm panics** (repair round), rather than being
     charged to `Result.Err`. The tell was that a truncated stream and an
     adapter bug shared one field behind one message prefix, so the test had to
     `strings.Contains` the message to learn which of two disjoint meanings it
     had. `Err` is also the walk's stop condition, so writing an adapter bug
     into it makes *"the walk stopped on a source fault"* a lie — and a CLI
     would report a bug in `jsonsrc` to a user as a broken document.
  8. **`Assess` carries no `GAP(` marker and says so at the site**: a marker
     tracks a construct whose verdict is withheld, and a scaffold that judges
     nothing withholds no verdict. It is not a fail-open.
- Surprises:
  1. **The issue's own import-ban criterion was unsatisfiable, and the fix was
     to ban two different things.** `encoding/json` is in the closure of every
     package in this module that logs, via `log/slog`'s `JSONHandler`, so
     banning it outright bans logging. `validate/imports_test.go` therefore
     bans `encoding/xml`, `encoding/asn1` and `parser/...` over the **whole
     transitive closure**, and adds `encoding/json` to a **module-edge** ban —
     no package of this module in the closure may import it — which is the only
     route by which the engine could actually decode with it. A `seen < 3`
     floor closes the vacuous-scan hole, and `doc.go` states the weaker claim
     instead of keeping the false stronger one. Warden's ruling on its own
     acceptance criterion: *"the import-ban deviation is approved, and its
     reasoning is right where my acceptance criterion was wrong."*
  2. **The `Enabled()` guards leave `walk.attribute` and `walk.text` with no
     body under the silent default.** Correct — a walk that decides no rule
     does nothing at an attribute — but two empty methods are what the next
     session inlines away, so both carry a comment naming the rule that lands
     in them (`cvc-attribute` §3.2.4.1; `cvc-type` clause 3.1.3's ·initial
     value·). The guards themselves are not a micro-optimization: every
     `slog.Any` argument boxes a `QName` and a `Loc` at the call site, on every
     information item of every instance document, to be discarded.
  3. **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s footnote `[1]` was written for a `validate` that
     had not shipped and carved it back out three sentences after calling its

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Both conjuncts as ONE test, one rule ID.** They read the same set, so
     `checkOwnTransitiveMembership` walks the membership and
     `checkMemberNotDerivedFrom` walks each member's base chain with M ITSELF at
     step zero — M = D there is conjunct 1, a later step is conjunct 2. The two
     are told apart in the message and not in the verdict (STYLE E2).
  2. **A per-root visited set, created and discarded inside the pass**, threaded
     into no later traversal (PRINCIPLES 9), for the reason above.
  3. **Roots are the named top-level types in document order** (STYLE D2), and
     no violation escapes: a cycle needs an edge INTO an already-visited node,
     an anonymous type is held by exactly one owning slot, and only a by-name
     `SimpleTypeRef` resolving through the type index can name a second referrer.
     A conjunct-2 violation whose D is an ANONYMOUS union is charged against the
     type that owns D as its base — provably complete, not merely convenient,
     since the offending member's chain must pass through that owner, and

- **The pre-flight is where this issue's cost was paid, and it was paid on the
  ISSUE BODY rather than on code.** Three rulings rewrote acceptance criteria
  before mason started:
  1. **No hint return, no third return value.** `Validate` keeps
     `(*validate.Result, error)` as committed, and `xsi:schemaLocation` /
     `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` reach the caller as ordinary
     `Attributes()` entries — three grounds, and the first is structural:
     `validate.Result`'s fields are unexported with no setter, so "reported
     through the `Result`" cannot be built without widening `validate`'s
     surface, which this issue forbids. The second is that the value would have
     no consumer — `Validate` already holds a compiled `*Validator` and has
     consumed `r`, so a caller learning hints from it can neither load a schema
     nor re-read the instance (STYLE T5). The third is that it drags `parser`
     into the instance adapter.
  2. **No `Resolver` parameter and no `Resolver` option** — the acceptance text
     was describing a test that cannot be written, since nothing reachable from
     `Validate` touches `loader`, so a failing double has no call site to
     observe and passing one proves only that an unused parameter is unused.
     The substitute pins MORE: `imports_test.go` asserts `go list -deps
     ./validate/xmlsrc` reaches neither `loader` nor `parser` — **exact match,
     because `parser/xmltree` is the legitimate dependency and the model test's
     `matchesPackage` is a prefix match** — with a positive control requiring
     `parser/xmltree` present, so a scan that walks nothing cannot pass.
  3. **`doc.go`'s dangling `parser.SchemaLocationHints` forward reference is
     DELETED, not reworded**, along with the "not yet implemented" heading. The
     instance-hint reader wants grounding this issue does not have (§4.3.2
     clause 4 base-URI resolution, §2.6.3's paired form) and already has named
     consumers at `cmd/goxsd8/doc.go:14` — a separate issue, not a split.
- Decisions made and why — the rest of the pre-flight, all of it design ahead
  of code, and the diff implements it without deviation:
  1. **The error channel splits on WHETHER THE WALK BEGAN, not on kind.**
     `(nil, err)` only when `Assess` never ran — nil `*Validator`, nil
     `io.Reader`, no root element — and `(result, nil)` in every case where it
     did, a mid-document source fault living in `Result.Err()` alone and never
     also returned. Nil-argument errors are plain `fmt.Errorf` on `validate.New`'s
     stated reasoning; a pre-root malformed document returns the `*xsderr.Error`
     xmltree already produced, with `RuleXMLWellFormed` and a `Loc`.
  2. **The cursor is DEPTH-TRACKED and does not rely on the engine's drain
     discipline for correctness.** The walker carries a `depth`, each cursor the
     depth of its owning element, and `Next` discards tokens while the walker
     is deeper before pulling its own. The #710 contract makes trusting the
     engine safe *today*, but the first path that yields a child element and
     does not descend is `processContents="skip"`, arriving in this milestone,
     and the failure mode is a subtree's tokens fed to the parent as siblings —
     misvalidating with no error at all. Cost is one int and a loop.
  3. **A `done` latch on the cursor** when it pulls its matching `EndElement`,
     so a second `Next()` after exhaustion returns false instead of stealing
     the parent's next sibling off the shared stream.
  4. **The source fault is latched ONCE, on the walker**, and every cursor's
     `Err()` reports that one field — `assess.go`'s `children` reads `Err()`
     only on the cursor whose loop ended and short-circuits every ancestor, so
     one latched fault is still reported exactly once (STYLE D4).
  5. **One `Text` per `*xmltree.CharData`, never coalesced**, and depth-0
     character data dropped: `<a>x<![CDATA[y]]>z</a>` is three runs the engine
     concatenates, and coalescing would leave `Loc()` on the first run while
     `Data()` spanned all three.
  6. **`*xmltree.CharData` is handed over unwrapped** — warden's own ruling
     after re-checking the tree, and the load-bearing reason is now in the
     `var _` block's comment: `validate/imports_test.go` bans
     `github.com/kud360/goxsd8/parser` by PREFIX over the whole closure, so the
     engine structurally cannot NAME the concrete type and the type switch a
     wrapper would prevent is not constructible.
  7. **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s three assertions ride THIS commit.** It said
     xmlsrc was `doc.go`-only and imported nothing from the module at `:35`,
     `:43` and `:411-412`; this landing falsifies all three and ARCHITECTURE
     owns that fact, so the repair is an ordering constraint, not a follow-up
     (STYLE T6).
  8. **`TestNamespaceDeclarationsAreNotAttributes` is absorbed onto the real
     adapter**, discharging #710's non-blocking verdict note: it asserted a
     property of the in-package double, where no production path could break
     it, and now fails for a real reason if `xmltree.resolveAttrs` or the
     adapter regresses. The fixture test stays; guarding the double against
     drift is its own job.
- **The repair round — three REQUIRED findings, and the third is the one worth
  remembering.**
  1. **`Children()` called out of the documented single-call-per-element
     contract was SILENTLY WRONG, and one branch of it reported `io.EOF` to a
     user for a well-formed document.** Take child A, call `parent.Next()`
     (which discards A's subtree), then call `A.Children()`: the cursor is
     keyed on depth alone, so it hands back the SIBLING's children as A's. The
     variant where the parent was drained first pulls at EOF and latches a bare
     `io.EOF` into `walker.err` — reaching `Result.Err()` as the only fault in
     the module that is not an `*xsderr.Error`. The fix is a monotone token
     counter `n` on the walker, an `n` recorded on each `element` at the moment
     it was yielded, and a **panic** when they differ — the same
     contract-violation panic `validate` itself takes in `ElementChild` and
     `walk.child`, and refusing loudly beats the only alternative a depth-keyed
     cursor has, which is answering with another element's children. The guard
     makes the `io.EOF` path unreachable, which the arbiter confirmed by probe
     over five well-formed documents rather than by reading the repair.
  2. **The `GAP(xml)` marker named no tracking issue** — both existing
     `GAP(xml)` markers end `Tracked by #361`, and WORKFLOW makes a `kind/gap`
     issue the condition for a fail-open site. Both marker texts now end
     `Tracked by #753`.
  3. **The gap was WIDER than its own marker said.** `walker.root`'s `continue`
     drops character data BEFORE the document element too, so `junk before<r/>`
     — not well-formed, XML 1.0 §2.1 admits only `Misc` in the prolog — returns
     `err == nil` with `Result.Err() == nil`; reproduced by warden and again by
     the arbiter. Both markers now read *"content OUTSIDE the document element
     is not inspected"* and spell out both halves, and `root`'s doc comment no
     longer asserts the dropped data "is the prolog's whitespace" when it can be
     anything. **Enforcement is not this issue's**: `parser/document.go:85-89`
     carries the identical leniency with the identical comment, so the check
     belongs in `parser/xmltree` where it fixes both.
  All four DISCRETIONARY findings were discharged in the same round:
  `c.done = true` is gone from the fault branch (the field keeps its single
  documented meaning, and the `c.w.err != nil` guard already stops the cursor);
  the switch over the sealed `xmltree.Node` sum gained a `default:` carrying the
  one sentence that justifies dropping an unmodelled arm; the `var _` comment
  gained the real reason above; and the char-data test is renamed
  `TestPrologCharDataIsDropped` with its trailing whitespace removed, because
  the trailing half is not dropped by the depth rule — it is never read, which

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The split is at the backend seam, and the spec licenses it.** Everything
     the original filing named divides cleanly into what a lexical value needs
     (`value.ValidateLexical`, so a `value.Backend` reaching the walk) and what
     an ·expanded name· settles on its own. cvc-au is *"equal or identical to"*
     the fixed `{value}` — value-space, never raw lexical string comparison —
     so it is VACUOUSLY true for a use with no fixed constraint and needs
     nothing, while clause 2's Note (*"the attribute use always takes
     precedence"*) makes 2.1 decidable without touching 2.2. That is the whole
     cut: **#714 is names, #766 is values.**
  2. **The root only, and its `[[attributes]]` only.** A descendant's
     ·governing type definition· comes from matching it to a content model,
     which is #715's; the walk carries no governing type below the root and
     charges nothing there. Attribute existence at the root is the largest
     decidable set available before that lands.
  3. **Clause 2 is charged on a STRUCTURAL fact about the rule, not on an
     approximation.** "The appropriate case among the following is true" ranges
     over exactly {2.1, 2.2}: an attribute matching no use, whose type has no
     `{attribute wildcard}` at all, satisfies neither disjunct and violates
     clause 2 outright. Wildcard PRESENCE is a `(Wildcard, bool)` read, not an
     evaluation — where one is present the attribute is declined instead.
  4. **The `{type table}` guard was added beyond the prompt and is right.**
     key-selected-type is two cases and case 2 (`D.{type definition}`) is
     reached only in a table's ABSENCE, with key-cta-select making the fallback
     a Type Alternative's type rather than the declaration's — so charging
     attributes against `D.{type definition}` under a table is wrong in both
     directions (#56).
  5. **`attributePropertiesFolded` reads anonymity off `{name}`, not off the
     slot arm it was reached through.** `SubstitutionGroupHeadTypeRef` hands
     back a head-declaration-owned anonymous type without
     `InlineTypeDefinition` ever being involved, and the fold's real
     precondition is membership in `{type definitions}` (§3.17.2, all named).
     One anonymous shape is admitted — a RESTRICTION of `xs:anyType` by name —
     because both folds are provably the identity there: §3.4.7 gives
     `xs:anyType` an empty `{attribute uses}` so §3.4.2.4 clause 3 inherits
     nothing, and §3.4.2.5 clause 2.1 gives a restriction the ·complete
     wildcard· with no base union to miss. The trap that `xs:anyType` carries a
     lax `##any` wildcard of its own is not sprung, and
     `TestAnonymousRestrictionOfAnyTypeIsAssessed` pins exactly that by
     building the base WITH the wildcard and still charging.
  6. **`decidedNotValid` drops its exactly-one-violation gate.** Clauses 2 and
     3 quantify independently — over the attributes present and over the uses
     required — so one root can honestly carry several charges. The condition
     becomes "at least one, every one an enumerated rule"; the COUNT is not
     evidence of anything, and each enumerated rule is unconditional on its
     own, so a set of them is one too.
  7. **The duplicate switch was deleted, not left standing.**
     `attributeUseDeclarationName` in `xsd/attributegroupdefinition.go` was the
     same walk of the same sealed sum that `DeclarationName()` now provides;
     its one caller (`NewAttributeGroupDefinition`, ag-props-correct clause 2)
     moved over and the `stylecitations_test.go` allowance for its `STYLE T5/8`
     token was dropped in the same diff rather than left dangling (STYLE T4).
  8. **`(*Validator).Schema()` deliberately did not change.** The walk reaches
     the new methods through `v.schema` directly; `Schema()`'s one consumer is
     an external adapter and no adapter here needs type resolution. The
     warden's two alternative shapes — widening that capability, or a component
     method taking a resolver — were rejected for re-deriving
     `TypeDefinitionOrRef`'s three arms outside `xsd`, where the `exhaustive`
     linter does not check interface type switches and a fourth arm would
     compile silently.

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The backend is a parameter of `New`, not an Option, and nil panics.** The
     warden pre-flight ran against the issue's `## Surface: undecided by design`
     and ruled the shape before implementation: an Option needs a default, and the
     two available ones fail in opposite directions that a caller cannot see —
     `builtin/strict` silently substitutes a value space the schema was not
     compiled with, and a decline-everything backend makes an empty `Result` mean
     both "valid so far" and "this Validator can charge nothing". A required
     parameter makes neither state representable (PRINCIPLES 7). It broke every
     existing caller, all updated in the same commit: `conformance/instance.go`,
     `conformance/instance_test.go`, `validate/xmlsrc/xmlsrc_test.go` and
     `validate`'s own suite.
  2. **The classification is by EXCLUSION and the direction is FAIL-CLOSED, which
     is why the bound is the two marking sites and not the predicate.** An error
     is a verdict unless it wraps `errTypeFault`, so a stage `value` grows later
     whose fault goes unmarked is charged as a verdict — the exact false reject
     the predicate exists to prevent. Exclusion is not a safety net: it is what
     makes the predicate TOTAL over backend `Parse` errors, an open set that
     cannot be enumerated. What bounds the risk is that marking has exactly two
     sites, `typeFault` and `facetPrecondition`, so `grep typeFault(` plus
     `grep facetPrecondition(` enumerates the class.
  3. **`errFacetPrecondition` WRAPS `errTypeFault` rather than sitting beside
     it.** A precondition fault is one KIND of type fault, so the narrow predicate
     (`IsFacetPrecondition`, "which fault", asked only by `dispatchUnion` and
     `checkEnumerationRestriction`) and the wide one read one chain and the
     classification has a single encoding (STYLE T4/D4). `valueSpace.ValidDefault`
     shed three of its four hand-written gates in the same move: the ungoverned-type
     and compile-failure pre-checks were the wide class stated twice, and only the
     `needsContext` gate — which must run BEFORE the pipeline — remains.
  4. **An ungoverned ·special· datatype is not a gap; a backend coverage hole
     is.** Datatype Valid is unconditionally true for `xs:anySimpleType`, so
     declining there loses nothing and marking it `GAP(validate)` would file a
     tracker against the spec. The genuine declines — an ungoverned type the
     backend SHOULD map, an absent/complex `{type definition}`, an undecided fixed
     comparison — carry markers and a tracker (#774).
  5. **cvc-attribute clause 4 and cvc-au are independent and BOTH can fire on one
     attribute.** Clause 4 tests `D.{value constraint}`, cvc-au tests
     `U.{value constraint}`; au-props-correct clause 3 reconciles the two at schema
     assembly rather than making either instance check redundant, so
     `matchedAttribute` calls `fixedAgreement` twice and neither call subsumes the
     other. `useFixed` reads the USE's own property and never the ·effective value
     constraint·, which would substitute the declaration's fixed value for a use
     carrying none and charge cvc-au for an agreement the rule does not demand.
  6. **`EffectiveValueConstraint` is exported on `*Schema`, not modeled on
     `AttributeUse`.** The Ref variant's declaration is reachable only through the
     schema's `{attribute declarations}`, so a method on the use would need a
     schema back-pointer or would silently answer for the Local variant alone; the
     receiver matches its sibling `ResolvedAttributeDeclaration`. Its two callers
     both invoke the term BY NAME — finalize's `checkAttributeValueConstraintSubsumes`
     (loc-testSubP clause 5.2) and the ·defaulted attribute· definition's own
     clause 3 — and its doc says outright that cvc-au and cvc-attribute clause 4
     are NOT among them.
  7. **`ResolvedSimpleType` replaced `simpleTypeOf` outright rather than being
     added beside it**, and the `stylecitations_test.go` T8 allowance went with the
     "unexported until a consumer justifies exporting it" sentence it decorated
     rather than being left dangling (STYLE T4, the same discipline #714 applied to
     `attributeUseDeclarationName`).
  8. **`ConstraintMatches` parses the two sides under DIFFERENT contexts, and that
     asymmetry is the export's whole justification.** The instance side resolves a
     QName lexical against the bindings in scope where the attribute was written,
     the constraint side against `constraintContext(vc)`'s — the bindings in scope
     where its `{lexical form}` was written in the schema document (§3.3.18). One
     shared context decides a QName agreement wrongly in both directions. The
     warden weighed a bare `equalOrIdentical`-style relation instead and rejected
     it: the caller would have had to re-derive `constraintContext`'s
     dual-namespace invariant outside `value`, which is where it is encoded.
  9. **A side that fails to validate is undecided, never a mismatch.** For the
     instance side no verdict is lost — a lexical outside the type's lexical space
     already fails clause 3, and reporting "not the same value" for what is really
     "not a value at all" charges twice for one defect
     (`TestAnInvalidLexicalChargesClauseThreeAlone` pins it). For the constraint
     side it is the schema's own cos-valid-simple-default obligation, charged at
     finalize.
  10. **Clause 4's charge is rare BY CONSTRUCTION, not by accident.** A schema
      finalized with a value space installed has already charged
      cos-valid-simple-default against the same `{lexical form}` under
      a-props-correct clause 2 or au-props-correct clause 2, so only a schema
      assembled through `xsd.SchemaBuilder.Finalize` — which installs none —
      reaches the instance with an invalid default still in it. It is charged
      anyway because `validate` may not assume its schema's provenance.
  11. **`imports_test.go`'s anti-vacuity assertion was FIXED, not widened.** The
      warden ruled the stale `seen < 3` message the defect: the closure is an
      ALLOWED-TO-GROW set, so a count assertion breaks every time the closure
      legitimately grows and says nothing about what was walked. It now asserts
      that three packages the closure cannot lose were each SEEN by name, and
      `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` note [2] — where the closure of the day is stated —
      gains `value` and `regex`, never `builtin/strict`.
  12. **The simple-content charge was split out rather than carried.**
      cvc-complex-type clause 1.2 needs its own ·initial value·-from-`Text`
      grounding that the four attribute charges do not share, so it is **#775**
      (`ready`), filed on the warden's own split guidance. Two `kind/gap` trackers
      went with it: **#773** (String Valid clause 3's ENTITY check) and **#774**
      (the three declines cvc-attribute and cvc-au must make).

## 2026-08-14 — #715 — xsd,validate: the CONTENT half of `cvc-complex-type` (§3.4.4.2) clause 1 lands and M5's pull driver exists — `xsd/contentmatcher.go` ships `(*Schema).ContentMatcher`, `Matcher`, `Next`, `Accepting` and the sealed `Attribution`, an instance-guided advance of a complex type's `{content type}` particle that **COUNTS occurrences over a flattened tree instead of unfolding them** (`maxOccurs="100000"` costs one `int`) and **commits to one particle per item with no backtracking**, licensed structurally rather than assumed: a `Matcher` is reachable only through a `*Schema`, which only `Finalize` produces, so `cos-nonambig` (§3.8.6.4) has already rejected two ·competing· element particles, and where an element particle and a wildcard both admit one name cvc-accept's own closing Note fixes the answer, which `Next` encodes as a search ORDER (elements first, wildcards only on a miss); the one non-determinism those two do not settle — cvc-accept's named nested-repetition partition, where `(a{1,2}, b?){2,2}` accepts `"aab"` as `(a)(ab)` and a greedy walk consumes it as one iteration and rejects — is **DECLINED at construction**, alongside `{open content}` (#717) and an all group holding an all group, so **a `Matcher` that exists decides every name put to it and never declines mid-sequence**; `validate/cvccomplexcontent.go` drives it for the ROOT's `[[children]]` and decides clause 1 in full (1.1 empty, 1.2 simple, 1.3 element-only white space, 1.4 into cvc-complex-content), charging the offending child's own `Loc` or the containing element's when the sequence ends short; the durable content is that **mason ran a false-reject probe MID-implementation and it found five, all one bug** — an all-group member was being held to its `{min occurs}` on exit, which §3.8.4.1.3's interleave forbids, since a member is SUSPENDED and resumed rather than finished — fixed and pinned before the arbiter ever saw it; **warden APPROVE against its own pre-flight, arbiter ACCEPT on round 1, zero repair rounds**, surface exactly **`+5 −0`**, **`Ratchet: instance 193 → 520 pass of 26361 (+327)`**, banked as **`060a235`**

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The walk COUNTS; it does not unfold.** State is one occurrence counter
     per particle of the flattened model plus the path the last item was
     ·attributed to·. This is the opposite trade from
     `xsd/particleattribution.go`'s automaton, and the two are deliberately NOT
     shared: `automaton.addAll` accepts a documented SUPERSET of the interleave
     language, which is the right direction for a schema constraint (·compete·
     is a question about the MODEL) and a **false accept** for an instance one,
     and its unfolding bound changes the accepted language outright — `e{3,6}`
     reads as `e{2,4}`. What IS reused is the determinism `cos-nonambig`
     already decided, which is why nothing here re-derives Glushkov.
  2. **Every decline is made ONCE, at construction.** `ContentMatcher` returns
     `(nil, false)` or a matcher that answers everything; there is no
     mid-sequence decline. A matcher that gave up halfway would have matched
     part of a sequence and withheld the rest, and the caller cannot tell that
     apart from an accepted prefix.
  3. **The nested-repetition shape is declined rather than answered greedily,
     and the file states the PROOF that the greedy walk is exact on everything
     else** — a differing partition needs one particle reachable both later in
     an open iteration and at the start of the next, the shorter alternative
     iteration then holds no mandatory particle unless it holds that particle
     ITSELF taken again, which is a repeating particle inside a repeating one.
     `supported` is that proof's contrapositive and nothing more.
  4. **`Attribution` is a sealed sum of `ElementDeclaration` and `Wildcard`,
     and `ModelGroup` is deliberately not a variant.** Those are the two kinds
     of ·basic particle· §3.4.4.4 attributes an item to; returning `Term` would
     make an attribution to a model group representable (STYLE T1/T2's
     closed-sum exception). An `ElementDeclaration` result is the PARTICLE's
     declaration D, not the ·substituting declaration· S — resolving S through
     clause 2.3.2 is the recursive assessment's job (§3.3.4.6), and the doc
     says so rather than leaving a reader to assume it.
  5. **`ContentMatcher` is a method on `*Schema`, not a free constructor.** The
     walk rests on constraints `Finalize` has already decided — `cos-nonambig`
     for determinism, `mg-props-correct` clause 2 for the `<group ref>`
     acyclicity that lets the flattening carry **no visited set** (STYLE D4,
     PRINCIPLES 5) — and a `*Schema` is the one thing that cannot exist before
     they ran. `resolveTerm` reads the two ref arms through the existing
     in-package indices, so no `Schema.ModelGroup` accessor was minted for an
     in-package reader (STYLE T5).
  6. **#714's `attributePropertiesFolded` decline moved from `rootComplexType`
     to `walk.attributes`, in this diff, on purpose.** No finalize pass folds a
     `{content type}` the way §3.4.2.4 clause 3 folds `{attribute uses}` — a
     complex type's particle is whatever its producer built for it, named or
     anonymous — so gating the WHOLE governing type on the attribute-fold
     predicate over-declined the corpus for content. The halves now decline
     separately from one shared `rootComplexType`, and
     `TestAnonymousGoverningTypeStillDecidesContent` pins the split. This was
     #714's standing obligation and it is discharged here rather than carried.
  7. **An element carrying `xsi:nil` decides NOTHING**, marked `GAP(xsd)`
     (#716). Clause 1 applies only where E is not ·nilled·, and ·nilled·
     (cvc-elt clause 3.2) needs the `{nillable}` of the ·governing element
     declaration· and the ·actual value· of the attribute, neither of which
     this dispatch has; attribute PRESENCE is the upper bound on it, exactly as
     `hasInstanceType` is for `xsi:type`. Withholding costs a rejection and
     manufactures none.
  8. **One element carries at most one content charge.** Every clause says the
     same thing about the element once charged — not locally ·valid·, so
     cvc-type clause 3.2 fails — and the first charge is the one at the
     offending position. Continuing to match past a rejected child would report
     the rest of the sequence against a position the document never reached.
     `TestContentChargesOneElementOnce` pins it.
  9. **A run of NO characters is not a character information item.** Both
     clause 1.1 and clause 1.3 quantify over items in `[[children]]`, and an
     adapter reporting an empty run for `<e></e>` has reported a run, not an
     item — so `<e></e>` against empty content is not charged.
  10. **Clause 1.2's other half was NOT absorbed.** The ·initial value· against
      the `{simple type definition}` (cvc-simple-type, §3.16.4) needs its own
      grounding and stays #775's; this file decides only that simple content
      admits no element information item child.
- Surprises:
  1. ***The false-reject probe found five real ones, all from a single bug, and
     it ran BEFORE the arbiter.*** Mason charged every suite-VALID instance
     case with the new unconditional rules and looked at what got rejected — a
     class the ratchet is structurally blind to, since this lane scores only
     negative expectations and a false reject on a valid case moves no number
     in either direction. The bug was `canExit` requiring an all-group member
     to have met its `{min occurs}` before the group could be left. §3.8.4.1.3
     makes an all group's language the INTERLEAVE `S1 × … × Sn` of its members'
     sequences, so a member is suspended and resumed when the next item belongs
     to a sibling; what the member owes is owed **to the group**, which
     `iterationComplete` collects from every member at once. The fix is that
     `canExit` skips the min test for a member of an all group, and
     `TestMatcherResumesAnAllGroupMemberThatOwesOccurrences` pins it. **A probe
     the ratchet cannot run found a defect no gate step would have caught.**
  2. ***The lane's largest movement to date came with zero repair rounds.***
     +327 is nearly twice #766's +164 and it landed on warden APPROVE and
     arbiter ACCEPT round 1. The reason is visible in the shape of the session:
     the surface was ruled BEFORE a line was written, by a pre-flight the
     session did not even pay for, and the one defect that would have drawn a
     reject was found and fixed by the implementer's own probe.
  3. ***`Open/open013.v1.xml` is a false reject, and its cause is in the
     PARSER, not in anything this diff touched.*** Mason reported the case; the
     arbiter traced it further. `parser/produce_complex.go`'s `boolAttr` is
     `return v == "true" || v == "1", true` — no `whiteSpace=collapse`, which
     `xs:boolean` mandates — and `open013.xsd` writes `<xs:complexType mixed="
     1 ">`. The literal is valid `xs:boolean`; goxsd8 reads it as `false`, the
     type comes out element-only, and the instance's `(` and `)` are charged
     clause 1.3 against a suite-valid document. **This is not a `mixed` bug: it
     affects every boolean-valued schema attribute** — `abstract`, `nillable`,
     `mixed`, `appliesToEmpty`, all of them — and wants its own issue at a
     generality mason's original framing did not reach.
  4. **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `xsd/doc.go` both still asserted that the

     labelled *"a destination"*. Corrected in the same commit. Two documents
     naming an absent component is cheap; two documents naming it after it

  implemented #775: gate green, `instance` +3, **#759 absorbed** with the
  **LEADING**-label decision. The checkpoint push was rejected — the

  #716 for **orthogonality to the live #775 diff** — correctly, and it still

  ·[schema actual value]·s, a notion §3.3.5.4 defines **only where a governing
  type is known**, compared under Datatypes §2.2 Equality/Identity with **no
  lexical-comparison fallback licensed by any clause**. The engine types the
  ·validation root· and nothing below it. **Root-only, there is no honest
  charge to make and no lane movement to win** — an implementation would have
  had to fabricate one. Stood down before a line was written.

  - ***#790 filed***: thread the ·context-determined declaration· into

     race rule decides this and there was nothing to weigh. Salvaging would
     mean rebasing an unjudged implementation onto a pushed one and asking an
