## 2026-08-15 — #722 — tooling: a `wip/issue-<N>` branch that has pushed **no commits of its own** stops being dated by git at all and reports **CLAIMED** — `go tool wipsurvey` was reading such a branch's tip as the branch's own age, but that tip is the landing it branched from, so a claim made minutes ago read as hours old, **EXPIRED, and therefore resumable**, which is how three sessions in two days walked into a live holder's work; `remoteRefs` now asks for `refs/heads/main` in the **same `ls-remote` round trip** that already enumerates `refs/heads/wip/*` — one network call for both — `gitAncestry` maps `git merge-base --is-ancestor`'s exit **0/1/other** onto `ancestryNoCommits`/`ancestryOwnCommits`/`ancestryUnresolved` (128, an unfetched object, is git declining to answer, not a "no"), and `classify` now answers **four ordered questions** — retirement, unfetched tip, no-commits-of-its-own, then age — so a CLAIMED branch is never retired on an age reading and `renderTable` prints **`main's`** in its TIP AGE column rather than a number the branch did not earn; the verdict's name is WORKFLOW's own sentence, ***"the name is the claim; the tip time is the lease"***; and the session that shipped it **opened by losing a race to exactly this defect**, on `wip/issue-790`, an hour before it picked the issue that describes it

- Shipped on `wip/issue-722`, base **`8e8b45b`**, resumed from a prior
  session's expired claim — that holder posted the **GROUNDING at 08:16Z** and
  went silent, **verified against the issue thread's own clock and not the tip
  clock**, which is the manual check this landing replaces. **Four commits plus
  this entry:** **`c30e31e`** (the resume claim), **`3521642`** (mason's
  implementation, merged at **`cde728c`**), **`a32960f`** (`origin/main` merged
  forward mid-session) and **`1d89cf2`** (arbiter advisory 3 absorbed). Landing
  diff `git diff origin/main...HEAD --numstat` is **5 files, +344/−32**:
  `tools/wipsurvey/main.go` (+143/−26), `tools/wipsurvey/main_test.go`
  (+190/−2), `.claude/commands/develop.md` (+6/−2), `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (+4/−1),
  `CLAUDE.md` (+1/−1). **Spec read: none — no XSD rule governs this.** The
  normative text is WORKFLOW's **claim-TTL invariant**, which now states that a
  branch with no commits of its own has no tip time of its own and is never
  EXPIRED on age; `.claude/commands/develop.md`'s verdict enumeration gains
  **CLAIMED and the previously-missing UNKNOWN**, and CLAUDE.md's survey comment
  enumerates all five. **Verdicts on the #722 thread: `5302729363`** (round 1)
  and **`5302859779`** (gate-only, on the merged tree).
- **Ratchet: unchanged, copied from the accept verdicts and not recomputed.**
  Round 1: **`datatypes` 1161/1173, `schema` 12832/15398, `instance`
  535/26361** — *"ratchet run, tree clean, nothing to bank"*, which is the
  expected result for a change that touches no library code. On the merged
  tree the arbiter re-read `instance` at **main's new 1017**, carried in by
  `a32960f` and **attributed to #790**, not to this landing. `go tool surface
  -base origin/main` **unchanged** — everything added is unexported. **No
  expectations file was edited**, in either direction. The **#740
  unbanked-improvements-on-a-merged-tree hazard was checked by two instruments
  and is absent.**
- ***The session lost the race the issue describes, before it picked the
  issue.*** Invoked as **`/develop 790`**. The survey was clean and **every
  remote `wip` branch read EXPIRED off tip age**; the session resumed
  `wip/issue-790` — **a zero-commit lease sitting exactly at main's tip
  `8e8b45b`** — posted a RESUME comment, and was **rejected at the heartbeat
  push**. The holder was alive: its GROUNDING was **12:29Z, an hour old**, and
  it pushed its implementation moments later. WORKFLOW's race rule was applied
  without argument — back off, pick something else — and **only survey time was
  lost, because the rejection came at the heartbeat and not after a mason
  round.** Recorded on #722 as **comment `5302465772`**: a fresh incident,
  observed by the session that then fixed it.
- **Mason round — worktree isolation, ~105k tokens, ~34 minutes.** The
  classification is four arms in one pure `classify`, tested without git or
  network; `partitionRefs` and `ancestryFromExit` were split out as pure
  functions for the same reason. `ancestryUnresolved` **falls back to the tip
  age** rather than raising a second unknown verdict — the grounding prescribed
  it, the arbiter recorded the consequence as accepted (below).
- **Arbiter round 1 — ~142k tokens, ~33 minutes — ACCEPT, five advisories,
  none blocking.** Two findings are worth more than the verdict.
  ***Mutation testing proved the core tests real***: reverting the CLAIMED arm
  alone **fails four tests**. It also proved one test hollow —
  **`TestGitAncestryWithoutMain` cannot fail on the mechanism its name
  claims**, and passes for another reason; owed to the post-land pass.
  ***Live verification against the real remote*** (through the `gh` 403, by
  hand) **found two more zero-commit leases — `wip/issue-271` and
  `wip/issue-718` — both of which the old tool called EXPIRED and the new one
  calls CLAIMED.**
- **The base moved twice mid-session and the merge was clean.** #790 landed on
  `main` (`instance` **535 → 1017**) and a `/backlog` pass followed
  (**`2d6ec5c`**); `origin/main` merged forward at **`a32960f`** with **no
  `docs/LOG` conflict — solely because the chronicler had not yet appended.**
  A **gate-only arbiter round** (~31 minutes; **~150k cumulative** across both
  arbiter rounds) re-confirmed ACCEPT on the merged tree, full gate green, and
  **verified that the CLAIMED classification tracks `main` as it moves** rather
  than a snapshot taken at survey time.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Back off the #790 race at the first rejection.** The lease was
     arguable — the holder's branch carried no commits — and arguing it is
     precisely the failure mode. The cheap loss is the point: **detection at
     the heartbeat cost survey time where yesterday's detection at the
     checkpoint cost a whole mason round.**
  2. **Re-pick #722 itself.** The session had just produced the freshest
     possible evidence for it, and the alternative was to carry that evidence
     onto a thread and work on something else.
  3. **Add a fifth verdict rather than suppress EXPIRED.** A branch with no
     commits is not "expired but ignore it" — **nothing is known about its
     age**, and a verdict that says so is readable by the next session; a
     suppressed EXPIRED is a silence.
  4. **`ancestryUnresolved` falls back to the tip age.** Inventing a second
     unknown verdict would split UNKNOWN's meaning across two labels for a
     case this checkout cannot distinguish. **The cost is recorded, not
     hidden:** an unresolved row is indistinguishable in the report, which the
     grounding prescribed and the arbiter accepted.
  5. **Absorb all three doc edits into this landing.** WORKFLOW's invariant,
     the command's enumeration and CLAUDE.md's comment all state the same
     verdict set; shipping the tool without them would leave three documents
     describing a tool that no longer exists.
  6. **Merge `origin/main` forward and re-run the arbiter gate-only.** Not a
     re-judgement — the verdict stood — but the accept was earned on a
     different tree, and #740 is the reason that distinction is now
     instrumented.
- Surprises:
  1. ***The defect claimed a third session while that session was choosing the
     fix for it.*** The two prior incidents were survey readings on stale
     information; **this one was a clean survey**, correctly run, reporting
     EXPIRED because the tool's arithmetic is wrong. That is the whole

  2. ***Two more CLAIMED branches exist on the real remote right now***

     happened twice; it is the ordinary state of a branch between claim and

  3. **Mutation testing found a passing test that cannot fail on its own
     subject.** Four tests died when the CLAIMED arm was reverted;

  4. **The base moved twice and nothing conflicted** — including `docs/LOG`,

- Friction:

  2. **`gh` still has no GitHub access in this container.** The arbiter's live

  3. **The borrowed-age fact is now encoded in six places** — package doc,

- Cost: **one mason round (~105k tokens, ~34 minutes), two arbiter rounds

- Next:

  tool surface -base origin/main` **unchanged** — `tools/wipsurvey` is
  `package main` and exports nothing. **No expectations file was edited, in
  either direction.**
- **Mason round — worktree isolation, ~116.5k tokens, 73 tool calls, ~29
  minutes.** The order of work is the finding: **the hypothesis was
  measured against real repositories before it was coded against.** A
  checkout whose last fetch predates the newest landing on `main` holds a
  stale local SHA relative to what `ls-remote` reports live; `merge-base
  --is-ancestor` then exits **128** — the unfetched object — which
  `ancestryFromExit` maps to `ancestryUnresolved`, and #722's fallback
  dates the branch from the borrowed tip. Reproduced end to end, including
  the misclassification to **EXPIRED with no `CLAIMED` row to show for
  it**, and confirmed that `git fetch origin` closes the window. Three
  table cases plus **`TestClassifyMarksOnlyUndecidedAncestry`**, which pins
  the marker to `ancestryUnresolved` in **both directions** — present when
  git declined, absent on `ancestryOwnCommits` and `ancestryNoCommits` —
  mutation-tested by mason and again by the arbiter. Three doc comments
  that would otherwise have gone stale were refreshed in the same commit.
- **Arbiter round 1 — ~95.5k tokens, 48 tool calls, ~18 minutes — ACCEPT,
  no repair round, no STYLE findings.** It re-ran the **full four-part
  gate independently**, initializing `testdata/xsdtests` itself because a
  fresh clone arrives without the submodule; it **re-derived the 128/0/1
  exit mapping from git directly** rather than trusting the code's comment;
  and it **re-ran the mutation test both directions itself** instead of
  accepting mason's report of it.
- ***The measurement found a second, worse defect, and it was deliberately
  not fixed.*** In a **shallow** clone — the shape this session's own
  container has — both SHAs can be present while `--is-ancestor` still
  exits **1**, which maps to **`ancestryOwnCommits`**, not
  `ancestryUnresolved`. That is a **false EXPIRED carrying no marker at
  all**: #722's hazard fully restored, invisible to the fix that just
  landed, and **not reachable by any reason-string change** because it is a
  wrong verdict rather than a thin explanation. It also **makes #802's
  exculpation stale** — #802 says `wipsurvey` "must not be blamed", but it
  predates #722's ancestry test, and that test *does* depend on local
  reachability. Mason left it; the arbiter agreed and flagged it
  separately, marking its own note **unverified**.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Extend the reason string, do not add a sixth verdict.** The verdict
     set was enumerated in three documents by #722 yesterday; a sixth
     entry would reopen all three to describe a case that is not a new
     *state* of the branch but a **missing answer about it**. The row's
     verdict is still the best evidence available — the reason now says
     what that evidence is worth.
  2. **Reuse the remedy wording the UNKNOWN row already prints** —
     ``run `git fetch origin` `` — rather than composing a second. One
     phrasing for one remedy; a second would make the two greppable
     separately (STYLE P2), which is the six-places friction #722 already
     logged.
  3. **Leave the shallow-clone false negative to the cartographer.** It
     changes **verdicts, not reason text**, needs its own grounding, and
     folding it in would have made a two-file landing into a scope
     question mid-session. Scope held; the finding is carried on the
     thread, not in the diff.
  4. **Do not touch WORKFLOW.** The claim-TTL invariant already says what
     is true; the tool was under-reporting against it, and the fix belongs
     in the tool (PRINCIPLES 27).
- Surprises:
  1. ***A ledger item filed yesterday as "recorded as accepted, so it is
     visible rather than reopened" was the right thing to reopen, one day
     later.*** #722's fallback was correct as designed and still wrong in
     the report; the entry that filed it predicted neither.
  2. **Fixing the known gap is what exposed the unknown one.** The
     shallow-clone exit-1 path was found *while measuring the 128 path*,
     by someone who had built the harness to observe it — not by reading
     the code, which reads correctly.
  3. **The arbiter initialized the submodule to run the gate.** A fresh
     clone cannot run part 4 as written; this is environment shape, not a
     gate failure, and it cost the arbiter time in a landing that touches
     no conformance code at all.
- Friction:
  1. ***`wipsurvey`'s correctness depends on the checkout's fetch state and
     clone depth, and nothing in the pipeline guarantees either.*** Two
     defects in two days, both from the same root: the tool asks git a
     question about objects the container may not have. **`/retro` item —
     the answer is probably a fetch in the survey path, not a fourth
     reason string.**
  2. **`#802`'s "must not be blamed" line is now stale** and will exculpate
     the wrong component next time someone greps it. Filed as part of the
     follow-up below rather than edited here.
  3. **The submodule is not present in a fresh clone**, so every arbiter
     pays for part 4 even on tooling-only landings. Restated `/retro`
     item.
- Cost: **one develop iteration, one issue landed, zero repair rounds.**
  One mason round (~116.5k tokens, 73 tool calls, ~29 minutes), one
  arbiter round (~95.5k tokens, 48 tool calls, ~18 minutes), one
  chronicler entry. **No oracle, no warden** — no spec text governs a
  survey tool and nothing exported changed.
- Next:
  1. **Land by PR squash-merge, closing #806.**
  2. **Post-land ledger, for the cartographer — one issue:** the
     **shallow-clone `ancestryOwnCommits` false negative**, flagged
     independently by mason and the arbiter, **distinct from #802** and

     "`wipsurvey` must not be blamed" predates #722's ancestry test** and

  3. **#805 and #802 remain open and untouched.** Same file, disjoint

  4. **`wip/issue-718` was LIVE at survey time** (pushed ~19 minutes

  cost nothing in conformance because the gain was already banked and the repair
  moved it by zero. The five findings:
  1. **[STYLE T4/D3] two independent encodings of ·nilled·** — `nilCheck`
     re-derived the determination from its own arms instead of reading
     `nilled(e, g)`. They agreed arm for arm, which is the failure mode, not the
     defense.
  2. **[tests that cannot fail] two production-behavior swaps** —
     `hasInstanceNil` → `nilled` at two call sites — **with no test that could
     fail if reverted.**
  3. **[prose] an inverted description of `key-val-sub-type-absolute`**:
     `key-overrides` clause 2's ·validly substitutable without limitation· is
     the **EMPTY** blocking set, not an unlimited one.
  4. **[prose] an incomplete `GAP(xsd)` reader census** on
     `ValidlySubstitutable` — `checkSubstitutionGroupTypes` reaches
     `derivedOKSimple`'s empty-blocking-set gap through `validlyDerived` and was
     unnamed.
  5. **[STYLE D3] one redundant cached field**, `contentCheck.governing`,
     derivable from `g` and `nilled` with no measured hot path licensing the
     copy.
- **The repair (`12fa962`) fixed all five and answered finding 2 with tests that
  spell the misreading.** `nilCheck` now calls `nilled(e, g)`, gates the clause
  3.2.3.2 charge on it and returns it — one encoding.
  `TestOnlyANilledElementDeclinesTheIDTable` and
  `TestOnlyANilledFieldNodeWithholdsItsKeySequenceMember` pin `key-nilled`'s
  **conjunction** at exactly the two swapped sites, and each fails under **both**
  mutations: `nilled` reduced to `xsi:nil` PRESENCE, and `nilled` with the
  `D.{nillable}` conjunct dropped. **Zero conformance movement from the repair**,
  confirmed independently by mason's read-only run and by the re-judging
  arbiter's own gate run. The accept verified each of the five against the diff
  and by mutation **rather than trusting the repair report**, and re-confirmed
  the banked figure had not moved further.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **An unresolvable `xsi:type` charges nothing.** The Note under `cvc-elt`
     (W3C issue 11764) settles it, and the alternative is a false reject on
     every instance naming a type the schema never saw. Charging clause 4 there
     would have been a rejection the spec does not authorize, banked as
     conformance gain.
  2. **Export `Schema.ValidlySubstitutable` rather than reimplement the
     derivation checks.** A second copy of `cos-ct-derived-ok`/
     `cos-st-derived-ok` in `validate` is two encodings of one rule (STYLE T4),
     which is finding 1 at package scale.
  3. **Rename the unexported symbol, do not wrap it.** One implementation, four
     in-package consumers plus `validate`; a wrapper would have made the
     exported and unexported names greppable separately for one behavior.
  4. **`·nilled·` is read from the decision everywhere, never from `xsi:nil`
     presence.** The presence reading was a correct UPPER BOUND while the
     determination was undecidable, and became a wrong answer the moment it was
     not; the four GAP markers that carried it were repointed rather than left
     to age into lies.
- Surprises:

     not.*** Every one of the five findings sat behind a passing four-part gate
     and a +183 ratchet gain. **Two independent encodings that agree, and two
     behavior swaps no test can distinguish, are exactly what a gate is blind
     to** — this is the case the two-round cap exists to buy.
  2. **The warden was scheduled by being wrong.** "Surface: none expected" in
     the issue body meant no pre-flight was budgeted; the export appeared
     mid-implementation and the review had to be taken there instead. It found
     two real defects, so the cost of the misprediction was scheduling, not

  3. **The reject's finding 5 has a twin the reject did not name.**
     `contentCheck.nilled` is the same STYLE D3 shape as
     `contentCheck.governing`, in the same struct, and only one of them was
     charged.

- Decisions made and why:

     footing `rejectProhibitedAttrs`, `topLevelName` and `<include>`-without-
     `schemaLocation` already stand on.

     alone.** Two adjacent `use="prohibited"` attributes on one grammar type,
     one guard, one loop in the grammar's own declaration order — so a document
     writing both is always reported at `name` (STYLE D2). Splitting would have
     spent a whole landing on one string in a slice.

     `parser/redefine_test.go` and `parser/override_redefine_test.go` already

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **A new Phase D step, AGAINST the issue's literal Acceptance criterion.**
     The criterion named `resolveTypeTable`, which is Phase A. Both sides are
     resolved there, so the placement was not unreasonable — it is wrong for a
     reason the issue could not see: the relation it calls is an unguarded chain
     walk, and Phase B is what makes such a walk safe. **The failure mode of the
     issue's placement is a HANG, not a wrong answer**, which is why it was
     overridden in implementation rather than repaired by a narrower charge.
  2. **Clause 7 runs AFTER clause 4** (`checkSubstitutionGroupTypes`), so a
     declaration failing both reports the failure that does not depend on its
     type table.
  3. **The step walks by DESCENT, not over `s.elements`.** §3.3.2.1's
     `{type table}` row is a COMMON mapping rule the parser serves from both
     local `<element>` paths, so a local declaration carries a table exactly as a
     top-level one does — the same conclusion `checkComponentValueConstraints`
     reaches for clause 2, and the opposite of clause 4's `s.elements`-only
     quantifier, which rests on clause 3 confining `{substitution group
     affiliations}` to global scope. **No clause confines a `{type table}`.**
  4. **Clause 7.2 by expanded name, decided first, unexported.** A `Schema`
     holds at most one component per expanded name and the alternative's QName is
     already namespace-resolved, so identity by name is sound and needs no
     `xsd.Error()` accessor for a singleton nothing else roots on (STYLE T5).
  5. **`{disallowed substitutions}` threaded through unchanged.** It is a subset
     of `{substitution, extension, restriction}` (§3.3.1) while
     `key-val-sub-type`'s blocking set also admits `list` and `union`; the
     members the narrower property cannot name are inert there, not errors. It is
     read off the unexported field rather than through `DisallowedSubstitutions()`,
     whose defensive copy would be allocated only to be discarded.
  6. **Two fail-open skips, both withholding a rejection and never inventing
     one:** an ·absent· or unresolvable declared type skips the whole table
     (clause 7.1 predicates over that component, so there is nothing for T to be
     substitutable FOR), and an alternative naming no component in the schema is
     skipped (a dangling name was already charged `src-resolve` in Phase A).
  7. **The three broken fixtures were absorbed, not filed.** They are the same
     edit as the change that invalidated them, which WORKFLOW's scope rule wants

## 2026-08-16 — /retro (weekly, sixth) — the two patterns the log had been COUNTING for two weeks are fixed at their entry points instead of routed a sixth time: the `gh` 403 becomes a fall-through rule in `docs/ROUTINES.md` and both surveys gain their no-`gh` spelling in CLAUDE.md, discharging **#527, #668 and #682** — three `ready`, doc-only, fully-specified issues that sat unpicked for ten days while their friction recurred in a dozen sessions; the base-drift merge-forward moves BEFORE the verdict, where a moved base costs no round instead of one; `retro.md` sheds the thirty lines that restated `chronicler.md`; and the durable finding is the META-pattern under all three — **a `ready` process issue is never picked**, because the cartographer's banding rule ranks on lane movement and process work moves no lane, so the fix lands there and not as another rule nobody reads

- Trigger: weekly `/retro` over the window since the fifth retro (2026-08-09
  → 2026-08-16). Evidence: **65 in-window LOG entries**, the `needs-replan`
  query (**1 issue, #822**, queried through the MCP channel, not assumed), the
  full `ready` list (**181**), `go tool lanestatus` on the committed tree, and
  the issue threads themselves — #527, #668, #682, #802, #831, #836, #741,
  #584, #822 read in full. Chronicler Part 1 only; the steward's Part 2
  architecture audit is delegated separately.
- **`git log` could not supply this retro's commit counts, and the reason is a
  finding.** The container's checkout is **shallow** — 50 commits visible,
  reaching back only to 08-12 — so `git log --since` over an eight-day window
  silently returns the whole visible history instead of the window. Every
  count below is therefore derived from the LOG entries, which are complete for
  the window, and **not** from `git log`. This is #802's defect hitting a
  reader rather than a planner, first-hand, and it is why the shallow clone is
  now written into `docs/ROUTINES.md` as an environment fact rather than
  living only in an issue body.

- **Recurring friction #1 (FIXED here) — the specialist sandbox has no GitHub
  channel, and the fix has been filed, specified and unpicked since 08-06.**
  - **The record is not a handful of sightings; it is a standing condition.**
    `grep` over `docs/LOG/2026-08.md` returns **thirty-one** entries recording
    a `gh` 403, and the entries' own counters climb from *"third consecutive
    session"* (#447) through *"the fifth"* (#738) to *"the twelfth-plus"*
    (#806, #722). In THIS window's last eight landings it cost the log its
    `issuecomment-*` pointers twice (#716, #830), forced the orchestrator to
    proxy-post for the warden once (#821), and reduced `go tool gapaudit` to
    marker-inventory-only in the arbiter's container twice (#813, #800).
  - **The problem statement everyone was using is wrong, and #822's entry is
    the one that says so.** Warden DID have a channel on #822 and posted
    directly. So the condition is not "specialist sandboxes have no `gh`" — it
    is that **`gh` is 403 everywhere and the MCP channel usually works**, and
    which agent holds which channel varies per invocation. Reproduced
    first-hand in this session: `gh api repos/kud360/goxsd8/issues/830` → 403
    *"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect
    the Claude GitHub App for this organization"*, while
    `mcp__github__issue_read` served every issue this retro needed.
  - **Entry point = `docs/ROUTINES.md`, which owns environment, and CLAUDE.md,

    order for setup* and said nothing about what to do when the preferred
    channel errors at call time; CLAUDE.md's survey block spelled both
    pipelines as `gh issue list … | go tool …` and nothing else, so a 403 read
    as "the tool is unavailable" — and #523's session hand-surveyed the branch

- **Recurring friction #3 (FIXED here) — an issue body's rule IDs read exactly
  like spec text.** #716's grounding caught **two** spec errors in the body,
  one citation and one verdict, and its entry names the cost precisely: *"the
  issue body's sub-clause IDs cannot be treated as spec text — but they read

  correcting, and propagated it into `docs/PLAN.md` where it was unbounded.

  park, which is the shape that works. WORKFLOW's filing discipline already
  binds the WRITER (*"check every citation against the tree … again before
  grounding something already filed"*); nothing bound the READER. **Fixed in
  `.claude/agents/oracle.md`**, integrated into the sentence that already
  forbids answering from memory: never from the issue body either — a body's
  rule IDs are a claim to check, not a premise to inherit, and the oracle says
  so when its reading contradicts them. One clause, no new section.
- **The meta-pattern, and the most durable thing this retro found: a `ready`
  process issue is never picked, so the process fixes itself only at retros.**
  - **#527 (filed 08-06), #668 (08-10) and #682 (08-11) were `ready`, doc-only,
    and specified down to the paragraph.** Every one names the file and the
    sentences to write. None was ever picked. Across the same ten days their
    friction was recorded in a dozen entries, each ending *"`/retro` item"* or
    *"restated `/retro` item"*. **#565** — which the fifth retro called *"the
    develop iteration to take next"* — and **#400** — which it called *"the
    oldest undischarged retro recommendation"* — are both still `ready`, still
    unmoved, one retro later.
  - **The mechanism is in `cartographer.md` step 4, and it is a sentence doing
    exactly what it says.** *"Prefer vertical slices that move a conformance
    lane over horizontal completeness"* is the banding rule, PLAN.md's band is
    what `/develop` picks from, and process work moves no lane — so it can
    never band, and 53 landings this window included **zero** `kind/process`
    issues. The queue was not neglected; it was correctly sorted to the bottom
    every single time.
  - **Fix applied, in the owner.** `cartographer.md` step 4 now bands
    `kind/process` and `kind/tooling` **on the sessions it costs, never on the
    lane it does not move**: an issue whose friction the log records in
    consecutive sessions outranks a lane slice, because the tax compounds and
    the fix is usually one session.
  - **Second fix, in the chronicler's own file, because a retro should not
    route what it can land.** `chronicler.md` Duty 2 gains: a `ready`,
    doc-only process issue about the process documents is discharged AT the
    retro, not routed to a develop iteration that has not picked it in the
    weeks its friction kept recurring — route back only what needs
    verification a retro cannot honestly perform, and name that verification.
    This is the rule under which #527/#668/#682 were applied above, and it is
    the fifth retro's own lesson (*"this retro's job was to RULE, not to
    discover"*) made structural. It does not license overriding a decline: the
    fifth retro's refusal of **#565** stands, because #565's acceptance
    requires verifying whether a norm ever existed, which is exactly the
    excluded case.
- **Recrafted for length, not for content — `retro.md` was restating
  `chronicler.md` almost verbatim.** Roughly thirty of its fifty-six lines
  re-specified the chronicler's method: read the evidence, find what recurs,
  audit the ledger, recraft-don't-append, the accretion warning, the ownership

## 2026-08-16 — backlog — **no issue body in this repository can currently be edited without corrupting it, and this pass proved the direction rather than asserting it**: `/backlog`'s standing rule is that a stale premise in an open body is fixed by editing that body, and **eighteen threads were touched this pass and zero bodies were edited**, because the MCP `issue_read` path returns `&#39;` where the stored body holds a plain ASCII apostrophe — measured at **44 escaped characters in #625, 32 in #492, 30 in #513, 26 in #687, 25 in #672, 17 in #670, 10 in #721**, on top of the angle-bracket stripping **#764** already named (#748, #669, #688, #16 come back with empty inline-code spans where an element name was), so a read-modify-write does not merely lose XML tokens, it **stores** the mangled entity in place of every apostrophe, quote and `>` in the body; the controlled half is that the cartographer authored **#852**'s body itself this session and knows what it wrote, and **this entry's own `WebFetch` of #852 settles the direction the experiment alone could not** — the stored apostrophe is plain, so the **write path is faithful and the read path escapes**, which keeps *unescape on read* as the fix and makes "write bodies from scratch" a workaround good only for issues authored in the same turn; the rest of the pass is a full cartographer survey (**#851**, **#852**, **#853**, **#854** filed, **#822** closed `not_planned` as superseded, **#725** retitled, `wip/issue-822` RETIRED and kept as re-planning evidence) plus two persona consultations whose seventeen findings were folded as **comments only, for that reason**, two of them **checked against the tree and found to be misreads** (#513, #688 stay open), one of them **re-scoping #409 in both directions** (`validate` and `bersrc` struck, `codec` and `codegen` the real targets), and one PLAN.md claim retired after four stamps: the `parser/produce_complex.go` `GAP(` marker **#815** calls "genuinely unowned" has been owned by **#471** since 2026-08-04

## 2026-08-16 — #842 — xpath: the §3.12.6 required-subset CTA evaluator SHIPS, and `xpath` stops being a `doc.go`-only package — one lexer, one recursive-descent parser, one sealed-sum AST over productions `[8]`–`[18]`, evaluating `ta-Test` through `ta-AttrName` (`xpath/cta.go`, `xpath/ctaparser.go`), wired into `validate` (`validate/cta.go`, `assess.go`'s `governingType`) so a `{type table}` **·conditionally selects·** through `key-cta-select` instead of the blanket `if _, tabled := d.TypeTable(); tabled { return nil }` decline that withheld the type of the element **and everything below it**; the shape is the warden pre-flight's, not the issue's — **the two error directions are two functions, not one return tuple**: `CompileCTATest(expr xsd.XPathExpression) (CTATest, bool)` where `ok=false` IS the withhold direction (covering out-of-subset syntax, an unresolvable prefix, AND in-grammar-but-unevaluable constructs alike), and `(CTATest).Evaluate(b value.Backend, attr AttributeValue) bool` which **always decides**, because §3.12.4 `key-cta-ta-select` clause 2 makes a dynamic or type error inside an evaluable construct a decided `false` and never a decline; `AttributeValue` is a func type, `func(name xsd.QName) (lexical string, present bool)`, so an absent attribute is the empty sequence over which §3.5.2 forms no pair and every comparison against it is `false`; **arbiter ACCEPT after one warden repair round** (a GAP marker sited on a function no wildcard spelling can reach), **`Ratchet: instance 1330 → 1334 pass (+4)`** banked at **`aaf06e1`**, and the durable content is **the one finding the arbiter took but declined to send back**: `fn:not` propagates its argument's error instead of absorbing it, so `not(@n = 5)` with `@n="abc"` answers `true` where clause 2 answers `false` — a wrong answer in a SUPPORTED construct, therefore an issue and never a `GAP(` marker

- **`{inherited attributes}` is marked UNESTABLISHED, not fail-open, and P3a's

  non-clashing merge is unimplemented (`{inheritable}` is not read at all,
  **#831**). A missing inherited attribute makes a comparison `false`, which can
  select the `{default type definition}` where the alternative's type was
  correct — **wrong in either direction**, which is the `cta0008.n01` shape #822

  because `xpath` sees one flat already-merged view and cannot enforce a merge
  it never performs.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **`validate` compiles alternatives LAZILY, in `key-cta-select` order.** A
     compile decline at position *i* withholds the ·governing type definition·
     and **stops the scan**; a `true` test selects and stops; a `false` test
     continues. An unevaluable alternative sitting BEHIND one that already
     returned true never costs the element its type, because "if any Type
     Alternative ·successfully selects· a type definition, none of the following
     Type Alternatives are tried." Eager whole-table compilation would have been
     strictly worse on the very cases this issue exists to move.
  2. **A decline withholds; it is never read as "unmatched".** Falling through
     to *i+1* or to the `{default type definition}` selects a type the rule may
     not have selected, and assessing against the wrong type manufactures a
     false reject **in both directions**. Withholding costs at most a rejection.
     `xpath/doc.go`'s old "an alternative's test as unmatched" sentence said the
     opposite and is deleted in the same diff.
  3. **`xs:string` comparison uses `strings.Compare`, bypassing the backend, and
     the alternative would have been a BUG.** `xs:string` deliberately defines
     no `Cmp` and `builtin/strict/strict_test.go`'s `TestStringEqNotOrdered`
     pins that it must not be `value.Ordered` (§3.3.1.3), so `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`
     could not be decided through `value.Ordered` at all — they would silently
     return `false` for every input. `xpath-valid` clause 2.2.10 fixes the
     collation as Unicode codepoint, which is UTF-8 byte order exactly. The
     dispatch is on the compile-time-settled `ctaSpace` discriminant — the
     sealed set's own tag, not a type switch (T2).
  4. **`ctaTypeError` is load-bearing, not an extra state.** It is the only
     thing keeping *decided false* apart from *cannot decide*; collapsing it
     into a parse decline would withhold a type where clause 2 says select on
     false — a bug in the opposite direction from the one the pre-flight was
     closing.
  5. **`attribute::NameTest` is implemented, not deferred.** `ta-props-correct`
     clause 2 is disjunctive and 2.2 admits the unabbreviated axis alongside
     2.1's `'@' NameTest`; it cost one token pair. Omitting it would have been a
     decline needing its own marker.
  6. **Six stale premises corrected in the same diff, three of them found by
     mason and absorbed.** The issue named `conformance/instance.go`'s decline
     enumeration, `xpath/doc.go` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "the package ships
     nothing" (plus its DAG import line and `[1]` note). Mason found three more
     — `validate/cvcid.go` and `validate/cvcidentityconstraint.go` both
     enumerated "a `{type table}`" as a cause of a non-determinable type, now
     false, and `parser/produce_typetable.go`'s fail-closed reader list named
     the deleted `governingType` branch. Each states a fact **this diff's own
     code falsifies**; leaving any of them ships a self-contradicting commit,
     which is the strongest form of WORKFLOW's absorption test.
  7. **`xpath/doc.go`'s growth tiers were restamped SHIPPED/PLANNED per tier,
     discharging the libuser obligation folded onto this thread.** The
     consultation singled `xpath/doc.go` out as the model `codec`/`codegen`
     should follow (#409) precisely because it showed no fake-present-tense
     signatures — and this landing is the moment that doc stops describing a
     plan and starts describing an API, i.e. the moment it can drift into
     `codec`'s failure mode. It still shows no Go signatures.
- Surprises:
  1. ***The wildcard NameTest could not be declined where its marker said it
     was.*** `*` is no token kind, so `@*`, `@p:*` and `@*:n` all die in
     `ctaTokenize` — `ctaScanQName` → `ctaScanNCName` returns `i` — long before
     `attrName` runs. The marker on `attrName` therefore falsified three claims
     the branch itself made: `ctaparser.go`'s header promise that a decline is
     "attributable to the construct rather than falling out of a generic syntax
     failure", the same header's "retiring one is a change to that production
     alone", and `doc.go`'s "each at its own marker". **`grep -rn "GAP("` is the
     debt sweep's whole interface, so a marker on the wrong function is a wrong
     answer to the only question anyone asks it.** Repaired by moving the marker
     to the lexical site and NARROWING both prose claims, rather than by adding
     a `ctaStarTok` to make the original claim true — the cheap direction on a
     landing already three reviews deep.
  2. **#858's body over-counts its retirable markers by one, and this landing
     is what proved it.** It promises three; the tree sites **two**
     (`castExpr:521`, `constructorFunction:552`). §3.12.6 clause 3's Note
     resolves the ambiguity by function NAME, which makes every non-`fn:not`
     `QName '(' … ')'` a constructor call — so `booleanExpr` routes it to
     `constructorFunction` and it declines under that one marker. Behaviour is
     right under either reading; the count is not. **A defect in the tracker,
     not in this landing** — see Next.
  3. **`and` and `or` do NOT diverge from the spec under the node-local error
     handling, and only `fn:not` does.** The arbiter traced all six error
     configurations against xpath20.md §3.4's tables: node-local `false` lands
     on a permitted XPath answer in every one (`error or true` → `true` is
     explicitly allowed; every other row coincides with `false`). That
     enumeration is why the finding below is one construct wide rather than a
     hole in the boolean layer.
  4. **A whole-`{test}` bare `ValueExpr` (`test="@type"`, in the suite) has no
     stated coercion in §3.12** — §3.13.1 and `cvc-assertion` clause 3 state an
     `fn:boolean` coercion for ASSERTIONS and §3.12.4 says only "A.`{test}`
     evaluates to true". `ctaEffectiveBoolean` gives it the EBV, which is what
     implementations do and what production `[11]`'s name implies; documented at
     the site with its citation, and none of the four banked cases depends on
     it. The arbiter recorded it as **seen and decided, deliberately not ruled**
     — worth knowing before someone "fixes" it.

## 2026-08-17 — #861 — xpath: a raised CTA `{test}` error falsifies the WHOLE `{test}`, not the comparison node that raised it — key-cta-ta-select clause 2 (§3.12.4) substitutes false for "the `{test}`", and the pre-change evaluator applied that substitution at the node, so `ctaCompare`'s failed cast (err:FORG0001) and inadmissible operand pair (err:XPTY0004) became a node-local `false` that an enclosing `fn:not` INVERTED: `not(@n = 5)` over `@n="abc"` answered `true` where the spec answers `false` — a shipped, fully-supported construct returning a WRONG boolean, not a fail-open decline; the walk now carries a three-state `ctaAnswer` (`ctaFalse`/`ctaTrue`/`ctaError`) through the whole expression tree, `negated()` propagates `ctaError` unconditionally per xpath20.md §3.6's fn:not, `ctaOr`/`ctaAnd` apply §3.6's truth tables (a determining sibling wins even over an error raised elsewhere), and **`CTATest.Evaluate` is the single collapse point** — `ctaEval(...) == ctaTrue`, clause 2's false-substitution performed exactly once, at the `{test}` root; **arbiter ACCEPT on the first round, zero findings, no repair**, `Ratchet: unchanged` and CONFIRMED so rather than assumed, `go tool surface -base origin/main` **`surface: unchanged`**

- Shipped on `wip/issue-861`, base **`0740b51`** (#851's landing),
  fast-forward from `origin/main`. **One commit, `c9dfac4`, plus this entry.**
  Landing diff `git diff origin/main...HEAD --numstat` is **2 files,
  +200/−42**: `xpath/cta.go` (+129/−42) and `xpath/cta_test.go` (+71/−0).
  Exported surface unchanged — `CompileCTATest`, `CTATest`, `Evaluate` and
  `AttributeValue` all keep their shapes; the whole change is below the
  package boundary.
- **Ratchet, copied from the verdict, not recomputed: unchanged.** The
  premise was verified directly rather than taken on report: the pinned suite
  holds **226 `<alternative>` tags and ZERO containing `not(`**, so no case
  exercises the construct whose answer moved. Full gate green, part 4's
  conformance run **331s**, no improved-but-unbanked case in the `-v` output.
  This is a pure correctness fix, and it is the shape where "unchanged" is the
  honest number rather than a missed opportunity.
- **The pick, over the two siblings filed beside it.** #861, #862 and #863 are
  the three fresh follow-ups from #842's post-land pass, all startable on
  `main` with no dependencies. #862 is dormant — it only bites once #858/#859
  widen the token set — and #863 is process-only. #861 was the sole LIVE
  correctness bug of the three: a supported construct answering wrongly beats
  a latent one and a doc one.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The three-state answer replaces the bare `bool` for the WHOLE walk, not
     just the `not()` arm.** Clause 2 names "the `{test}`" as the subject of
     its false-substitution, so the raised state has to survive every operator
     between the raising node and the root. A local patch at `fn:not` would
     have fixed the reported symptom and left the same conflation one operator
     further out.
  2. **`ctaOr`/`ctaAnd` follow §3.6's truth tables, so a determining sibling
     beats a raised error.** `true or <error>` is `true` and `false and
     <error>` is `false`; otherwise the error survives to the top. This is
     xpath20.md's answer, not a convenience.
  3. **`ctaFalse` is the zero value.** The nil root of a zero `CTATest` then
     decides `false` without a special case, and neither loop accumulator ever
     leans on it implicitly — both are assigned their operator's identity
     explicitly.
  4. **`ctaBool` became `ctaEval` and the `or`/`and` loops moved onto the node
     types as `eval` methods.** Scope absorbed beyond the issue body, all of
     it forced by the change: the old name asserted a return type that no
     longer existed, two of the four arms already carried an `eval` method, and
     several doc comments asserted node-local absorption — prose the diff made
     false. Repairing a sentence the same diff falsified is not scope creep
     (PRINCIPLES 22 governs the unrelated move, not the consequential one).
  5. **Two tests, one for the fix and one for what must NOT move.**
     `TestEvaluateRaisedErrorFalsifiesTheWholeTest` pins `not(@n = 5)`,
     `not('a' = 5)` and nesting; `TestEvaluateRaisedErrorUnderConnectives`
     pins every relevant and/or truth-table cell with a raised operand, so the
     "and/or answers are unmoved" claim is a test, not an assertion in a
     verdict.
- Surprises:
  1. **The flat n-ary loops are provably equal to §3.6's binary
     left-associative grammar, and STRICTER than it.** The arbiter derived it
     rather than checking cases: `and`'s policy is `max` over the order
     `F < E < T` and `or`'s is `max` over `T < E < F`, both associative and
     commutative, so the loop's answer is independent of evaluation order.
     §3.6 explicitly PERMITS a processor to differ here — an implementation may
     raise or absorb depending on which operand it evaluates first — and the
     ratchet-visible consequence is that **CTA no longer carries that
     nondeterminism at all**. Removing licensed nondeterminism was not a stated
     goal of the issue; it fell out of the shape.
  2. **The arbiter re-derived the fix instead of reading the diff for it.** All
     eighteen §3.6 truth-table cells traced against `ctaAnd.eval`/`ctaOr.eval`,
     the "and/or unmoved" and "six rows fail on pre-change code" claims
     verified empirically by planting the new tests UNMODIFIED into a detached
     worktree at `origin/main`, and the ratchet premise checked by grepping the
     suite. Zero findings after that much independent work is a stronger
     signal than zero findings after a read-through, and it is worth recording
     which of the two produced this ACCEPT.
- Friction: **none worth the name.** One grounding, one mason round, one
  arbiter round, no repair, no forward merge, no parked scope, no deviation
  needing escalation. The and/or short-circuit policy was mason's own design
  call, made inside the implementation and FLAGGED for scrutiny in the
  hand-off rather than buried — which is why the arbiter spent its round
  proving it rather than discovering it.
- Cost: **one oracle grounding, one mason round** (worktree isolation)**, one
  arbiter round** (ACCEPT, zero findings, one non-diff note — the LOG entry
  precondition, which this entry discharges)**, one chronicler entry.**

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The guard sits in `prescan`, not at the walk sites.** §5.1 (:4296) makes
     it an error if *the schema document* would not be fully valid against the
     s4s — the document, not the subset a producer happens to walk — so a
     per-site guard would under-reject exactly the subtrees the producer skips,
     which is the fault this issue is about. `prescan` runs once per assembled
     document from both entry points (`parser/produce.go:124` for `Produce`,
     `parser/parse.go:795` for `assembly.compile`), so the whole
     `<include>`/`<import>`/`<redefine>`/`<override>` closure is covered. One
     extra O(n) walk per document, no cache added (STYLE D4).
  2. **The walk never descends into an `<annotation>`.** `<appinfo>` and
     `<documentation>` hold `<xs:any processContents="lax"/>` content (:5727,
     :5740), where an element literally named `{XMLSchemaNS}annotation` is
     content and counting it would be a false rejection. The skip is taken at
     `<annotation>` rather than at `<appinfo>`/`<documentation>` — broader than
     strictly needed, but `<annotation>`'s own content model admits only those
     two children, so below an s4s-valid point the two skips are the same skip.
  3. **A plain `fmt.Errorf`, and no rule ID minted.** Three sections answer
     "None as such"; inventing an `src-*` or `s4s-*` verdict is the fabrication
     STYLE E2 exists to prevent. E3 is satisfied through `found[1].Loc()`
     (uri:line:col), and `childElements` returns document order, so `found[1]`
     is genuinely the second annotation and the diagnostic lands on the token
     the author wrote (STYLE D2).
  4. **The `<annotation>`-inside-`<annotation>` fault was left alone.** It is a
     different s4s violation — `<annotation>`'s own content model, not
     `xs:annotated`'s cardinality — no suite case decides on it, and this issue
     did not claim it. Not smuggled in.

  from `origin/main`. **Two commits plus this entry:** **`b42b313`** (the guard,
  its three doc comments and the tests) and **`793df1f`** (the comment
  correction the verdict required). Landing diff

  `parser/produce_absentname_test.go` (+201/−0),
  `parser/redefine.go` (+28/−0) and `parser/produce.go` (+5/−4). The arbiter

  `rejectProhibitedAttrs` call and its error return; everything else is prose

- **Ratchet, copied from the verdict, not recomputed: unchanged.** All six
  lanes. Verified rather than inherited: `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run `ok` (454.9s),
  exit 0, so no `Regressed` and no `Vanished`, and
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` immediately

  `GAP(` census **94 on both `origin/main` and `HEAD`**.
- **`unchanged` was the predicted number and the prediction rested on a
  measurement, which is why the shape is unit-test-only rather than
  under-tested.** All **15470** suite `.xsd` files were walked at `3ce313c`:
  36 carry a top-level `xs:override` and **not one also carries an
  `xs:redefine`**, and following each of the 37 override directives'
  `schemaLocation` through `include`/`import`/`override`/`redefine` to depth 3
  reaches no document containing an `xs:redefine` either. Unreachable from the
  suite in both directions, exactly as #699's `attributeGroup` arm already was.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **`prescanRedefine` over `produceRedefinition`, and the choice is a test
     row rather than a preference.** Both mason and the arbiter reverted the
     guard and re-ran: the *substituted `<group ref=>` naming no original* row
     then reports `mid.xsd:1:136: [src-expredef] …`, which is precisely the
     fault a `produceRedefinition`-sited guard would leave standing. That row
     discriminates between the two candidate SITES, not merely between guard
     and no guard.
  2. **Keyed on `decl != e.elem`, so only a substitute is charged here.**
     `replacement` returns `e.elem` when nothing substitutes, so an unguarded
     second call would re-check what `newRedefineSet:222` already checked; a
     control row pins that the unsubstituted child under an `<override>` is
     still reported exactly once, at its own position.
  3. **Above the `chainedOriginal` branch.** The chained-redefine path also
     calls `replacement`, and the prohibition is a syntactic property of the
     substitute element itself, independent of which document ends up owning
     the component — so one call covers both, which is the placement the
     grounding's edge case asked for.
  4. **Plain `fmt.Errorf` through the existing `rejectProhibitedAttrs`, no rule
     ID minted (STYLE E2).** `src-mgd` and every `s4s-*` identifier remain
     fabrications — zero grep hits across `docs/specs/md/`, re-confirmed. Every
     rejection row asserts `errors.As(err, &xe)` is **false**, so a future
     invented rule ID fails the test instead of passing silently. E3 is carried
     by `decl.Loc()` — the substitute's own `main.xsd:3:`, with the rows
     asserting `mid.xsd` does *not* appear.
  5. **No third prohibition list (STYLE T4).** `minOccurs` on a substituted
     `<attributeGroup>` is **absent from the grammar, not prohibited** —
     `xs:attributeGroup`'s type never pulls in `xs:occurs` (:5167) — and a
     control row pins that the guard may not claim it.
- Surprises:
  1. **The issue body forbade a grounding and the grounding found an error in
     the issue body.** *"No fresh grounding is needed and none should be
     commissioned"*; one was taken anyway, all eight citations checked out, and
     the D_old′-not-D_old Note is **not clause 3.1.1's** as the body labelled
     it — in the flattened markdown it trails clause 3.2.2 and refers to
     `D_old′` without branch qualification, so it governs 3.1.1's and 3.2.1's
     definitions alike. Cite it as **§4.2.5 src-override clause 3's closing
     Note**. Substance unaffected, anchor wrong, and the corrected label is what
     the commit message and all three doc comments now carry. Obeying the
     instruction would have shipped the bad anchor into the tree.
  2. **§5.1's :4296 bullet is not direct authority for this fault, and the body
     leaned on it as if it were.** :4295 scopes that bullet to a document
     *"after the conditional-inclusion pre-processing described in [§4.2.2]"* —
     conditional inclusion (`xs:if`/`xs:then`), **not** override
     pre-processing. It stands as the general *governed by the s4s even absent a
     numbered rule* footing that `produce.go`'s own doc already uses it for; the
     authority that the BUILT document is the substituted one is §4.2.5's own
     `D_old′` language plus that Note, which the body cited separately and
     correctly.
  3. **The accept's one finding is a comment asserting the opposite of the
     code, and it was concealing a real false reject.** Reproduced directly: an
     `<override>` substituting a **clean** `<group name="G">` for a `<redefine>`

     once per POSITION. Left as written, the comment would have told the next
     agent the substituted-away original is unguarded and suppressed the very
     follow-up the behaviour needs.

## 2026-08-17 — #872 — parked (needs-replan): the 404 that opened the issue never reproduced — two arbiter rounds and 20+ orchestrator probes all returned 200 — and the defect the two rounds actually converged on outlives any HTTP status: `WebFetch` on a GitHub issue page is not a faithful re-read channel EVEN AT 200, because it returns a model-mediated summary of the RENDERED page rather than the stored markdown body, and can re-escape the very token the body-edit rule exists to protect (`&amp;lt;xs:element&amp;gt;`, measured on #764) or return no body at all; round 1 asserted "issue pages 404" as permanent fact and was rejected for committing the same class of defect #872 was filed to fix with the polarity flipped, round 2 restored `WebFetch` as PRIMARY behind an "if the fetch fails" hedge that guards TRANSPORT while every fetch succeeded and still came back unfaithful — so the guard never fires on the actual failure mode, and the rewritten bullet placed an unfaithful path ahead of the honest one in the one document meant to prevent silent body corruption

  — **not merged, retired in place** after two arbiter rejections (the hard cap,
  docs/WORKFLOW.md's Parking section / PRINCIPLES 30). Two commits, both

  (`process: restore WebFetch as the body re-read, with a fall-through (#872)`),

  round, so its final state is round 2's commit and the tip has not moved since

  added** — WORKFLOW's parking rule asks for the findings that killed the
  attempt to be on the thread, and the two arbiter verdicts already carry them

  Nothing renamed, nothing deleted, never force-pushed; `wip/issue-872` stands
  at `0b34c21` as re-planning evidence and is never resumed or branched from.
  This entry lands separately off `origin/main` @ `85fe690`, since a park leaves
  the WIP branch untouched: **one commit, one file — `docs/LOG/2026-08.md`,
  +164/−0, append-only.**
- **Ratchet: unchanged on `main` — nothing landed, so `main`'s figures are
  untouched by definition.** Both commits are doc-only against
  `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, and both arbiter rounds ran `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` and found
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` **empty**

  rounds, **41759 cases** (round 2 at 384s), no improved-but-unbanked case in
  either `-v` output. Ratchet integrity clean — the diff never opened
  `conformance/`.
- What was attempted: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s filing-discipline bullet forbidding a
  write-back of a body obtained from `issue_read` (that read path strips
  angle-bracketed tokens and HTML-entity-escapes the punctuation that survives —
  #764's finding) named **`WebFetch` on the issue URL** as the safe re-read
  before editing. #872's premise: `WebFetch` against an issue page returned HTTP
  404 in this container while the repo root fetched 200, measured twice
  independently before the session opened — so the documented remedy did not
  exist here and a session following WORKFLOW as written hit a dead end
  mid-task. Scope as filed: rewrite that one bullet so it names a path that
  works. Surface: none, both rounds; no warden review, per the issue's own
  `## Surface: none`.
- Grounding, and one deliberate omission: the queue search for `docs/WORKFLOW.md`
  against `re-read` / `WebFetch` / `issue_read` / `body-edit` returned exactly
  two hits and no unnamed one — **#764** (closed, the rule's origin, not a
  duplicate) and **#857** (open, *related, not duplicate* per #872's own body:
  #857 measures `issue_read` round-trip FIDELITY, #872 measures `WebFetch`
  re-read AVAILABILITY; neither blocks the other). **Oracle grounding was
  skipped on purpose and the skip recorded** on the thread — this is repo
  process and tooling, and no XSD, XPath, F&O or precisionDecimal rule applies
  (the #246 precedent, 2026-08-01).
- Decisions:
  - **Round 1 promoted the repair path and asserted the 404 as permanent fact,
    and that assertion is what killed it.** `0ea5b1f` made "repair the
    `issue_read` copy" (undo the entity-escaping, re-derive stripped tokens from
    the tree) the PRIMARY path and wrote into WORKFLOW that `WebFetch` "is not
    the way around this here: issue pages 404 while the repo root fetches" —
    grounded in mason's own fresh measurement, 2 calls both 404, matching the
    pre-session pair. The arbiter re-measured independently after the commit and
    got **HTTP 200 on every issue page tried** (872, 764, 857) by both
    `WebFetch` and `curl`. Gate was fully green; the reject was purely the
    factual-claim finding. **A permanent claim about a transient observation is
    the same defect #872 exists to fix, written in the other direction.**
  - **Between rounds the orchestrator tried to reproduce the 404 and could
    not.** 20 requests — 1 `WebFetch` plus a 15-request rapid-fire `curl` burst
    at zero delay — against `/issues/872` and `/issues/764`, **all 200**, no
    flakiness under load. Round 2's repair re-measured again from scratch (1
    `WebFetch` + 36 rapid `curl` requests across 3 issue URLs, all 200). The
    404 is not reproducible by any probe this session ran.
  - **Round 2 restructured the bullet as attempt-then-fall-through, which is the
    right SHAPE and the wrong PRIMARY.** `0b34c21` led with the `WebFetch`
    re-read, fell through to the repair procedure "if the fetch fails", and left
    that arm terminating on an unrecoverable token by commenting on the thread
    rather than concluding the correction is impossible — the #527 pattern,
    structural rather than asserted. #764's original strip/escape substance
    (angle-bracket stripping, `&#39;`/`&#34;`/`&gt;` escaping) was preserved
    byte-identical, which round 1 had also got right and the arbiter confirmed
    across both rounds.
  - **The second reject is the durable finding, and it is not about HTTP.** The
    arbiter measured `WebFetch` against `issue_read`'s output directly rather
    than against a status code, and found `WebFetch` returns a **model-mediated
    summary of the rendered page**, not the stored markdown body: on #764 a
    short titled-link paraphrase with the target token **re-escaped inside it**
    (`&amp;lt;xs:element&amp;gt;`), plus Markdown reformatting (ATX→setext
    headings, `-`→`*` bullets, dropped code fences, #733); on an explicitly
    verbatim-worded prompt, a model summary with no body at all. So round 2's
    new PRIMARY claim — "`WebFetch`… which returns those tokens intact" — is
    false on its own terms, and the "if the fetch fails" hedge guards the wrong
    axis: **every fetch succeeded, at 200, and still returned an unfaithful
    copy.** The guard cannot fire on the real failure mode.
  - **Two rejections is the cap and no third round was solicited.** The branch
    was checkpointed, the label moved, and the verdicts left as the record.
- Surprises:
  1. **The issue's own premise was false by the time it was judged, and no
     probe this session ran could bring it back.** Four independent measurement
     campaigns (orchestrator pre-session, mason round 1, arbiter round 1,
     orchestrator between rounds, mason round 2, arbiter round 2) split
     cleanly by TIME rather than by tool: everything before the session says
     404, everything from round 1's verdict onward says 200, across
     `WebFetch` and `curl` alike. A transient outage read as a permanent
     property is how #872 came to be filed.
  2. **The real defect was always availability-independent, and both rounds
     spent themselves on availability.** `WebFetch` being a summarizer of
     rendered HTML is true at 404 and true at 200; it was the reason the
     documented remedy was wrong even in the weeks it returned 200. Neither
     round asked what `WebFetch` RETURNS until the arbiter compared its output
     to `issue_read`'s side by side — which is a four-minute check that was
     available from the first minute of the session.
  3. **A doc-only, one-bullet issue reached the park cap on the truth of two
     English sentences**, the #256 and #636 pattern again: every gate leg green
     in both rounds, both times, and every finding about whether a sentence is
     true. The gate proves nothing about the product of a commit whose product
     IS prose.
- Friction:
  1. **`gh` is not available in this container**, so the WIP survey ran on a

  3. **Neither round's claim was checkable by anything in the repo.** Both

## 2026-08-17 — #878 (replacing #872) — process: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s body-edit bullet leads with the REPAIR path and states its own limit in the same breath — "never write back a body ***as*** `issue_read` returned it": undo the entity-escaping, author only the section you came to change, leave every other section as it stands, write that back; **the escaping is mechanically reversible and the stripping is not** — an empty inline-code span carries no residue, no length and no first letter, so nothing in the body or the tree says which token it held, and where a stripped token will not re-derive **the write is blocked while the correction is not**: comment on the thread naming the section the body still gets wrong, because *a body known to be wrong is never landed silently*; `WebFetch` survives in the bullet **described by what it returns** — a small model's answer over the RENDERED page, a summary and not the stored body — and is therefore licensed for reading what an issue says and forbidden as *"the body you intend to write back"*, with no conditional keyed on a fetch failing anywhere in the text; **arbiter ACCEPT round 1, no repair round**, one mason round, `Ratchet: unchanged` at **`9384d93`**, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` alone, **+15/−6**, one bullet, no `.go` file in the diff

the engine grows a second narrow entry point `xpath.CTATestStaticError(expr xsd.XPathExpression, types xsd.TypeResolver) error` — nil unless a static error is PROVEN — over a shared unexported core, `CompileCTATest`'s `(CTATest, bool)` RESULT shape survives verbatim, and the invariant **unsupported dominates static** discards a mid-parse defect whenever the parse then fails for any other reason, so a legal-but-declined full-XPath expression that happens to also carry an unbound prefix is never turned into a false reject (PRINCIPLES 9); **and then the branch was overtaken by its own neighbour** — **#858 landed as `d02aa59`** off the same base with no knowledge of this mechanism, making the three cast-shaped CTA constructs EVALUATE, so the forward merge **`8bfdf2e`** (two parents, real conflicts in `xpath/cta.go`, `xpath/ctaparser.go`, `xpath/cta_test.go`, `xpath/doc.go`) had to resolve one name-resolution rewrite against the other, RE-POINT a `GAP(xpath)` marker #858 wrote in good faith naming CLOSED #886 as owner of err:XPST0051/err:XPST0080 (filed as **#894** rather than extended under time pressure), and hand the charge site a construction-time `xsd.TypeResolver` — `parser.ctaStaticTypes`, because no `*xsd.Schema` exists at production time and `CTATestStaticError` now takes one;   charge `ta-props-correct` on none of them, rather than by grep alone.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **A second narrow entry point, NOT a widened `(CTATest, error)`.** The
     orchestrator's first candidate shape was rejected at design pre-flight:
     `error` is an open interface, so "exactly two sealed kinds" cannot be
     sealed at the package boundary — every caller would classify by assertion
     (T2 erosion), and the fail-open decline would land in the one channel Go
     idiom says to wrap and propagate, making a false reject a one-line
     mistake. Two façades over one unexported traversal (`compileCTATest`,
     `ctaDefect`) make the illegal state unrepresentable by construction: the
     function that returns a verdict can never produce a decline, and the
     function that declines can never produce a verdict.
  2. **Unsupported dominates static, enforced structurally at one place.** An
     unbound prefix records a provisional defect on `*ctaParser` and the parse
     continues with a placeholder ·expanded name·; unless the token stream
     then reached the end of a complete `[8] ta-Test`, the defect is DISCARDED.
     Over-charging refuses a conforming schema (§3.12.6 clause 2's Note:
     processors *may but are not required to* support expressions outside the
     required subset); under-charging is a missed rejection the ratchet can
     take later. The asymmetry decides the rule. The merge added one new
     discard path (`ctaResolveTypes`) and no new escape.
  3. **`xpath` mints no `xsderr.Rule` and does not import `xsderr`.** It
     returns the rendered fact — `err:XPST0081: no in-scope namespace binding
     for prefix "p"` — and the assembler decorates it. The Schema Component
     Constraint belongs to whoever builds components, and `xsderr/catalog.go`
     reserves the bare `ta-props-correct` (no clause-suffixed variant, no
     `xpath-valid`), which is where the charge site follows from.
  4. **Charged in `typeTableOf`, after `checkSrcTA` and `alternativeTypes`,
     at `alt.Loc()`.** Representation constraints before component
     constraints, in document order, first offender wins; it is the only site
     in the module that builds a `{test}` and the only one with the
     `<xs:alternative>`'s own location in hand. No post-parse pass was
     invented and no checker seam was added to `xsd` — `parser` is the sole
     writer of components, so production-time charging covers every
     `TypeAlternative` a consumer can obtain.
  5. **The merge RE-POINTED #858's `GAP(xpath)` marker to a new tracker
     (#894) and did NOT extend this mechanism to the cast-target arm.** Two
     independent reasons, both stated at the marker itself. *"Unsupported
     dominates static"* needs a placeholder the type system does not have: an
     unbound prefix carries on under `ctaUnresolvedName` because `xsd.QName`
     has a zero value the grammar provably cannot write, while `ctaCast.target`
     is a `*xsd.SimpleType` whose nil is a landmine for every downstream
     consumer and whose substitution by a real type changes what
     `ctaTypes.comparison` settles for the rest of the expression — a NEW
     design decision, not the reuse of an approved one. And the classification
     itself is an open spec question: #858 reads a user-defined in-scope atomic
     target as declinable under §3.12.6 clause 2's Note, while `xpath-valid`
     clause 2.2.5 puts only the BUILT-INS in scope, which makes that same
     target err:XPST0051. The two readings disagree about which schemas a
     charge rejects, and that wants the oracle before either becomes a
     rejection.
  6. **The construction-time resolver is clause 2.2.5's set, not a stand-in for
     an unavailable schema.** `parser` has no `*xsd.Schema` at production time
     and `CTATestStaticError` now needs a resolver (the shared traversal
     resolves `xs:string`/`xs:decimal`/`xs:double` before it parses, so a
     resolver-less façade would decline every `{test}` and charge nothing).
     `ctaStaticTypes` answers exactly *"those components that are present in
     every schema by definition"* — a strict SUBSET of what `validate`'s schema
     resolver admits, so it can only under-charge. No new type was added to
     `xsd`, and `xsd/typealternative.go` changes one doc sentence and no code.
  7. **The repair indexes the seed once instead of filtering the memo.**
     `symbols.builtins` is written in exactly one place (`newSymbols`, from the
     same `builtin.Seed` slice already in hand) and read in exactly one place;
     `built` starts as `maps.Clone` of it and grows as before, so the two are
     not derivable from each other (D3) and no resolution path changed. The
     `QName.Space` guard went with it — every key in the index already carries
     `xsd.XMLSchemaNS` — which makes clause 2.2.5's set true BY CONSTRUCTION
     rather than by a false premise about the namespace.
  8. **`<xs:assert>`'s `{test}` deliberately out of scope.** No compile path
     exists for assertions and full XPath is fail-open there;
     `buildXPathExpression` is shared, the check is not.

**round 1 was REJECTED on two P1s, both reduced to failing witnesses** — `xpath20.md` §B.1 **rule 1.1**'s float→double promotion implemented as a ·canonical representation· round-trip, which is a DIFFERENT VALUE (float's canonical is the shortest decimal round-tripping to the FLOAT), so `@f="0.1"`, `@f cast as xs:float = 1e-1` answered **true** where the spec says false, while rule **1.2**'s decimal promotion genuinely *is* "created by casting" and a unifying repair would have broken the arm that worked; the repair **withholds** rule 1.1 rather than faking it and moves rule 2 to the value comparison, which forced a third state into existence (`ctaTyping`: `ctaTypeErrored` zero value / `ctaTypeDeclined` / `ctaTypeSettled`) because `comparison`'s old `(type, bool)` turned a promotion the engine CANNOT PERFORM into a **decided false** under key-cta-ta-select clause 2 — an `err:XPTY0004` the spec never raised; - Decisions made and why:
  1. **The warden pre-flight ran on a `## Surface` that said "Expected none",
     and that section was FALSE.** The issue body anticipated it might be
     (*"if reaching `value`'s lexical mapping forces a new exported parameter,
     that is a warden pass in this session"*), and **#484** is the standing
     argument that making the pre-flight conditional on a non-empty Surface
     means **the issues most needing a design read are exactly the ones that
     skip it**. It returned `revise` and rewrote the shape: the resolver on
     both entry points; `ctaSpace` deleted; no `xpath → builtin` edge, because
     the XSD namespace is closed to user declarations so a type resolvable
     there is one of the 49 by construction; and `value.ValidateLexical`
     identified as **already being** F&O §17.1.1's operation, facets and
     `whiteSpace` and the nearest-mapped-ancestor walk included — so #858
     needed nothing from **#721** and must not pre-empt its shape.
  2. **Rule 1.1 is a WITHHOLD, not a fix, and the withhold is routed to
     `CompileCTATest`.** Over the `strict` backend `float.Eq(double)` is false
     and `float.Cmp(double)` is Incomparable, so there is no cheap in-place
     route; the value-level widening is a `value` surface change with its own
     warden pass, which is **#889**. Any pair whose comparison type is
     `xs:double` while an operand's `{primitive type definition}` is `xs:float`
     now declines at compile time, at both sites — `ctaWider` and
     `untypedAgainst`'s clause 2.1 arm. Rule 1.2's `xs:decimal` promotion IS
     "created by casting", so the same round-trip is right there and those
     pairs stay admitted.
  3. **`ctaTyping` as a three-state enum, not a bool.** A bool cannot carry
     three directions, and conflating the withhold with `err:XPTY0004` is
     precisely the defect finding 1 exposed. The zero value is the
     load-bearing detail and it is the safe one: `ctaTypeErrored` is what a
     `t.primitive` fault returns, so a fault reports the error direction and
     **cannot leak into the withhold**. Same shape as `ctaAnswer` and
     `ctaItem`, already in the file; no separate `declines(l, r) bool`
     predicate, which would resolve every operand's primitive twice (T4).
  4. **B.1 rule 2's URI promotion belongs at the value comparison, not in the
     type.** `ctaCompare.eval` routes an `xs:anyURI` comparison type through

## 2026-08-18 — #887 — xpath: the CTA `{test}` comparator stops asking the VALUES which operators they admit and asks xpath20.md Appendix B.2's rows — `holdsBetween` decided `eq`/`ne` from `value.Eq` and ordering from `value.Ordered`, and B.2's per-(operator, type, type) rows disagree in BOTH directions: an ordering comparison over `xs:duration`, a Gregorian type, `xs:hexBinary` or `xs:base64Binary` decided from the value space where B.2 holds eq/ne rows and NO ordering rows (§3.5.1, xpath20.md:2133 — *"not a valid combination for the given operator, according to the rules in B.2"* — raises `err:XPTY0004`, folded to `ctaError` by `key-cta-ta-select` clause 2, §3.12.4, and NOT by `ta-props-correct`, which is the STATIC sibling the grounding explicitly forbids citing here), while `xs:boolean` decided `ctaError` where B.2 gives it all six rows including `op:boolean-less-than` (:3317) — the counter-intuitive half, and the one that proves the encoding was wrong rather than merely incomplete, because a type whose value space is deliberately not ordered still has a legal `lt`; the answer is a GENERATED table, ruled before a line was written by a **warden pre-flight that REJECTED the obvious alternative** — a per-operator `value` capability would let each backend answer a spec-fixed question, so two backends could disagree with B.2 and with each other, and it re-encodes spec data once per backend (PRINCIPLES 26, STYLE T2/T4) — so `tools/opmapgen` reads B.2's markdown out of `docs/specs/md/xpath20.md`, expands the `numeric` and `Gregorian` prose macros, fails loudly on an unrecognized comparison row, and emits **160 rows** into `xpath/gen_opmap.go`; legality is settled at **COMPILE** time in `ctaTypes.comparison` (`ctaparser.go`, one construction site, one caller) so a constructed `ctaCompare` is B.2-legal BY CONSTRUCTION and `holdsBetween` can never meet a pair its operator does not admit, and boolean ordering now routes through `value.Eq` against the value of `"true"` per `op:boolean-less-than`'s own definition, never through `value.Ordered` and never through `value.Canonical` string order; **arbiter ACCEPT round 1, zero findings, no repair**, `Ratchet: unchanged` MEASURED at **`1f2998e`**, `surface: unchanged`, the `GAP(xpath)` marker at `holdsBetween` retired outright rather than narrowed

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The encoding decision was taken BEFORE writing, by the warden, because
     the issue body said the encoding IS the issue.** Option (b) — a
     per-operator `value` capability — was rejected on T2/T4 and PRINCIPLES 26:
     B.2 legality is a judgment about STATIC operand types, not about a value,
     and a capability hands a spec-fixed answer to each backend independently.
     Option (a), generation, was approved with two corrections that both held
     up under implementation (the compile-time site, and the `shared` narrowing
     below). **Without the pre-flight this lands as a new `value` interface** —
     the issue body offered both options and named neither as preferred.
  2. **Generate the WHOLE comparison-row set, not the 6-entry exception list.**
     The exception list is DERIVED from the rows; hand-typing it is exactly the
     transcription PRINCIPLES 26 forbids. 160 rows, eq 32 / ne 32 / 24 each for
     gt, lt, ge, le.
  3. **Charge at compile time, not in `holdsBetween`.** `ctaparser.go` already
     has the typing settled, so an illegal pair returns the existing
     `ctaTypeError{}` node — §3.12.4 clause 2's fold — and no `legal bool` field
     joins `ctaCompare` (STYLE D4/T1: no state derivable from other state).
  4. **`xs:boolean` ordering needs no new capability.** With the comparison type
     known to be `xs:boolean`, `op:boolean-less-than` is *"false is less than
     true"* (`xpath-functions.md` §9.2.2), decidable through `value.Eq` against
     the backend's own value for `"true"`. `value.Ordered` stays absent and
     stays correct: B.2's rows are not a claim that the datatype is ordered.
  5. **`sharedNamed` narrows before the lookup.** `ctaTypes.shared` reduces both
     operands to their `{primitive type definition}`, which turns two
     `xs:yearMonthDuration` casts into `xs:duration` — and B.2 gives ordering
     rows to the two named duration subtypes and NOT to their primitive, so the
     new table would have rejected a comparison the spec admits by subtype
     substitution. The narrowing answers the shared NAMED subtype when both
     operands carry it, matching `untypedAgainst`'s clauses 2.2/2.3.
  6. **The lookup walks the `{base type definition}` chain**, because B.2's
     general note (:3228) reaches its rows *"by a combination of type promotion
     and subtype substitution"* — the table is checked against the promoted
     type, never the raw dynamic one.
  7. **B.2's arithmetic rows are read and SKIPPED by the generator**, not
     absent from it: they carry their own XPTY0004 clause (§3.4) and §3.12.6's
     required subset admits no arithmetic in `{test}` at all.
- **Two behaviour changes past the issue's named set, absorbed under
  docs/WORKFLOW.md's scope rule and confirmed absorbed by the arbiter** — each
  needs no rule ID the grounding lacks, adds no surface, and cannot move a lane
  alone:
  1. **`xs:precisionDecimal` `eq`/`ne` is now `err:XPTY0004`** where it
     previously decided through `value.Eq`. B.2 holds no row of ANY kind for

     sole legality authority, inventing a row is fabricating spec data.

  2. **`xs:QName`/`xs:NOTATION`, the issue's *"if reachable"* clause, are
     confirmed NOT reachable.** `ctaTypes.castTarget` excludes `xs:NOTATION` by
