- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The capability is an ENUMERATION and it REPLACES `AttributeValue`** —
     ruled by the warden's pre-flight, before implementation, because the issue's
     `## Surface` section was non-none. Keeping the by-name lookup for `@foo` and
     adding an enumeration for `@*` is the two-encoding shape STYLE D4 forbids,
     and it is worse than it looks: it would put "is this NameTest a wildcard" in
     the compiler AND in the evaluator's choice of capability. Enumeration over a
     predicate because `[37]`'s matching semantics are spec knowledge and belong
     inside `xpath` where the grammar is, and because document order and
     short-circuit stay `xpath`'s to guarantee (STYLE D1/D2) rather than becoming
     a split obligation.
  2. **`[36] NameTest` closes the set, so the matcher is a sealed sum** (STYLE
     T2's schema-closed-set exception): `ctaNameTest` with the unexported marker
     plus `matches`, and five arms — `ctaExactName`, `ctaAnyName`, `ctaAnyLocal`,
     `ctaAnySpace`, `ctaUnresolvedTest`. `ctaAnySpace{local}` and
     `ctaAnyLocal{space}` being distinct TYPES is what makes "any-space with a
     non-empty space" unrepresentable (T1); a name plus `anySpace`/`anyLocal`
     flags is the shape refused. No type switch over the sum exists anywhere —
     the only uses are `ctaAttr.test.matches` and the five method bodies.
  3. **`err:XPST0081` is a compile-time withhold carried by a TYPE, not a
     sentinel value.** `ctaUnresolvedName` works for a QName only because no
     writable QName has an empty local part; there is no such uninhabited
     namespace, so building `ctaAnyLocal{space: ""}` from an unbound prefix would
     be a silent wrong answer ("every attribute in no namespace"). The arm comes
     with a `ctaStaticError` defect, `CompileCTATest` withholds, and
     `CTATestStaticError` charges — never a dynamic `false`. Failing the PARSE
     instead was explicitly refused: an unsupported decline dominates a static
     one and would under-charge the schema.
  4. **One new token kind, one scanner.** `ctaWildcardTok` sits beside
     `ctaNameTok` and scans `*`, `NCName ':' '*'` and `'*' ':' NCName` as a single
     token with no interior whitespace; the existing `ctaScanQName` was FOLDED
     into the NameTest scan rather than joined by a second QName scanner (T4). No
     bare `:` token is emitted (it would make `@p : name` parse), `ctaNameTok` was
     not widened (it also carries keywords and the axis name), and
     `ctaWildcardTok` is accepted by `attrName` and by nothing else — so `1 * 2`
     still declines and no multiplicative production is implied.
  5. **The operand becomes sequence-valued once, by generalizing the existing
     sum.** `ctaAbsent` RETIRES into a zero-length `ctaAtoms{vs []value.Value}` —
     the XDM's own encoding of the empty sequence, and keeping both would be two
     encodings of "no items" (STYLE D3) — and the `ctaRaisedItem` helper goes with
     it. A comparison is then §3.5.2's existential: true iff some pair holds,
     **false and not an error** over an empty match set, which is a legitimate
     non-error selection outcome under `key-cta-ta-select` clause 2.
  6. **The operand is converted WHOLE, eagerly**, on §3.5.2's own latitude ("may
     raise a dynamic error as soon as it encounters an error in evaluating either
     operand"), with the cost stated at `ctaAttrItem`'s doc rather than
     discovered: `@* = 3` over attributes `n="3" s="abc"` answers error (hence
     false) rather than true. The licensed fallback — per-PAIR conversion, which
     must then be `ctaAtoms{items []ctaItem}` and never a `raisedSome bool` beside
     the values — stays recorded and unbuilt. What would reopen it is an arbiter
     finding a `CTA/` suite case with a mixed-type wildcard operand: a
     measurement, not a design question.
  7. **Two or more matched items under `cast as T` is `err:XPTY0004` whether or
     not `?` is written**, since §3.10.2 rule 3's `?` widens "exactly one" to *at
     most* one. Only a wildcard can create that case, and it has its own test.
  8. **The commit ORDER was a constraint and not a reason to split**
     (docs/WORKFLOW.md, *Scope*): writing the wildcard evaluation against a
     capability that
     cannot serve it is the failure mode, but landing the swap alone would ship a
     rename justified by nothing, since its wildcard arms would have no consumer.

An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization"* — **reproduces nowhere**, so the document had been quoting a string no probe produces; the lossy-read claim is re-scoped from "GitHub" to **the MCP channel specifically** and gains the escaping half (`'` `"` `&` read back as `&#39;` `&#34;` `&amp;`) beside #764's angle-bracket deletion; CLAUDE.md's Surveys block stops printing the `gh issue list --json` spelling — that spelling **is** the GraphQL path and therefore 403s here — and points instead at a new `## Survey input` section carrying #840's paginate-and-reshape recipe with all three of its traps; **doc-only, two files, `Spec: n/a`, `Ratchet: unchanged`, arbiter ACCEPT round 1 with zero findings against the diff**, the one blocking finding being the absence of this entry

     unproduced sibling — and became a bare `return true`.

  literal chain is cvc-complex-type cl.1.2 (or cvc-attribute cl.3, or cvc-type

  separated String Valid clause 1 (whitespace/pre-lexical facets) and clause 3
  (ENTITY checks) from Datatype Valid so the three are not conflated. **No spec
  rule governs Go error-wrapping mechanics** — confirmed absent by design, not
  merely unfound, which is what let `Spec:` carry rule IDs while the change
  itself is a representation decision.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **`New`-plus-`Err`, not `xsderr.Wrap`.** `Wrap` overwrites `Msg` with
     `err.Error()` verbatim — right for attaching a rule and a `Loc` to a deeper
     *plain* error (its five `value` and three `parser`/`xmltree` uses), wrong
     here, where it would leave only the datatype verdict and drop the sentence
     naming the construct. The Acceptance forbids exactly that regression, so
     the issue title's *"`xsderr.Wrap` is used ZERO times in the package"* is
     **still true after the landing** and is no longer a defect.
  2. **The chain gets no synthetic `cvc-simple-type` node.**
     `value.ValidateLexical` already returns the Datatype Valid verdict itself,
     so `errors.Unwrap` reaches it in one hop; inventing an intermediate node
     would assert a charge this package does not make.
  3. **#913's third site was absorbed, not filed.** `contentCheck.simpleTypeValue`
     (cvc-type cl.3.1.3) landed on `main` at `abd64bf` **after** #914 was filed
     and is the same one-line fix through the same helper over the same verdict;
     it needs no rule ID the grounding does not cover, adds no surface, and
     cannot move a lane on its own. The arbiter checked and found the absorption
     **narrower than the commit body claimed** — the post-#913 body correction
     had already re-scoped Acceptance to a grep whose snapshot lists
     `cvccomplexcontent.go:508`, so the site was inside the issue all along.
  4. **Clause 4 is NAMED, not fixed.** Wrapping it means changing `ValidDefault`
     to return a verdict: an exported method on the `xsd.ValueSpace` interface
     (`xsd/valuespace.go:130`), its `value` implementation, `undecidedValueSpace`,
     and the second consumer at `xsd/valueconstraintvalid.go:452`
     (a-props-correct/au-props-correct at assembly) — an exported-surface change
     across two other packages with its own T5 review and its own ratchet
     attribution, so a separate issue under WORKFLOW's scope rule. `xsd`'s own
     doc makes the discard **deliberate**: *"The specific per-facet reason is
     deliberately dropped rather than returned … threading the datatype-layer
     reason out would file a `cvc-*` message under a schema-component rule ID."*
  5. **The inner `Loc` still renders as `?` and that is correct here.**
     `value.ValidateLexical(b, schema, st, lexical, ctx)` takes no `Loc`, so

## 2026-08-20 — #901 — parser: an EMPTY `xs:sequence`/`xs:all` carrying `maxOccurs="0"` at the TOP model-group position is finally charged `p-props-correct`, and the whole fix is ARM ORDER — §3.4.2.3.3 clause 2.1 is a **disjunction** over 2.1.1-2.1.4 whose arms all reach the same ***empty*** ·explicit content· (`xmlschema11-1.md:1746`), so which arm answers may not also decide whether the model-group child maps to a Particle at all; `explicitContent` tested 2.1.2 (an `all`/`sequence` with no children of its own) ahead of 2.1.4 (`maxOccurs="0"`) and returned `nil, nil` before #883's Particle-building arm ran, while §3.8.2 (`:2383`) maps that same element to a Particle whose `{min occurs}` of 1 — `minOccurs` defaults to 1, verified at `:2270`/`:2367`/`:2373`/`:2379` — exceeds its `{max occurs}` of 0, which is exactly what already rejects the identical element one level down; **2.1.4 now runs first** and **no new rule ID or charging logic** was needed, because `occursOf` → `xsd.NewOccurs` already charges `p-props-correct` clause 2.1 once a Particle is built, so the executable content of this landing is one `if` block moved up nine lines; the both-zero gate (§3.7.2/§3.8.2's *"corresponds to no component at all"*, conjunctive `minOccurs=maxOccurs=0`) is **untouched and deliberately unreconciled** with clause 2.1.4's max-only test, pinned by two new ACCEPT rows; the `GAP(xsd)` marker #883 landed and retargeted here is **REMOVED, not repointed** — the gap is closed — and replaced by a normative paragraph on the arm ordering; **arbiter ACCEPT in one round, no repair round**, `Ratchet: unchanged` **explained by the corpus rather than merely observed** (17 of the 39 candidates are empty-bodied and all 17 are `xsd:group ref`, which took 2.1.4 before AND after — zero witnesses of the flipped shape), `go tool surface -base origin/main` **`surface: unchanged`**; - Decisions made and why:
  1. **The skip was NARROWED, not replaced by a second walk.** The old first line
     returned for `el.Name().Space() != xsd.XMLSchemaNS || isXSD(el,
     "annotation")`; the annotation half of that disjunction is what protected
     lax content, so it becomes an `<appinfo>`/`<documentation>` return and the
     walk descends into `<annotation>` to reach its direct children — one walk,
     two faults, no duplicated traversal (STYLE T4/D3). The doc comment is
     restructured to name the two footings **as two**, opening on *"two DISTINCT
     annotation faults resting on two DIFFERENT spec footings — do not conflate
     them"*, because the whole history of this pair (#836, then this) is
     conflation.
  2. **The `{schema, redefine}` exemption is not inherited, and the new check
     runs FIRST.** Both witnesses nest under `<schema>`'s own `<annotation>` —
     the exact parent #836's guard exempts — so a check that reused the
     exemption would reject neither. Ordering the content-model test above the
     cardinality test also means an `<annotation>` bearing two `<annotation>`
     children earns the content-model diagnostic naming the FIRST child, not a
     cardinality diagnostic naming the second; `annotB005` is that shape, and
     the test pins line 3 for both the one- and two-nested rows.
  3. **The charge is `fmt.Errorf`, and the test ASSERTS the absence of a rule
     ID** — `errors.As(err, &xe)` on `*xsderr.Error` must fail. STYLE E2 is
     otherwise unpinnable: nothing else would catch a later hand adding a
     plausible-looking `src-annotation` to the catalog, and `xsderr`'s own
     anchor-derived entries make that easy to do by accident (the #908 entry's
     `"src-notation"` generation artifact, one landing ago).
  4. ***The grounding asked the commit to acknowledge §2.4's MAY, and the landed
     tree does not — this bullet is the acknowledgement.*** The grounding's final
     citation list said *"must acknowledge"* that §2.4 (`:615`-`:616`) **permits**
     a processor to treat such a document as valid, so §5.1 should not be implied
     to mandate rejection. Neither `b35f2c6`'s message nor the doc comment says
     it. What actually decides the direction is the grounding's own EDGE CASES:
     `annotB001`/`annotB005` are recorded `invalid` by the W3C suite and banked
     `fail`, so **rejecting is what makes the ratchet agree with the suite** —
     conformant under clause 1, and the reason is the corpus rather than a spec
     MUST. Left as a Next item rather than a repair round: no measured thing
     changes, and #929's precedent is that a doc-sentence correction rides a pen
     commit or the next landing.
  5. **The arbiter's STYLE 4 nit was judged and KEPT.** `parser/produce.go:539`'s
     `!isXSD(el, "annotation")` guard on the cardinality branch is provably
     redundant — the content-model check above it returns for any `<annotation>`

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **A decision VALUE, not a fake `testing.TB`.** `unusableSuiteEnd` returns
     `suiteRunEnd{fatal, msg}` and `endUnusableSuiteRun` binds `os.Getenv` and
     reports it. A `TB` fake would be a large surface maintained for a two-bit

     `removalAssertions` already set — pure decision plus thin env binding — and
     the two doc comments now point at each other, which is what makes a repeated
     shape legible rather than accidental (STYLE T4).

     ends the run, so the `return` after `endUnusableSuiteRun` is unreachable
     today and untestable without an actual missing suite. Its doc comment names
     that reason, which is the only place the constraint can live: the fault it
     prevents is a *future* `t.Errorf`, and no test can be written against a
     branch that does not exist yet.
  3. **`t.Fatal`/`t.Skip`, not the `...f` variants.** The message is now a
     computed string, so a `%` inside a suite path or a wrapped `os.Stat` error
     would be eaten as a format verb by `t.Fatalf(msg)`. Not incidental to the
     extraction — it is forced by it.

     interpolating `suiteOptionalEnv`.** Routing the golden through the constant
     would go blind to a rename of the env var's *value*, which is the

     reads at first glance as an inconsistency with the same test's use of

- **Spec: the tableau's case discriminator is the BASE's own `{content
  type}.{variety}`, never the presence of the inline `<simpleType>`.** Case 1
  fires on a base whose own content type is simple, case 2 on mixed with an
  ·emptiable· particle; the inline `<simpleType>` chooses B *within* case 1
  (clause 1.1 against 1.2) and SB *within* case 2, and gating case selection on
  it builds the wrong component silently. Under `<simpleContent>`, `base=` is
  `use="required"` on `xs:restrictionType` (`xmlschema11-1.md:4846`), so the
  inline child is **not** an alternative to it — unlike the datatype-level
  `xs:restriction`, whose own doc note calls the two mutually exclusive
  (`xmlschema11-2.md:3940-3956`). The grounding's other load-bearing separation
  is `<assert>` against `<assertion>`: the trailing `assert*` is the CTD's
  `{assertions}` via §3.4.2.1, the `<assertion>` inside the facet choice is a
  facet of the synthesized simple type, two element names feeding two properties
  with no error raised if conflated.

  by construction.** `src-element` clause 5 (§3.3.3, `xmlschema11-1.md`) —
  *"Every `<alternative>` element but the last has a `test` attribute; the last
  `<alternative>` element may have such an attribute"* — is the only constraint
  in §3.3 that sees the shape. `e-props-correct` clause 6 (§3.3.6.1) reads like
  a redundant catch (*"for each Type Alternative in
  E.{type table}.{alternatives}, the {test} property is not ·absent·"*) and
  cannot be one: `{alternatives}` is built per `dcl.elt.common` from the tested
  children ONLY, so a test-less member can never appear there to violate it.

  type-attribute-versus-child shape, never sibling ordering. The arbiter
  re-derived all three from the spec text rather than accepting the oracle's
  argument, and the charge sits in the right phase: `src-element` is a Schema
  **Representation** Constraint, charged at mapping time before any component
  is built.
- Decisions made and why:

     slice for a one-line predicate that needs the index; charging in

     the child list `typeTableOf` already holds.

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **An ordered position walk, not a fixed linear order over element names.**
     The four fixtures read at a glance like a five-name sequence check, and
     that check would falsely reject every legal `attribute`/`attributeGroup`
     interleaving (PRINCIPLES 14, the hazard the GROUNDING named explicitly):
     `xs:attrDecls` is ONE `maxOccurs="unbounded"` choice over the two, so it
     is one repeated position, and `ctD043`'s fault is specifically that
     `<anyAttribute>` holds the position *behind* that block with no re-entry.
     The accept row `attribute, attributeGroup, attribute, attributeGroup,
     anyAttribute, assert, assert` under a `simpleContent` extension is what
     pins the difference — a real interleaving, not a single-instance case.
  2. **No rule ID, a plain wrapped `fmt.Errorf`, and the issue's own
     instruction obeyed.** The body forbade answering #444's grammar-fault
     versus named-`src-*` fork unilaterally; the oracle answered it from the
     spec texts above, and the repo's own precedent settled the
     representation — `rejectProhibitedAttrs` (`produce.go:1106`) already
     stands on exactly this footing, as do `rejectMisplacedNotation` and
     `rejectRepeatedAnnotations`, each returning a plain error carrying no
     `xsderr.Rule`. The error names the offending child, its position, the
     owning element, its position, the Appendix A production and the quoted
     content model (STYLE E1/E3/E4). No new `xsderr` constant, no catalog
     entry.
  3. **The shared tails are held once, not repeated per model** (STYLE T4).
     `s4sAttributeTail` (`xs:attrDecls` + `xs:assertions`) and
     `s4sStructuralTail` (`openContent?` + `typeDefParticle?` in front of it)
     are each one var used by the five models that carry them, so they cannot
     drift apart; the facet position asks `builtin.FacetKindByName` — the
     bridge `facetKindOf` already uses — instead of retyping thirteen facet
     names.
  4. **Charged ahead of every `src-ct` clause and behind the alternant
     guards.** `src-ct`'s preamble settles the ordering question on the spec's
     own terms: the grammar's shape is decided before the additions apply. It
     runs behind `repeatedContentAlternative`, `repeatedDerivationAlternant`
     and `misplacedOpenContent`, whose diagnostics name the offending sibling
     and its wrapper where this check could only say "repeats a position", and
     ahead of `repeatedFacetChild` without usurping it — the facet position is
     `repeated: true`, so facet repetition passes this check and `src-ct`
     clause 2 still gets its case, pinned by the `repeated enumeration pattern
     and assertion facets` accept row.
  5. **`produceImplicitContent` gets no call of its own.** The positions are
     the `<complexType>`'s, so the check is charged where the disjunct is
     chosen. Every complex type funnels through `produceComplexType`
     (`produce.go:1347`, `:1477`, `:2092`, `produce_complex.go:2058`,
     `produce_typetable.go:208` — the arbiter checked there is no other entry),
     which is what makes all five sites reachable from three call sites.
  6. **The Summary's looser reading of `s4sStructuralTail`, deliberately.**
     Appendix A's `xs:complexRestrictionType` (`:4850`) wraps `openContent?`
     and a **required** `typeDefParticle` in one optional sequence, so
     `<openContent>` with no model group fails there and passes here. Taking
     the summary's reading means this check only ever rejects what both
     readings reject; if it is wrong the fix is one extra rejection, not a
     redesign, and the divergence is recorded on the var.
  7. **A child no position of the model admits is stepped over, not rejected**,
     and so is every non-XSD-namespace child — the latter is what
     `xs:simpleRestrictionModel`'s `{any with namespace: ##other}` position
     admits. The admitted-nowhere class is a different fault this check does
     not charge.
  8. **The gate side is untouched** — `attrDeclsDecidable`,
     `contentDecidable` and `simpleContentRestrictionDecidable` in
     `conformance/schema.go` all stay as they are. All four named cases were
     already DECIDED and merely flip ACCEPT → REJECT; narrowing the gate to
     re-decline them is the ratchet-integrity fault the issue named.
     `combineAttributeWildcards` still intersects, because `ctD034` is now
     rejected at the grammar layer before that code is reached and the
     intersection path remains right for legal single-wildcard folds.
  9. **`parser/doc.go`'s closing enumeration of the error kinds this package
     emits gained the no-rule-ID class** (STYLE T6). It listed `src-*`,
     `cos-*`, `derivation-ok-*` and `cvc-datatype-valid` and was already silent
     about the plain grammar fault; this change makes that class much larger.

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **`kind != xsd.FacetAssertions`, not a literal `"assertions"` guard.** The
     bridge is a bijection (`builtin/seed_test.go`'s
     `TestFacetKindByNameCoversTheGeneratedTable` pins injectivity), so the two
     are behaviourally identical today; the kind check is the SAME exclusion
     shape `facetKindOf` (`parser/produce.go:2889`) already uses one package
     over, so there is one idiom at one seam rather than two (STYLE T4), and it
     keeps working if the generated table's spelling changes.
     `xsd.FacetEnumeration` is deliberately NOT excluded alongside it:
     `<enumeration>` is a real element name and `restrictionFacets` folds it.
     Mason nominated this choice for the hardest scrutiny and the arbiter
     re-derived it from the table rather than ratifying the argument.
  2. **Nothing singularizes anything, so `<assert>` is untouched.** The oracle's
     edge case: `assert` is a THIRD distinct name in the same production, the
     CTD-level assertion of the trailing position, and `attrDeclsDecidable`
     takes it before `facetElement` is reached. The doc comment now says so
     rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.
  3. **Item 2's acceptance criterion has two halves that pull apart, and the
     normative half won.** "Name the real reason" and "one place to update, not
     two" cannot both hold while the reason is fixture-specific; the message was
     made true, the explanation kept in the doc comment, and the repointing
     instruction extended to `"REPOINT this test at another undecidable fixture
     and restate the reason in the failure message with it"`. A
     fixture-independent message would have satisfied the second half by
     retiring the guard the first half exists to keep sharp.
  4. **The case-5 arm is poisoned on purpose.** `restrictedSimpleBase`
     (`parser/produce_complex.go:802`) discriminates the case off the base alone
     and returns before the inline `<simpleType>` is read, so a benign inline —

## 2026-08-23 — #950 — an out-of-enumeration `processContents` is charged `cvc-datatype-valid`, not `w-props-correct`, because `produceWildcard` raises the fault BEFORE `xsd.NewWildcard` builds the component the constraint quantifies over — the same two-layer split #932 settled one attribute group over, and settled here by the identical argument: Appendix A's wildcard attribute group declares `processContents` as an `xs:NMTOKEN` restricted by `xs:enumeration` to skip/lax/strict (`xmlschema11-1.md:5346-5353`), so a lexical outside that value space is §5.1's first bullet — one attribute failing its own declared type — and `w-props-correct` clause 1 stays charged, untouched, by `xsd.NewWildcard` (`xsd/wildcard.go:56`) on the component-exists path; `ruleWildcardCorr` had exactly one use and is **deleted with it**, the rule ID surviving in `xsd`'s own `ruleWildcardCorrect` (`xsd/namespaceconstraint.go:21`) and in `xsderr/catalog.go:222`; **arbiter ACCEPT in ONE round, ZERO findings**, `Ratchet: unchanged` and — the point worth carrying — unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by observation, since `decidableRules` (`conformance/instance.go:357`) scores neither `w-props-correct` nor `cvc-datatype-valid` and no conformance case can see this attribution at all; the durable correction is mason's to its own brief: `parser/produce_wildcard_internal_test.go:40-41` was said to assert the old charge and to need updating, and it does not — those lines belong to `TestDisallowedNameKeywordOf` and already assert `ruleDatatypeValid` — so `parser/produce_wildcardrule_test.go` is **FIRST coverage of a bogus `processContents` lexical, not a moved assertion**, and the deletion was safe because nothing in the package ever pinned the constant

  none` and true by construction: `processContentsOf` and `produceWildcard` are

- **Spec: the two layers are declared in different parts and neither reaches the
  other.** Appendix A declares `processContents` in the wildcard attribute group
  both `<any>` and `<anyAttribute>` use, as an `xs:NMTOKEN` restricted by
  `xs:enumeration` to skip/lax/strict (`xmlschema11-1.md:5346-5353`) — an
  attribute whose value space is fixed by its own declared type, which puts a
  lexical outside it under §5.1's first bullet, charged `cvc-datatype-valid`
  (Datatypes §4.1.4, `xmlschema11-2.md:2820`). `w-props-correct` (§3.10.6.1) is a
  Schema Component Constraint: clause 1 reads an existing Wildcard's `{process
  contents}` property, so it has nothing to quantify over until `xsd.NewWildcard`
  returns. The shape is structurally identical to the `minOccurs`/`maxOccurs`
  attributes #932 already moved, which is why this landing needed a grounding to
  confirm the analogy holds and not one to invent an argument. Rules charged or
  played against: `cvc-datatype-valid`, `w-props-correct`.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **`cvc-datatype-valid`, not a Schema Representation Constraint and not a new
     rule ID.** The oracle checked whether any `src-`/`-props-correct` constraint
     covers an out-of-enumeration `processContents` and found none; the fault is
     the schema document failing the schema for schema documents, which is the
     convention `parser/produce.go`'s `ruleDatatypeValid` doc comment already
     states for exactly this class. That comment's precedent list gained this
     site, so the next occurrence of the shape reads the settled answer instead of
     re-deriving it.
  2. **`w-props-correct` stays exactly where it is.** The charge at
     `xsd/wildcard.go:56` is correct — a Wildcard exists there — and covers the
     programmatic construction path that bypasses the producer entirely,
     already pinned by `xsd/wildcard_test.go`. Nothing about this landing weakens
     that side; it removes a second, wrong claimant to the same rule ID.
  3. **`ruleWildcardCorr` DELETED rather than left unused.** The changed site was
     its only use in `parser`, and an unused rule constant is a false signal that
     the package charges a component constraint it no longer charges (STYLE D3).
     The ID itself is not lost: `xsd` owns it as `ruleWildcardCorrect` and
     `xsderr/catalog.go` still lists it.
  4. **The `parser/doc.go:242` package-contract paragraph was absorbed, not
     deferred.** It enumerates the sites that charge `cvc-datatype-valid`, so the
     same commit that adds a site either updates it or leaves it false —
     **STYLE T6**, and the arbiter independently ruled the absorption in-scope
     rather than creep. A one-line addition to a paragraph the diff falsifies is
     not a second change.
  5. **A new external test file rather than an addition to
     `produce_wildcard_internal_test.go`.** The table drives whole documents
     through `produce` and asserts rule ID plus position, which is the external
     package's job; the internal file tests an unexported helper directly. Four
     fault rows (`<any>` and `<anyAttribute>`, a plain bogus token, the
     case-sensitivity row `"Strict"`, and a lexical that is not even an NMTOKEN)
     and three accept controls for skip/lax/strict on both wildcard kinds.

     needed updating. Those lines are inside `TestDisallowedNameKeywordOf`, an
     unrelated test that has always asserted `ruleDatatypeValid`. Nothing in the

     rule ID could have been changed in either direction with the whole suite
     still green, and the new table is first coverage rather than a relocated

     unchanged by this diff and correct, and **filed nothing** — a non-finding

the oracle re-derived that there is no numbered `cvc-*`/`src-*`/`cos-*` ID for general grammar conformance at all — `sd-valid` appears exactly ONCE in the whole document and ZERO times in Appendix B's catalog line range, §5.1's parallel bullet (`:4296`) has no anchor, and §2.3's `gloss-src` (`:607`) plus every `src-*` preamble (`src-ct` `:1946`, `src-ta` `:3218`) put the `src-*` catalog **"beyond"/"in addition to"** the grammar rather than over it, which yields a genuine three-population reading (XML well-formedness / s4s-grammar conformance / catalog violation) with these sites in the middle one; the ruling is written **BY SHAPE, naming `rejectProhibitedAttrs` and `checkS4SChildOrder` as the exemplars to copy, and deliberately not by count or by site list** — the population had already drifted 8 → 21 between the issue's filing and this landing without the doc's normative claim breaking, and the next producer landing will move it again;   3. **#881 → keep the gate uniform, and that closes it.** Its own Acceptance

     CLAUDE.md's one rule and `arbiter.md`'s ratchet-integrity section reserve
     to a human-filed issue — a retro may not take it; the condition's only

     have left #867 unlanded, and #867's takeover was right — it banked `schema`
     +2 off a grounding that was the branch's whole asset. **The clock is the
     newest issue-thread comment against the same 2h TTL, not a second
     threshold**: a lease-only branch is lease-only *because* its holder
     produced no commit, and a session still working would have checkpointed
     inside the TTL, so one clock covers both cases and #946's *"a grep for
     CLAIMED returns one rule"* holds. #722 is preserved exactly — no age
     reading RETIRES a lease-only branch; the thread licenses **taking** the
     work, and the taker posts a takeover comment and pushes the heartbeat, so
     the ref settles the race as it does everywhere else. `develop.md` step 2
     loses the sentence that contradicted itself and points at the invariant;
     the pick step's *"Resuming beats starting"* now names takeable CLAIMED
     beside EXPIRED. **`wip/issue-862` is the live case and is takeable under
     this rule** — ~3 days past its last thread comment — but a branch is not a
     chronicler's to touch, so it is named here for the next `/develop`.

     detection"* — and STYLE P3 (`docs/STYLE.md:161`) does state it exactly
     right, so more STYLE prose would be the accretion this command exists to
     prevent, and P3's *"no matter how honest the prose around it is"* is
     already the sentence a sharpening would rewrite. **The criterion**: flag a
     doc comment that discloses incompleteness — an uncharged rule, a decline,
     a fail-open — where the enclosing declaration carries no `GAP(`, report it
     as heuristic in the tool's own output the way `gapaudit` already reports
     its matching, and never fail a gate on it. Under-report rather than
     over-report, on #779's stated reasoning. **Routed back, not discharged**:
     the verification is a Go change plus table tests over the four witnesses
     (#957's `parser/produce_typetable.go:81-88`, #398's `notImplemented`, and
     the two closed ones), which a retro cannot honestly perform.

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Ruled on all five retro-blocked issues rather than reading them and
     carrying them.** A question routed to an audit and left unruled is worse
     than one never routed, because the routing reads as a plan. #881's ruling
     changes nothing and is still a ruling.
  2. **Hoisted the claims rule out of Filing discipline instead of adding a
     second copy to `mason.md` and `arbiter.md`.** All three witnesses failed in
     artefacts those files own, which is the argument for putting it where every
     session reads it exactly once.
  3. **One fix for three friction classes.** The submodule paragraph, the
     doc-only gate cost and PLAN staleness are one failure — an entry
     re-deriving what a document already says — and three separate rules would
     have been the accretion.
  4. **Extended banding to `kind/refactor` rather than filing an issue about
     it.** The band is `cartographer.md` step 4's, the paragraph was being
     rewritten anyway, and the mechanism is identical to the one the sixth retro
     landed for process work. Filing an issue would have put the fix in the
     queue that does not drain.
  5. **`docs/STYLE.md` and `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` read and NOT touched.** Nothing
     this window earned an invariant or a code-shape rule, and #960's ruling is
     explicitly that STYLE P3 needs no sharpening.
  6. **CLAUDE.md's "one rule" and `arbiter.md`'s ratchet-integrity section were
     not touched**, and #881's ruling turns on that boundary rather than merely
     respecting it. CLAUDE.md is unedited in this commit entirely.
- Surprises:
  1. ***Ten issues were addressed to this audit and the audit had no mailbox.***
     Five name it as their trigger in `## Depends on`, a sixth is blocked on
     those five, and the cartographer had already written the list into a LOG
     entry's Next. Every part of the pipeline worked except the one where the
     recipient looks.
  2. **The regex that produced two retros' repair rates matches almost every
     entry.** `REJECT` appears in 35 of 39 landings and `repair round` in 22 —
     because these entries reason *about* rejects and repairs. Two published
     trend lines rest on that classifier.
  3. **96% of the window's ratchet movement is one landing.** The headline
     figure more than doubled per session while the median landing moved
     essentially nothing.
  4. **#968 parked with zero arbiter rounds** — no verdict was solicited or
     needed, because the blocker was a ratchet fact. The two-reject cap is not
     the only way an attempt ends.
- Friction — what this session paid that the documents did not predict:
  1. **`docs/ROUTINES.md`'s Survey input recipe cannot be run by an isolated
     agent.** It is a `for` loop plus a `jq -s` glob, and a worktree-isolated
     agent's bash is refused on any compound command (*"too complex to verify
     that it stays inside the worktree"*). Worked around by writing the loop to
     a scratch `.sh` and invoking `sh <path>`, which passes. Not filed from here
     and not written into ROUTINES either — the constraint is the harness's, the
     workaround is one line, and a document that starts encoding one agent
     type's shell restrictions has taken on a subject it cannot keep true.
  2. **`docs/LOG/2026-08.md` is 3.3 MB / 42,057 lines across 220 entries**, mean
     **173 lines per entry**, and the `##` headline alone now averages **1,745
     characters** — up from 661 in the month's first week. Every survey of the
     file is a full-file scan and no single read covers a retro window. **#600
     tracks the layout question and is now four retros old**; the entry-length
     question underneath it is not filed, and Duty 1's Friction rule landed here
     is the first thing to bite on it. Re-measure next retro before filing:
     if mean entry length has not fallen, the rule is not enough.

## 2026-08-23 — #884 — **the diagnosis-only issue was a CRASH fix, and the same one line is both**: `buildDefinitionModelGroup` returning `rejectNamedGroupBody(el)` where it used to return a zero `xsd.ModelGroup` closes a **panic** on the path its own doc comment never described — `produceGroupRefParticle`'s `src-expredef` clause 2 branch, reached by a `<redefine>` over a **bodyless original** `<group>` and NEVER through `produceModelGroupDefinition`, so `mgd-props-correct` was not late there, it was **unreachable**: the zero `ModelGroup` became a `Particle` that `xsd.NewParticle` admits (its `{term}` is a non-nil `ResolvedTerm` wrapping a zero value) and the content automaton then hit `xsd: automaton.addModelGroup: non-exhaustive Compositor switch` (`xsd/particleattribution.go:483`), reachable from `parser.ParseReport` on an untrusted schema document — **the arbiter reproduced it independently by reverting that single line**, and `TestParseRedefineGroupBodylessOriginalRejected` is genuine new coverage of a crash `origin/main` carried uncovered; the issue's own Acceptance said *"diagnosis-only — all four shapes are already REJECTED today and stay rejected"*, which is true of the four shapes it repro'd and **wrong about the change**, in the safe direction; the message half is what was asked for and lands as specified: the oracle re-derived `xs:namedGroup`'s grammar (`xmlschema11-1.md:5187`-`:5216`, a three-arm `all`/`choice`/`sequence` choice each pinned `minOccurs="1" maxOccurs="1"`, admitting neither a nested `<group ref=>` nor a bare `<element>`), confirmed §3.7.3 (`:2286`) answers *"None as such."* and that `src-mgd` matches **zero times** in the whole spec, so the fault is **#966's s4s-grammar class in its first application, hours after that class was ruled in the same session** — a plain `fmt.Errorf`, no `Rule`, naming the offending item, its `Loc` and the Appendix A production, positioned at the first child `xs:namedGroup` does not admit and only at the `<group>` when there is none; `xs:groupRef` (the reference-form production) was deliberately NOT touched and `mgd-props-correct` was NOT deleted, only stopped from being reached down a document-fault path — it keeps its real route at `xsd/redefinition.go:207`; - **Spec.** `xs:namedGroup`'s content model is `(annotation?, (all | choice |
  sequence))` with the inner choice `minOccurs="1" maxOccurs="1"`
  (`xmlschema11-1.md:5187`-`:5216`) — the reference form lives in a **different
  production**, `xs:groupRef`, which is why a nested `<group ref= name=>` body is
  charged here and not for its prohibited `name`. §3.7.3 (`:2286`-`:2288`) reads
  *"None as such."* in full and `src-mgd` returns **zero matches** spec-wide, so
  there is no Schema Representation Constraint to cite; `mgd-props-correct`
  (§3.7.6, `:2302`, confirmed bold-labeled) is a **Schema Component Constraint
  over an already-built tableau** — one phase later than, and one element up
  from, the document fault. What binds is §2.4 clause 1, `sd-valid` (`:615`),
  the uncataloged class `xsderr/doc.go` owns as of #966. Rules played against,
  none charged: `mgd-props-correct`, `cos-all-limited` (§3.8.6.2 clause 1.1

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The rejection belongs in `buildDefinitionModelGroup`, not in
     `produceModelGroupDefinition`** — and that placement is the whole crash
     fix. `produceModelGroupDefinition` is not the only caller; `src-expredef`
     clause 2 builds the original a redefining `<group>`'s self-reference
     resolves to through `buildDefinitionModelGroup` **alone**, because clause
     4.1.2 keeps the redefined name out of the top-level tables. Guarding at the
     producer would have fixed the message and left the panic.
  2. **Report at the first child `xs:namedGroup` does not admit; report at the
     `<group>` only when there is none.** An unadmitted child IS the mistake; an
     unfilled required position is all that is left to say when the document
     wrote nothing. That is `rejectProhibitedRefAttrs`'s ordering read from the
     other side.
  3. **Embed the Appendix A production line in the message** — `xs:namedGroup`
     plus `xmlschema11-1.md:5187`. Not novel: `checkS4SChildOrder` already does
     the identical thing through `s4sModel.spec`, so mason copied precedent
     rather than inventing a shape (see Surprise 2).
  4. **Foreign-namespace children are skipped, not charged.** `xs:namedGroup`
     admits none of them either, but saying so is a different fault this check
     does not claim — `checkS4SChildOrder`'s reasoning for the same skip.
  5. **`mgd-props-correct` is not deleted.** It keeps its genuine route
     (`xsd/redefinition.go:207`), where it judges a built component. Only the
     document-fault path stopped reaching it.
  6. **Three doc comments were corrected in the same commit**, one in
     `parser/produce_complex.go` and two in `conformance/schema.go`, because
     each described a document fault as routing through `mgd-props-correct` and
     each is false the moment the code lands (**STYLE T6**).

  shape. #999 states deletion as the live option, since `dispatchCases` already

  goxsd8 -q parse a.xsd        exit=2  goxsd8: no subcommand given
  goxsd8 -v gen -schema a.xsd  exit=2  goxsd8: no subcommand given

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **Full unification, not the design-only fallback the issue permitted.**
     After reading all four functions the three non-Phase-A descents were
     structurally identical — charge on entry, descend, skip every by-name arm —
     and Phase A was the same tree with charges at the by-name arms as well, so
     **one walk with per-component-kind fields covers all four with no per-phase
     conditional**. The sizing question the band flagged as open resolved in the
     reading, not in the design.
  2. **Fields on a struct, never a `descendBase bool` and never an interface.**
     A per-phase `bool` is exactly the representable-wrong-state STYLE D3 forbids
     and **would have preserved the bug as a configuration**; an interface would
     force every phase to spell five methods, four of them empty, which is the
     no-consumer cost T5 objects to, times four. With nil-defaulting fields each
     phase's descent reads as literally its charge list. **A nil field means
     "this phase owes that kind nothing", never "skip that subtree"** — the
     descent is identical for every phase and a component charged at by nobody is
     still walked THROUGH. That contract is in the type's doc, and it is the
     property that makes a fifth phase unable to reintroduce the bug by omission.
  3. **No cycle guard, and it is argued rather than assumed.** The edges that
     could close a cycle are exactly the by-name ones the descent does not
     follow, and an inline base is a `ComplexType` *value* owned by one slot, so
     the walked structure is finite by ownership. The arbiter verified the
     premise rather than reading it, enumerating every producer of an
     `InlineTypeDefinition` in a base slot and finding the `src-expredef`
     clause-1.1 original is the only one that reaches a walk. `ct-props-correct`
     clause 3 owns circular base chains in Phase B; a seen-set here would mask
     that check's absence rather than defend against anything (PRINCIPLES 9).
  4. **`{attribute wildcard}`, `{open content}` and `{assertions}` get no field.**
     Each is a leaf of this tree — none nests a type definition, attribute use or
     element declaration — and a field no phase fills is parameterization without
     a consumer (STYLE T5). The doc says where to add one when a phase needs one.
  5. **Root loops stay per-phase and no root loop changed what it enumerates.**
     Each phase's roots are what its RULE quantifies over; #843 is about the
     descent, not the roots. The two coverage gaps that live in the roots rather
     than the descent are therefore untouched and stay owned elsewhere — see
     #584 under Next.
  6. **`<override>` untouched** (PRINCIPLES 16, the redefine/override asymmetry).
     `grep -i override` over the whole diff returns nothing.
  7. **`noSchema`'s null-`TypeResolver` cleanup was SKIPPED, correctly.** #843's
     body conditioned it on being free; it did not fall out of this diff, so it
     was not taken. Named here so it is not lost.

     circular chain is still representable while this phase runs"* — one file

     each was maintained by eye, and the unification's own justification
     paragraph diverged from the package that already stated the fact.

     allowance ONTO `componentwalk.go` — so the file is now where the repo keeps

     believing acyclicity established when it is not, gets a hang rather than a

## 2026-08-24 — #1001 — **five of §4.2.2's six attributes ship, the sixth is declined in writing, and the split the `/backlog` performed is what let either half land**: every schema document in the assembly closure is now ·conditional-inclusion pre-processed· as it is read — root, `<include>`d, `<import>`ed, `<override>`n, `<redefine>`d, and the one `Produce` is handed — so what every Schema Representation Constraint sees is **S2 = ci(S1)**, and a declaration §4.2.2 removes no longer collides with the sibling it was written to replace, which was the false reject under `sch-props-correct` clause 2; the four availability attributes go through **one** "every item is known" predicate so §4.2.2's empty-list inversion falls out of vacuous truth instead of being written twice and getting exactly one of them backwards; `vc:maxVersion` PRUNING is declined behind a `GAP(parser)` marker naming **#1002**, which is blocked on a human ruling because pruning it removes the `<xs:pattern>` a banked instance case's `pass` rides on — **an agent does not downgrade a banked case** (CLAUDE.md's one rule) — while its lexical validity is still charged `src-cip` independently, a design call the issue delegated and mason both took and MEASURED (every `vc:maxVersion` lexical in the suite is a valid decimal, so the charge moves nothing); **arbiter ACCEPT in ONE round, zero blocking findings, two non-blocking, no repair round**, `Ratchet: schema +8, instance +5, zero regressions` **matching the issue's predicted table case for case**, banked by the arbiter itself as **`4b659bd`**, `surface: unchanged`

- Decisions made and why:
  1. **One universal predicate for all four availability attributes**, not two
     coded arms. `vc:typeAvailable`/`vc:facetAvailable` ignore when NOT every item
     is known; `vc:typeUnavailable`/`vc:facetUnavailable` ignore when every item
     IS known — the empty list satisfies "every item is known" vacuously, so both
     behaviours and the inversion fall out of one function. The issue named this
     as §4.2.2's easiest trap and predicted that coding them separately gets
     exactly one backwards; the shape makes that outcome unrepresentable rather
     than merely tested for.
  2. **`vc:maxVersion` pruning DECLINED, and the decline is a marker, not a
     silence** (STYLE P3, PRINCIPLES 9). The `GAP(parser)` at
     `parser/conditional.go:208` states what is not done — an element
     `vc:maxVersion` excludes is RETAINED — names #1002, and records the reason
     the arm cannot be taken by an agent: it turns a banked instance `pass` over
     to an `<xs:assertion>` this processor does not evaluate.
  3. **`vc:maxVersion`'s lexical validity IS still charged `src-cip`.** The issue
     delegated this call explicitly and required it be stated and measured. The
     argument: `src-cip` constrains the attribute's ·initial value· and is
     independent of what the transform does with the verdict — one clause of rule
     text covers both attributes — so declining the pruning arm is no licence to
     accept a value outside `xs:decimal`. Measured: every `vc:maxVersion` lexical
     in the W3C suite is a valid decimal, so it moves no case either way today.
  4. **An ignored `<schema>` root becomes the stub §4.2.2 prescribes, not an
     empty document**, retaining `targetNamespace` and both version attributes
     unconditionally. No suite fixture reaches the stub through `vc:minVersion`
     alone — `saxonData/VC/vc006.xsd` reaches it through `vc:maxVersion="0.9"`,
     which is #1002's — so it is pinned by a parser-level test, as the issue
     required.
  5. **Two absorbs under WORKFLOW's scope rule, both forced by the diff.**
     `qnameLexical` extracted out of `producer.bindQName` rather than a second
     QName splitter written for the availability lists (STYLE T4); and `Element`
     gaining ownership of its attribute list, because the stub is **the one
     element §4.2.2 strips attributes from without removing** and there was no
     way to represent it while `Attributes()` delegated straight to the start tag.
     Neither adds a rule ID outside the grounding, neither exports anything and
     neither moves a lane independently. The cost of the second is on the record
     in `tree.go`'s own doc: `Attributes()` now returns this package's slice on
     that one element rather than the reader's, `src` staying the source of name,
     location and namespace scope, none of which any pre-processing touches.
  6. **Pruning runs at the shared assembly-fetch path, not at each of five call
     sites.** One seam covers `<include>`/`<import>`/`<override>`/`<redefine>`
     together with the root read and `Produce`; the arbiter's mutation testing

  **re-derived against the tree at `0b259a2`**, not taken from the
  cross-reference, because #1001 shipped **five** of §4.2.2's six attributes and
  a 27-case census is worth one check: `retainedElement` drops an ignored child
  with its whole subtree before the producer runs, so `vc003.xsd`'s out-of-model
  `<xs:last-day-of-month vc:minVersion="5.0"/>` is gone before `restrictionFacets`
  sees it, and the min arm alone fires (V = 1.1 < 5.0). The `vc:maxVersion` arm
  is **not** in #972's path: retention is the safe direction, and the one case in
  the 27 that does need it — `VC/vc007` — was already carved out to #1002 by
  #972's own Acceptance 5. `vc006.xsd` carries `vc:maxVersion="0.9"` on its root,
  so that root is **not** stubbed today and its `<xs:include>` of `vc003` is
  still processed, which is what keeps Acceptance 7 honest rather than
  accidentally vacuous. All four of `vc003`/`vc004-11`/`vc005`/`vc006` verified
  still banked `pass`. Recorded at `issuecomment-5401741418`; the body needed no

- Filed: **#1014** (`ready`, `kind/process`, `area/meta`) — **MCP `issue_read`
  truncates a long issue body with no marker**, which is a different axis from
  the token-stripping `docs/ROUTINES.md`:84-89 and `docs/WORKFLOW.md`:350-366
  both document. Re-measured here independently rather than taken from the
  chronicler's account: #1001's body is **10393 chars** through

  with **`## Surface`, `## Notes` and `## Depends on` entirely absent**. So the
  session that landed #1001 read an issue that appeared to declare no
  dependencies, because the heading carrying them was past the cut. **The
  sharper half is not the read but the write**: WORKFLOW's repair procedure says
  *"leave every other section as it stands, and write that back"*, and under
  truncation those sections are not in the copy — the rule that exists to
  prevent silent body damage **causes** it, through a byte-faithful write that

- **Spec: Structures §5.1 first bullet (`xmlschema11-1.md:4296`) and Datatypes
  §4.1.2 (`xmlschema11-2.md:2748`, grammar `:3929`–`:3939`, group
  `xs:simpleRestrictionModel`).** §5.1's first bullet is **unlabeled** — no
  `cvc-*`, `src-*` or `cos-*` ID exists for "the document is not valid against
  the schema for schema documents" — so the rejection cites §5.1 plain, which is
  the footing `checkS4SChildOrder` and `rejectProhibitedAttrs` already stand on
  and not a fabricated verdict (STYLE E2). The model's only wildcard position is
  `namespace="##other"`, which EXCLUDES the XSD namespace: that single fact is
  what makes an unlisted XSD-namespace name admitted nowhere rather than
  swept up by the wildcard, and it is the whole argument for the reject.
- Decisions made and why:
  1. **The check lives at `constructSimpleType`'s `<restriction>` arm, not in
     `restrictionFacets`.** `restrictionFacets` has two callers reading two
     different content models: §4.1.2's `xs:simpleRestrictionModel`, and
     `simpleContentSimpleType`'s (`parser/produce_complex.go`)
     `xs:simpleRestrictionType`, whose tail legally admits `attribute`,
     `attributeGroup`, `anyAttribute` and `assert` at the position this check
     rejects. One shared answer false-rejects every document in the second
     family. The check therefore sits at the caller that knows which model it
     read, and the seam is pinned by test **from both sides**.
  2. **It runs before `resolveBase`.** The grammar fault is charged
     content-independently, so the verdict on an s4s-invalid `<restriction>`
     does not depend on whether its `base=` resolves — the discipline
     `rejectProhibitedAttrs` already records.
  3. **The membership predicate is `facetKindOf` plus `annotation`,
     `simpleType`, `enumeration`, `assertion` — explicitly NOT
     `s4sFacetElement`** (`parser/produce_s4sorder.go`). That function's own doc
     records that it over-admits `assertions` (plural), `maxScale` and
     `minScale`, which is harmless for the ORDERING check it serves and fatal
     for a membership check. Reusing the nearest-looking predicate is the
     available mistake here, and it is refused in writing at the call site.
  4. **Producer-level, not gate-level: `conformance/schema.go` is untouched.**
     #968 tried the same family by narrowing `simpleTypeDecidable` and could not
     clear the ratchet; the measurement is on **#968's own thread** and is not
     re-derived here. The fault is in what the producer builds, so that is where
     it is charged (#972), and the check's own doc comment carries the same bare
     cite so a later reader reaches the census without this entry.
- Surprises:
  1. **Four Acceptance-6 cases stay `pass` for a DIFFERENT reason than before,
     and the new reason is the right one.** `stC012`, `stC013`, `stC023` and
     `stC028` were rejected by `[src-resolve]` clause 1.1 (three) and
     `[src-attribute]` clause 3 (one); they are now rejected by the s4s check,
     which fires first. The arbiter ruled this **verdict-neutral by
     construction** rather than by re-running: `rejectOutOfModelFacetChildren`
     returns nil unless an out-of-model child exists, so every document without
     one reaches `resolveBase` byte-identically to `origin/main`. It is also the
     **better order** — §5.1 lists s4s validity ahead of the Schema
     Representation Constraints — so it is recorded, not treated as a finding.
  2. **The `vc:` cohort needed no code at all.** `vc003`–`vc006` (Acceptance 7)
     stay banked `pass` because §4.2.2's conditional-inclusion machinery, landed
     by #1001 the day before, prunes the out-of-model child before
     `restrictionFacets` ever sees it. The dependency was real and the interface
     between the two landings held exactly as the #1001 post-land pass
     re-derived it.
  3. **The grounding round caught a premise error in the prompt that launched
     it.** The oracle was asked about `assert` at this position; §4.1.2 spells
     the assertions facet's element `assertion` (**singular**), and `assert` is
     a different, unrelated element legal only in the `xs:simpleRestrictionType`
     model the OTHER caller reads. **The existing code already had this right,
     so no code change followed** — the correction's whole value was preventing
     one, and it is the second decision above that the confusion would have
     broken.
- Friction:
  1. **The `assert`/`assertion` error entered through this session's own oracle
     prompt, not through #972's body** — the issue is correct as filed. An
     orchestrating session paraphrasing a spec name into a specialist's brief is
     a **first sighting** of that shape here; the nearest neighbours are the
     window's agent-account-contradicting-its-source witnesses, which
     `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s **Claims that outlive the session** already governs for
     bodies, verdicts and implementation accounts. A prompt is not one of those
     three, and one sighting is an anecdote — **recorded here so a second can be
     counted**, not filed.
  2. **Nothing else this session paid was unpredicted.** The
     ground-then-implement-then-judge order, the no-warden call on
     `surface: unchanged`, the arbiter banking the ratchet itself, and the
     `docs/PLAN.md` Status stamp being stale between `/backlog` runs are
     `docs/WORKFLOW.md` and `.claude/agents/arbiter.md` working as written.
- Cost — **1 oracle, 1 mason, 1 arbiter.** No repair round, no reject, no warden
  (`surface: unchanged`, nothing exported), no cartographer, no steward. One
  session, one container, one branch, no park. **The oracle round bought the
  `##other` wildcard reading** — the single fact the reject rests on — **and the
  `assert`/`assertion` correction** that kept decision 1's seam intact. **The
  arbiter round bought the independent four-part gate, the ratchet, the
  `surface` check, and two mutations that probe the seam rather than the
  behaviour**: neutering the call fails all nine reject rows, and moving the
  check into the shared `restrictionFacets` fails two new tests **plus three
  pre-existing ones** — which is how "at one caller" was proved load-bearing
  instead of asserted. Predicate completeness was checked independently against
  `builtin/restriction.go`'s facet table rather than against the diff.
- Thread pointers (kud360/goxsd8 #972): **GROUNDING** `issuecomment-5403255035`
  (§4.1.2's content model and grammar lines, §5.1's unlabeled first bullet, and
  the `assert`/`assertion` correction). **Verdict (ACCEPT, round 1, zero
  blocking findings)** `issuecomment-5403636242` (the gate table, the ratchet by

- Next:

  2. **Owed to the post-land pass: #846 is now unblocked and has its first

  3. **`VC/vc007` stays `fail` and that is in scope for nobody here.** It is the
     `vc:maxVersion` arm, carved out to **#1002** by #972's own Acceptance 5, and

  4. **`docs/PLAN.md` was deliberately NOT restamped.** Its Status stamp is the

  5. **Discharged before landing, not owed:** the check at the one call site

- Decisions:
  - **The set is defined operationally, by a pipeline, not descriptively, by a
    noun phrase.** Both #993 rounds failed because a session could execute their
    prose in good faith and still reach `{#669}`; there is no such reading of
    `grep -oE '#[0-9]+' | sort -u` over `%B`. This is the one substantive change
    over `246bba7` — everything else on the branch is that diff lifted
    byte-identical modulo rewrap, so the parts the second #993 verdict already
    ruled sound arrive re-judged rather than re-derived, and
    `.claude/commands/develop.md` carries no hunk against it at all.
  - **`%B`, not `%b` — the subject is in the set.** The procedure is strictly a
    superset of the heading's word "body", never a narrowing, so the heading
    cannot make a session under-enumerate. It costs nothing on either fixture
    (#998's subject carries its own comma list and `sort -u` still yields five)
    and buys the landing whose subject names an absorbed issue the body does not.
  - **Both rejected sets are ruled out BY NAME, each with the one clause that
    says why it collapses.** A negative naming one wrong answer invites the
    other.

    it" — is scoped after enumeration.** Every extracted number is stated
    `closed` or `open` before judgment enters, so the set cannot shrink
    retroactively; a bare `(#N)` citation is inside the set by construction and
    auto-closing it would be wrong.

    which is not the repeated toil PRINCIPLES 27 sends to `kind/tooling`; a Go
    tool for a two-command extraction would be a separate surface, review and
    ratchet attribution for no gain.

- Decisions:
  - **Two markers, not one, and the new one is minted to match the old.**
    `TAKEOVER:` joins the existing `RESUME:` because taking a claim and resuming
    your own are the same assertion — *a session is holding this branch now* —
    and the rule needed to name both or the takeover this very session posted
    would have dated nothing. Matching is case-sensitive against the body's first
    non-whitespace characters: every marker in this corpus is shouted, and a
    lease is not a thing to settle on a fuzzy match.
  - **An undated claim stays CLAIMED indefinitely — option (a) of the two the
    reject offered — and the indefinite case is the accepted cost.** The
    alternative (treat the branch's push time as the zeroth heartbeat) needs a
    ref-creation timestamp the tool cannot get from a clone. `docs/WORKFLOW.md`
    closes the hole prospectively instead of mechanically: `:96` makes the
    `--allow-empty` push the thing that gives a bare claim a tip of its own, and
    `:139`'s `RESUME:` guidance is now unconditional, so a claim that never
    heartbeats is a workflow violation rather than the normal case.
  - **`commentsRead` is a tri-state on purpose: absent ≠ empty.** An issue with
    no `comments` key keeps every verdict it would have had and only its empty
    claim goes undated; an issue whose comments were read and hold no heartbeat
    is a different fact with a different reason string. `Comments *[]ghComment`
    is what carries the distinction through the JSON round trip, and the arbiter
    confirmed it survives the `jq` merge in the ROUTINES recipe.

    (STYLE D3). The proxy and the git fact came apart on exactly one row shape —

  - **The `TIP AGE` → `LEASE AGE` rename is the finding's other half.** Once a
    column says *lease*, a cell holding main's landing age is a doc/code
    mismatch (STYLE P2) and not merely an imprecision; nil now renders `main's`

    happens after re-planning by the cartographer, and collapsing them would
    assert a timing that is false. The binding delivered is lexical: both
    sentences name `needs-replan`, so a grep for the token returns both
    instructions and they cannot drift apart.
  - **"and clear `ready`" is stated here even though `## GitHub conventions`
    twelve lines below implies it**, and that is not a "state it once"
    violation: `relabel` is genuinely ambiguous between *replace the queue
    label* and *add one*, the park paragraph carries the instruction and the
    conventions paragraph carries the consequence, and neither repeats the
    other's half.

- Decisions:
  - **`Unevaluated` deliberately does not satisfy `error`, and that is the
    answer to STYLE T4's "why not a second `[]*xsderr.Error`".** The two
    records differ in KIND, not in fields, and the `error` method is precisely
    what would let them mix — `errors.Is` could match one, `errors.Join` fold
    one in, and `w.res.violations = append(…, u)` would compile.
    `*xsderr.Error`'s own doc fixes that interface as "every schema- or
    instance-validity violation in the module". Stated in the commit message
    per T4, and pinned by `TestUnevaluatedIsNotAnError`.
  - **One type, two rule IDs, discriminated by `Rule()`** — `cvc-assertion`
    (§3.13.4.1, reached from `cvc-complex-type` clause 6 `c-as` and nowhere
    else) and `cvc-assertions-valid` (§4.3.13.3, reached from
    `cvc-datatype-valid` clause 3 `dv_vfacets`), both already catalog IDs at
    `xsderr/catalog.go:40-41`. The GROUNDING is what forbids conflating them:
    `cvc-datatype-valid` never calls `cvc-assertion`; the simple-type side has
    its own rule, and datatypes §4.3.13.2 `xr-assertions` hands the *component*
    construction back to Structures §3.13.2 while defining only how the facet's
    `{value}` sequence is assembled.
  - **No `Level` field and no variety enum.** `Loc` plus `Msg` suffices; a
    `Level` would be a closed set needing a sealed sum (T2) with no consumer
    (T5), and the sites are collected statically, so "which level fired" is a
    property of the type, not an outcome. Several records at one `Loc` — a
    list's own facet and its `{item type definition}`'s — are expected and are
    not de-duplicated.
  - **The recursion is `cvc-datatype-valid`'s own order, per PRINCIPLES 12:**
    constituents (clause 2) then the type's own effective facet (clause 3) —
    list → `{item type definition}` then own; union → each
    `{member type definition}` in document order then own; atomic → own alone.
    `{assertions}` is read as GIVEN and the base chain is never walked:
    `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.7 / `derivation-ok-restriction` clause 5 /
    `cos-assertions-restriction` make the base's a prefix of the derived one,
    so unioning the chain would report every inherited assertion once per
    derivation step.
  - **FOUR recording calls, not the pre-flight's two, and the arbiter ruled it
    follows the inventory rather than expanding it.** `validate/doc.go:93-98`
    has enumerated four String Valid charges since before this branch:
    `cvcattribute.go:92` (clause 3), `cvcattribute.go:262` (clause 4 over a
    ·defaulted attribute·, recorded at the ELEMENT's `Loc` there being no
    attribute item), `cvccomplexcontent.go:477` (`stringValid`, serving
    cvc-type clause 3.1.3 and cvc-complex-type clause 1.2), plus
    `assess.go:686` (`wildcardAttributeAssertions`). The converse check the
    pre-flight demanded found two paths reaching a simple type's facets without
    passing a named charge site — a wildcard-matched attribute, and an element
    with an EMPTY ·initial value· whose lexical `idElement`/`elementKeyMember`
    still decide — so recording sits at the TOP of `stringValid`, before its
    `Len() == 0` decline, and is skipped for a ·nilled· element (§3.3.5.4,
    the gate `simpleTypeValue` already applies).
  - **No gate in the `instance` lane, and ZERO new declines** —
    `conformance/instance.go`'s `execInstanceCase` ends
    `if !decidedNotValid(result.Violations()) { return Fail() }` and banks only
    a "not valid" verdict. An `Unevaluated` adds no violation, so it can
    neither rescue a document another conjunct already rejected (validity is a
    conjunction) nor manufacture a "valid" bank the lane never emits. **A gate
    placed BEFORE that line flips correctly-banked not-valid cases into
    declines and REGRESSES the ratchet; after it, it is dead.**
  - **`{inherited attributes}` (§3.3.5.6) is out of scope and stays
    unbuilt.** The oracle grepped every occurrence in `xmlschema11-1.md`: the
    property is used exactly once, by Type Alternative §3.12.4 clause 1.1.3.
    `cvc-assertion` clause 1.3 builds its XDM instance from E's attributes,
    children and descendants and names it nowhere. CTA's existing
    `GAP(xpath):` markers (`xpath/cta.go:68`, `validate/cta.go:87`) are the
    wording precedent, not evidence of missing plumbing.
  - **No `seen` set in the recursion** (STYLE D4): `checkUnionMembershipAcyclic`
    (`xsd/resolve.go:1017`) rejects union circularity at construction and

    `value/list.go` recurse unguarded today. A guard here would be a leaked
    construction phase.

- Decisions:
  - **STOP at stage 1 rather than repoint `assembleCase`, and the reason the
    direction LOOKS safe is the reason it is not.** Making the decline set
    `len(d.Unmapped) > 0` yields a strict subset of today's declines, short by
    670 discoveries — it cannot regress a lane, it can only turn declines into
    decisions. That is precisely the hazard: 584 of those are documents where
    the anonymous complex type gets no Phase D verdict at all (the #414 folds
    and every #438 verdict quantifying over `Schema.types` — `cos-nonambig`,
    `cos-element-consistent`, `ct-props-correct` clause 4, `cos-ct-extends`
    clause 1.2), so a "valid" reached there is the vacuous accept
    `schemaShapeDecidable` exists to refuse, **and it would BANK.** CLAUDE.md's
    one rule settles it without a judgement call.
  - **A narrow census plus a filed producer fix, over a complete census plus a
    widened gate** — because widening the gate to decline the two latent false
    accepts **measurably costs a ratchet win**:
    `TypeAlternativeTests/s3_12si01/schema/s3_12si01s` goes Pass → decline. The
    correct fix charges the §5.1 first-bullet fault on the producer side, which
    is a widening with its own grounding and its own measurement, not a census
    change. `parser/census.go`'s "Scope" section names both as deliberately
    not censused, with the reason.
  - **The census is NAME-based, not positional.** A child dropped because the
    position its name fills was already filled is never reported (a second
    `<all>` in a `<group>`, a second `<anyAttribute>` in an `<attributeGroup>`);
    a positional census would make the answer depend on how many siblings a
    name has, which no reader can act on without re-walking the document.
  - **A name is reported only where no pass rejects it either.** The walk stops
    at a repeated content alternative and a repeated derivation alternant; a
    model group reports nothing of its own because `groupParticles`' default arm
    rejects. The 55 rejection-caused residuals stay residual for this reason —
    they are verdicts, not silences.
  - **One `container` walk parameterised by a per-site predicate**, five
    containers through it, reporting and descent sharing one loop so the census
    stays in document order at any depth (STYLE D2) and a region is added by
    naming a vocabulary rather than by writing another walk (STYLE T4).
  - **`mappedFacetElement` factored out of `rejectOutOfModelFacetChildren`**
    (#972) and now that function's own predicate too, keeping MAPPING facet
    membership apart from `s4sFacetElement`'s ORDERING membership — the latter

    `xs:namedAttributeGroup` has no `xs:assertions` position and `assertionsOf`
    is reached from a complex type alone, so an `<assert>` child of a top-level

## 2026-08-27 — #1004 — **the sixth consecutive libuser consultation to hit the same gap gets it closed by a field-by-field read instead of an inference**: `validate.Validator` has exactly 3 fields, all set once in `New` and never rewritten, and `Assess`'s walk state is allocated fresh per call; the one shipped `value.Backend` (`builtin/strict.backend`) is a stateless empty struct; `*xsd.Schema`'s mutating methods run exclusively inside `finalize()`; the one stateful exception, `Schema.ContentMatcher`'s `*Matcher` (already documented "not safe for concurrent use"), is traced to its single call site and confirmed never shared across calls; one sentence added to each of `xsd/doc.go` and `validate/doc.go`, backed by a committed `-race` test (`validate/concurrency_test.go`, 50 goroutines sharing one `Schema`+`Validator`); **arbiter ACCEPT in one round, zero findings, independently re-derived every finding rather than trusting mason's account**, gate green all four parts, `Ratchet: unchanged`, `surface: unchanged`

  by the arbiter, clean, nothing to bank. `go tool surface -base origin/main`
  → unchanged, matching the issue's own `Surface: none`: no exported
  identifier added, removed, or renamed.
- Cost — `1 mason, 1 arbiter`. No oracle: the issue body says `Spec: n/a`, so
  grounding read STYLE D5 ("no concurrency in library code") directly rather
  than delegating to the oracle, matching #963's precedent. No warden:
  surface unchanged, nothing exported. No repair round, no reject, one
  session, one worktree, no park. **The mason round bought the actual proof
  the issue demanded** — a field-by-field read of `Validator`'s 3 fields,
  every shipped `value.Backend`, and every `*Schema` method's write site,
  rather than re-running the external `-race` measurement and calling that

  analysis** — its own read of `validate.go`, `assess.go`, `strict.go`,
  `valuespace.go`, `backend.go`, `schema.go`, and `contentmatcher.go`, plus
  its own `-race` run of the committed test — rather than accepting mason's
  account, per the issue's own warning that "naming a guarantee this library
  does not hold is the failure mode that matters."
- Decisions made and why:
  - **Answered "safe", not "undecided"** — the issue's Acceptance left both
    on the table, but the field-by-field read found no unsynchronized
    per-call mutable state anywhere on the `Assess` path, so the honest
    answer is the positive one.
  - **Qualified the `Validator` sentence on the caller's own
    `value.Backend`.** Every shipped backend is stateless, but a
    caller-supplied `value.Backend` with its own unsynchronized state would

    untouched and cited it as the exemplar**, rather than restating its
    caveat on `Schema` — `ContentMatcher` builds one per element per

    reaches a caller sharing `*Schema` across goroutines through the
    published `validate` API.

    measurement.** The 2026-08-26 `/backlog` consultation had already run

## 2026-08-27 — #852 — **`tools/gapaudit`'s matcher reads the `(#N)` a marker prints before it reaches for a heuristic, and a phrase run no longer counts the same in both directions**: four markers citing OPEN trackers verbatim (`#414`, `#774` ×3) stopped reporting untracked, and the stale-tracker report went 5→8 rows once a coincidental phrase collision could no longer silently retire a genuinely markerless tracker (`#592`, `#731`, `#921` recovered); the documented `kind/gap` input filter STAYS and reports an out-of-band citation instead of widening the feed 142→618; **arbiter REJECT on round 1 (two blocking), ACCEPT on round 2 — one repair round consumed of the two allowed**, `Ratchet: unchanged`, `surface: unchanged`

- Attempted/shipped on `wip/issue-852`, base `origin/main` at **`1f5edbf`**, four
  commits: **`4236221`** (mason, all four defects, 2 files, +529/−56),
  **`1c1ad7d`** (merge absorbing #963's `tools/landcheck` landing),
  **`a0fd3f1`** (the round-1 repair — `STYLE D3` citation plus verbatim
  fixtures, 2 files, +10/−7), **`1d2ee5a`** (merge absorbing #1032's
  identity-constraint doc landing). Branch total against `1f5edbf`: **2 files,
  +532/−56** — `tools/gapaudit/main.go`, `tools/gapaudit/main_test.go`. No new
  files, nothing outside `tools/gapaudit/`.
- **Ratchet: unchanged — verified twice, once per arbiter round**, each a full
  read-only `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run with `conformance/testdata/expectations/`
  byte-identical after. Structurally guaranteed besides: `tools/gapaudit` is a
  `go tool` binary (`package main`) with **zero importers module-wide**, so no
  edit here is reachable from the validation path. **`go tool surface -base
  origin/main` → unchanged**; nothing exported moved.
- Cost — **2 mason (1 repair), 2 arbiter (1 reject).** No oracle (process-only
  issue, `Spec: n/a`; the oracle declines these, the same disposition #963's
  own session recorded, so the grounding was self-authored), no warden
  (`surface: unchanged`), no cartographer, no steward. One session, one branch,
  no park. **The reject round bought two things mason could not have found by
  re-reading its own work**: a `STYLE D4` citation that should have read `D3`,
  and — the one that mattered — two of four table-test fixtures whose doc
  comment claimed *verbatim* marker text that had in fact been silently
  abbreviated against the real source at `validate/cvcid.go:196` and `:290` (an
  elided inner quotation, a dropped trailing sentence). **Round 2 re-verified
  all four fixtures byte-for-byte, not just the two repaired**, and confirmed
  they match.
- **The survey declined a LIVE branch rather than racing it.** `wip/issue-963`
  read LIVE under a concurrent session — a fresh GROUNDING comment posted
  almost the same minute — so this session claimed #852 instead. That session's
  landing is the `1c1ad7d` merge above; the tools/-vs-tools/ adjacency never
  became a file overlap.
- Decisions made and why:
  - **Citation-first, and the ordering is a type rather than a convention.**
    `matches` returns a `matchKind` closed sum (`none < phrase < file < cited`)
    instead of a bare bool — a `STYLE T1` improvement that makes the
    "which signal decided this?" state unrepresentable-if-illegal, and is what
    lets the report and the retirement rule ask different questions of the same
    call.
  - **Kept the `kind/gap`-only input pipeline; report the out-of-band citation
    instead of widening it.** A marker may legitimately cite a tracker under
    another label (`#717`, `kind/feature`), which the documented filter
    structurally excludes — but widening to all labels 4×s the feed (142→618)
    and destroys group 2's own definition, since a "stale `kind/gap` tracker" is
    only meaningful against a `kind/gap` census. `printReportTo` now names the
    out-of-band citation in a line rather than the tool silently mis-reporting.
  - **Split `dead end: cites CLOSED #N` from `resemblance: phrase-matches
    CLOSED #N`.** One line for both overstated confidence a reader could act on
    wrongly — a genuine citation and a coincidental phrase collision are not the
    same evidence and must not print the same sentence.
  - **Group-2 retirement now requires a citation or a file-path match, never a
    phrase match alone.** This is the fourth defect's fix and it runs in the
    opposite direction from the other three.
  - **The repair re-derived the true fixture text mechanically, not by eye.** A
    throwaway `go/ast` diagnostic compared the fixture literals against a live
    `extractMarkers` run and was deleted before commit; the `STYLE` letter was
    verified by reading `docs/STYLE.md` directly rather than trusting the
    relayed claim.
- Surprises:
  - **The fourth defect points the other way, and only appears once the first
    three are fixed.** Defects 1–3 are all "the tool under-credits a marker";
    defect 4 is the tool **over-crediting** one — a phrase collision suppressing
    a genuinely stale, markerless tracker from group 2. Reproduced live: 5→8
    rows, recovering `#592`, `#731`, `#921`. A matcher that is too eager in one
    report is too eager in the other, and the bool return hid that they were the
    same call.
  - **Scope discipline held under temptation.** The repair found a second
    pre-existing `D4`-should-be-`D3` miscitation at
    `conformance/schema_closure.go:98`, flagged it, and correctly left it
    untouched.
- Friction — **none charged against this session's process.** Two `origin/main`
  moves mid-flight (#963, then #1032), both clean, both re-gated in full on the
  merged tree per `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s "a conflict-free auto-merge is not
  evidence of a compatible one" — the rule working, not friction. One finding
  about a document, which is not this session's to fix: **`docs/ROUTINES.md`'s
  paginate recipe (`for p in $(seq 1 9)`) is under-provisioned** — the repo is
