- Cost — **1 oracle, 1 warden, 2 mason (1 repair), 2 arbiter (1 reject).** No
  cartographer, no steward. **The warden round was the expensive one and it paid
  before a line was written**: it turned the issue's `TBD` surface into a
  measured "none", and it killed a `GAP(xsd)` carve-out for the
  `{attribute wildcard}` half that would have been extra code AND unsound. **The
  reject bought a marker, not a fix** — see Friction.
- Decisions made and why:
  - **The precondition enters through clause 2, not clause 3, and the issue body
    said clause 3.** The GROUNDING read §3.4.2.4 at
    `docs/specs/md/xmlschema11-1.md:1760` — the synthesized `<attributeGroup>`
    child "appearing after any other `<attributeGroup>` [children]" — sitting
    ahead of the union at `:1762`, so the fold is on the same footing as a
    written `<attributeGroup ref>` and reaches `{attribute uses}` through clause
    2. `docs/PLAN.md:503` and the issue body both said clause 3, which is the
    base type's inherited uses and a different mechanism entirely. Nothing
    downstream depended on the wrong attribution, but it is what the fold's
    ordering requirement hangs off: clause 2 is where "after any other
    `<attributeGroup>` children" has meaning.
  - **The synthesized ref goes through the SAME splice a written one does, so
    §3.4.2.5 costs nothing.** `spliceAttributeGroup(qn, loc, construct, ...)` is
    `collectReferencedGroup`'s resolve-and-descend tail, extracted; the fold
    calls it with `"<schema defaultAttributes>"` as the construct and reproduces
    the `src-resolve` diagnostic byte-for-byte. A second path that resolved and
    walked the group itself would have needed its own wildcard threading — the
    half that silently regresses — and warden ruled the carve-out out before
    mason wrote it: a `GAP` there is not merely incomplete, it is a **false
    accept** via `cos-aw-intersect`, because a wildcard the default group
    narrows would go unnarrowed.
  - **Nothing is stored on a component.** Neither `defaultAttributes` nor
    `defaultAttributesApply` is a Schema-component property — §3.17.1's tableau
    has no `{default attribute group}` and §3.4.1 none for the opt-out — so both
    are read at the mapping that consumes them and travel no further, which is
    the ruling `wildcardElement` already gives `appliesToEmpty`. `xsd.Schema` and
    `xsd.ComplexType` gain no field and the surface does not move.
  - **`visited` is the caller's, shared with the container walk.** A
    `<complexType>` that ALSO writes an explicit `<attributeGroup ref>` to the
    default group splices it once. Clause 2 unions SETS, so the duplicate is not
    in the spec's answer; splicing twice would trip `ct-props-correct`
    (`:2027`) clause 4 on a schema the spec accepts.
  - **The QName resolves at `p.schemaElem`, never at the `<complexType>`** — it
    is written at `<schema>`, so that is the element whose prefixes bind it,
    whose `<import>`s license it, and whose §F.1 task (b) chameleon rewrite
    reaches it. Under `<override>` this also picks the OVERRIDDEN document's
    root for a `<complexType>` substituted in from the overriding one, the
    reading `defaultOpenContentElem` already takes.
  - **There is no eager check that `defaultAttributes` resolves.** A document
    that declares one and defines no `<complexType>` never invokes ·resolve· on
    it, so an unresolvable QName there is charged nothing — the reference exists
    only where the precondition synthesizes it, and a test pins that.
  - **The gate was DELETED, not narrowed.** `schemaShapeDecidable`'s blanket
    decline existed to close a false ACCEPT that no longer exists once the fold
    is real, so no narrower replacement is owed; `census_test.go`'s residual-list
    entry goes with it, leaving `anonymousComplexTypeDecidable` alone in that
    paragraph. The arbiter confirmed the removal stranded no dead code (`hasAttr`
    keeps many callers).
  - **The extension-base collision is routed around in a fixture and tracked,
    not fixed.** Warden ruled `xsd/attributeusefold.go` out of #1046's scope,
    mason took the ruling, and #1082 owns the fix.
- Surprises:
  - **The reject found a defect that predates the diff, and the arbiter proved it
    rather than accepting mason's proof.** A `<complexContent>`/`<simpleContent>`
    EXTENSION whose base folds the same default group is falsely rejected
    `ct-props-correct` clause 4: the group's uses reach the derived type once
    from clause 2's fold and once from clause 3.1's unconditional inheritance of
    the base's already-folded uses. Clause 3.1 unions sets;
    `inheritAttributeUses` concatenates. The arbiter reproduced it on
    `origin/main` with a throwaway probe — a base and its extension each writing
    one plain `<attributeGroup ref>`, **no `defaultAttributes` anywhere** — and
    got the identical diagnostic, so the mechanism is `xsd/attributeusefold.go`'s
    and this fold only makes it easy to reach, since the base need merely not opt
    out and nobody has to write a duplicate ref.
  - **The repair was 100% comments, and that was VERIFIED rather than asserted.**
    `cd21579..9aad830` is +23/−5 with every changed line beginning `//`; the

  - **Warden's suggested wildcard fixture tested nothing, and mason said so

- Decisions made and why:
  - **The router is the addition, and this issue's own thread is the precedent
    that forces it.** The issue proposed folding the mandate into the grounding
    round, which already reads the body and already goes to a specialist. But
    grounding is not always oracle-taking — #1052's own `GROUNDING:` says "no
    oracle grounding needed, in-repo prose only" — so an **oracle-only mandate
    leaves unruled exactly the class of issue that produced #1029 and #719**.
    Hence the two-way route.
  - **The arbiter is domain-correct for the non-spec half**: an `## Acceptance`
    bullet states the bar the arbiter's own later verdict applies, and #1030
    ("an unchanged ratchet is the proof") and #719 (a bullet that would have
    REGRESSED the ratchet) are its subject matter exactly. Every rejected
    alternative fails on a rule already in the tree — **orchestrator** (develop.md
    delegates all specialist work, and it is the agent that then wants to
    proceed), **mason** (never judges its own work), **cartographer** (wrote the
    body; same defect the issue exists to fix), **warden** (surface/type-safety
    domain), **oracle always** (grading a domain it does not own).
  - **The ruling goes in the EXISTING `GROUNDING:` comment, not a new one** —
    the arbiter called this the strongest move in the diff. Step 3 already calls
    that comment "the only durable copy" and `mason.md:25` already obliges mason
    to read it, so the ruling lands where the implementer is already required to
    look and **no new read obligation was invented**.
  - **Posted with the grounding, explicitly NOT as a `VERDICT:` block**, so an
    "unsatisfiable" can never be miscounted as a rejection in the one-repair-round
    accounting; and "before step 4 starts" gates implementation on cartographer's
    correction, which is why `mason.md` needs no new STOP clause to pair with its
    existing one for missing rule IDs.
  - **`arbiter.md` absorbed, not filed** — no rule ID, no exported surface, no
    lane movement, so WORKFLOW's scope rule says absorb and name it in the commit
    body, which it does. It is also NECESSARY rather than merely permitted:
    arbiter.md's frame is post-diff throughout (establish the base, judge the
    diff, run the gate), so without the paragraph develop.md would route a
    pre-diff duty to a file that contradicts it. The constitutional
    ratchet-integrity section is untouched.
  - **`cartographer.md` deliberately NOT touched**, though the issue's Spec
    section names it — a Spec section names where to look, not what must change.
    Neither candidate duty belongs there: the ruling itself cannot be
    cartographer's without recreating the defect (it wrote the bullet), and the
    re-statement of an unsatisfiable bullet is already carried, because

    directs** — nothing added about citation-checking (#635) or stale enumerated
    site lists (#912). "Judge the bullet on what it would PROVE if met... a bar
    that holds however the change turns out is unsatisfiable **however correctly

- Decisions made and why:
  - **`key-cta-ta-select`, not `key-cta-select`, and not an invented `cvc-cta*`.**
    Line 3221 of `xmlschema11-1.md` is the anchor and names exactly the check the
    record reports — *"A Type Alternative A **successfully selects** a Type
    Definition T for an element information item E if and only if A.{test}
    evaluates to `true` and A.{type definition} = T"*. The reached-and-not-performed
    check is the **per-alternative** one, so it is `Rule()`; the table-level
    determination (`key-cta-select`, §3.3.4.1) was not reached and skipped but
    made impossible, so it is named in `Msg()`. Three independent greps agree no
    `cvc-cta*` anchor exists and every `key-cta*` hit is a `[Definition:]` or a
    glossary restatement, none `**Validation Rule:**`-labeled.
  - **The catalog entry went through the GENERATOR, never the table** (PRINCIPLES
    26/27). `tools/rulecat`'s patterns (`cvc-`/`cos-`/`src-`/`sic-`,
    `err:XXXX0000`, `*-props-correct`) match none of it, so one entry was
    appended to `irregularRules` and `xsderr/catalog.go` regenerated by `go
    generate ./xsderr/...`, generator and output in the same commit. The doc
    paragraph was widened from "genuine Schema Component Constraint:-labeled rule
    IDs" to "spec anchors the module cites as an `xsderr.Rule`", with the single
    admitting condition stated: **the spec names a check and names no rule for
    it**. Whole-word matching still gates it, so the string had to be genuinely
    in the spec text.
  - **A dynamic error in an evaluable `{test}` records nothing, and no guard was
    added to enforce that.** `xpath.CompileCTATest(...) (CTATest, bool)` is the
    only decline direction and `(CTATest).Evaluate(...) bool` has no error
    channel, so recording on `!evaluable` alone *is* the implementation of clause
    2. `Evaluate` was not touched. The arbiter ruled this load-bearing
    correctness rather than a missing feature: routing a dynamic error into
    `Unevaluated` would be an affirmative violation of clause 2's *"treated as if
    it had evaluated (without error) to `false`"*.
  - **One record per element, per alternative index**, not per table: the
    `for range` became `for i, alt := range alts` so the message can say
    *"alternative 2 of 3 ... whose {test} is `count(@kind) > 0`"*. Rejected the
    vaguer per-table form because `key-cta-select`'s scan is ordered and an
    index is actionable where "this element's table" is not — and one record
    lands either way, so the vaguer form bought nothing.
  - **The two `ResolvedType` declines in the same function stay silent, and this
    is not a deferral.** In both arms the `·successfully selects·` check **was
    performed** — the test compiled, evaluated true, the alternative selected —
    and what failed is resolving a component reference, `src-resolve` clause 1.1
    territory that `SchemaBuilder.Finalize` rejects before a finalized schema can
    reach `validate`. The arbiter checked reachability rather than taking the
    argument, enumerating the arms a `{type definition}` can hold post-`Finalize`,
    and confirmed a record there would assert a falsehood, not merely a vague
    truth. Same precedent `validate/cvcassertion.go:139` already sets for its own
    three arms.
  - **Five prose sites absorbed as T6, not filed** — each one my own diff would
    have falsified: `xsderr/error.go`'s `Rule` doc ("a spec **validation** rule
    ID"), `xsderr/doc.go`'s Contract restatement of it, the generated
    `catalog.go` header ("all normative validation rule IDs"),
    `validate/validate.go`'s `Unevaluated.Rule()` doc ("the ID it would have been
    charged under had it been performed and failed" — exactly wrong for CTA,
    where a failed `key-cta-ta-select` charges nothing), and `validate/doc.go`'s
    conditional-type-assignment bullet.

    append fails `TestUnevaluableTestIsRecordedAsUnevaluated` on the record count;

- **Ratchet: unchanged. Zero regressions, nothing banked, no expectations file
  written.** The arbiter's figures, copied not recomputed: it ran
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` itself rather than inheriting mason's, and the committed lane
  table is byte-identical to the one #1076 left — `schema` 13353/2045,

- Cost — **1 oracle, 1 warden, 1 mason, 1 arbiter.** Zero repair rounds, zero
  rejects, no cartographer, no steward. The warden ran as a **pre-flight** rather
  than a post-diff review, which is what bought the session its cheapest fact and
  also its one wrong one (Friction).
- Decisions made and why:
  - **The dedup is keyed on `attributeUsesIdentical`, not on `DeclarationName`,
    and the distinction is the whole issue.** `dcl.ctd.attuses` builds
    `{attribute uses}` as a union of sets, so a member reached twice — once by the
    type's own clause 1/2 fold, once by clause 3.1 from a base that folded the same
    group — is ONE member. `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.2 supplies the sameness test
    the spec itself uses between two attribute uses, so nothing new is encoded. A
    value-DISTINCT re-declaration under a name the base carries is still two
    members and still charged `ct-props-correct` clause 4.
  - **The guard is on the EXTENSION arm alone.** Clause 3.2.1 (restriction) is a
    separate, name-based exclusion that the oracle confirmed untouched by any of
    this; the two arms and their two tests stay apart rather than collapsing into
    one parameterised helper.
  - **`ownAttributeUses` was rebuilt FIRST, in its own commit, because the dedup
    is what breaks it.** Clause 3.1's fold is not invertible — own `[y]`, `[y,x]`
    and `[y,x,z]` over base `[x,z]` all fold to `[y,x,z]` — and the old positional
    `len(folded(c)) - len(folded(b))` prefix recovers one of that family by
    comparing names, answering the EMPTY set for own `[x]` over base `[x]`: exactly
    the shape the dedup makes reachable. It is now a `*Schema` method answering
    `c`'s whole folded set, verified by identity, which is the same statement as
    `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.2's subset test.
  - **No new exported surface, and the warden's pre-flight is why.** The identity
    predicate already existed in-tree as `(*Schema).attributeUsesIdentical`
    (`xsd/complexextension.go`); nothing was exported and T5 never came into play.
- Surprises:
  - **The arbiter withdrew part of its own pre-flight input rather than banking
    it.** The warden had reported `ownAttributeUses`'s old tail-verification
    logic independently broken, with a counter-example. Re-derived against
    `origin/main`: the positional recovery was **exact** there, because the
    counter-example shapes were themselves already `ct-props-correct` clause-4
    rejects pre-fix and so unreachable. The warden had reasoned against the
    post-fix fold. **The redesign was still necessary** — the new dedup is what
    invalidates the old positional arithmetic — but the reason it shipped is not
    the reason it was proposed, and the commit body carries the corrected one.
  - **A false-reject fix with zero lane movement.** The bug is reproducible on
    `origin/main` with two plain `<attributeGroup ref>`s and no `defaultAttributes`
    involved, and the suite scores none of it. What holds the fix in place is the
    arbiter's mutation check: removing the dedup guard fails real tests, and
    weakening its key from identity to name fails different real tests, so both the
    guard and its keying are pinned.
  - **The fix opens no false-accept hole, probed rather than asserted.** The
    arbiter took an anonymous-type-slot edge case through the new fold; it is still
    correctly rejected, by `cos-ct-extends` clause 1.6 rather than by clause 4.
  - **#1046's `GAP(xsd)` marker at `foldDefaultAttributes` is removed, not
    repointed.** It was filed as debt #1046 made REACHABLE and did not create; this
    landing is the thing it was waiting for.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **The label predicate is a new line of code, not an assumption about the
    feed.** Widening the input without gating group 2 is not a neutral change
    to it: every open issue in the repository becomes a stale-tracker
    candidate, 8 rows to about 116, and the group stops meaning what its header
    says. `reconcile`'s loop guard is `!iss.open() || !iss.hasLabel(gapLabel)`,
    and `gapLabel`'s doc says outright that it selects **group 2 and nothing
    else**: group 1 weighs a marker against every issue fed, whatever it is
    labeled. That asymmetry is the whole issue.
  - **`Labeled`/`anyLabeled` is absorbed, and mason flagged it unprompted.**
    The widening opens a silent-failure mode that did not exist before: an old
    `kind/gap`-shaped input reshaped without `labels`, fed to the new tool,
    selects nothing into group 2, and an empty group 2 then reads as "no
    tracker is stale" when it means "no tracker was seen". The report now says
    which, and names the `jq` projection to fix it. Ruled in scope and
    STYLE-clean; a tool that changes what its input must carry owes a message
    for the input that does not.
  - **`unresolvedCitations` changed MEANING without changing behavior, so its
    prose changed and its code did not.** Under the narrow feed an absent
    citation was an expected consequence of the filter — the printed line said
    so, and said "not a leak". On a whole-repository feed the same absence
    means the number names no issue at all: a mistyped citation, or a PR number
    the reshape drops. The line now reads *"cites #N, which names no issue in
    the fed list — the citation itself is the defect"*. One fact, one encoding
    (STYLE D3): the finding was always "this number resolves to nothing", and
    only what that implies moved.
  - **The recipe is a loop, not a larger literal.** `for p in $(seq 1 9)` was
    two pages short of the repository on the day it was read. Mason's judgment
    call, and the justification is that a fixed literal **cannot** honor the
    caveat the recipe already carries — stop while the last page is non-empty —
    and would go stale again within about a fortnight at the observed filing
    rate. `while :` … `break` on the first short page, `|| exit 1` on a failed
    fetch grounded in ROUTINES.md's own "no human is watching, abort and log"
    convention, and the pages moved into their own emptied-first directory
    because a bare `p[0-9]*.json` glob swallows unrelated files and reads a
    leftover page from a longer earlier run back in as current.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **Rewriting, not visiting, and that is the design call.** A `ComplexType`
    is a value, so a folded component is observable only if every slot from a
    root down to it is re-seated with the copy that holds it —
    `componentwalk.go`'s shared read-only descent cannot serve, and hanging a
    `complexType func(...)` field on `componentWalk` would have made a descent
    five phases depend on return rewritten components to phases that only read
    them. The same argument `baseAttributeUses` already makes one level up for
    an owned inline `{base type definition}` (#505).
  - **Two passes, not one.** The owned walk runs *after* `storeFolded…`
    because the content-model graph is not the `{base type definition}` graph
    Phase B proved acyclic — a type declared inside `T` may extend `T` — so
    folding owned types inside the position walk could re-enter a position
    still mid-fold. Every position is memoised before the descent starts, so an
    owned type deriving by name takes a memo hit. `noTypePosition = -1`
    bypasses the `j == i` self-edge guard for owned types, which is right
    rather than merely harmless: that guard exists to cut ·xs:anyType·'s self
    edge, ·xs:anyType· is named, and no anonymous type is it.
  - **`{attribute declarations}` and `{attribute group definitions}` are NOT
    roots, and after the reject that exclusion carries a marker instead of a
    silence.** Widening to them needs a third root the descent cannot simply
    add: `complexType` would have to walk `c.attributeUses`, the very slice
    `inheritAttributeUses` rewrites, and clause 3.1 copies a base's
    `AttributeUse` **values** into every derived type, so one
    `LocalAttributeDeclaration` is reachable from every link of a derivation
    chain — the fold-once-per-referring-site hazard the ownership restriction
    exists to avoid. Both mason and the arbiter checked that independently.
  - **The new marker is left explicitly UNOWNED, deliberately.** STYLE P3
    permits an ownerless marker and forbids one citing a closed issue, and
    #414 closes with this landing, so `(#414)` was a dead end. It says
    *"Nothing owns the retirement"* in so many words, names
    `checkTypeDefinitionOrRef`/`attributeTypeSlot` as the cause, enumerates all
    three reaching slots, records that the parser cannot produce the shape, and
    gives the P3a direction per reader.
  - **`validate/assess.go`'s `attributePropertiesFolded` was NOT retired, and
    the arbiter ruled that the right scope line.** Its xsd-side premise is
    closed by this landing and it is now a pure over-decline, but deleting it
    is an instance-lane behaviour widening with its own ratchet attribution,
    woven through `idTable.declined`, `icCheck.fieldAttributes`,
    `walk.attributes` and four fixtures. The three markers that described
    *this* package's gap became `GAP(validate)` — behaviour untouched.
  - **The flat ratchet is accounted for at two named gates, not shrugged at.**
    `conformance/schema.go`'s `anonymousComplexTypeDecidable` still declines
    every non-implicit inline `<complexType>` — the 584 documents #1030
    measured — so those never reach an executor; and

- Decisions made and why:
  - **`-schema`'s notation was unified with `gen`'s rather than invented.**
    `goxsd8 validate -schema <schema.xsd> [-schema <s2>]... <instance>...` is the
    bracket-repetition form the page already uses for `gen`'s `-schema`/`-out`
    pairs, so the two repeated flags now read the same way; the trailing `...`
    on a bare `<schema.xsd>` had been the thing that made the boundary
    ambiguous, and a following sentence states outright that every positional
    argument after the schemas is an instance.
  - **The exit code is stated as aggregating, and the SHORT-CIRCUIT question is
    left explicitly to #720.** "1 if any one of them is invalid" is what a batch
    caller needs and what the contract can honestly promise; whether the run
    stops at the first invalid instance is a behaviour decision that was not
    this issue's to make, and the page does not imply an answer to it.
  - **`parse`'s two streams were QUOTED, `validate`'s was DECIDED.** The
    stdout-summary/stderr-errors split for `parse` is taken verbatim from #472's
    already-decided Acceptance rather than re-derived. `validate`'s violation
    lines going to **stdout** is settled here for the first time, and the
    arbiter judged it correct on the principle that each subcommand's stream
    assignment tracks its *product*: `validate`'s product is the violation
    report, so it is stdout, while `parse`'s schema errors are its failure mode,
    so they are stderr.
  - **#1031 absorbed, and its values inferred.** `-format xml|json|ber` is read

    stated case-sensitive, following `doc.go`'s existing `# Argument vocabulary`
    convention, and the scope is stated invocation-wide — one `-format` governs
    every instance, there is no per-instance spelling.

reading.** The landing entry's Next item 2 asked for the tracker and named one
scope hazard (`alternativeTypesDecidable` gates an `<alternative>`'s inline type
through `complexTypeDecidable`, not through this predicate, so the two admit
different shapes and the widening is not one function's). Reading

behaviourally equivalent mutation, which is exactly what

derivation-aware predicates `complexTypeDecidable` already uses
(`simpleContentExtensionDecidable`, `simpleContentRestrictionDecidable`,
`contentDecidable(derivation)`) and to say what survives, if anything.

point marked: `alternativeTypesDecidable`'s own doc comment records that this
lane ALREADY decides six schema cases and one instance case whose anonymous type
receives no Phase D verdict, and rules that residual acceptable per reader — but
whether the same reasoning carries to a `<complexContent>` restriction, where an
unreached `derivation-ok-restriction` bites hardest, is marked a **hypothesis**
for grounding, with the honest alternative (scope behind #438/#584) named in the
same paragraph.

## 2026-08-29 — post-land pass for #1109

**ZERO unblocked, ONE filed (#1129), TWO threads ruled, and this entry is the
first to land by the route #1109 wrote — its own branch, its own PR,
squash-merged in the same pass.** The landing that made a post-land PR mandatory
is also the landing whose advisory said that PR has no stated preconditions;
both facts are disposed of here rather than recorded. `docs/PLAN.md` was not
touched: nothing in this pass moved a lane, a milestone or a queue count.

**Unblock sweep: a measured zero.** All **246** open non-PR issues fetched over
repository-scoped REST — 3 pages by explicit `page=`, since `--paginate` still
fails in this container against the numeric-ID redirect the proxy refuses — of
which **20** carry `blocked`. Every `## Depends on` section read. **No open
issue names #1109 as a dependency, and none names it anywhere in its body.** The
only two open bodies containing the string `1109` are **#1108**, where it is a
`ready` issue's mention of the #1060/#1062 preconditions, and **#594**, where it
is the suite filename `test111092.xml`. #1109 was unblocked work throughout and
blocked nothing, so the zero is a property of the issue, not of the sweep.

**Advisory 2 → #1129, filed, not dismissed.** The arbiter marked it
pre-existing — five precedent post-land PRs merged the same way, and the count
is higher than that: of the 24 `meta: post-land pass…` commits on `main` at
`48310e8`, **18** carry a squash-merge `(#<PR>)` suffix and 6 are direct
commits. Pre-existing settles blame, not tracking, and two things settled it the
other way:

- **It is a live contradiction between two normative texts, not a habit.**
  `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s Landing says its four preconditions are *"verified and
  stated by the orchestrating session — none is anyone else's to volunteer"*,
  while `.claude/commands/develop.md` step 7 now has the cartographer
  squash-merge its own PR. CLAUDE.md's ownership rule resolves a disagreement in
  the owner's favour, which would make `cartographer.md` duty 3 the bug — and it
  is not, since #1109 put it there deliberately against an oracle that found the
  rule stated three times over. A contradiction that cannot be resolved in
  favour of the owner has to be resolved by editing the owner, and something has
  to hold that until it is.
- **This landing changed the frequency.** Before it a post-land pass could reach
  `main` by direct commit; after it, every post-land pass lands by a PR of
  exactly the uncovered shape — occasional became once per landing.

#1129 (`ready`, `kind/process`, `area/meta`) carries more than the advisory
named. The advisory cited preconditions 2 and 4; **3 is unsatisfiable for this
shape too** — it asks for mason's account on the issue thread, and the pass runs
no mason and closes no issue. So 3 and 4 are unsatisfiable by construction, 2's
sentence keys on *"the verdict's base"* that a pass with no arbiter does not
have while its substance still applies, 1 already carves the shape out by name,
and the verifier clause names an agent that is not the one merging. Its
Acceptance forbids duplicating precondition 1's existing carve-out and forbids
weakening any of the four for the code-landing shape.

**#797 → ruled, scope survives intact, NOT closed**
(`#797` `issuecomment-5464962916`). Checked bullet by bullet against `48310e8`,
and all three of its Acceptance bullets are untouched: #1109's diff is
`.claude/agents/cartographer.md` and `.claude/commands/develop.md` only,
`docs/WORKFLOW.md` is deliberately absent from it, no landed line cites #797 or
#112, and nothing in it addresses stray-branch recovery. **The subjects are
different passes** — #1109 governs a delegated pass that always produces exactly
one docs commit and knows it in advance; #797 governs a `/develop` iteration
that meant to land code and could not (race lost, premise falsified), holding no
lease it may push to. What #797 gains is real but is not coverage: a landed
precedent for the shape, which its own 2026-08-15 comment recorded as the
missing piece, and one adjacent case removed from its space.

**#112 → precedent note, stays closed** (`#112` `issuecomment-5464963977`). Its
(b) required the PR for maintenance-trigger landings and landed no preconditions
for it. It now has two live descendants — #797 (does the PR exist at all) and
#1129 (given it exists, what is verified and by whom) — and both are pointed at
widening it rather than sitting beside it, which is what #797's body already
asked of whoever takes it.

- Landed from `meta/post-land-1109`, base `origin/main` at `48310e8`, verified
  current (`git log HEAD..origin/main` empty) before the PR was opened. One
  commit, this entry alone. No code, no gate parts owed: the four-part gate
  measures a tree this pass did not change.
- Cost — cartographer only. No mason, no arbiter, no oracle.
- Next — **none owed by this pass.** #1129 is filed and startable; #797 is ruled
  and stays `ready`; the unblock sweep found nothing. The two follow-ups #1109's
  entry handed forward are both discharged, neither by a hand-off.

## 2026-08-31 — #1097 — **both of `simpleTypeBody`'s rejections lose the fabricated `src-simple-type` charge and stand on §5.1's first bullet, which carries no rule ID — and the branch the issue was NOT about is the live one**: `src-simple-type`'s four clauses (§3.16.3, `xmlschema11-1.md:3658`) are one duplicate-facet condition and three attribute-vs-child XORs each opening *"If the X alternative is chosen"*, so none of them states how many of `<restriction>`/`<list>`/`<union>` are present and charging either branch was a fabricated verdict (STYLE E2); the content model at `:3608` — `(annotation?, (restriction | list | union))`, no `?` on the alternative group — puts BOTH shapes in §5.1's first bullet (`:4296`), the unnumbered class `checkS4SChildOrder` and `rejectLocalSimpleTypeAttrs` already stand on with a plain `fmt.Errorf`; **the NEITHER branch was ABSORBED because two issue bodies said to absorb it** — #1097's own Notes (*"if the answer is that it too may charge no rule, absorb it here: one function, one constant, one landing"*) and #742's *"the grounding is owed once, on #1097, and both messages settle on it"* — and the oracle answered the hypothesis rather than leaving it open; **the two branches differ in REACH, not in class**, and the reach splits the opposite way to the band's premise: MORE-THAN-ONE is dead from any schema document since #1076, while the NEITHER branch is reached by `constructSimpleType` directly and its wrong rule ID had been reaching real callers all along; `Ratchet: unchanged` run rather than inferred and **ENTAILED** — `conformance/schema.go:255` records that the lane does no `errors.As` over `*xsderr.Error` at all, so re-footing an error cannot move a verdict; **arbiter ACCEPT in one round, zero blocking findings, three non-blocking** — one fixed on the branch before landing, two tracking — `surface: unchanged`

- Shipped on `wip/issue-1097`, base `origin/main` at **`0abeab6`**, unmoved
  through grounding, implementation and verdict — no merge forward, no
  re-judgment on a moved base. Three commits: `f05f316` (empty grounding
  checkpoint), **`94a0640`** (mason, 7 files, **+166/−26**, from worktree
  isolation on `worktree-agent-aa1c248ddd75adcf5`) and **`6d7eacb`** (the
  orchestrator's post-verdict fix of finding 1, `parser/doc.go` alone, +3/−2).
  Net over the base: 8 files, **+169/−28**, of which the new internal test file
  is +99. `conformance/testdata/expectations/` is not in it. This entry rides
  the squash.
- **Ratchet: unchanged.** The arbiter's figures, copied not recomputed:
  `GOXSD_RATCHET=1 go test ./conformance -run TestConformance -count=1` →
  `ok … 379.245s`, exit 0, no `Regressed` and no `Vanished`, with
  `git status --porcelain -- conformance/testdata/expectations/` checked empty
  immediately after and the whole-tree status empty too — nothing to bank,
  nothing stranded. `GOXSD_RATCHET_REMOVALS` was not used and no removal count
  is claimed: discovery is untouched by this diff. Gate part 4
  `--- PASS: TestConformance (388.31s)`, its `-v` output carrying the standard
  informational lines only — 41759 cases across 6 lanes, 99 withheld as
  inapplicable, datatypes 1173 / schema 15398 / instance 26361 — and **no**
  improved-but-unbanked line for any lane. Parts 1–3 clean: 27 `ok` with zero
  FAIL, `0 issues.`, no reflow (checked, not `-fix`ed). `go tool surface -base
  origin/main` → `surface: unchanged` (T5), which the issue's `Surface: none`
  predicted and which `simpleTypeBody` being unexported makes structural.
  **Flat is entailed, not merely expected.** The arbiter's reason is stronger
  than mason's *"only the error's footing changed"*: `conformance/schema.go:255`
  states the schema lane needs no error-type discrimination at all — *"No
  error-type discrimination (`errors.As` over `*xsderr.Error`) is needed to make
  that trustworthy"* — because steps 1–3 rule out the non-verdict failure modes
  across the whole closure. A conformance verdict cannot read a rule ID here, so
  no assembled case's verdict CAN move when one changes.
- Cost — **1 oracle, 1 mason, 1 arbiter.** Zero repair rounds, zero rejects; no
  warden (`Surface: none`, so no pre-flight was owed and `surface: unchanged`
  confirmed it after), no cartographer, no steward. Plus one post-verdict
  orchestrator commit under WORKFLOW's third **After the verdict** class. What
  the single arbiter round bought is not a code correction — it moved no
  non-comment line — but three things the account could not supply itself: an
  independent mutation run against both new tests, a stronger precedent than
  mason argued (below), and the discovery that the account's one negative
  verification reported the opposite of the truth (Surprises).
- Decisions made and why:
  - **The NEITHER branch was absorbed, and absorbing it was following two issue
    bodies rather than widening scope.** #1097's Notes made it conditional on
    the grounding's answer; #742's narrowed body routed the same question here
    in as many words. The oracle settled it: the content model's alternative
    group carries no `?`, so zero alternatives fails it exactly as two do, and
    `src-simple-type`'s clauses 2–4 are each conditioned on an alternative
    *already chosen*. Same unnumbered class, so one function, one constant, one
    landing.
  - **The NEITHER branch's REJECTION stays; only its footing moved.** `s4sSlot`
    carries no `required`/`minOccurs` notion, so `checkS4SChildOrder` walks only
    the children that are present and an unfilled alternative position is
    invisible to it. That leaves this the one site enforcing "at least one
    alternative" against a real document, and deleting it would silently accept
    a zero-alternative `<simpleType>` — a ratchet regression dressed as a
    cleanup, which the grounding flagged as an edge case before mason started.
    Folding the enforcement into the s4s walk instead (giving `s4sSlot` a
    required notion, so this branch too becomes unreachable) is a design change
    and was ruled out of scope by the grounding, not overlooked.
  - **Plain `fmt.Errorf`, not a package-level sentinel.** Census
    (`census.go:292-295`) discards the value with a bare `return` and
    `constructSimpleType` propagates it verbatim, so an `errors.Is` target would
    have no reader — STYLE 4 state kept for nobody — and the sentinel form
    cannot carry the element position without a wrapper type. Mason offered to
    defer this call; the arbiter declined the deferral and ruled it correct as
    made, on a precedent one step stronger than mason's: not merely
    `checkS4SChildOrder` (`produce_s4sorder.go:337-346`) but
    `rejectLocalSimpleTypeAttrs` at `produce.go:1735` — same file, thirty lines
    up the page, same fault class, same `fmt.Errorf` + `elem.Loc()`-in-the-text
    shape, and its own doc comment already derives the identical footing and
    already names charging `src-simple-type` an E2 fabrication. `xsderr/doc.go:26-31`
    settles it normatively.
  - **No substitute rule ID.** §5.1's first bullet carries none, and swapping
    `ruleSrcSimpleType` for another `src-*`/`cvc-*`/`cos-*` constant repeats the
    same fabrication under a different name — the grounding's sharpest edge
    case, and the arbiter verified by grep that neither new message carries one.
  - **`ruleSrcSimpleType` was NOT swept.** It stands at its three genuine
    functions, five call sites: `listItem` (`:1851`, `:1855`, clause 3),
    `unionMembers` (`:1932`, clause 4), `resolveBase` (`:2026`, `:2030`,
    clause 2). Removing a constant from two wrong sites is not a reason to
    remove it from five right ones.
  - **The `§3.16.2.1` pointer stays verbatim in both message strings.** It is
    genuinely wrong in both — §3.16.2.1 is `map.std.common` (`:3631`), which
    assigns `{base type definition}`, `{variety}` and `{facets}` and says
    nothing about how many children a `<simpleType>` carries — but **#742 owns
    the message text**, its Acceptance asks for more than a pointer swap, and
    fixing it here would half-do that landing's tree-wide grep. The arbiter
    ruled this correct scope discipline for the NEITHER message and a tracking
    gap for the other one (finding 2, Next).
  - **The MORE-THAN-ONE branch is pinned by a new internal test, not through
    `Produce`.** `constructSimpleType` runs `checkS4SChildOrder` ahead of
    `simpleTypeBody` and charges the repeated child first, so a fixture driven
    through `Produce` pins the s4s walk's verdict and never this function's;
    census is the only caller that still reaches the branch and it discards the
    value. Without `parser/produce_simpletypebody_internal_test.go` the
    branch's footing would be asserted nowhere. Both new tests were
    mutation-verified by mason and again independently by the arbiter, which
    reinstated `xsderr.New(ruleSrcSimpleType, …)` on each branch in turn and
    confirmed each failure on both the `RuleOf` and the position assertion.
    `TestSimpleTypeBodyReturnsTheChosenAlternative` is a real positive control
    rather than decoration.
  - **Absorbed rather than filed** (WORKFLOW's scope rule, each named in the
    account and each falsified by the diff itself): four stale comments still
    asserting the old `src-simple-type` footing — `parser/census.go:277-281`,
    `parser/census_region_test.go:219-222`, `parser/produce_s4sorder.go:266-268`
    (which called the rejection a "verdict", which it no longer is) and
    `conformance/schema.go:1442-1446`. `conformance/schema.go:234` and `:262-267`
    were checked and left alone: they name `src-simple-type` correctly, for
    clauses 2/3/4.
- Surprises:
  - **The band's premise was half wrong, and the wrong half was the ranking
    argument.** `docs/PLAN.md`'s Working band row 4 read the defect as *"since
    #1076 no consumer can read the charge at all, so the defect is now silent as
    well as wrong"*, and ranked #1097 below #1099 because *"this one's
    reachability is what has to be established first"*. Reachability was
    established and it SPLITS: the MORE-THAN-ONE branch is indeed dead from any
    schema document, but the NEITHER branch — the one the issue disclaimed to
    #742 and #742 disclaimed back — is reached by `constructSimpleType`
    directly, so the wrong rule ID was reaching real callers the whole time.
    The issue was under-ranked on the strength of a fact about the branch that
    was not its subject.
  - **A verification that rendered the right document and asked it the wrong
    question.** Mason's account states *"`parser/doc.go` carries no claim about
    this — verified by rendering `go doc ./parser`"*. It does carry the claim:
    `doc.go:285-292` enumerates the no-rule-ID §5.1-first-bullet class by member
    function, and this landing was about to promote `simpleTypeBody` into it.
    Rendering the package doc finds nothing when the search term is the function
    name and the claim is a class-membership list. The arbiter caught it and
    said why it is worth a finding rather than a shrug — *"a later agent will
    trust that"* — which is the failure mode of a negative result reported as
    verified rather than as searched-for-and-not-found.
  - **A verdict with zero blocking findings still moved the tree before it
    landed.** Finding 1 was a real defect in a file the diff had already
    touched; it was non-blocking only because `rejectLocalSimpleTypeAttrs` was
    missing from the same list before this diff, which made the enumeration
    illustrative rather than exhaustive to begin with.

  read `git log origin/main..origin/wip/issue-<n>` and got hundreds of commits

  visible history, and does **not** name the two-dot `git log` range — which is
  the command a branch survey actually reaches for — and it names no remedy at
  all. `git fetch --unshallow origin` fixed it in one call and every reading
  after it was trustworthy. A documented hazard whose document omits both the
  common command and the one-line fix is a finding about the document; filed
  below rather than re-derived next session. Documented costs, one clause each:
